## What a round is for

*2026-09-13, later. Conformance **2432 → 2441/2441**, strict **173 →
164**, `errors` **503** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 113
silent. The "Expected a function of type" family and the rest of
`template-instance-identifiers.k` but two shapes.*

The cross-module round of the morning opened a next round for exactly two
reasons: a copy mentioning a template, or a foreign spec pending. Both are
about copies. The reference's loop has no such gate — it runs while
`decidedInstances` decides anything (`Template.hs:55`) — and two shapes of
the module's *own* text need a second round with no copy saying so:

* **A postponed candidate.** `A<uint32>::A1_t Do(A<uint1>::A1_t x)`: the
  reference decides the parameter's instance in round one and the return
  type's in round two (`--template-iterations 1` against `2`,
  `scratchpad/fn/v4.k`), and this census agrees with it — the return
  type's argument has no type in the table until the parameter's instance
  has landed. The census now records what it declined of a known template
  (`ModuleInstances::postponed`), and a postponed site in the module's
  text opens the next round.
* **A depth-two decision.** `A<A<bool>::A1_t>` is decided at depth two by
  the program census, so no copy of it lands in round one and nothing in
  a copy mentions it. The depth alone opens the round
  (`census_left_work`). Multi-round instances in a module's own text had
  never worked through the gate; `xtask ir` grades one iteration and could
  not say.

Both cost a twin census on modules that would not otherwise have had one.
`bench --filter keystroke` reads 366 and 363 ms on `risc-v.k`, inside the
slow mode's band (348–368 across the day); the tripwire did not fire, and the
change is not an order of magnitude anywhere.

Four more things, each one probe wide:

* An argument of a written list is parsed as a value path either way
  (`A<bool>::A2_t<2>` inside `A<…>`); whether it is a type is the
  parameter's kind to say. `typename_argument` reads it off the template,
  the same line `path_is_a_type` draws for `limits<uint8>::max` under
  `template <auto N>`.
* `N::A<uint32>`: an import alias or a namespace before the instance is
  stripped, as `lookupSymbol` over the whole name strips it
  (`findInImport`, `SymbolTable.hs:272-278`); and the twin's import view
  now answers *every* import's finished map under that same key rule —
  `__kg_m0::__kg_m1` reaches an unaliased import's nested copy, and
  `N::__kg_m0::A1_t` an aliased one's. The integration test that pinned
  silence for `lib::Hold(z)` was wrong: the reference rejects the aliased
  program exactly as the unaliased one (`scratchpad/al/m.k`, 6:16), and
  the test now says so.
* The CST template index reaches a member template of a class nested in a
  class (`Templates::of`), which is what a receiver typed
  `T3<uint4>::T4<bool>` is in the twin, so `c.Bar<uint33, Go>` validates
  `Fn` under the copy's substituted signature.
* A written class qualifier survives a copy: `A<C::W>` put `using A1_t =
  W;` in the copy, and `W` alone names nothing. The printer spells a
  qualifier chain whose own head ranges spell their identifiers
  (`Printer::written_qualifier`) — a written `C::`, never the chain
  `makeQualified` minted for a declaration's scope, which wears a donor's
  range.

The census and the CST check are held to one answer by `xtask ir`'s
differential, and it caught the drift at once: `template_instance.k`
showed five IR-only sites until `Cx::instance_qualified` read the same
two rules off the CST — the lead stripped, the argument's position off
the parameter — and 287 instances now resolve on both sides, 282 before.

One expectation corrected by the oracle rather than the code: `const bool
x = {false, 10};` is reported **twice** by the reference, at the list and
at the element (`scratchpad/fn/n1.k`, 1:17 and 1:24), and so it is here.

Left in the file: `::26` (a nested foreign instance argument returned
from a function, whose conversion message spells the whole instance type)
and `::37,38,40` (`using Bbool = B<bool>;` — an alias *to* an instance,
whose members the census would have to reach through the alias).

## The cross-module second round

*2026-09-13. Conformance **2420 → 2432/2432**, strict **185 → 173**,
`errors` **494** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 122 silent. Every
`template-instance-identifiers.k` shape that names a member of a foreign
class instance now reports where the reference does; A1's last
architectural piece.*

Phase 2 now iterates. A twin's census can decide an instance of a template
it does not own — `__kg_m0::A<bool>`, a member of a copy the *helper's*
twin declares — and that decision (`TwinDecision`) is handed to the owner
as a foreign spec on the next pass over phase 2; the owner's round-two
gate fires on a pending foreign spec even when its own copies mention
nothing (`foreign_pending`), and the importer's next twin resolves the
mention. Up to `MAX_PROGRAM_PASSES` passes, each re-running every target
until no twin decides anything new.

The hand-off was the small part. Three things stood between the decision
and the verdict, none of them in the elaborator's loop:

1. **The importer's twin could not sort the mention.** `twin_sorted`
   lowers a twin under the program's own import view, and the program
   never heard of `__kg_m0`; `__kg_m0::A<bool>::A1_t` stayed an unsorted
   `Path` (`ArgsOnNonTemplate`), so there was no `TemplateInstance` node
   for `resolve` to rewrite and the decision sat in the census doing
   nothing. The sorter now has a second door (`sorted::find_in_twins`):
   the finished twins' harvested shapes, under `findInImport`'s own alias
   stripping and namespace prefixing, asked only when the program's
   tables are silent — a twin re-declares everything its source declares,
   and offering those again would only hand `nub` duplicates.
2. **The finished map carried round one's names alone.** `__kg_m1`, made
   in the helper's third round, was invisible to the importer's table.
   Every round's twin declares what the previous one did and more, so the
   last round's map is the whole and earlier rounds fall back
   (`Round::names`).
3. **One instance, two aliases.** An argument spelled through a copy's
   alias — `A<__kg_m0::__kg_m1::A3_t>` — mangles as written at the mention
   (`Mangle.hs:57`) and from the census's *shape* at the owner's copy
   (`mint_foreign_specs` has nothing else), and the pool minted `__kg_m3`
   for one and `__kg_m4` for the other. In the reference the two agree by
   construction: one tree, one `args` (`Template.hs:159-163`). Here the
   mention is brought to the shape's spelling by the same minter before
   `resolve` mangles it (`canonical_foreign_args`), and only where a twin
   alias is in the spelling — a written argument keeps the spelling the
   reference's own names are graded against.

The seam test moved and was right to: with the door, the read-back pairs
the written `T1<int32>` with the twin's node and types it at home as the
copy's class, and the home run's message then spelled
`h::T1<|$int@32|>`. `validateArg`'s value clause spells both types with
`showUnmangled` (`TypeCheck.hs:293-294`); this port had `show_pretty` at
that one arm.

Two smaller gaps fell with the same probes, in-file as well as across
modules. Pass 12's arity check read only single-segment paths; `C::M<…>`
is `lookupSymbol` over the whole scoped name (`Frontend.hs:411-412`), and
in the twin every `A<bool>::A2_t<2, 3>` is one — the error at the member's
segment, as the reference's note. And a file whose only template was a
class member was never elaborated at all (`declares_a_template`), while a
copy's member copy — `__kg_m0::__kg_m1::A2_t<2>`, a class inside a class
— was a candidate neither the census (`IrTemplates::build`) nor the
owner's template list (`template_items`, `member_class`) could see; both
now descend nested plain classes, keyed by the innermost class's simple
name, which `IrTemplates::member` already guarded for uniqueness.

A dead end, deleted: `home_range` grew an enclosing-node fallback when the
decision's site — a path *segment* — matched no start-aligned pair. That
was the unsorted path again; once the door sorts the member segment into
its own `TemplateInstance` node, the pair exists, and the fallback pinned
nothing (the test stayed green with it off). Seven of eight breakages went
red; the eighth is the one that went.

---

## A member template's instance lands inside its class

*2026-09-12. Conformance **2420/2420**, strict **185**, `errors` **484**
agreeing at 25 disagreements, 132 silent — unmoved, and the reason is the
useful part. A1's member-template piece, the materialising half.*

`C::B_t<2>` through a plain class and `Foo<bool>::A_t<2>` through a class
instance: the reference makes `B_t<|@2|>` in round one and `A_t<|@2|>` in
round two, once `Foo<|$bool|>` is a plain class (`kg-oracle --tree
--template-iterations 1` against `2`, `scratchpad/mt/b.k`), each copy
beside its template *inside the class body* — `instantiate`'s `SeqF` is
in place wherever the template sits, and `removeNestedSeq` splices it
(`Template.hs:112-121`). The rewrite here already did that by path; what
did not know member templates was everything upstream of it. The census
now reads `C::M<…>` — a bare qualifier naming a plain class, then the
member's own list — as a candidate at the member's segment
(`IrTemplates::members`, `ArgFold::segment_range`); the module's own
templates include the members of its plain classes, so a spec finds its
node; the round-two gate fires for a mention of a copy's member from the
module's own text (`__kg_m0::A_t<2>`); and the printer spells a copy's leaf
under its class (`C::B_t<|@2|>`), since a member copy is nothing without
its qualifier. `scratchpad/mt/b.k` reports both excess elements where the
reference does, in-file.

Three things bit, and two of them were the same mistake in different
places. The printer rule as first written spelled *every* qualifier before
an alias leaf, and 137 of 353 twins stopped parsing — a materialised scope
component (`$`, `?lambdaN`) is not a name; the rule takes a bare class
name and nothing else. Phase 1 resolved a deduced call by simple name
among *all* owned templates, and a member named like a top-level template
made the name ambiguous, which silenced five deductions
(`template-argument-deduction.k::21,50,55,76,195`); the simple-name map
is over the top-level templates alone. And `nested-templates.k::14` moved
from silent to disagreeing: the reference types an alias copy `TInstance`
and spells the target `C<bool>::X<uint32>`, where this table reads through
the alias to `uint32` — the same verdict, differently spelled — so a
conversion whose declared type is written as a member instance is
declined until the read-back wraps an alias copy as the reference does.

Why the corpus did not move: every `template-instance-identifiers.k`
shape names a member of a *foreign* class instance —
`B<bool>::A<uint32>::A1_t` with `B` in the helper — and the copy of
`B<bool>` lives in the helper's twin, which phase 2 finishes before the
importing module's twin decides `__kg_m0::A<uint32>`. That is the
cross-module second round: phase 2 iterating until no twin decides a
foreign instance. It is the next slice, and this one is what it needs
first.

---

## The seam: a foreign instance's verdicts in the importing module

*2026-09-11, night. Conformance 2406 → **2420/2420**, strict 199 →
**185**, `errors` 470 → **484** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 132 silent.
A1's cross-module piece, the half that needs no new copy.*

`static T1<bool> c; c.Bar<uint16, 6>(true);` with `T1` in another module
was silent for three reasons stacked, and each was one rule.

**The base run cannot see the type.** Its table types the foreign
instance `Unresolved`; the twin types it as the copy, through the
finished twin's map laid over the imports (`elaborated_hit`) — but the
twin's verdicts at the module's *own* text, outside every copy, were
dropped as "the base run's business". They are carried home now,
unframed, at the start-aligned pair of the module's own text (the
*seam*), and the base run keeps any node it spoke at itself; a
`while compiling` frame still marks the ones raised inside a copy.

**The twin's index did not know the copy.** `Templates` for a twin was
built over the *base* parses of the other modules, which hold the
template and never `class __kg_m0`; and the type the twin reads names the
copy by its mangled original, `T1<|$bool|>`, while the declaring twin
spells the alias. `Elaboration::twin_roots` keeps every finished twin's
parse — a `Parse`, not a `SourceFile`: the latter is a thread-local
cursor and `kg-lsp` shares the database across threads, which the build
said before any test could — and `Templates::with_aliases` retries a
class lookup under its alias.

**The copy was misnamed.** The importing module spells the instance
`Bux<|@@helper@initializer_list@Bar$bool|>`, as the reference does at the
mention and at the copy (`kg-oracle --tree --passes 8`); the declaring
module's twin, handed the foreign spec, minted the argument `Bar` as a
bare leaf and mangled it `@Bar` — a copy no mention could reach, so the
importing twin's `__kg_m1` resolved to nothing. `mint_leaf` now hangs the
owner's namespace on the minted `ScopedName` as a prefix chain the
printer spells as nothing and the mangler reads. `xtask ir`'s resolve and
instance diffs stayed at 0 DIFF, which is the check.

Fourteen assertions came home: the member call on a foreign instance,
the initializer list against a foreign struct instance and its element
conversions, `T X` under `T = T1<int32>`. Measured with the seam carry
stubbed out: eleven of them are the base run's, over the read-back table
— the read-back pairs every `Own` node of the module, not only the
copies', so the elaborated table types `c` — with the twin roots and
aliases in its index; three are the seam's alone, `T X` under a foreign
instance among them, and the test pins that one. Still silent nearby: a nested
initializer list's element against a foreign struct's field
(`initializer-list.k::56`), and the member *instance* that needs a copy
landed inside a class body (`B<bool>::A<uint32>::A1_t`).

## A member template under its class instance's bindings

*2026-09-11, evening. Conformance 2405 → **2406/2406**, strict 200 →
**199**, `errors` 469 → **470** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 146 silent.
A1's member-template piece, the validating half.*

`Foo<bool>::S<4>` over `template <T N> struct S` inside `template
<typename T> class Foo`: the reference's copy `Foo<|$bool|>` holds
`template <bool N> struct S`, and the second segment's `4` is validated
against *that* (`kg-oracle --tree --passes 8`, `scratchpad/mt/a.k`). Pass
8 here declined every qualified segment. It now binds the class template's
`typename` parameters from the qualifier's written arguments
(`Instance::outer`) and validates the member's own list under them — a
kind that is a bare mention of an outer parameter is the bound type, a
kind mentioning one inside a larger type still declines. `Templates`
indexes a class *template's* member templates as it did a plain class's;
the twin's copy of the class is the plain-class case already served.
`nested-templates.k::8` came home at the argument.

What this does not reach, and why: the twin's own verdicts at a mention
*outside* a copy are not carried home — the base run owns those — and the
base run types `static T1<bool> c;` in the importing module `Unresolved`,
so `c.Bar<uint16, 6>()` (`member-function-template.k::9`) waits on the
cross-module read-back of a foreign instance's type, which is also what
`Bux<Bar, bool> x = {{0, 1}, 10}` (`initializer-list.k::54-58`) needs.
The materialising half — `B<bool>::A<uint32>::A1_t`, a member template
*instance* landing inside the copy — is the census's `Class::Member<…>`
candidate and `instantiate` placing a copy in a class body, still open.

## A value parameter's written type, read off its module

*2026-09-11, later still. Conformance 2398 → **2405/2405**, strict 207 →
**200**, `errors` 462 → **469** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 147 silent.
`docs/gaps.md` A3.*

Pass 8's `templateTypeCheck` declined every instance whose value
parameter's type was not a written built-in: `template <foo N>` over
`using foo = uint5`, `template <Bar B>` over an imported enum, `T x` under
`T = S` for a struct — "only a written built-in is decidable without the
declaring module's type table" was the silence, and the declaring
module's table is exactly what `resolveTemplateParamType`
(`TypeCheck.hs:349-362`) re-infers the type in. `Whole::tables` hands pass
8 any module's converged table by file, and `Instance::substitute` reads
the written type there — the template's own parameter type off *its*
module, a substituted argument off this one — into `Kind::Resolved`, whose
validation clause already existed for the dependent `int<N>` width. Seven
snippets came home with the reference's messages, `showPretty` spelling
the expected type as `helper.enum::Bar` and the initializer list as
`{uint4, uint4}`. The census had to learn the same reading
(`instances::Env::written`, off the declaring module's parse and table),
or `xtask ir`'s differential caught the two readings deciding different
instances on `test/library/data/fifo/array.k` — `TestArray<TestType::One>`
over an enum-typed parameter.

Three of the same family stay silent for other reasons: `T X` under `T =
T1<int32>` needs the instance argument's type resolved in this module's
table, which the read-back gives only where the census decided the
instance; and `c.Bar<uint16, 6>()` on a `T1<bool>` and `Foo<bool>::S<4>`
are member templates through a class instance — A1's remaining piece.

## A template's parameter list is judged, and a function's scope is its body

*2026-09-11. Conformance 2391 → **2395/2395**, strict 214 → **210**,
`errors` 455 → **459** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 157 silent.*

Pass 9 skipped a template whole. The reference does not: `undefinedSymbol
(Template _ b) x` rebuilds the node from the pass's own *parameter list*
and the *original* body (`Frontend.hs:93-94`), so an error in the list
survives and one in the body is thrown away. `template <Foo N>` with no
`Foo`, `(S, T) -> R F` with no `S`, and `uint<N>[M] A` before `M` is
declared are the three corpus shapes (`template.k::46,19,4`). The last
needs order: `paramList` nests one `unscopedWith [x]` per parameter
(`Parser.hs:361-364`) and `getSymbols` files none of them (`:362`), while
the item tree seeds every parameter into one scope — so inside a list the
probe reads the parameters *before* the use off the CST and skips the
template's own scope.

And the function scope's range was the whole declaration, which put the
signature inside the body: `inline Return Foo() { using Return = uint32; … }`
found its return type in the body's table (`using.k::29`), and the hint
machinery — `use_scope` read off the innermost item plus `$` for any use
inside a function — offered the body's alias for its own return type.
The scope now spans the body block, as `functionScoped $ braces …`
(`Parser.hs:424`) says, and `use_scope` is the replayed qualifier
(`scope_at`, `qualifier_at`) — which changed no hint the errors gate
grades.

## What a string's holes say, read off the token

*2026-09-10, night, last. Conformance 2381 → **2391/2391**, strict 224 →
**214**, `errors` 445 → **455** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 161 silent. `docs/gaps.md` A7, the ten `interpolated-string.k`
rejections.*

The lexer keeps a whole `"…"` as one token and the event stream cannot
split one (divergence #15), so a hole's expression is not a node: pass 6
never typed it, pass 9 never resolved it, and pass 18 could judge only
literals. The structural fix — re-lexing the token's text into
`INTERPOLATED_STRING`/`INTERPOLATION` nodes — is still the right one for
the backend bridge, which needs the reference's `InterpolatedStringF`
segments; this slice takes the other route for the diagnostics, over the
scanner pass 18 already owned.

**A name → declared type over the whole program.** `Whole::names` is this
module's own `ModuleTypes` (keyed with its namespace) and `findInImports`
behind it (`passes::types::Imports`), built by `frontend_diagnostics` and
handed down to pass 18 as an `Option<&dyn Fn>` — `None` at the one-file
door, which has no program. A hole that reparses to a name, or a call of
one, is typed from a local declaration at its own node or from the
resolver, and the value-type and format clauses run over it exactly as they
ran over a literal (`Frontend.hs:263-270`): `{boolConst:x}` over a `const
auto boolConst = true` is "Invalid format specifier `x` for the value of
type `const bool`", `{c}` over `static C c` is not a value type, `{foo()}`
is `void`. The note is the expression's own — I first wrote it one column
before, having miscounted the snippet's columns; the probe corrected it.

**Bare names are pass 9's.** `{intConst1}` and `{intConst,intConst1}` are
"Symbol name not in scope", from the string's own offset through the
scoped probe. And an import used *only* inside a hole had been warned
redundant: `mark_used_imports`' probes now reparse each hole and push its
paths as written, which is what justifies `import .options as opt` in
`logic/context_saver_depth.k`'s `"{opt::stall}"`.

**Two parse errors.** `format`'s grammar (`Parser.hs:895,900-903`) rejects
`{x=:}` — "unexpected '}' expecting 'X', 'b', 'd', 'o', or 'x'" — and
`{x=:d 10}` — "unexpected '1' expecting '}'" — at the offending character.
Raised before pass 1's checkpoint, since a parse error keeps the reference
out of the frontend; the `split` that fed pass 18 stops declining such a
body on the format's account, because a name is resolved before the
format is parsed.

## The imports' constants, and four more verdicts off the silent list

*2026-09-10, night, later. Conformance 2376 → **2381/2381**, strict 229 →
**224**, `errors` 440 → **445** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 171 silent.*

**A fold environment that stops at the file.** `FileScope` folded one
file's constants and nothing more, so `static assert("foo" != also_str_foo)`
over `import helper.string`, `Bar::B1 != 0` over `helper.enum`, and every
`opt::X` through an alias were undecidable — the reference's `lookupSymbol`
reaches an imported constant through `findInImports` (`SymbolTable.hs:263-270`)
exactly as it reaches a local one. `Db::file_scope` now folds each module
once per item tree *with its imports' constants already in the environment*
(`FileScope::of_with`): every key of each import target's `visibleSymbols`,
namespace stripped and the alias prepended when the import has one, read off
the declaring module's own memoized scope — post-order over the import
graph, which is acyclic or already an error. Two things bit. Laid under
*after* the file's own fixpoint, `F = Bar::B1` in an enum of the importing
module was declined first and `G = F` reported as never evaluating
(`enum.k::8,9`, both `expected:0`); the imports go in before the fold. And
`.options` holds the backend options' *defaults*: the reference compiles
`options.k` with `--stall 3` and `static assert(stall == 3)` holds there,
while `xtask conformance` drops those flags as having no frontend meaning
— so folding the default invented two failures. `.options` is left out;
`.cmdargs`' defines are the program's own and fold.

**`decltype` of a variable or a call** is a type the fold compares. The
2026-09-07 rule trusted only a literal, an initializer list or a function
under `decltype`, each widening needing its own evidence; the evidence is
now in `scratchpad/sc/dt5-8`: `const uint32 v` makes `decltype(v) ==
uint32` hold (the `const` is the variable's), a local `uint32 v` fails
`decltype(v) != uint32`, and `decltype(x())` over `inline uint32 x()` is
`uint32`. `type-constexpr.k::49` came home; `::48` — `static uint32 x;
decltype(x())` — is the reference's "static assertion failed" against this
port's "Undefined function" and stays booked.

**A capture of an undeclared name** is judged on the `CAPTURE`, from the
offset just before the lambda: the capture is *declared* inside the
lambda's scope, so asked from within, the probe would find the capture
itself. And the `static if` predicate verdict moved to the statement, where
`desugarError` renotes it — `Ten` folding through the import made
`static-if.k::39` decidable and the first report sat on the predicate.

## Pass 9 at the use site's own scope

*2026-09-10, late night. Conformance 2370 → **2376/2376**, strict 235 →
**229**, `errors` 434 → **440** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 176 silent.
`docs/gaps.md` A5's main half.*

Pass 9 judged "declared anywhere in this file" because the finished item
tree kept only each scope's *end* qualifier, and the reference's
`localScoped` rewrites a parent's qualifier every time a block closes
(`Parser.hs:153-155`): a `y` declared in a `case` body is
`[main,$,$quasi0,y]`, and the `y` after the `switch` is looked up from
`[main,$,$quasi1]`, which walks outward to nothing. What was missing was
not a lookup but a *replay*. Each scope now records the node it was pushed
for and, on the parent, the offset every local child closed at together
with the parent's qualifier from then on (`ScopeData::range`, `deepened`);
`scope_at(offset)` is the innermost scope live at a use and
`qualifier_at` is its qualifier at that moment. Pass 9's first source then
asks the reference's two questions at that point — `findInScopes` over
the chain's tables (their finished state, so a later declaration in the
same scope counts as seen: an over-approximation, toward silence) and
`lookupInScope` from the replayed qualifier over the program map — and
falls back to the file-wide answer only where the use cannot be placed.

Two things were in `declared_here` and in no scope's table, and both
surfaced as the same 900 false positives across `test/library` on the
first run: the intrinsics (`assert`, `__cycles`; `Type.hs:1074-1082`) and
the import aliases (`SymbolTable.hs:276-278`). Both are now the probe's
first answer. A name any `static if` declares still counts everywhere:
only the taken branch's declarations survive to pass 9, and which branch
that is remains pass 16's.

Still silent, by shape: a nested function's body sees the enclosing
function's locals here and not in the reference, because `moveFunctions`
has hoisted it to the module by pass 9 (`local-functions.k::1`); a lambda
capture of an undeclared name is judged on a `CAPTURE`, not a `PATH`; and
`f.Bar()` on a class with no `Bar` needs the receiver typed.

## Four verdicts from the silent list, and a written array that never left home

*2026-09-10, night. Conformance 2356 → **2370/2370**, strict 249 → **235**,
`errors` 420 → **434** agreeing at 25 disagreements, 196 → 182 silent.*

Read off `xtask errors --verbose`'s silent list after the second round
landed, smallest families first, each probed against `kg-oracle --errors`
before a line was written (`scratchpad/nt3/`).

**Pass 12's `unresolveArgError` arm** (`Frontend.hs:423-428`): an argument
`templateArgResolved` refuses is "Unresolved argument for the parameter `p`
of template `e`" on the argument. Decided only where the refusal is certain
from the tree — a value argument naming a runtime value, bare or inside an
initializer list, and `auto` as a type argument to a class template — which
is seven snippets; a `cast<int32[2]>(1000)` the reference cannot fold is
left alone, since "this folder cannot" is not "the reference cannot". The
first cut invented two errors on `constexpr.k::72,73`: `T1<1 == 0 ? x : 1>`
names a runtime `x`, and `names_a_runtime_value` said so, but pass 6's
`eval (MuxF …)` (`Constexpr.hs:311-314`) selects the literal case before
anything judges the other. A `mux` anywhere in the argument is no verdict.

**A union initializer's second element** is excess (`checkUnionInit`,
`TypeCheck.hs:168-172`), designated or not. The port had skipped union
targets whole on the belief that the excess error was the rule's only
output; it is, and the port was not producing it.

**"template arguments missing" through an import.** The parse-time rule
judged only a template the file itself declares, because a program-wide
index by simple name cannot tell "imported" from "declared somewhere". The
module graph can: `Templates::with_visible` records, per file, the names
its *unaliased* imports make visible and the file declaring each
(`visibleSymbols`, `SymbolTable.hs:135-181`; an aliased import hides its
names, `:276-278`), and the rule fires when the index's declaring file is
that one.

**A written array type never reached a foreign twin.** `arg_shapes` read
named types off the table for the alias route and left everything else
opaque, so `A<uint32[2]>` and `FnT<uint32[2][3]>` were decided by the
census, handed to the declaring module's twin, and dropped there:
`const A<uint32[2]>::A1_t x = {1, 2, 3}` had no excess element and the
call's three rows against `uint32[2][3]` no verdict. A resolved `Ty::Array`
travels now; `mint_ty` already spelled it.

## An instance in prefix position, and a callee a copy could not spell

*2026-09-10, latest. Conformance 2351 → **2356/2356**, strict 254 → **249**,
`errors` 418 → **420** agreeing at 25 disagreements, `xtask ir`'s
differential 404 → **405/405**, its resolve diff back to 0 DIFF and its type
agreement 15/30 → **18/29**.*

**`A<uint32>::A1_t`.** An instance that is the *first* segment of a longer
path was nobody's: the census read only a path's last segment, the CST
differential declined any segment of a multi-segment path (`is_qualified`),
the printer's `ScopedName` fallback dropped a prefix it could not slice, and
the rename survey skipped prefix leaves — so a resolved
`A<|$uint@32|>::A1_t` reached the twin unrenamed and failed its parse
twenty-four times over the corpus before the survey learned the exception
(`ident_is_mangled`). Each reading now admits the first segment on its own
range, in a **type position only**. The value position is the reference's
line, not ours: `limits<uint8>::max` in `test/library/data/counter/saturating.k`
is folded by `evaluateConstexpr`'s `TemplateInstanceF` arm
(`Constexpr.hs:133-151`) before `decidedInstances` runs, and deciding it here
put a name in the resolve diff the reference never writes. The body lowering
allocates one bare `Exp::Path` for either position, so the census asks the
parse (`ArgFold::path_is_a_type`) rather than the IR. The trailing segment —
`Foo<bool>::S<4>`, a member template — is still declined; it needs a copy
landed inside a class body.

**A callee a copy could not spell.** The whole-program sweep of
`test/library` (a manifest over `library/` and `test/library/`, which the
per-snippet corpus never runs) found `unit::assert(tag, cond)` rejected
inside every copy of `test/library/data/hash_table.k`'s tests: "Invalid
number of arguments, expected 1". The sorted leaf names the *declaring*
namespace, `@test@internal@assert`, because `test.unit` re-exports it — and
that is the reference's own shape (`findSymbol`, `Parser.hs:642-645`), not a
bug to fix in the IR, which the oracle diff pins node-for-node. A copy sits
past `lowered_len`, so it cannot slice its written spelling, and no import
of the module is named `@test@internal@assert`; the printer wrote `assert`,
and the twin read the base intrinsic. `pretty_with_spellings` now carries
`(namespace, alias)` for every namespace an aliased import makes visible —
the keys of the target's `visibleSymbols` (`SymbolTable.hs:135-181`) — and
`import_alias` consults it first. The first guess, skipping a *qualified*
callee's argument count in `check_call`, was right for the wrong reason and
stays: an alias is no verdict until it resolves to its own declaration.

**The keystroke tripwire read 368 ms, and it was the machine.** The
recorded 170 ms (2026-09-10, morning) against 352-368 ms after the second
round looked like the pass-4 shape of disaster. An interleaved A/B — a
worktree at the commit before the round, its own target directory, the
`keystroke` stage alone, alternating — reads 349.8/347.4 ms for the baseline
and 356.3/354.2 ms for this tree: two per cent apart, inside the noise band, and
the machine is in its slow mode. The sample that was taken before the A/B (`sample(1)` over `kg
dump twin` on `risc-v.k`) says where a keystroke goes today, none of it new:
a quarter in `sorted_program`'s shape fingerprints, a quarter in the
rewrites and the per-module sorted lowering, a sixth in the error gate's
`check_with`. Round two itself is under the sampler's floor. The
`copies_mention_a_template` gate stays, cheap and exact.

## The twin's second round, and the names a twin cannot spell

*2026-09-10, later. Roadmap item 14's architectural piece, begun; the small
families of `docs/gaps.md` A4, A5, A6 and A8 landed the same day in seven
commits before it. Conformance 2348 → **2351/2351**, strict 257 → **254**,
`errors` 415 → **418** agreeing at 25 disagreements, `xtask ir`'s type
agreement 14/29 → 15/30; the corpus barely moved and the reason is the
useful part.*

**The second round.** A copy's body mentions instances of its own — `Bar<T>
b` inside `Foo<uint32>::Do` is `Bar<uint32>` — and no twin held them: pass
8's route printed one twin, inferred it, checked it, and stopped. The
reference's fixpoint is `desugar (instantiate . resolve)` to a budget
(`Template.hs:56-58`), so `elaborate_module` now loops: census the twin,
instantiate what it decided, print and reparse, infer, until a twin decides
nothing new (`MAX_ROUNDS = 8`). The passes run over the *last* twin, and
their diagnostics come home through every round, latest first — each round
translates ranges into the text it printed from and appends its own
`while compiling` frames (`translate_down`), and the first round decides what
was inside a copy at all, taking an already-framed diagnostic as inside by
construction. Two things bit on the way. The census reads `Path` nodes with
arguments, which only the *body* lowering has — the sorted lowering the
rewrites run on already holds `TemplateInstance` nodes — so a twin is lowered
twice, once each way, and the sites match by range as they do in round one.
And the probe that proved the loop (`scratchpad/el/a.k`: the reference's
"Invalid conversion from `uint32` to `bool`" at the body line, framed by the
instantiation) moved **zero** corpus assertions: none of the seventeen
`while compiling` silences is the same-module shape.

**What they are** (`scratchpad/snip2.py`, the extractor that finally counts
markers the way `syntax-test.py` does — `warning:` lines take an index too,
and the helper import is a header line): six are arguments the template's
twin cannot spell — a struct, an enum, a function or a template declared in
the *importing* module; four are member templates reached through a class
instance (`Foo<bool>::S<false>`, `c.Foo<uint16>(x)` on a `T1<bool>`); two
are a second round across modules; the rest are one each.

**The names a twin cannot spell** are now aliases. `mint_leaf` used to
decline a named type whose owner the template's module does not import; it
now draws `__kg_mN` from the one `RenamePool` for the type's unmangled
spelling, prints the alias where the name would be, and tells the twin's
import view what it denotes (`Imports::with_foreign`, a third route beside
the item trees and the elaborated maps — `TType t`, since a type *name*
denotes a type). A message that spells the alias is read back through the
same `Renames` every parse alias is, so it says `S`, which is how the
reference prints a headerless module's struct (probed, `scratchpad/fo/`).
The census records a named type's `Ty` instead of `Opaque` for that
(`ArgFold::type_at`). Arrays mint too — the deduction's `T[10]` under `T =
uint4[4]` — and the printer had to learn that a *nested* array node, which
only substitution creates, prints outer dimensions first: the reference's
type there is `TArray uint4 [10, 4]`, and `uint4[4][10]` is a different type.
`template-argument-deduction.k::50` is the one that came home: the
reference's single conversion error at the call, exactly.

**A deduced `auto N` never completed a call.** `deduced_calls` accepted
type slots only, so every template deducing a dimension — `Fn_T_N_T_N(x, y)`
over `uint3[10]`, `Fn_T_T_N(Enum::Zero, es)` — was silent, and the first
guess (a conflict in the array arm) was wrong: the deduction was fine, the
completion test was not. Integer slots are accepted, minted as literals by
the rewrite, and carried as values into a foreign spec; both calls now end
in the reference's conversion error at the call. The member-template shapes
need the census to admit `Class::Member<…>` candidates and `instantiate` to
land a copy inside a class body. The cross-module second round needs the
module loop of phase 2 to iterate, since a helper's twin is finished before
the snippet's mentions it. Each is its own slice.

## Nine verdicts off the silent list, and a fixpoint that was not monotone

*2026-09-10. The small families of `cargo xtask errors --verbose`, taken by
mechanism rather than by file. Conformance 2267 → **2296/2296**, strict 338
→ **309**, `errors` 349 → **374** agreeing at the same 26 disagreements,
`repoint` 14 → **15/72**.*

The verbose errors gate lists 281 snippets we compiled cleanly, with the
reference's message for each. Bucketed by message the list is a long tail:
57 conversions, 42 template arguments, 17 `while compiling`, and then
twenty-odd families of one to six. This pass took the families a written
tree plus the type table can decide outright, probing each against the
oracle first (`scratchpad/probe/*.k`, 2026-09-10). Two probes changed a
design before any code: a call through a closure says "expected 2" for a
one-parameter lambda, because `closureCalls` has prepended the capture by
pass 19; and a function-typed parameter written `(auto) -> void cb` is
*accepted*, because `higherOrderFunctions` makes a template of the function
before `AutoF` is ever checked.

**What landed, and the reference clause for each:**

* `Invalid number of arguments, expected N` (`TypeCheck.hs:91`) — in the
  conversion pass, which already paired parameters with arguments and
  returned on a mismatch. The note is the argument list's, which begins at
  the first argument or at the `)` of an empty one. A callee with an `auto`
  parameter is pass 12's "Could not deduce all arguments" and a callee with
  a function-typed parameter is rewritten first; both are passed over. The
  test that pinned the silence as a known gap now pins the error.
* `Function with [[reset]] …` (`:73-82`) — at the `[[reset]]`, the
  function's note; the return is the table's deduced one, so `auto foo() {
  return 3; }` is rejected and `auto bar() { }` is not.
* `Could not deduce type` (`:51`) — the three `auto`s no pass replaces: any
  inside a `using`, a `const auto` return (`isAuto` does not match `Const
  Auto`; only variables get `isConstAuto`, `Type.hs:1030-1035`), and the
  return of a bodiless `auto Do();`.
* `Expected 'const'. Mutable variables of a function type` (`:140`) through
  the table's reading of the written type — `decltype(Go)`, an alias.
* `Closures that capture value(s) are not allowed in global scope`
  (`:146-148`) — a module-scope variable initialized with a lambda whose
  captures' widths sum above zero; `[e]` over an empty struct is fine.
* `Expected a constant expression that evaluates to non-negative integer`
  (`:198-199`) — the set of `IntAttrF` attributes is closed
  (`Parser.hs:173,389-391,564,581,874-876`), so a `bool` or float argument
  is decidable, and so is an argument that *cannot* fold: an arithmetic
  expression over names one of which is a parameter or a non-`const`
  variable, found by the innermost-declaration walk pass 16 already had.
* `bytesizeof is undefined for a type with bit size of N` and `Illegal
  operands for bitoffsetof` (`Constexpr.hs:162-166,274-275`) — the folder
  spelled both messages since it was written and nothing ever reached them:
  `sizeOf` and `offsetOf` are `tWidth . typeOf` questions and pass 6 folds
  over the file-scope environment, which answers none. Pass 6 now folds
  those roots through the typed evaluator under pass 16's trust rule, and
  `WidthEnv::bit_offset_of` answers from the table (it delegated to an
  environment that always said `None` — a valid `bitoffsetof` would have
  been "Illegal" the day anything folded it).
* Enum constants that name each other (`:205-215`) — `E2 = E1 + 2` never
  folded, because the constants are keyed `Foo::E1` and the initializer
  was folded from an empty scope. `lookup_const` and the name-is-a-constant
  gate now walk outward from the enum, and the "doesn't evaluate to an
  integer constant" arm is reported for the one shape where unfolded is
  unfoldable: every constant the fixpoint left behind is closed over
  literals and this enum's own names. The first cut broke
  `enum.k`'s `G = 2 * F, F = 0`: the running-value loop `?`-ed out on `G`
  before reaching `F`, so a failed earlier initializer poisoned every later
  one.

**Two bugs outside the slice, found by its tests.**

The parser's statement lookahead had no arm for a function type, so a
local `const (uint32) -> uint32 f = foo;` fell through to the expression
parser and was "expected `;`" — at module scope it parsed fine, which is
why the corpus never said. One arm in `skip_type_head`.

And `inline auto foo() { return bar(); }` tripped `kg-ty`'s monotonicity
assertion (`Inference.hs:36`) on round three — under `cargo test` only,
since every corpus gate runs `--release` with the assertion compiled out.
`setTypeOfTemplateCall` from the `FunctionF` clause stamps each returned
call's callee with `theType funcReturnType`, which for a written `auto` is
`TUnresolved`; the reference's node is an unresolved `TemplateInstance`
and stays so, but this port's bare path segment reads `Untyped`, which
counts as resolved, so the stamp raised the unresolved count. An
unresolved stamp is read by nobody — deduction's third source takes
`tReturn` of it — so it is now skipped. The invariant is the reason the
fixpoint terminates; a count that can rise is a loop that can oscillate.

**What is left in the families this touched, each its own blocker:** a
closure callee, which the table types `Unresolved` (the count case is
pinned as silence with the number it must say); array dimensions inside a
`static for` or a nested template; attribute arguments inside a copy; an
enum constant naming an imported one. The next families by size are the
name-not-in-scope class (24), most of it pass 9's "declared anywhere in
the file" under-approximation and a bogus second segment on a resolved
class or enum, and the seven `symbol is ambiguous` plus six `import
qualifier` cases, both `findSymbol` (`SymbolTable.hs:229-250`).

## The parser's own template check, and where a designator's error sits

*2026-09-09. Two small verdicts from the silent list.*

`static X x;` for a `template <auto N = uint32> struct X` is not a pass's
error: `typeSpecifier'` (`Parser.hs:712-721`) looks the name up in the
parse-time table and, finding a template with no `<…>` written, says
"`X`: template arguments missing" as a `PARSE-ERROR`. It exists before pass
1's checkpoint and outranks anything the passes say, so it runs first in
`run_through_8`, before pass 1. Three positions had to be excused where a
bare template name is meant: a template-template argument (`T1<S1>`), such
a parameter's default (`typename TT = S1`), and an `export`/`extern` of a
template, which is pass 13's verdict. And it judges only a template *this
file* declares: the parser's table holds what is in scope, and a same-named
template in a module this one does not import is not in it — there, pass
9's "Type name not in scope" is the reference's answer, and a program-wide
index by simple name cannot tell the two cases apart.

The designator: `Go({.x = 10, .x = 11})` against a `uint32[2]` is "Member
designator cannot initialize type uint32[2]" *once*, at the first
designator's `.` — one `TError` for the whole list, worn by the designator
node `.x = 10`, not by the list and not by the `10`. Two gate runs to get
that right: the first cut put it on the element, the second on the list.

## Two exclusions in the conversion pass, and the test that pinned one

*2026-09-08, night. From the survey of the "Invalid conversion" class, the
largest silent one at 67.*

Two shapes in that class were not blocked on anything: a function value
against a function-typed constant, and a designated initializer's fields.
Both were *exclusions* the pass had written for itself — `t.is_function()`
returned early, and `starts_with_designator` returned early — and the
second had a test whose name was `a_designated_initializer_is_silent` and
whose comment said the reference reports an error there. A test that pins
a known gap is fine; it just has to be read as one when the gap closes.
Both now convert: `const (bool) -> uint3 fn = Foo;` is "Invalid conversion
from `(bool) -> uint32` to `const (bool) -> uint3`", and `{.field1 = -10}`
on a `uint32` field takes `errorNarrowingConversions` (`TypeCheck.hs:130,
157`) — the error form with the cast hint, which the engine's `Narrowing`
already had a variant for that nothing called. A designated element's slot
is `TDesignator field (typeOf e)` to `tInitializedType` (`Type.hs:293-300`),
in a union as in a struct.

One position came back from the gate: a designator the target cannot take
is the *list's* error — `tInitializedType` of the whole initializer is the
`TError` and `checkConversion` renotes the list (`TypeCheck.hs:153`) —
where a positional excess element stays on the element. And pass 8 now
validates a member template's written instance, `c.Bar<bool, Go>(false)`,
through the same class index pass 4's member arm reads: the `<…>` list is
a sibling of the member's name under the `FIELD_EXPR`, which is the shape
that had made the plain arm's test pass while six corpus cases stayed
silent.

What the survey put beyond this pass: a member alias of a class-template

argument against the instantiated parameter (`Fn_T_10(x)` with a

## The closure a callback becomes, without the rewrite that makes it

*2026-09-08, night. Queue item 8's second half.*

Every remaining message in the class showed a type nobody wrote:
`(data.closure.core::make_capture0::$::Capture, uint32) -> uint32`. It is
what `higherOrderFunctions` makes of `inline uint32 Go((uint32) -> uint32
Do, uint32 x)` — a `typename Do$capture` and a `(Do$capture, uint32) ->
uint32 Do` (`Function.hs:313-345`) — and what `addLambdaWrappers` and
`desugarLambdas` make of the argument: a closure whose function type has
the capture class first (`:365-392`). The check itself is the plain one,
`validate typ@FunctionType{}` (`TypeCheck.hs:269-275`), over those two
types.

The roadmap row said this needed the twin route, because only the twin
holds a post-pass-8 signature. That was true of the *general* form and
false of what the check reads: the declared function type is written text
with the enclosing template's bound parameters substituted, the lambda's
function type is its written parameters and return, and the capture class
is a name — `data.closure.core::make_capture0::$::Capture` for no captures,
`data.closure::make_captureN<…>::$::Capture` for N, with the captured
declarations' types as the arguments. All three are readable from the tree
and the base table at pass 4, where the call is deduced. So the closure
check sits beside the plain one in `deduce_template_args`: on a template
whose function has a function-typed formal, after deduction and with the
deduced or explicit bindings as the substitution; and on a plain
higher-order function, which this tree never sees as a template, through
its own index.

Seven probes, six exact on the first run; the seventh — one capture — was
silent because the engine types a `CaptureF` by `typeOfSymbol` from the
lambda's own scope, which is the far side of a seam. The capture's type is
now read off the declaration the walk out from the lambda finds, and so is
the lambda a `const auto fn = […] …` holds, which was the commonest shape
left. A callback position given no function is the LT verdict, with the
function as its frame: `Go(3)`, `Go()`, and — from the survey — `Go(x, fn)`
with the arguments swapped. Two more corrections came from the gates: a
`void` position is dropped (`Type.hs:1353-1355`), which is `(void) -> R`
and every variadic slot a `= void` default leaves — three `expected:0`s
said so; and a lambda's closure type takes part in deduction, so `T` bound
from both `10` and `(uint3 x)` is the conflict, not the closure mismatch.
Pass 8's declared function type reads a named type through the table too:
`(T) -> T` under `T = E` is `(E) -> E` for an enum `E`. What declines: a
lambda returning `auto`, a method as the callback, an attribute on a
lambda's parameter, and a member template's written instance — pass 8
still validates only a path.

## The gate the reference runs its passes behind, and ten small verdicts

*2026-09-08, later. Queue item 7: the errors gate's 43 disagreements.*

The list partitioned into eighteen parse-recovery positions, five hint
lists, a handful of one-offs, and a class nobody had named: **pass
ordering**. `type-identifier.k::12` reports the undefined `Otter` on line 9
and not the "Global state" on line 5, and it is not because the reference
sorts them — it is because pass 19 never ran. `desugarPasses` is `foldr ($)
(program, False)` over wrappers that carry a `hasErrors` flag
(`Frontend.hs:38-52`): `pass`/`passPar` do nothing once it is set, and
`checkPar` sets it after the pass-1 composite; `instantiateTemplates` sets
it after pass 8; `undefinedSymbols` after pass 9. Three checkpoints, and
every error after the first of them to fire is an error the reference never
mints. `passes::run` is now `run_through_8` and `run_from_10` with pass 9
between them and the three checkpoints in place — per file rather than
program-wide, which loses nothing conformance grades and is the shape the
language server publishes in. One exemption had to be written down: pass 4
reports pass 12's LT verdict from where the list is decided, and pass 12 is
after the checkpoint, so that message does not close the pipeline.

The rest were each one line of the reference, and each one a probe:

* a `?:` arm that is a type is pass 19's error and the fold never reaches
  the selector — `2 ? bool : 3` is one error, not two (`type-check.k::6,7`);
  the file-scope environment answers `typeResolved` from names alone and
  cannot see a `TError`, so the fold reads the arm;
* an attribute's argument is the reference's *parser's* error, before any
  pass: `--passes 1` prints it as a `PARSE-ERROR` (`::17`);
* a width with a type error inside cannot fold, so pass 16's verdict stands
  at the declaration, first by position, and the operand error stays
  (`::1-4,14,15`);
* an array dimension is reported at its `[`, whatever was written — four
  probes, one column, and a comment in `validate_program.rs` that had
  claimed the opposite on a reading of `basics.k::173` the oracle does not
  bear out;
* a `clog2` that does not fold, written as a call's argument, is reached two
  passes earlier by `unresolvedFunctionTemplateArgs` (`Frontend.hs:436-444`)
  — the one shape of pass 11 worth porting, since its general clause fires
  on every argument this table leaves unresolved;
* a call through a resolved receiver with no such member is the member's
  name not in scope (`Frontend.hs:106-108`), never "Invalid member access":
  as a callee the access is `FunctionSpecifierF (Just a) b` and `method`
  gives `TUnresolved` for anything but a class. The first cut read that
  `TUnresolved` as "no such member" and invented seventy errors on `o.Fn_T(x)`
  and every `extern` class's `c.Do()` — `method` is as silent for a member
  it found untyped as for one it did not find, and the silence is kept;
* the supertype message spells its types when the engine hands the string
  table down (`basics.k::199`);
* `inScope` (`Frontend.hs:125-127`): a hint's declaring scope must prefix
  the referring expression's, which admits a local of the same function and
  refuses another's; the variable whose own initializer holds the undefined
  name is not offered (`tResolved`), the enclosing function is, a local
  function is not;
* and pass 12's EQ arm, "Failed to instantiate template"
  (`Frontend.hs:430`), for the one mismatch `templateArgsResolved` refuses
  that `templateArgResolved` does not: a template-template parameter given
  a type, a literal or a function.

What is left in the errors gate: the eighteen parse positions, where ours
is often the better one (an unterminated comment at its start, not at end
of input); the closure half of item 8, which also hides one pass-9 report
behind pass 8's checkpoint; a helper's `umul27` the device library declares;
and two the reference gets from reading a file it cannot decode.

*2026-09-08. Queue items 14 and 8, first batch after the twin's diagnostics.*

The survey that opened item 14 grouped the forty still-silent cross-module
cases by mechanism, and most of them were not cross-module at all. Six were
clauses no pass had ported, each a line in the reference: `checkEnumBaseType`
(`TypeCheck.hs:201-203`), "Type template cannot be exported"
(`Frontend.hs:340-341`), `exportableClasses` reaching a class *another
module* declares (`Frontend.hs:346-366` — the error's head is the member in
the declaring file and the export statement is the tail, so it is a `while
compiling` note without any twin), the abbreviated function template's LT
verdict (`a.Go()` against `inline void Go(auto x)`: the synthesized
parameter past the argument list is the unbound one, `Function.hs:296`,
`Type.hs:1477`), `deduceAuto`'s return-type arm after a failed deduction
(`Type.hs:1603`), and the LT verdict's own `while compiling` frame — the
template's declaration, which `new = flip newNote t` copies onto the
instance the rewrite mints (`Type.hs:1409,1462`).

The first cut of the cross-module export arm invented two errors, and the
cause was a pass that runs *before* pass 13: `higherOrderFunctions` rewrites
a function with a function-typed parameter into a template
(`Function.hs:313-316`), so `check PublicMember x@Function{}` never sees it.
`export PublicHOF;` is `expected:0` and said so.

Then the plain half of item 8. A `(bool) -> uint32 Fn` parameter is
`validate typ@FunctionType{}` (`TypeCheck.hs:269-275`): the argument's
function type must be a subtype of the declared one, with the earlier
`typename` arguments substituted into it — `(T) -> T` under `T = uint32` is
`(uint32) -> uint32` — and a method is "Expected a non-member function". The
closure half stays silent: a lambda's reference type is the desugared
`(Capture, …) -> R` of `closureFunctionType` (`Function.hs:328-331`), and
no table here holds it.

**And the one that was under everything: a member call had no type.**
`c.M(true)` typed `Undefined` at the `FIELD_EXPR`, because the arm ported
`infer (MemberAccessF a b)` — `fields c`, which is the data members only
(`Type.hs:1343-1346`) — and never `method (typeOf a) (getName b)`
(`Type.hs:1222,1358-1362`), the callee arm every member call takes. So
`bool b = c.M(true)` had nothing to convert from, and the reference's

engine. The field-access arm now falls back to it for a class receiver.
That one line is why this batch moved more than its six clauses: the
conversion pass sees every member call's result for the first time.

`kg dump twin` landed on the way — the counters of each elaborated module
and the text the passes ran over — and its first use found that the case
it was built for had been fixed by the previous commit and measured with a
stale binary. Rebuild before you survey.

What the survey left, by mechanism, is in the roadmap: instances mentioned
inside a copy (a second elaboration round), foreign arguments the route
cannot mint, template-template parameter checks, and the closure half of

## The twin's diagnostics come home, and a divergence stops being invisible

*2026-09-07, night. Queue item 10. The DX half — `while compiling` in three
renderers and as related information — driven over stdio and by hand.*

The read-back carried types home and nothing else, so an error the reference
raises on a materialised copy was silent here: the passes walked the original
CST and `reached_only_after_elaboration` skipped every template body. The
reference does not skip them — `instantiate` leaves each template as `SeqF $
map makeInstance … ++ [template]` (`Template.hs:118-121`) and every pass
after `instantiateTemplates` walks the copies like any other node. So the
twin — the reparse of the rewritten module the read-back already infers over
— is now also *checked*: the same wired pass list, over the twin's own
environment and table, and what it raises inside a copy is carried home.

Carrying is the read-back's walk in the other direction. A diagnostic's twin
range names a twin node; `SideMap` pairs it with the rewritten node it
printed from; that node's `Src` *is* the reference's note — `head` the body
range to report at (`desugarWithNote` keeps the copied node's own note on
the left, `Desugar.hs:92-94`), `via` the chain of instantiation sites
`expandErrorStack` renders as `while compiling` (`Error.hs:176-195`). Three
rules, each a refusal rather than a guess: only a node inside a copy
(`via != ROOT`) is carried — everything else the twin raises is the module's
own text seen twice, and the base run owns it; only a *start-aligned* pair
carries, because the reference reports the head's offset and nothing else
(`fixErrorOffset`, `Error.hs:183`); and a message that spells a `__kg_mN`
alias with no un-manglable original is declined, because the reference's
`showUnmangled` never prints a mangled name. Two copies raising one body
line are one report with two notes (`Set.insert (ErrorCustom …)`,
`Error.hs:194`).

**The first cut invented two errors, and the cause was a divergence this
repo had written down as unobservable.** `T5<uint5, 78, 14>` under `template
<typename T, T X, auto Y> class T5 { static assert(X == Y); }` is
`expected:0`, twice, in `constexpr.k`. `validateArg` re-stamps the literal
argument to the parameter's width *in the tree* — `78` under a `uint5` is
`14u5` (`TypeCheck.hs:281-283`) — before `instantiate` reads it, so the
reference's copy folds `14u5 == 14`. Ours substituted the written `78`, and
the instantiate test that pinned the mangled name said so in as many words:
"the body keeps whatever the deciding site wrote — a stated divergence …
not observable here". It was not observable because no copy was ever
diagnosed. The fix is the re-stamp at the point the copy reads its argument
list; the test now asserts the narrowed, stamped literal in the copy, and the
sentence is gone.

What it moved: conformance 2182 → 2196 decidable, strict 423 → 409, `errors`
260 → 271 agreeing at the same 43 disagreements — the copies of `enum.k`,
`export-class.k`, `template-argument-deduction.k` and
`template-template-parameter.k` whose bodies are in the snippet, then three
more from the fold below. What it did *not* move is the instructive part:
24 of the 25 `while compiling` lines in the silent list are still there,
and they are four different blockers, none of them the carrying.
`Bar<uint16, 32>` from `helper/function_template.k` materialises and is
checked, and its body is
`static assert(bitsizeof x == N)`, which pass 16 never folded *anywhere*: the
file-scope environment answers no width question, and the typed evaluator
was consulted only for type comparisons. So the second change of the night
hands `bitsizeof`/`bytesizeof` to the typed evaluator when every operand is
trusted — a written type, a name the table types as a type, `decltype` under
the existing rule, or a name whose *declaration* spells a type that is not
`auto` (found by walking outward; `const auto` is `ConstType(AutoType)` and
was the second test to go red). The typed evaluator's own `typeResolved`
gate had to learn the same thing: the table never types a `bitsizeof` node,
and the file-scope answer — every name a known constant — is the wrong
question for `bitsizeof x` when `x` is a parameter. The other three
blockers are queued below: a member template of a class instance (depth
two, declined by the route), a deduced call into a helper with a value
argument (`ArgShape::Opaque`), and `export X;` of a helper's instance,
whose pass-13 check runs over the helper's twin and never sees the snippet's
`export`.

Two things about the DX half. The legacy renderer prints a note as the
reference does — `note: ` and a whole nested bundle with its own excerpt —
and a note into another file needs that file, so `render_legacy_located`
takes a locator and the compat binary hands it the database; the modern
renderer prints a rustc-style secondary span with one gutter for the whole
diagnostic. And the language server's `relatedInformation` was `None` since
the day diagnostics were published; now a label becomes a clickable
location for any file the server can name. The stdio drive showed the
payload with the site's range; the e2e test pins it.

Hover inside a template body still says "Type not yet inferred" — the
read-back writes types home under the body's own ranges with the instance's
`via`, and the hover handler reads the `ROOT` key. That is the next DX
item this route makes possible, not a regression.

## Signature help reads the declaration, not the type

*2026-09-07, late. Queue item 13, the DX slice after item 12. Driven over
stdio before it was called done.*

The obvious source for a signature is `type_of_definition`: a
`Ty::Function` with its parameters. It is the wrong one, for the reason the
inlay-hint survey found in August: a template function's type is not
resolved before pass 8, so `Fn_T(x)` — most of what a Kanagawa library
exports — would have no signature. Its *parameter list* is text, `T x`,
and text is exactly what a signature box shows. So the handler resolves the
callee's last name token with `definition_at` (the jump's own answer),
walks two levels up from the name to the `FN_DECL`, and prints the
parameters as written with whitespace collapsed — attributes and
function-typed parameters included — with each span recorded in UTF-16
units as the label is built.

What declines is what the jump declines, plus one case the jump answers
and this must not: a call through a function-typed value, `fn(x)` with
`fn` a parameter, resolves to the *parameter*, which has no parameter list.
Two lines of the first cut were wrong and a test found each: `then_some`
evaluates its argument eagerly, so a zero-parameter function underflowed
the clamp; and `void` is a written return type like any other, so the
label is `f() -> void`, not `f()`.

## Two silent classes, and the operand the type table must not judge

*2026-09-07, evening. Queue item 12. Conformance 2161 → **2182/2182**,
strict 444 → **423**, `errors` 239 → **260** agree at the same 43; tests
1293 → 1296.*

**Excess elements** was one clause away. `checkInitItem` hands each element
`tInitializedType t (typeOf e)` as its target, and `checkConversion`'s
first clause reports a target that *is* an error (`TypeCheck.hs:153`) —
"Excess elements in array initializer" on the element at the dimension
(only that one; later indices read `tElement` again), "Excess element in
initializer of type S" on every struct overflow, "Non-empty initializer
list cannot initialize type uint32" on a scalar's first. `initialized_type`
already computed all three and `check` threw the error target away. One
`if let Ty::Error` before the call; six oracle probes for the texts.

**Type comparisons** were two environments away. `static assert(uint32 ==
uint30)` is `evalBinaryType` over `<:` (`Constexpr.hs:244-249`), and the
file-scope environment every pass folds with answers no type question, so
the assertion never folded. The type table's environment answers it — and
then `S < uint32` still declined, because the folder's `typeResolved` gate
asks the environment whether every *name* is a known constant, and a
struct's name is not one. `typeResolved` is a fact about the node's type;
for a type-valued node the table answers it directly, and the gate holds
for value-typed nodes as before.

Then `literal-operand.k`'s ninth snippet, `warning:0`, failed: seven
`static assert(decltype(o) == decltype(-200))` over `const auto o = 10 *
(-20)`, and two of them folded to `false`. The reference folds the product
to the literal before it types the declaration, so `decltype(o)` is the
literal's `int9`; this table's width algebra reads the unfolded product.
That is the `SEAM` `conversion.rs` already skips `auto` for, met from the
other side. So the verdict is confined to operands the table reads as the
reference does — a written type, a named type, `decltype` of an initializer
list, a literal or a function — and `decltype` of anything folded declines.
One corpus site was given back for it (`type-constexpr.k::49`) and one
warning assertion kept; that is the right trade every time.

Three plants: the error slot never the verdict, comparisons never deciding,
every `decltype` trusted — one test red each.

## Rename refuses, and that is the feature

*2026-09-07. Queue item 11, the DX slice interleaved after item 9. Tests
1285 → 1293; driven over stdio before it was called done.*

Rename is find-references with a replacement attached, and it was written
that way — `occurrences` over `search_plan`, every hit a resolution, nothing
decided by spelling. The design work was all in what it refuses.

`references` under-reports honestly: a use in a file nobody opened and
nothing open imports is invisible, and its docs say so. An edit that
under-reports is not honest; it is a file the user did not have open that no
longer compiles. So a rename of a file-scope declaration walks the project's
import directories for a `.k` the search did not reach that `import`s the
declaring module, and refuses naming that file. Open it, and its program
reaches the use, and the rename lands in both. A local, a parameter, a class
member is never scanned for: nothing outside its file can name it.

The second refusal was found by a test that was wrong. It asserted that
`"{total}"` would be rewritten, on the belief that the parser splits an
interpolation hole into nodes — the AST has `InterpolatedString` and
`Interpolation`, after all. The CST printed a single `STRING` token: the
grammar test at `grammar/tests.rs:1039` says why, the lexer emits a whole
string and the event stream can merge tokens but never split one, so those
node kinds are never produced. The hole is text the search cannot see, and
the reference reads it at pass 18 in the string's own scope. The test now
pins the refusal, naming the line; the hole finder is pass 18's own,
re-exported from `kg-db` so the two cannot disagree about what a hole is.

Refusals are request *errors* carrying a sentence, never `null`: the
dispatcher grew a second macro for a handler whose failure has something to
say. `prepareRename` applies the same refusals, so the client declines before
the user types, and answers `null` only off a name. Four plants — every name
an identifier, no hole ever mentions anything, no importer ever found, the
scope test inverted — each turned exactly one test red.

---

## Deduction's two failure verdicts, and the guard that made them reportable

Two silent classes, measured off `errors --verbose`: "Conflicting template
argument deduction" (16) and "Could not deduce all arguments" (13). They
turned out to be one mechanism and one guard.

**The mechanism.** Every conflict we missed was a member call, `static Class
o; o.Fn_T(x)`. Pass 4 fired only on a path callee, on the reasoning that a
member template is what `lookupInScope` finds *before* module scope and the
top-level index must not reach past it. That reasoning is right for a bare
`Fn_T(x)` inside the class and wrong for `o.Fn_T(x)`: `rewrite`'s first
clause (`Type.hs:1390-1391`) replaces the member access with the receiver's
*class* qualified name plus the member, an absolute key the scope walk never
sees. So a second index — top-level classes by simple name, members by
(class, member), collisions dropped the way the first index drops them —
answers that key exactly, and the same deduction runs. The stamp had the
same blind spot: `setTypeOfTemplateCall`'s descent through the receiver
ended on a `NAME_REF` it then refused to stamp, so the return context was
never a deduction source for a member call.

**The guard.** "Could not deduce all arguments" is pass 12's message
(`Frontend.hs:421`) for a list `sequence` threw away at pass 4
(`Type.hs:1407`). There is no rewritten tree here for pass 12 to count, so
the count is taken where the list is decided — and the danger is obvious:
the reference's deduction runs again inside every materialisation round
(`Template.hs:73`), so a slot pass 4 leaves empty for want of a type may
still fill. The verdict is therefore taken only when **every input was
decided** — each actual resolved and spellable, the return context present
and resolved wherever the call sits in one of the four positions the stamp
is applied at — and only on formal shapes whose `deduceType` clauses are
ported whole. The second half was learned the hard way: the first run
invented "Could not deduce" on `Foo(i)` with `index_t<10> i`, because
clause 3's match is by qualified name through an *alias* template this port
does not resolve, and on seven `expected:0` member calls with written
arguments, because `c.Bar<bool, false>()` parses the `<…>` as a sibling of
the `NAME_REF`, not as a segment's own list — every parameter looked
deduced. Both were caught by `conformance`, not by the unit tests, which is
what the scoreboard is for.

Nine probe texts went to the oracle before any code, and two of them changed
the design: a call with too few arguments *is* the LT verdict (`zipWithM_`
zips the shorter list; the oracle says so), and an initializer-list argument
is *not* (the oracle accepts `Fn_T_10({1, 2, 3})`, deducing through a clause
this port lacks). Three tests that pinned silence were corrected with the
oracle's message, and each new test was planted red: the verdict never
informed, the member index never answering, the pass-12 tail always
deducible — four, two and two tests down, respectively.

**What did not move, and why.** Four must-reject snippets in the deduction
file are the same member call inside a template body, `Go<N>`. The twin
route carries *types* home and nothing else; the passes walk the original
CST and skip every template body. A probe the oracle rejects at the member
name compiles clean here through every door. That is queue item 10.

## The twins link, and the survey that made it a re-mint rather than a copy

*2026-09-06. The cross-module twin program, §1e item 1, and item 3 with it.
Conformance 2137 → **2144/2144**, strict 469 → **461**, `errors` 215 → **222**
agree at the same 43 disagreements; tests 1275 → 1278.*

`elaborate.rs` had named two blockers: an imported name resolves through the
defining module's item tree, which no materialised declaration is in; and
the rename bijection was per module, so two twins could not spell one
mangled name the same way. A third stood behind them unnamed: an instance
decided in M of a template declared in H needs its *arguments* in H's arena,
and H's arena holds no node of M's.

**Survey before you schedule**, and this time the survey chose the design.
A probe over every per-file root counted the cross-module decided
instances: **16**, against 31 same-module — and every one of the 16 carries
only built-in scalar types or integer literals (`<Unsigned 8>`,
`<int:16, int:10>`). So the arguments are **re-minted** in H from a
structured shape the census now records beside its key
(`instances::ArgShape`), under the template's own node as donor, and nothing
ever crosses an arena. The deduced route brought the one shape the census
did not: an enum declared *beside* the template (`Fn_T(Enum::Zero)`), which
mints as a bare leaf wherever the twin can spell it — its own namespace or an
unaliased import's (`leaf_spellable`). A name from anywhere else is a counted
decline, because the twin could not resolve it either.

The other two blockers took one change each. `RenamePool` shares the alias
state across every module of one elaboration, so the declaration in H's twin
and the mention in M's wear one `__kg_mN`. And modules are elaborated in
`Program::files` order — imports first — with each twin's `ModuleTypes` laid
over its base map for the twins after it; `Imports::for_twin` looks a name
no item tree holds up there, by namespace, and *only* for a twin: on a real
program that route is over-resolution, so the flag is off.

Two things the first run got wrong. Only template-*declaring* modules were
elaborated, so M's mention was never resolved and its twin never built —
`targets` now includes every module with a deduced call or a census site.
And the twin's diagnostics then said `Invalid conversion from Enum to bool`
where the reference says `Conflicting template argument deduction` — because
`setTypeOfTemplateCall` here stamped only a callee with a *written* argument
list. The reference's lowering wraps every callee in a `TemplateInstance`
(`decomposeInstance`), so its `not $ typeResolved a` matches a bare `Fn_T(x)`
too. Three guards were tried on the bare segment: the path typed `Template`
(never — a template's name is no value, the base table reads it
`Undefined`), then `Function` (only in the twin, after the read-back), then
`Unresolved`. None was the right instrument; the segment is read by
deduction's third source alone, so "not already stamped" is the whole guard.
Four snippets moved from `Invalid conversion` to the reference's own conflict
message, expected type first, and pass 19 stays silent on them because the
conflict poisons the expression.

`showUnmangled` (`TypeCheck.hs:36`) is the last piece: the read-back carries
a struct type whose leaf is the mangled instance name, and a conversion
message printed `UINT<|@4|>` where the reference prints `UINT<4>`.
`show_unmangled` inverts `Mangle.hs` for the scalar and name shapes and
leaves anything else as written.

Falsified: minting planted out reds the cross-module test on `foreign`; the
stamp planted out reds the conflict test. The `--typed` oracle mode needs a
pass count to print types — the second time this session that cost an hour.

---

## The conversion error, and the pass-16 rewrite that had to be honoured first

*2026-09-06. `checkConversion'`'s error clause and the `checkReturn` site.
Conformance 2098 → **2137/2137**, strict 508 → **469**, `errors` agreement
181 → **215** with no new disagreement; tests 1272 → 1275.*

`conversion.rs` reported the narrowing *warning* and, by design, none of
`checkConversion'`'s five error outcomes — "an `Error 1` this door invents
breaks an `expected:0` assertion and every one of the 241 pass-through
ones". The errors gate said the price: `Invalid conversion from `bool` to
`uint32`` and its siblings were the largest class of must-reject snippets we
compiled cleanly. The clause that fires on two *fully resolved, non-error,
non-instance* types is the one whose ground the warning already stood on, so
it lands under the same guards: `| otherwise = conversionError s t ""`
(`TypeCheck.hs:178`), at the argument, the initialiser, and — new — the
`return` (`checkReturn`, `:84`), whose `allowNarrowingConversions` silences a
narrowing and nothing else.

The first run moved strict by 37 and broke **two** `expected:21` assertions:
`return Fn_void();` in a `uint32` function, which the reference's frontend
lets through and its backend rejects. Reading `checkReturn` predicted an
error; the oracle (`--errors`) showed none, and `--typed --passes 19` showed
*why* — the body held a bare call and no `ReturnF` at all. `returnVoid`
(`Frontend.hs:293-296`, inside `postDesugar`, pass 16) rewrites `return e`
with a void-typed `e` into `e; return;` three passes before `checkReturn`
runs. One guard reproduces it, and two corpus assertions with a backend code
are what pin the guard.

Two lessons kept. **A pass's input is the tree the earlier passes left**, and
a clause that reads the reference's *source* for pass 19 without the pass-16
rewrite in mind reads a tree the reference never type-checks — the same
hazard the journal named for `evaluateConstexpr` on 2026-08-14. And **the
oracle's `--typed` needs a pass count**: with every count at its default the
driver prints bare notes, and half an hour went to a regex before that was
noticed.

Falsified twice: the error arm planted out turns the three-site test red,
and the `returnVoid` guard planted out turns the backend-code test red. The
first attempt at that used `git stash` on the file holding both the code and
the tests, which "proved" nothing — the count fell because the tests left
with the arm.

## Completion, answered the way resolution answers

*2026-09-06, the second DX slice. Tests 1263 → 1272; every other gate at
baseline.*

`textDocument/completion` had been the one capability the server advertised
it did not have. It is answered now by `kg_db::Db::completions_at`, and the
rule that shaped it is the one that shaped goto-definition: **offer exactly
what resolution would accept.** After a `.` the candidates are the members of
the base expression's type — the field slice's route, `tLookupField`'s — and
elsewhere they are the names `findSymbol` would try, in its order
(`SymbolTable.hs:242-270`): the enclosing scopes innermost first, with a
sibling block's locals absent because `binder` says so; this file's top
level; then what each import exposes, and nothing from an aliased import,
which hides its names from bare use (`SymbolTable.hs:276-278`). A struct
field is not offered bare, because it is not a symbol. No keywords and no
snippets — an editor's own snippet list is the honest home for those, and
`bitsizeof` offered as a symbol would misdescribe it.

The parser's recovery is what makes the member context possible on half-typed
text: `s.` before a newline parses to a `FIELD_EXPR` holding the base and the
`.` and no selector, so the base is there to ask about.

Driven over stdio before it was called done (`CLAUDE.md`, "The recurring
failure"): a raw client sent `initialize`, `didOpen` and two completion
requests to `kg lsp`, and got `x: uint32, y: bool` after `s.` and
`s, S, main` at a bare position. The capability test and the whole-session
e2e that pinned "completion is *not* advertised" flipped to pin the trigger
character.
