real `textDocument/inlayHint` handler over stdio, because the last time this
number was published it was wrong in three places before it was measured once. If
it is near zero, the unlock is a rooting change and the roadmap should say so
instead of attributing 846 hints to pass 8.

**What a keystroke actually costs.** The existing `bench --filter keystroke`
appends a trailing space to whatever file the sweep lands on, which is outside
every template body by construction — it measures the best case. Two new stages:
an edit inside a template in a base-library module every file imports, and then
`Db::diagnostics` for a *different, unedited, open* file, so the `ModuleTypes`
fan-out is what is on the clock. Interleaved A/B, four non-overlapping pairs,
reported as a delta against 107.7 ms, never as an absolute threshold — "p99 under
50 ms" would license a 50% regression.

**Whether inference can stay on the CST.** Port `inferType` over one instance
body and diff the resulting `TypeTable` against the CST-built one for a
non-template file. If they agree, the trait-over-two-trees route is live; if they
do not, inference moves and the estimate doubles. That experiment is cheap and it
should be run before the second slice, not after.

## The `auto` inlay hints: right cause, insufficient fix

The pass 8 entry above lists, as its first unknown, whether the library's
unannotated `auto` bindings are actually unblocked by pass 8 or whether the
roadmap has been crediting the wrong item. It is the cheapest of the experiments
and it needs no IR, so it went first.

All 124 library files driven through the real `textDocument/inlayHint` handler
over stdio, one `didOpen` each — the way this journal already insists, because
the last number published about this was wrong before it was measured once.

**962 `auto` bindings that a hint could annotate. 203 hinted. 759 not.** The
roadmap's "four fifths" was right to two significant figures, which is more than
it had any right to be.

That first ran as 188/774, and the difference is a lesson rather than a rounding
error. The measurement drove the real server against the reference library,
which contains no `kanagawa.toml` — and the CLI discovered manifests from the
working directory, so nothing in the run had a configured import path and none
of the library's imports resolved. The number was of a program that does not
compile. Re-run against a configured copy it is 203/759, the qualified-path
bucket falls 46 → 31, and every conclusion below is unchanged. The bug that
caused it is fixed (`kg-cli`, discovery starts beside the file), and the shape of
it is worth keeping: **an instrument pointed at a misconfigured program reports
confidently and is wrong by a little** — which is far harder to notice than being
wrong by a lot.

Where they are is the useful part. Ten files hold 536 of the 759, and they are
`numeric/float32.k` (211 of its 267), `numeric/fixed.k` (136 of 156),
`numeric/float/internal.k` (35 of 35), `processor/risc_v/internal/core.k` (34 of
34) — the template-heavy ones, several of them total blackouts. And the
initializers are not exotic. A random sample of the largest bucket is
`= 3;`, `= 36;`, `= 0xa2f9836e4e;`, `= x.value;`, `= temp.first;`,
`= EXP2_PRIMARY_TABLE_LG_SIZE + EXP2_LEAST_TABLE_LG_SIZE;`. Nothing there needs a
template argument. They are unhinted because **inference never enters a template
body at all**:

```haskell
go (NotedExp n (TemplateF a b)) = Note n (TemplateF (inferExpTree' alg <$> a) b)
```

`Inference.hs:63` recurses into `a`, the parameters, and leaves `b`, the
declaration, untouched. `facts::reached_only_after_elaboration` reproduces it
exactly and cites it. The line above postpones `LambdaF` the same way. So a
`const auto x = 3;` inside a template body has no type in the reference either,
and it acquires one only on an instance — which is pass 8. **The roadmap's
attribution of cause is correct.**

What the roadmap has wrong is that pass 8 is *sufficient*. Instantiation gives
types to instance bodies; a hint on the template body the user is actually
looking at comes from the reverse index over `written == Own` nodes, and that
index is only as populated as the instance set. Every LSP handler roots at
`&[snap.file]` (`hover.rs:69`, `inlay_hints.rs:98`, `definition.rs:60`) and
`Program::files` is the import closure *downward*, while a template's instances
are decided by the files that **import** it. Open `numeric/float32.k` on its own
after pass 8 lands and the instance set is still empty, and all 211 of its
unhinted bindings stay unhinted.

So the entry above was right to flag it, and the number now says how much rides
on it: **pass 8 and a rooting change together are worth ~536 hints; pass 8 alone
is worth approximately none of them.** The roadmap should stop listing the hints
under pass 8 as though the pass delivers them.

One smaller bucket looked like a separate cause and **does not exist**, which is
the second thing this measurement got wrong. It was defined as "the initializer
contains `::`" and read as the import-qualifier gap listed in `status.md`. It is
not. `::` in this language is mostly **enum member access**: the 46 matches are
`Denorm::On`, `Extension::None` and `Optimize::Area` far more often than
`device::version`. Hovering every one gives 15 typed — all in
`compiler/config.k`, all fixed by the manifest bug above — and 31 untyped, of
which **31 of 31 sit in a file containing a template**. The three shapes, spot
checked: `data/vector.k:412` is inside a template body; `numeric/float32.k:128`
is `getSpecialCases<Denorm::On>(…)`, a call whose return type needs the instance;
`processor/risc_v.k:313` is a template parameter's default. All three are pass 8.
Aliased qualified paths infer fine on their own — `import dep as d; const auto v
= d::x;` hovers as `const uint3 v`.

So the bucket dissolves into the pass 8 story and there is no separate cause to
schedule. Both taxonomies this measurement used — "is the line inside a template
body", by brace-tracking, and "does the initializer contain `::`" — were
**syntactic proxies for semantic questions, and both were wrong the same way**. A
classifier that greps a character finds that character. The counts it produces
are real and the categories are fiction, and that is the more dangerous half,
because the counts make the categories look measured.

The measurement is `hints.py` in the job scratch, not in the repo: it is an
experiment, not a gate. If it becomes a number anyone quotes twice, it should
become `xtask hints` instead, for the same reason the keystroke benchmark had to
become one — a number nobody can re-run is a claim, not a measurement.

## Two gates that did not pin what they were specified to pin

Slice 1 of pass 8 landed — `kg-hir`, `Src`, and the three gates the design entry
above specified. Two of the three were weaker than the entry claimed, and both
failures are of the same species: **a gate whose specification sounds like a
proof and is not one.**

### The round trip cancels the bug it was written to catch

The entry specifies `lower(parse(pretty(lower(parse(f)))))` structurally equal to
`lower(parse(f))`, and says this "catches a lowering that drops a field, which is
the failure mode a variant-per-construct IR actually has."

It does not, whenever the bug is deterministic. A deterministic lowering error
sits on *both* sides of that equation and cancels.

The demonstration is exact. Reverse the ternary arms — `Mux c (Seq [then, else])`
instead of `Mux c (Seq [else, then])`, inverting the meaning of every `a ? b : c`
in the corpus, and precisely the field `Parser.hs:968` exists to warn about. The
round trip reads **403/403**. Both sides print `mux(c, x, y)`, both relower it
the same wrong way, and the gate sees two identical trees. The only thing that
catches it is a unit test that pins `Seq [else, then]` against the citation.

What the round trip *does* pin is printer↔lowering agreement and asymmetry
between two surface spellings of one construct — reversing the `mux` arms (a
different construct, reached by two different syntaxes) did go red on 87 files.
That is worth having. It is not what it says on the tin.

The consequence is a reordering of priorities. The entry lists a `--dump-source`
differential against the reference's own instantiated output as a nice-to-have
blocked on a Haskell toolchain nobody has built here. It is not a nice-to-have.
**It is the only proposed instrument that can catch a symmetric lowering error**,
because it is the only one whose two sides do not share this port's lowering. A
day of toolchain work buys the gate that the round trip was assumed to be.

### The provenance gate was vacuous against the entry's own planted bug

The entry specifies: every `Src::head` resolves to a live CST node, and every
`written == Own` node has a CST node at exactly that range whose kind matches. It
then prescribes, as the red test, planting "one `head` at a donor without setting
`Donated`".

That test stays green. A donor's head *is* a live CST node, and a synthesized
node wears its donor's kind, so both clauses hold for exactly the bug they were
written to detect. The specification and its own falsification test disagree, and
nobody noticed because both were written in prose.

The invariant that bites is a third clause the entry does not have: **no two
structurally different `Own` nodes may claim the same `(range, kind)` TypeKey.**
That is what `Own` actually means — the claim that `(head, kind)` is a legal type
key — and divergence #21 is the record of what a key collision costs. With it,
the planted bug fails 1/479. It also caught a real bug in the new lowering on its
first run: `Unsupported` holes were claiming their host node's key, which three
corpus files noticed.

The one legitimate duplicate is the compound-assignment double-read: `x += e`
lowers to `Assign x (Binary Add x' e)`, and the lvalue and rvalue readings of `x`
share a range. They are compared modulo the `ArrayAccessLValue → ArrayAccess`
erasure the reference itself performs (`Parser.hs:637`).

### The shape both share

Both gates were specified by someone reasoning carefully about code they could
not run — which the entry says about itself, and which is the honest condition of
any design written before its implementation. The lesson is not "designs are
unreliable". It is narrower and more useful: **a gate's specification is a
hypothesis, and the falsification test is the experiment.** Writing "break X and
watch it go red" into the design is worth little; *running* it is the whole
value, and in both cases here the running is what found the gap. This project
already had the rule — CLAUDE.md's "prove a new test is load-bearing" — and this
is the first time it has been applied to a gate specified in advance rather than
to a test written alongside its code. It caught two of three.


## The constraint that was half true

Every design note in this file that reached for a reference binary and stopped
wrote some version of the same sentence: there is no GHC here, so we grade
against the corpus assertions and against our own reading of the Haskell. The
pass 8 entry says it while proposing `--dump-source` as the strongest gate
available and shelving it. The entry before this one promotes that oracle from
nice-to-have to necessary and still assumes it is blocked on "a day of toolchain
work".

It was blocked on running `ghcup list`. The toolchain was already installed and
not on `PATH`; `command -v ghc` said absent and nobody looked further.

The other half is the part worth keeping, because it is a real distinction that
the word "the compiler" hides. `compiler/kanagawa.cabal` declares an
**executable** that links `kanagawa-backend` — a C++ shared library, with FFI
modules and a CMake build — and a **library** that is the entire frontend, all 26
`Language.Kanagawa.*` modules, depending on nothing but Hackage. This port
reimplements the library. Building the executable is a C++ project; building the
library is `cabal build`. "There is no GHC here" was true of a thing we do not
need and false of the thing we do, and the two were never separated because the
first attempt hit the C++ dependency and generalised from it.

So `oracle/` exists: `build.sh` copies the sources out of the read-only tree at
build time — tracking the reference rather than vendoring a snapshot nobody
remembers taking — and builds a driver against the library alone. `--tree` prints
the tree as the reference holds it, notes elided, which is what `kg dump ir`
should be graded against. Plain mode prints `prettySource`, the same function
`--dump-source` uses.

It paid immediately. Every tree-shaping rule `kg_hir::lower` claims in its module
doc is now checked against the reference instead of against our reading of it:
`true ? a : b` really does become `MuxF cond (SeqF [else, then])` with the arms
reversed, `x += 2` really does re-read its lvalue as an rvalue, `x++` really does
add a literal `1`. It also shows a bare `SeqF []` leading every program — the
redundant-import warning seed (`Parser.hs:234-241`) that `kg-hir` deliberately
omits, which we knew from reading and can now see.

The lesson is not about Haskell. Twice this week a written constraint turned out
to be a previous session's inference rather than a fact — "the corpus pins all
six fold sites" and now "there is no GHC here" — and both had survived because
they were plausible, specific, and never re-tested. A constraint that shapes the
plan deserves the same treatment as a claim that shapes the code: check it
before you build around it. This one had been shaping the plan since phase 0.

## `decidedInstances` lands wired to nothing, and the corpus cannot reach round two

Slice 2 of pass 8: `Db::body_ir`, `Db::module_instances`, `Db::instances`
(`kg-db/src/instances.rs`, `db.rs`), `kg dump instances`, and three new gates in
`xtask ir`. Still called by no pass; the predicted assertion delta was zero and
the measured delta is zero — 2049/2049, 557 strict, 479/479 + 355/355, 1054
tests, clippy 0.

### Rule 1: restated, not resolved — and why

`all Map.null x` is true in the reference only because `resolve` replaced inner
decided instances with mangled names on the previous round (`Template.hs:58,
159-163`). The literal port would need the mangler *and* a materialized
declaration for the mangled name to denote — `templateArgResolved` passes on the
rewritten argument because `typeOf` answers `TType` about the instance copy, and
there is no copy until `makeInstance` lands. So the guard is restated: an
argument that **is** a nested instance resolves iff that instance is already in
the decided set, no undecided instance may remain anywhere in the argument
subtrees, and a round admits only instances whose nested instances were decided
in an **earlier** round. That last clause is not a convenience — it is the
reference's own round structure (a child decided this round has not been
resolved away yet, so its parent waits), it makes the per-instance `depth` equal
the round number, and it is what a `templateIterations` budget will meter when
the fixpoint gets one.

`indirectInstances` (rule 2's second half) is **not computed**: it is
`resolveTemplateParam`, a five-stage pipeline that re-infers a rewritten subtree
(`TypeCheck.hs:364-372`), and inference over the IR does not exist. Declining it
loses instances — the silent direction. The speculative-`templateTypeCheck`
discard sink it will need is specified in `instances.rs`'s module comment, and
the zero-diagnostics gate below is armed for the day it arrives.

### The numbers, and what they say about the design entry

Over the corpus, rooted per file the way `bench`'s keystroke stage roots:
**233 root sets decide instances, 246 gate on errors; 26 templates, 49 distinct
instances, max nesting depth 1, max fixpoint rounds 1.** The differential finds
232 resolved instances over the 403 clean parses.

Two of those numbers correct impressions the design entry left:

* **The 424 nested argument lists are not decidable today, and could never
  have been.** They sit inside template bodies (rule 4 excludes them until
  instantiation walks the copies) or carry template parameters and named
  constants (silence 2). Depth 1, everywhere. Rule 1's restatement is still
  required — the unit fixpoint proves depth 2 works, and `kg dump instances`
  on a two-file fixture shows it — but the corpus exercises the fixpoint's
  second round **zero** times until instance bodies are themselves re-walked.
  The 424 figure describes work for *later* rounds over materialized copies,
  not the written program.
* **246 of 479 gated is mostly harness rooting, not program errors.** The
  uniform `bench` settings (mini-base, `library` + `test/syntax` import dirs)
  leave many `test/` programs with unresolved imports, and 76 files are
  snippet accumulators that fail the parse gate by design. The gate is doing
  exactly what `Template.hs:55,84` does; the rooting is what decides how often
  it fires.

The memo-bound arithmetic the design entry wanted: at 49 distinct instances and
depth 1, the `Bounded` cap of 8 root sets (`MAX_INSTANCE_ROOT_SETS`) is
generous, and the binding constraint is the `Arc<ModuleIr>` pins per entry, not
the instance count. Revisit both when `indirectInstances` or materialization
moves the numbers.

### Four plants, one test that sailed, two gates the corpus cannot make bite

Every new gate was falsified, per the rule the last entry added:

1. **Differential** (CST vs IR readings of `templateResolved`, both file-local,
   inference region): planting silence 2's violation on the IR side only —
   `Exp::Path(_) => true` in `constexpr_resolved` — went red **401/403**,
   naming `library/numeric/float32.k` (8 instances) and
   `test/logic/test_cases_31.k`. Restored.
2. **Zero diagnostics**: planting the exact trap-4 leak — an error published
   for every declined candidate — went red with **298 diagnostics** over the
   corpus. The unit test `deciding_instances_emits_no_diagnostics` **stayed
   green under the same plant**, because its fixture decided everything and had
   nothing to leak about. It now contains a declined instance and goes red.
   That is the second time this project has caught a test that pins nothing by
   running the falsification rather than reading it.
3. **Trap 2's arm** (`StaticForF → forLimit`): deleting it turned
   `a_static_for_body_is_not_decided_but_its_limit_is` red. The corpus
   statistics did **not** move — no decidable instance sits in a `static for`
   body anywhere in the corpus under this rooting — so the unit test is the
   only thing pinning the arm, and the differential is deliberately blind to it
   (it runs the inference region *because* `Cx::instance` does).
4. **The fixpoint**: capping at one round turned the nested-instance unit test
   red and dropped the fixture dump from depth 2 to depth 1. Corpus statistics
   unmoved, same finding as above.
5. **`body_ir`'s identity memo**: dropping the `Arc::ptr_eq` check turned
   `body_ir_is_reused_while_the_parse_is` red at "a real edit must re-lower".

One clause could not be made to bite and is reported as such: the
check-before/after comparison in the instances gate (`Db::check` byte-identical
around `Db::instances`). Nothing reachable from the instances path today can
mutate shared state — the computation only reads memos — so no realistic plant
exists. It is a tripwire for the slice that adds speculative sub-pass runs, kept
because it costs one already-memoized check per file.

### Bookkeeping that will matter later

The instance key is the argument subtrees' structural rendering with
`validateArg`'s literal re-stamp applied (`TypeCheck.hs:280-285`) — truncated to
the parameter's width, stamp dropped under `auto` — so `Foo<300>` and `Foo<44>`
under `uint8 N` are one instance with two sites, first-in-program-order winning
the note (`Map.unionsWith Map.union`, left-biased, `Template.hs:88`). Pinned by
`an_oversized_literal_shares_the_key_of_its_truncation`. Mangling is untouched
and `deduplicateInstances` unwritten; both belong to the slice that materializes
copies, and the key deliberately does not know they exist.

One asymmetry is documented rather than fixed: the CST reading parses a
`uint<N>` width from the literal's decimal text, the IR reading takes the
lowered `ConstInt` (which no longer remembers its radix). A hex width in a
parameter's declared type would split the readings; the corpus has none, and
the differential is the instrument that will say so if one appears.

## Four of the five rewrites never ask a type, and the fifth is the one that can wait

Five specifications for pass 8's rewriting sub-passes were written independently, one per pass, each against `Function.hs`/`Closure.hs` and against the oracle. This entry turns them into one implementation sequence, records where they contradict each other, and resizes the item.

The result that reorders everything: the design entry above names moving `kg_ty::infer` onto the IR as "the single most likely thing to blow the estimate". That is still true, and it is a dependency of **exactly one of the five** — the one that can land last. `desugarLambdas`, `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` and `moveFunctions` read no type and take no whole-program symbol map, which is checked three ways: their signatures (`Function.hs:189,288`), their position in the inner list (`Template.hs:76-78` passes all three bare, where `:71,73,79` wrap theirs in `withSymbols`/`withSymbols'`, and `moveFunctions` is 4th while the first `inferType` is 5th), and the oracle, which produces their entire output at `--template-passes 4 --template-iterations 0`, below both `inferType` calls. `addLambdaWrappers` does read types, in two arms that fire **zero** times across the corpus. Only `closureCalls` is dead without inference over the IR — and nothing in pass 8 consumes what it emits.

So four syntactic rewrites can land before the hard part starts, on top of `Db::body_ir` and one 40-line symbol walk. That is roughly 4,000 lines and four slices, every one of them predicting a zero assertion delta.

### The instrument, and what it settled that reading could not

`instantiateTemplates` honours `templatePasses` only when `templateIterations == 0`, and then runs `drop (length passes - templatePasses) passes` (`Template.hs:62-64`) — the *last* entries, which under `foldr ($)` (`:60`) execute *first*. So `--template-passes N --template-iterations 0` runs exactly the first N inner sub-passes in execution order, and the N→N+1 diff is one sub-pass in isolation. Four of the five surveyors found this independently. It is the difference between describing a pass and grading it.

What it overturned, in five commands:

**Roadmap §1b row 2 is wrong.** `desugarLambdas` does not "lift each lambda body to a sibling declaration". It prepends a capture alias and a `LambdaFunction` into the *enclosing block's own* `Seq`, where they stay, named `?lambda0` — `tp=2` shows both still inside `main`. The hoist to module scope and the `main@?lambda0` rename are `moveFunctions` at `tp=4`. `oracle/README.md`'s own transcript attributes the wrong pass. Correct both.

**`abbreviatedFunctionTemplate`'s second clause is a revert, not a skip.** `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate _ TemplateF{} = Nothing` (`Function.hs:310`) under `desugarShallow' f = para f'` with `f' e' (Note n e) = maybe e' (NotedExp n) (f n e)` (`Desugar.hs:81-84`) restores `para`'s *first* argument — the original, unrewritten subtree (`Recursion.hs:73-74`). `template <typename T> inline void G(T a, auto b)` and an abbreviated member of a class template both come out of pass 8 byte-identical to their pass-7 input, even though the inner `FunctionF` did rewrite and the `ClassF` did propagate it. That is the single largest behavioural constraint on that port and nothing in the roadmap hints at it.

**`moveFunctions` has two bugs that are the answer key.** There is no `UnrolledForF` arm, so a `static for` that `inferType` already unrolled keeps its hoisted declaration inside the loop body, half-renamed. And mangled names collide silently: two sibling blocks in one function are both `$quasi0`, both their `g`s mangle to `f@$quasi0@g`, `deduplicateInstances`' `nubBy` (`Template.hs:144-156`) drops the second, and the second call site runs the first body. No diagnostic. Both look like defects a reviewer would wave through a fix for.

**`closureCalls` never fires at iteration 0.** Measured minimum rounds: 1 for a module-scope lambda, 2 for a capturing lambda called directly, 3 for the higher-order form. The guard `tIsClosure $ typeOf b` needs a `TInstance` stamped by `setTypeOfInstance` (`Type.hs:426-431`), which only `makeInstance` produces. And it is not neutral — it *enables* a diagnostic: a closure call is not arity-checked at all until it becomes a function call, because `tIsFunction` is false for a `TClosure` (`Type.hs:659-660`), so `Do(1)` on a zero-parameter closure reports "expected 1" only after the rewrite, counting the capture parameter.

**Two retractions, both from running rather than reading.** The const-member inlining at `Function.hs:55` was first attributed to `moveFunctions`; bisecting `--template-passes` showed the *scalar* case first appearing at 5, which makes it `inferType`'s. And a corpus census that counted the `--passes 7`→`8` delta in `cast<` occurrences reported 174 firings in `library/`; instantiation duplicates template bodies, so it was counting user casts multiplied. The corrected fingerprint — `make_captureN::$::Capture`, a type not spellable in user source — gives **zero** for all 124 `library/` files.

Two things the oracle cannot do as it stands, and both should be fixed in the first slice. `--tree` elides notes by design, so provenance is unfalsifiable; three surveyors each built a note-printing driver outside the tree to get it. And `driver/Main.hs:99` is `evalStateT`, keeping only `parseProgram`'s return value — the command-line roots — where the reference's own executable is `execStateT` and runs the frontend over every file the parse cache accumulated (`app/Main.hs:69-73`). Imported modules never reach `frontend`, so `undefinedSymbols` reports every library symbol missing and `getSymbols' NoTemplate` cannot see a cross-module callee. **Any whole-program symbol conclusion drawn from the shipped oracle is suspect**, including the `Symbol name not in scope: make_capture0` that two surveyors initially took for a real closure-library gap. Two flags, `--notes`, and one `evalStateT` is about fifteen lines.

### The order, and the one claimed dependency that does not survive

Forced edges, each confirmed by at least two of the specs or by a transcript:

| edge | why |
|---|---|
| substrate → all five | unanimous |
| `captureThis` on the IR → `desugarLambdas` | `Exp::This` is never built by `lower.rs` (`exp.rs:125`), so a class-member lambda's captures are short by one and every `make_captureN` gets the wrong arity |
| `addLambdaWrappers` → `desugarLambdas` | its wrappers *are* lambdas; alone it changes nothing observable |
| `desugarLambdas` → `moveFunctions` | `lambdaFunctions` (`Function.hs:126-128`) selects `funcKind == LambdaFunction`, which only `desugarLambdas` creates |
| `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` → `moveFunctions` | `move t@Function{} _ \| isAbbreviatedTemplate t = t` (`:88-89`) exists to defer the leftover copy abbreviated emits |
| `desugarLambdas` → `closureCalls` | with `higherOrderFunctions`' rewrite, the only producers of a closure-typed value |
| `makeInstance` + IR inference + a constructible `Ty::Closure` → `closureCalls` | the guard is unsatisfiable before an instance exists |

`moveFunctions`' spec claims to be "the one of the five that can go first". It is not: its own dependency section then lists `desugarLambdas` and `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` as prerequisites once the chain is assembled, and it is the largest of the five, rewriting 137 of 300 parseable corpus files. The claim is true only of a `moveFunctions` running alone over written source, which is not a chain. `addLambdaWrappers` and `desugarLambdas` are correctly described as one deliverable — for *observability*. They are still two landings.

The sequence: **substrate + `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` → `captureThis` + `desugarLambdas` → `addLambdaWrappers` → `moveFunctions` → materialisation → IR inference → `closureCalls` and the second `inferType`.** Five zero-delta slices before the first assertion moves.

`abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` goes first because it is the smallest genuine rewrite (24 lines of Haskell), needs no symbol map, no types, no cross-arena copy and no `captureThis`; because it forces the substrate's hardest semantics — the revert — while the blast radius is 18 files and 88 synthetic parameters; and because its red test is available and sharp: run the rewrite on the class-template fixture and assert the output is **`ExpId`-identical** to the input, which is only expressible if `None` returns the original id.

### The first shippable slice

`Exp::map_children` (the functor half of `children`, 92 arms, written beside it so the two are diffed in review); `kg_hir::rewrite` with `cata`/`desugar`, the `Src`-carrying `desugar'`, `para`, `desugar_shallow`, `desugar_shallow_prime` and `remove_nested_seq`; `kg_hir::rewrite::abbreviated_function_template`; `kg dump ir --rewrite`; the oracle driver's two flags plus `--notes` plus the `execStateT` fix; and the gate consolidation below. Nothing wired into `passes::run`, nothing wired into `Db::instances`.

That last exclusion is deliberate and easy to get wrong. Feeding the rewritten IR to `Db::instances` the day the first rewrite lands would move the instance statistics and the differential gate simultaneously with the rewrite, and there would be no way to attribute a change to either. The chain stays off `Db::instances` until all five exist.

Predicted: `conformance` 2049/2049, `--strict` **557 with a byte-identical name set**, `corpus` 479/479 and 355/355, `repoint` 13/72, `bench` inside the A/B noise band, `kg dump instances` unchanged at 26 templates and 49 instances. **The assertion delta is exactly zero**, stated first so it is a prediction. Anything moving means the rewrite reached a diagnostic path, which it cannot, because nothing calls it.

Three falsifications to *run*, not to write down: delete the `Template{} => None` arm and watch the id-identity test go red on the two template fixtures; swap the two donors at `Function.hs:296` (the `auto` FuncParam) and `:307` (the `Auto` node) and watch the `--notes` differential go red — if it stays green the provenance gate is still vacuous and the entry above's lesson has repeated; re-allocate an unchanged subtree and watch the "a rewrite allocates no `Own` node that `lower` did not" clause go red.

### Where the five specifications disagree, which is where the risk is

**The substrate, four ways.** `desugarLambdas`, `moveFunctions` and `addLambdaWrappers` all specify a rebuild into a *fresh* arena. `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` specifies appending into the *same* arena with unchanged subtrees keeping their ids, and argues — correctly — that a literal cata inflates the arena by a whole `funcParams` subtree per site, five rewrites over 480 files. `closureCalls` specifies in-place mutation via `node_mut`. Whoever lands first decides for the other four, and two of the positions are already contradicted by code in the tree: `arena.rs:112-116` records the standing rule that "sharing in an arena makes a DAG that every tree-shaped walk here would visit twice", which `moveFunctions` cites and `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` proposes to violate by sharing one `Typename` node between a `TemplateParam` and its `TypeParam` (faithful to `Function.hs:130-132`, and a DAG).

There is also a consequence nobody noticed. `check_provenance` iterates `ir.arena.iter()` (`xtask/src/ir.rs:331`), not the tree reachable from `ModuleIr.root`. Under an append substrate the superseded nodes are still in the arena, so every replacement produces two `Own` claimants of one `(range, kind)` with different shapes and clause three fails on the first rewrite. Either the gate walks from the root or the substrate rebuilds. The resolution that satisfies every constraint: **one arena for the whole pass-8 run, not one per sub-pass; `Db::body_ir`'s `Arc<ModuleIr>` is copied once at the top; rewrites append and unchanged subtrees keep their ids; anything that would appear in two positions goes through `deep_copy`; and the gate walks from the root.** That keeps `None`-returns-the-original free, kills the nine whole-file copies per round that `moveFunctions` flags as its cost risk, and preserves the DAG rule.

**`written`, four positions on a field the reference does not have.** `desugarLambdas` says the `Cast` replacing a lambda is `Own` (`desugarShallow` re-wears the lambda's note). `moveFunctions` says the rebuilt `If` is `Own` but the mangled `Identifier` must be `Donated` even though the reference reuses the note. `closureCalls` says all seven of its synthesised rows are `Donated`, explicitly diverging from `copyNote`. `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` says everything is `Donated` and that `Own` would collide. All four are locally right, which means the field is being re-derived per pass. It has one job — the claim that `(head, kind)` is a legal `TypeKey` — so the rule is mechanical and belongs in `src.rs` once: **`Own` iff the node is the sole claimant of that `(range, kind)` in the tree it lives in.** A *replacement* may keep `Own`, because the donor is gone; a *duplication*, or a splice from a declaration that still exists elsewhere, must be `Donated`. That rule decides all four cases identically to the four specs and stops the next surveyor deriving a fifth.

**`None`: revert or stop.** `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` and `moveFunctions` say the deferral arms discard the children's rewrites; `desugarLambdas` says `desugar_shallow` "stops descending". These are the same answer — in Haskell the rewritten children are never forced, in Rust returning the original subtree is indistinguishable from not recursing — and the sane port is the top-down guard, which is also cheaper. But "stop descending" invites a third reading neither spec endorses: skip *this node* and keep the rewritten children. That reading hoists out of templates, `static if`s and local classes, and it is `moveFunctions`' risk 3. Write the combinator once, with both citations, and never as an algebra option.

**`deduplicateInstances` is not materialisation's.** Slice 2's entry booked mangling and `deduplicateInstances` with "the slice that materializes copies". `Template.hs:57` runs `parallel (desugar deduplicateInstances) program'` on the **exit path of every invocation**, including `templateIterations == 0`, and `userDefinedTypes FunctionF{} FunctionF{} = True` (`:154`) is what silently absorbs the `moveFunctions` name collision. So `moveFunctions` either lands with the dedup step or lands able to emit two identically named declarations — an invented redefinition error on a program the reference accepts. No corpus file has the shape, so the corpus does not force it; the unit test built from the collision fixture does, and any duplicate-definition check must be kept off the rewritten IR. **"No corpus file has the shape" is false, measured 2026-08-13**: at `--template-passes 4` the reference emits **35 duplicated `(landing scope, mangled name)` pairs across 11 files**, every one a `Template`-wrapped/bare pair, because `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` emits `SeqF [Template f', f]` (`Function.hs:290-292`) and `functionsAndClasses` selects **both** (`:121-122`), so both move and both mangle to the same name. **14 of the 35, in 5 files, are not `$wrapper$`** and this port will produce them — `test/library/data/buffer/burst_write.k`, `test/library/data/function.k`, `test/library/data/optional.k`, `test/library/processor/risc-v.k`, `test/logic/lambda_test_cases.k`. The conclusion stands and is now corpus-forced rather than fixture-forced; the consequence for the gate is that a move ledger must be a **multiset**, not a set.

**`captureThis` contradicts `status.md`.** The pass table says row 3 has "nothing left to port … `captureThis` is read only by `desugarLambdas`, inside pass 8, and is codegen shape. No module exists and none should." True today, false the day `desugarLambdas` lands: `Exp::This` is never constructed (`lower.rs` has no site; `exp.rs:125` says so in a doc comment), so every `this`-capturing lambda would get `make_capture{N-1}`, no `auto $this = …x0;` binding and a wrong capture type — and no existing gate can see it, because the round trip cancels a deterministic lowering bug and no assertion counts capture arity. The oracle differential is the only instrument, which is the strongest argument for landing it as a gate rather than using it once.

**One disagreement that is already in shipped code.** `getSymbols' NoTemplate`'s `symbol e@Template{} = tail` (`Symbols.hs:59-60`) drops exactly one entry — for a `Class`, which inserts twice (`:66`), that leaves `Aa::$this` behind. The port's `in_config` skips the whole item and its test asserts the two-entry version. `addLambdaWrappers` is `NoTemplate`'s only consumer and never looks up a `$this` key, so nothing observes it; it is a reading, not a transcript, and it is recorded here so it is not rediscovered as a bug.

**Three proposed gate extensions, which are one gate.** Key `kinds_at` and `own_claims` on `FileId` as well as offsets (`addLambdaWrappers` — 40 of 904 wrappers splice a parameter list out of another module's IR, and today the gate would either fail with a misleading "no CST node at X..Y" or pass by coincidence); resolve `head` against `head.file` rather than the root file (`closureCalls`, for instance bodies); and forbid an `Own` node the lowering did not create (`moveFunctions`, whose spliced member-name `Identifier` is shape-*equal* to the declaration it was copied from and therefore sails through clause three). All four — with the walk-from-root fix — land together, before the first rewrite, or the gate quietly stops being evidence.

### "Fail toward silence" stops being uniformly safe here

Three of the five emit no diagnostic on any path, so they cannot diagnose earlier than the reference directly. `addLambdaWrappers` inverts the house rule and says so with a transcript: `higherOrderFunctions` has already turned `hof2((uint8)->uint8 cb)`'s parameter into a `Closure<…>` before pass 8 runs, and the reference accepts `hof2(g)` *because* the wrapper turns `g` into a lambda that becomes that closure. A port that lands a closure-conversion check without the wrapper reports `Invalid conversion from … to Closure<…>` on a correct program. Nothing is at risk today — `passes/higher_order.rs` is 61 lines and diagnostic-only — but the ordering constraint is precise and should be written down before it becomes live: **no closure-conversion diagnostic before `addLambdaWrappers` + `desugarLambdas`.**

`closureCalls` is the mirror. Skipping it is safe silence: an un-rewritten closure call is not arity-checked and the call's type is the same either way (`tReturn (TClosure _ x _ _) = tReturn x`, `Type.hs:576`). Doing it half-right invents errors four ways, and the two worth naming are that `fromJust $ expFromType …` (`Closure.hs:25`) is a *crash* in the reference, not a diagnostic — decline the rewrite on `None`, never report — and that `tIsClosure` is satisfiable strictly before `tClosureFunction`/`tClosureCapture` are total, so the guard must be on the concrete `Ty::Closure`, not on `is_closure`. The reference is saved from that only by ordering, with `inferType` immediately before at inner position 5.

### What must exist first: confirmed, refuted, resized

The design entry's four prerequisites, graded against five independent readings.

**An IR-resident symbol map: half confirmed, and much smaller than "about the size of the one specified here".** Two different things wear that name. `moveFunctions` needs `getSymbols'' AllSymbols` over **one body** (`Function.hs:33`) — a local walk of about forty lines, with four load-bearing details (the key is the absolute path; `Class` inserts twice; `Struct`/`Union` do not descend; `fromList . reverse` makes the first declaration win a duplicate key, which is what makes the collision reproducible). Reusing `Db::global_symbols` there would be *wrong*, not merely heavy: `qualifyName` finds a nested function's parameter and does not find the enclosing function's own, and the `local-functions.k` diagnostic turns on exactly that asymmetry. `addLambdaWrappers` is the only pass needing a whole-program answer, `SymbolsConfig::NoTemplate` already exists and is tested (`lower.rs:404-407,1741-1757`), and what is genuinely missing is one index — `DefId -> (Arc<ModuleIr>, ExpId)` — modelled on `Db::ir_templates` (`db.rs:750`), plus `ExpArena::graft`, a cross-arena `deep_copy`. Roadmap §1b's note that `NoTemplate` "is a real complication for a port with one symbol query" should be struck; the port has three.

**Mangling: refuted, by three specs independently.** `moveFunctions`' `parent@child` is string concatenation (`Function.hs:40`); `desugarLambdas`' `@data@closure` is `moduleNamespace` (`Parser/Syntax.hs:273-274`); `closureCalls` spells whatever the type already carries. `Mangle.hs` is materialisation's, and the `<|$uint@32|>` in a hoisted name comes from `instantiate` having renamed the parent.

**`makeInstance`: only `closureCalls` is dead without it.** The other four are correct-but-partial: `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` fires again on the instantiated copy a round later, `moveFunctions` hoists instance bodies from round 1, and `addLambdaWrappers` gets **8%** of its sites in round 1 (5 of 60 on `callback_test_cases.k`, 28 of 88 on `lambda_test_cases.k`). A one-shot port is not wrong, it is a floor — which is the right shape for wired-to-nothing slices and a wrong shape for a claim about coverage. **"A floor" is too generous, measured 2026-08-13: 186 of 351 oracle-readable roots need two or more instantiation rounds and the maximum is twelve. See "Twelve rounds, and a convergence test that is not one" below.**

**Inference over the IR: confirmed by one, refuted by four, and it is the estimate.** `closureCalls` needs `typeOf b` for a node inside a materialised copy, where `TypeKey`'s `(file, offset, end, kind)` names the *template body* and answers the uninstantiated type. It also needs `Ty::Closure` to be constructible, which it is not: ten sites read it and every one is a consumer; the reference's constructor is `Type.hs:1176-1177` and `infer.rs:1534-1537` is a comment saying PHASE 4. So the design entry's warning stands — it is just not in the way. The experiment that entry asked for and nobody has run (port `inferType` over one instance body, diff the `TypeTable` against the CST-built one for a non-template file) is now the *fifth* slice's gate, not the first's, and there is no longer any reason to run it early.

### The honest size

Slice 1 was ~4,300 lines and slice 2 ~1,000, both landing zero assertions. This work is booked at ~110.

The five rewrites are 294 lines of Haskell — 55, 74, 24, 133, 8 — plus the helpers each spec names: `expFromType` (`Type.hs:1612-1651`), `getSymbols''` (`Symbols.hs:43-88`), `modifyDeclScopeName` (`Desugar.hs:139-172`), `scopedQualifier`, `removeNestedSeq`, and the recursion schemes. Call it 600. This project's measured Haskell→Rust rate for pass code with citations and hand formatting is 8–10× (`templateTypeCheck`: ~150 → 1,565; `deduceTemplateArgs`: ~100 → 818), and `Exp::map_children` is 92 mechanical arms on top. **Four to six thousand lines across four slices, all predicting zero.** Materialisation — `makeInstance`, `instantiate`, `resolve`, `deduplicateInstances`, mangling, the fixpoint, the `Src::expanded` frames and the diagnostic re-aiming the design entry specified and nobody has built (`Template.hs:111-163`, `Mangle.hs`) — is another 1,000 to 1,500. Then inference, which is 4,579 lines of `SyntaxNode` walking that a trait over two trees does not shrink.

Against that, what the five deliver directly, as each spec measured it rather than estimated it: `closureCalls` **+1** (`syntax::lambdas::4`, and only after materialisation); the other four **zero**, each by construction, because none of them emits a diagnostic. What they put at risk is larger and better measured: 271 `expected:0` assertions across the four lambda files plus 124 that route through `closureCalls`, 118 whole programs that wrap, 27 that contain lambdas and carry no assertions at all, and 137 of 300 parseable files that `moveFunctions` rewrites. **Pass 8's rewriting half can lose several hundred assertions and gain about one.**

The ~110 is real and it is downstream. It belongs to `unresolvedFunctionTemplateArgs` (11), `unresolvedTemplates` (12), `removeTemplate` (15) and `deduceAuto` (17), to `deduceTemplateArgs`' rewrite half, and to the second `inferType` putting a deduced type back on a call node — all of which need a tree that only these five can produce. That is the same correction §2 already records for pass 18 and pass 5: **count by blocking cause, not by filename**, and do not let five enabling passes carry a number the passes behind them will collect. Roadmap §1 should say pass 8's rewrites unlock ~110 rather than deliver them, and it should say the sequence is six slices, five of which predict nothing.


## Paths sort, and the oracle differential becomes a gate by catching exactly the class it was built for

Pass 8 slice 3. `kg_hir::lower` gains a second mode: `lower_sorted` takes an
`ImportSymbols` door and reproduces the reference's parse-time sort of every
written path (`prefixedScopedNameAndSymbol`, `Parser.hs:652-695`, and the
position sorters at `:702-801`) against an incremental symbol table
(`kg_hir::sort`) that declares as the lowering walks, the way `parseSymbol`
does. `kg_db::sorted::sorted_program` lowers a program in import topological
order and harvests each module's exportable shapes for the next; `kg dump ir`
on a file routes through it. The unsorted mode is untouched — every
pre-existing gate is byte-identical, as predicted — and `passes::run` calls
none of this. The grade is `oracle/differential.py` run raw (the
spine-collapsing normalizer is deleted, not extended), now also wired into
`cargo xtask ir` as a gate over `library/` whenever the oracle binary is
built: **116/124 files agree with the reference's own tree node-for-node**,
6 diverge only at interpolated strings (divergence #15), 2 are rejected by
the oracle itself, 0 unsorted paths remain across the 124 roots.

**The differential caught, on its first full run, precisely the bug class it
was specified for.** `FieldExpr::path_segment()` never returns anything — the
parser writes a method member as loose `TEMPLATE_KW`/`NAME_REF`/
`TEMPLATE_ARG_LIST` children, never a `PATH_SEGMENT` (`grammar/exprs.rs:269-279`)
— so both `field_member` and `field_callee` carried a dead branch and the
fallback dropped written method template arguments **in both modes**:
`_requests.enqueue_one<Index>(req)` lowered with `<Index>` gone. The round
trip cannot see this — the drop is deterministic, so it sits on both sides
and cancels; totality and provenance are structurally blind to it. It
survived every gate this project has, for as long as the code existed, until
a comparison whose other side does not share our lowering ran over a file
containing it.

Two smaller sorts the oracle corrected: an `identAttr` argument is a bare
`qualifiedIdentifier`, no position sorter and no `NamedValue` (`Parser.hs:175`,
`ecc(make_ecc<T>)` in `data/memory.k`); a template-template parameter default
sorts through `templateSpecifier`, not `typ` (`Parser.hs:368`).

**`nub` compares trees, and device overrides depend on it.** Under
`-I library` and the default `mock` target device, `base` re-exposes
`device/mock/hardware/dsp.k`, and `filterExposed` keeps every key whose
*second* component is exposed (`SymbolTable.hs:163-164`) — nested keys
included, so a device root's own locals collide with mock's copy of the same
function. The reference resolves them anyway because `findSymbol`'s `nub`
(`:229`) compares symbol **trees** with notes ignored
(`Parser/Syntax.hs:594-599`): a declaration textually identical to mock's
collapses with it. Ported as `kg_hir::sort::fingerprint` — a hash of the
position-free structural rendering, carried per declaration locally and per
harvested key across modules. The collapse is per-symbol, and
`stratix-10-nx-2100/hardware/dsp.k` — identical to mock in `fmul32`,
different elsewhere — agrees node-for-node only because of that. The two
files the oracle rejects (`agilex-7-f-023`, `stratix-10-gx-2800`) are the
overrides whose `fmul32` *differs* from mock's: the ambiguity is real there,
and `registerSymbolError` rides megaparsec's deferred-error channel, which
fails the whole parse at end of input. A root path handed to the sorted
program must be canonicalized for the same reason the reference calls
`canonicalizePath` (`Parser/IO.hs:107`): a root that `base` also imports must
get one `FileId` from both doors, or the program holds the module twice and
every seed-backed lookup goes ambiguous against its own twin.

Planted bugs, both runs recorded: dropping the `TemplateInstanceF s (Seq [])`
rule for function symbols (`Parser.hs:694`) turns 52 library files red with
the missing `TemplateInstance` named at its exact pre-order index; reverting
`nub` to positional identity turns exactly the two device-override files red
and nothing else. The interpolation exemption is keyed to an
`InterpolatedString` at the divergence point, not to a file list, so neither
plant could hide behind it.

Numbers: tests 1054 → 1063 (the sort's oracle-pinned tests), clippy 0,
corpus 479/479 and 355/355, conformance 2049/2049, `--strict` 557 —
unchanged, delta zero as predicted. `xtask ir` keeps totality 403/403,
round trip 403/403, provenance 479/479, template differential 403/403, and
adds the oracle gate. `bench` unchanged (sorting is not in `check`'s path).


## The rewrite substrate, and a gate clause that had to be weakened to bite

Pass 8 slice 4: `kg_hir::rewrite`, `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate`, and the four
gate extensions the entry above said must land with it "or the gate quietly
stops being evidence". They did. Numbers first, because they were predicted:
`conformance` 2049/2049, `--strict` **557 with the same name set**, `corpus`
479/479 and 355/355, tests 1063 → **1073**, clippy 0, `bench` keystroke 110.5 ms
inside the A/B band. `xtask ir` keeps totality 403/403, round trip 403/403,
provenance 479/479, differential 403/403, oracle diff 116/124, and adds
**rewrite 479/479, 65 declarations rewritten**. Assertion delta exactly zero, as
predicted, because nothing calls it.

### The oracle overturned three things reading had settled

Every expectation in the new tests is read off `kg-oracle --passes 8
--template-passes {2,3} --template-iterations 0`. `--passes 8` is not optional
and this cost two people time: without it the frontend runs all nineteen passes
and `removeTemplate x | isAbbreviatedTemplate x = SeqF []`
(`Frontend.hs:300-302`, execution order 15) deletes **both** halves of this
pass's output, so a fixture prints `SeqF []` and reads as a parse failure.

**The two `Typename` nodes are two nodes, and the entry above was wrong to say
otherwise.** It recorded that `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` "proposes to violate
[the no-sharing rule] by sharing one `Typename` node between a `TemplateParam`
and its `TypeParam` (faithful to `Function.hs:130-132`, and a DAG)". It is not.
`typeParam` reuses field `b` *of the `TemplateParamF` it is handed*, and the one
handed to it at `Function.hs:307` is a second, independently constructed value —
`templateParam (findParam p)`, which evaluates `newNote TypenameF e` again. Two
allocations, no DAG, no `deep_copy` needed. Retracted.

**The donors inside one synthesized node differ.** `--notes` on
`inline void f(auto a, uint8 b, auto c) { }`: the `TemplateParam` and its
`Typename` both wear the **`FuncParam`**'s span (`auto a`, 14..20); the
`TypeParam` wears the **`Auto`** node's (`auto`, 14..19) while *its* `Typename`
wears the `FuncParam`'s again. A port that donates uniformly is wrong at one of
the two sites and no gate here can see it — see the falsification below.

**Clause 1 fires for `FunctionDecl`, and `const auto` is not abbreviated.**
`isAbbreviatedTemplate` has a `FunctionDeclF` arm (`Parser/Syntax.hs:723`) and
the record update is total over both; `class Foo { public: void Do(auto x); }`
emits a template beside the declaration. And `isAuto AutoF = True; isAuto _ =
False` (`:706-707`) looks through nothing — `const auto` parses as `ConstF AutoF`
and is untouched. Descending through `Exp::Const` would have fabricated a
template parameter for every `const auto` parameter in the corpus.

### The blast radius was more than double what the entry booked

The entry said "18 files and 88 synthetic parameters". Measured off `kg dump ir`
rather than estimated: **35 files, 102 declarations, 125 `auto` parameters**, of
which **37 declarations / 41 parameters in 14 files revert** under an enclosing
template, leaving **65 declarations firing** — which is exactly what the new gate
reports, from a different instrument. The 18 is reproducible as an artifact of
taking `tail -1` of the oracle's output as the target file's tree: `parseProgram`
parses base first, so for any file in base's import closure the last tree printed
is *base's*. Thirty-three corpus files are mis-attributed that way.

### One arena, and why `fork` is not `#[derive(Clone)]`

The substrate resolution from the entry above held: one arena for the whole
pass-8 run, rewrites append, unchanged subtrees keep their ids, duplications go
through `deep_copy`, the gate walks from the root. The one thing it did not
settle is how to copy an arena at all, and both obvious answers are wrong.
`#[derive(Clone)]` copies the stamp, and two live arenas sharing a stamp is
precisely the "silently wrong node" the stamp exists to prevent. A fresh stamp
alone invalidates every id anyone holds, `ModuleIr::root` included.

`ExpArena::fork` mints a fresh stamp **and** records `(parent stamp, parent
len)`, which makes the accept rule exact rather than lenient: an id this arena
minted resolves; an id an ancestor minted at an index predating the fork
resolves, because the prefix is identical and stays identical (a forked-from
arena is never appended to again — `Db::body_ir` hands out `Arc<ModuleIr>`); an
id from a **sibling** fork does not. That last case is the one a shared stamp
could not have caught, and it is a unit test.

### `written`, and the half that keeps `Own`

The rule from the entry — `Own` iff the sole claimant of that `(range, kind)` in
its tree — became three constructors and nothing else: `Rewriter::replace` for a
node whose original goes unreachable in the same step, `donate` for one the
algebra invented, `deep_copy` for a subtree needed in two positions.

That leaves one real decision, because clause 1 puts **both** copies of the
function in the tree and exactly one may be `Own`. It is the **template's** half
that keeps the ids. Two reasons, and the second is the one that settles it:
`Src::expanded` deliberately preserves `written` (`kg-base/src/src.rs:76-88`),
so an instantiated body inherits `Own` from the template body it was copied
from; and the leftover is deleted seven frontend passes later anyway
(`Frontend.hs:300-302`). Copying the half that survives would have emptied every
`Own` index the editor answers from, for the half that lives. The leftover is
the `deep_copy`.

### The clause that had to be weakened before it could bite

The entry specified clause four as "forbid an `Own` node the lowering did not
create". Landed as written it rejects the **first file it sees**: an append-only
arena has no way to change a node in place, so every *replacement* — a node
whose children were rewritten — is a fresh index, and the rewritten root `Seq`
of any file containing an abbreviated function is exactly that. It may
legitimately keep `Own`, because what it replaced goes unreachable in the same
step and leaves no second claimant.

What must be forbidden is a **copy** wearing `Own`, which is the case the entry
actually named: `moveFunctions`' spliced member-name `Identifier` is
shape-*equal* to the declaration it was copied from and sails through the
equal-shape tolerance in clause three. So:

> an `Own` node reachable from the root, appended after the lowering finished,
> must not be structurally equal to a node the lowering built at the same
> `(file, range, kind)`.

A replacement differs in shape from what it replaced, by definition. A copy does
not. This also keeps the entry's third falsification pointed at something: a
driver that re-allocates an unchanged subtree produces a node shape-equal to the
lowered one at its own key. Note the gate now needs *both* walks — from the root
for the claims, over the whole arena for the "what did the lowering build here"
table.

### What the gate still cannot see, measured rather than argued

Three of the four extensions are **numerically vacuous today** and the landing
note has to say so, or the next surveyor reads a green gate as evidence.

* **Walking from root changes nothing**: 479/479 both ways. It found one
  genuinely unreachable node across the corpus — a `FunctionModifier` in
  `test/syntax/function-type.k`, allocated at `lower.rs:577-583` and then
  dropped when error recovery reaches the `FunctionDecl` branch, which has no
  `modifier` field (faithfully: `FunctionDeclF` has none, `Parser/Syntax.hs:556-562`,
  and the reference can only reach it where `modi` is provably `Nothing`,
  `Parser.hs:418-421`). Only error-recovered files reach it.
* **Keying on `FileId` and resolving against `head.file` measure zero**: 0
  cross-file heads in 473,003 nodes, and not by luck — `FnInit::Foreign`
  (`kg-hir/src/sort.rs:141-147`) exists precisely to decline rather than splice
  across arenas. `addLambdaWrappers` is the pass that makes it bite.
* **The `Donated` half of the tree is unchecked.** Every clause *but the
  resolution one* fires only on `Own` — that one fires on every reachable node,
  so a `Donated` node's whole obligation is that its range resolves to some CST
  node, which `Src::donated` makes true by construction. So a rewrite that
  donates the *wrong* donor is invisible here — which is why the entry above
  paired that falsification with the `--notes` oracle and not with this gate.

### The one finding that is bigger than the slice

`check_provenance` has never run over `lower_sorted`'s output — the lowering the
oracle differential grades and the one a rewrite will eventually run on. Run the
**current** gate verbatim over `kg_db::sorted::sorted_program` and it fails **30
of 124 library modules**, and walking from the root rescues none of them: the
colliding pair is live.

The collision is `_counter.count()` in `library/sync/lock.k` and its like — the
leaf `Identifier` allocated `Own` at the `NAME_REF` (`lower.rs:2273-2276`) and
the enclosing `QualifiedIdentifier` re-stamped `Own` at the same donor by
`finish_sorted`'s `own()` (`lower.rs:2413-2418`). **And the reference does the
same thing**: `let s = copyNote (ScopedNameF scope prefix ident) ident`
(`Parser.hs:655`) and `return (copyNote (QualifiedIdentifierF s) s, sym)`
(`:644`) give three nested nodes one identical `Src`, confirmed with
`kg-oracle --notes`.

So "no two structurally different `Own` nodes share a `(range, kind)`" is false
against the reference's own note assignment once paths are sorted. That is
divergence #21's key-space problem arriving early, not a bug in the sorter's
shapes — the oracle differential grades those at 116/124. Either `Own` becomes
exclusive per `(range, kind)` (demote the inner leaf; the outermost sorted node
is what answers a position question) or `TypeKey` grows a discriminator. This
slice deliberately does neither, and points the rewrite gate at `lower()`, where
the invariant holds — and says so in the code rather than leaving a green number
to imply otherwise.

### Four falsifications, run by four agents who did not write the code

Every one of them was worth running, and two changed the code.

**The revert gate went red for the wrong reason, and therefore not everywhere.**
Deleting the `Template => None` guard turned `xtask ir` red — 467/479, 65 → 102
declarations rewritten — but through **clause three**, on a plumbing artifact.
`desugar_shallow` ends with `replace`, so the two-element `Seq` clause 1 returns
is allocated at the function's own `(range, FN_DECL)` key and `f_prime` inside it
claims the same key; normally the parent's `remove_nested_seq` splices the pair
flat and the wrapper goes unreachable, but where the abbreviated declaration is
the direct `decl` of a `Template` there is no enclosing `Seq` and the wrapper
survives. So the gate saw 12 of the 14 damaged files and missed the two whose
parent *is* a `Seq` — `library/processor/risc_v.k` and
`test/syntax/helper/template_argument_deduction.k`, both the class-template-member
form, which is the **sharpest** case of the revert rather than the weakest.

Fixed by stating the pass's own invariant instead of inferring it from a
collision: **no `Template` node's id ever changes.** Re-planted with that in
place: 14 files, including both misses.

Also recorded: for this pass the "bottom-up revert" reading and "no guard at all"
compile to the same program. A `Template` sent down clause 3 hits
`remove_nested_seq`, which is the identity on anything that is not a `Seq`. There
is no third probe here.

**The arena's ancestry bound was unpinned, and the sibling test passed by
accident.** Three breaks were planted in `ExpArena::resolves`/`fork`. Two went
red. Dropping the `id.index < n` bound stayed **green across the whole
workspace** — 30 kg-hir tests, 40 suites, every `xtask ir` number identical —
because no test ever mints an id in the *base* after taking a fork, which is the
only quadrant the bound governs. The probe that catches it is now a test: the
fork answers `Public` for an id naming `Private`, which is the silently-wrong
node the module exists to prevent. And `a_forks_own_id_does_not_resolve_in_its_base`
was surviving the shared-stamp break only through its `expected =` string — the
index was out of bounds, so it panicked for an unrelated reason. The base now
grows too, so the scenario itself bites. Both breaks re-run here: red through
"did not panic as expected", not through a message.

**Clause four is load-bearing, and it is the only thing that sees its own bug.**
Three plants, all red. The discriminating one is a shape-equal `Own` replacement
— rebuild the `FuncParam` but leave its `auto` type in place. With clause four
short-circuited the whole gate exits **0**: clause three is silent because there
is only one *live* `Own` claimant, the lowered original having gone unreachable,
and the walk starts at the root on purpose. Clause four is the only check that
consults the table built by scanning the arena *including* superseded nodes, and
that scan is exactly what lets it see what a reachability walk cannot. Deleting
the id-preservation short-circuit is also caught, at 0/479, and costs 1.80×
arena growth per sub-pass (the median file exactly doubles; 1.80 rather than 2.00
because the `Template` guard returns before descending).

**The donor swap is invisible to the gate — confirmed, and worse than expected.**
Swapping the two donors at `Function.hs:296` and `:307` leaves `cargo xtask ir`
**byte-identical**. One unit test catches it and nothing else. The reason is
structural: every clause of `check_provenance` sits inside
`if written == Own`, so a `Donated` node's entire obligation is that its range
resolves to *some* CST node — and `Src::donated` makes that true by construction.
A wilder plant confirmed it: hang both synthesized nodes on the parameter's
**name** token, a `NAME` standing in for a type, and the gate does not move a
digit. It is not weakly wrong about donors; it is silent about them.

The instrument that does catch it exists and was built and run: compare
`kg dump ir --rewrite` against `kg-oracle --notes --template-passes 3`, resolving
each note to the CST node it names rather than comparing raw offsets (ours are
trivia-trimmed, the reference's include trailing whitespace). Green on the
committed code, red on the swap, red on a real corpus file. Cost: `--notes`
prints the whole transitive import closure on one line — 11 MB and 3.4 s for one
library file against 0.7 s for `--tree` — so a standing gate wants a driver flag
that emits notes for the root module only. Booked in the roadmap; the same
instrument grades all five rewrites, because what it compares is "which node
donated", not anything specific to this pass.

**And an audit found the gate's own honest limit.** `rewrite: 479/479 (65
declarations)` says the pass ran, kept provenance sound and touched nothing
else. It does **not** grade the 65 against the reference, and the reference does
not agree with it: 16 hand fixtures and a 351-file sweep found no divergence in
the three clauses — same `$T` names, same filter-then-`zip` indices, same
`init declScopeName` across every scope shape, same `findByName`, same revert —
but the reference fires on 12 declarations we decline and declines 4 we fire on.
Both are unported **upstream** sub-passes: the 12 are desugared generic lambdas
(`desugarLambdas` has not landed, and nothing in this tree constructs
`FunctionKind::LambdaFunction`, so the arm that was commented as handling them is
dead code today — the comment now says so); the 4 are
`library/data/function.k`'s `apply`/`bind`/`bind1st`/`bind2nd`, which
`higherOrderFunctions` has already wrapped in a `Template` upstream of this
sub-pass in the reference, so *its* clause 2 reverts where ours fires. Neither is
a clause bug. Both are written at the call site, so the number is not read as a
score it is not.


## The donor gate that cannot exist, and the 6.6% that says why

Slice 5 was going to be the gate the last slice's falsifiers proved is missing:
`xtask ir` is byte-identical under a swapped `Src` donor, and the four remaining
pass-8 rewrites synthesize far more nodes than the first one did. It is not that
gate. What it is: a driver flag that makes the oracle affordable, a heuristic
deleted, a measurement, and a house rule that does the job a gate cannot.

**`--roots-only`.** `kg-oracle` prints one tree per parsed file, so the cost of
`--notes` scaled with the *import closure* rather than the file: 11,462,524 bytes
and 3.16 s for `library/codec/crc.k`, against 0.71 s for `--tree`. The flag
filters the printing — never the parsing, because `getSymbols` is over every
parsed file and dropping the imports is the bug this driver already shipped once
— by the canonical path `parseProgram` recorded (`Parser/IO.hs:95`). Result:
354,307 bytes, 0.74 s. A 32× reduction, and the root's line is byte-identical to
the one the old output contained.

It also **deleted a heuristic**. `oracle_names` had to *find* the root among one
line per file, by matching its `module` header and taking the last hit, because
the root is only usually last (one that `base.k` itself imports completes
mid-list) and a device file can share its module name with the copy base pulled
in. That is now the driver's job, keyed on the same identity the reference uses.
`oracle diff` unchanged at 116/124 and slightly faster.

**Then the measurement, which killed the gate.** The oracle differential now
reads `--notes` rather than `--tree` and parses the note out of each node. That
needs one non-obvious thing: `emit Notes` renders a node as
`show e ++ " @" ++ show n`, so the notes arrive in **post**-order while the
constructors arrive in pre-order, and a zip is wrong. A stack is exactly right —
children complete before parents, so a note always belongs to the most recent
un-noted constructor.

With the reference's span first resolved to the CST node it names (a megaparsec
lexeme consumes its trailing trivia: `auto ` where ours is `auto`), **93.4% of
nodes agree exactly** — 256,348 of 274,406 across the 116 files whose trees
already match node-for-node. The other 6.6% is not one thing and not a few clean
categories: 6,315 `Seq`, 2,641 `ScopedName`, 1,706 `Binary`, 1,438 `Identifier`,
1,325 `TemplateInstance`, and a long tail. A `ModuleIdentifier`'s span covers the
`module` keyword where ours covers the name; a `ModuleDecl`'s note is
`SrcUnknown` where ours donates the header; a `Seq` is sometimes handed a note by
`copyNote` from a node it does not contain.

Ours is the more precise object and there is no reason to give it up — `Src::head`
exists so an editor can answer a position question from `(head, kind)`, and a
span covering a keyword the node is not answers the wrong query. The reference
has no such consumer. So the number is **printed and not gated** (divergence
#25), and it earns its place by moving: a change that makes provenance
systematically worse shows up in it.

Three relational encodings were tried before settling: comparing starts only
(the swap keeps the start, so it does not bite), comparing the equality partition
over donors (the reference shares notes between nodes where we do not), and
comparing parent/child containment (our `ModuleDecl` body `Seq` does not contain
its own children, so it disagrees everywhere). Each fails for a different reason
and each failure is the same underlying fact.

**So the donor protection is a house rule, not a gate.** Each rewrite lands with
donor assertions read off `kg-oracle --notes`, proven by swapping two donors and
watching the test go red — which is exactly what
`the_two_donors_inside_one_synthesized_type_param_differ` already does, and what
the falsifier showed is the only thing in the tree that catches it. Written into
`CLAUDE.md` so the next four rewrites inherit it.

## Surveying `moveFunctions` by mutating the oracle, and the corpus that grades nothing

*2026-08-13, before the port. Scratch — fixtures, sweeps, and a mutant oracle
with one clause commented out at a time — was `/tmp`-resident and is gone; the
numbers are here because they cost an hour of oracle CPU each.*

The survey technique is the reusable part. `moveFunctions` has ten distinguishable
behaviours and no way to ask which of them the corpus exercises. So: **build the
reference ten more times, each with one clause deleted, and re-sweep all 357
oracle-readable corpus files after each build.** The count of files whose tree
changes is that clause's reach. It is slow and it is exact, and it answers a
question that reading the corpus cannot.

| clause | `Function.hs` | files changed / 357 |
|---|---|---|
| `Template{}` defer | `:88` | 58 |
| abbreviated `Function{}` defer | `:89-90` | 4 |
| `StaticIf{}` defer | `:91` | 1 (`test/logic/memory_test_cases_3.k`) |
| `StaticFor{}` defer | `:92` | **0 — arm 1 shadows both instances** |
| local `Class{}` defer | `:93-94` | 10 |
| `NestedScopeF` arm | `:99` | **0** |
| statement lifts (`DoWhile`/`RangeFor`/`If`) | `:104-117` | **0** |
| `memberAccess` const-inlining | `:55` | 11 |
| `memberAccess` `thisMethod` | `:58-62` | 21 |
| `qualifyName` | `:72-77` | 132 — the largest single behaviour |

Five arms are unreachable in every file the oracle can read. They are **not
dead**: their shapes live in `test/syntax/local-functions.k`, which the oracle
rejects whole (it is a multi-fixture file). Extracted to a scratch fixture they
fire. So five of ten behaviours can only ever be pinned by unit tests, and any
whole-corpus gate that reports a perfect score is silent about half the pass.
Writing that down is the point; a gate whose blind spots are unstated reads as
total coverage.

**`library/` grades nothing here.** Of the 357 files, 138 change between
`--template-passes 3` and `4`. **Zero are `library/` files** — all 122
oracle-readable `library/` trees are byte-identical across the boundary. All 144
`library/` `LambdaFunction`s sit under a `Template` (141) or in the leftover copy
of an abbreviated function (3, all `library/data/function.k`), and both are
deferral arms. Had the previous slice not already widened the reference-graded
lines to `test/` — which found a defect in the gate on its first run — this pass
would have landed behind a green number measuring an empty set. The general form:
**check that your instrument's corpus contains the phenomenon before trusting its
score**, and check it by counting, not by expecting.

Three findings that change the code rather than the gate. The pass builds a
symbol map after all — `getSymbols'' AllSymbols $ body parent` (`:33`) — but
per-node and from one body, and substituting `Db::global_symbols` is *wrong*, not
merely heavy: `body parent` excludes the parent's own parameter list, so a
whole-program map qualifies a name the reference leaves bare. Only the `ClassF`
arm does the `$this.` rewrite (`:102`), because only there does `body parent`
hold `DeclareClass` variables — a function inside a function inside a class
reads the member as a bare `m`. And the `$this._x` rewrite is `memberAccess`,
`Function.hs:52-64`; `:152-158`, which two files in this tree cited for it, is
`makeCapture`.

**Cost, measured on the reference itself.** Its whole-corpus sweep goes from
386 s CPU at `tp=3` to 465 s at `tp=4` — **+20% for this one sub-pass**, because
`getSymbols''` is rebuilt at every `Function`/`NestedScope`/`Class` node over
that node's entire body. Haskell survives it on laziness (`:30`'s guard never
forces the map when nothing is selected); an eager port pays it on the **219 of
357 files where the pass is a no-op**. The exact — not approximate —
optimisation: `cond` and `getQualifiedName` read only the top constructor,
`funcKind`, `declScopeName` and `declName`, none of which the pass's own
rewrites change, so the selection can be computed on the *unrewritten* body and
both catas skipped when it is empty. This is the shape `CLAUDE.md`'s pass-4
story warns about, one pass earlier than it bit last time.

## Twelve rounds, and a convergence test that is not one

*2026-08-13. Measured over all 469 corpus roots (351 the oracle accepts; 118
rejected, 69 of those multi-fixture `expected:` files that are not programs).*

The question was how many template-instantiation rounds the corpus actually
reaches, because §8's entries have twice assumed one round is a floor worth
shipping. The answer is **twelve**, on `test/library/processor/risc-v.k` and
`test/library/data/vector.k`, and **186 of 351 roots (53%) need at least two**.
Distribution of the smallest sufficient `--template-iterations`: `0:165, 1:15,
2:15, 3:46, 4:18, 5:29, 6:19, 7:12, 8:10, 12:2`, plus 20 roots pinned only as
`>8` — the deep re-probe was halted after 5 of 33 on a time check, which can
only move mass *up* the tail. `library/` is nearly flat (84% at zero) because it
only *defines* generics; `test/` has a median of 3.

**The methodological finding is the convergence test.** The obvious rule —
"round N has converged when `out(N) == out(N+1)`" — is **unsound here**, and
this survey was specified with it. `library/sync/atomic/init.k` plateaus at 1–2,
moves at 3, plateaus at 4–6, moves at 7, and only settles at 8; the rule reports
1. **11 of 351 roots have such a false plateau.** Trajectories are not even
monotone in size: `vector.k` oscillates for twelve rounds, deterministically.
The sound test is to compare each bounded run against the *unbounded* one and
take the smallest N that matches, confirmed at N+1 — three times the oracle
CPU, and the only reason the maximum is known to be twelve rather than one.
Generalises past this survey: a fixpoint whose steps can be *locally* idempotent
cannot be detected by comparing adjacent steps.

**So a one-shot port of pass 8's inner sub-passes is a defect, not a floor.**
The real compiler is unbounded by default — `passes`, `template_iterations` and
`template_passes` all default to `maxBound` (`app/Options/CmdArgs.hs:104-106`).
And rounds are not syntactic nesting depth that a smarter single pass could
flatten: on `xoshiro.k`, round 1 yields `<|$uint@32|>` and round 2 yields
`<|$uint@41|>` and `<|$uint@43|>` — widths that exist *only* because round 1
substituted and `inferType` then re-ran over the substituted tree. A one-shot
pass cannot produce them; it under-instantiates silently, which is the failure
mode this repo has agreed to call a lie rather than a gap. Iterating is
affordable: `float32.k` 2.86 s → 5.97 s (N=0→7), `risc-v.k` 10.52 s → 42.37 s
(N=0→12).

Also corrected here: the inner sub-pass order had 7 and 8 swapped everywhere in
this repo. `passes` is consumed by `foldr ($)` (`Template.hs:60`) so the list
reads backwards, and `:74` `closureCalls` runs sixth while `:73`
`deduceTemplateArgs` runs seventh. Confirmed by measurement as well as by
reading — the `TemplateInstanceF` jump lands at `--template-passes 6→7`. The
`tp=3` vs `4` boundary the `moveFunctions` gates are built on is unaffected.

## Materialisation is not blocked on inference, and the provenance gate cannot survive it

*2026-08-13, from a survey run against the oracle over all 469 corpus roots.
Scratch in a scratch directory (not kept).*

**The premise everything downstream was scheduled on is false.** Materialisation
was booked as blocked on IR inference because it "reads `typeOf` and calls
`expFromType`". Grepping the two files that *are* materialisation —
`Template.hs` and `Mangle.hs` — for `expFromType|typeOf|theType|tIs` returns
**zero matches**. `instantiate`, `makeInstance`, `resolve`, `deduplicateInstances`
and the whole mangler read no type. The single type read in the path is
`setTypeOfInstance` (`Type.hs:426-440`), and it reads `typeOf` of the *written
argument* nodes — `Own`, in the instantiating file, already keyed in today's
`TypeTable`. **One round of materialisation is a syntactic rewrite, unblocked
today.** Roadmap §1b's sequence already had this right; the brief that scheduled
the survey inverted it.

The counterweight is that one round is not the compiler. Measured
independently by two surveys that agree: **53% of the 351 oracle-readable roots
need two or more instantiation rounds, and the maximum is twelve** — see "Twelve
rounds, and a convergence test that is not one". Round 2 is not "more deeply
nested instances": on `library/data/random/xoshiro.k` it holds `<|$uint@41|>`
and `<|$uint@43|>`, widths produced by shift-widening *inference* over round 1's
copies. `Template.hs:58`'s inter-round `inferType` is load-bearing, and this
journal's claim that "the per-instance `depth` equals the round number" is wrong
as a general statement.

**Pass 8 has seven rewrites, not five.** `inferExpTree`'s algebra is
`staticControl . unfix . evaluateConstexpr . unfix . inferExpType`
(`Inference.hs:50`). Two thirds of it are tree rewrites — `staticControl`
deletes the untaken `static if` branch and unrolls a `static for` into a
body-copy per iteration (`Constexpr.hs:44-54`) — and `passes::types` implements
only `inferExpType`, which its own `SEAM:` comments say. Measured: on 13 of 16
`test/logic` roots the sub-pass-5 boundary changes the tree, net −13,110 bytes
of folding. Separately, `deduceTemplateArgs` is `desugar' rewrite`
(`Type.hs:1386`) and only its *reporter* half is ported; its rewrite half is
what fills a short `<…>` list to full arity, and `instances.rs:593-595` declines
every such instance. Three unported type-dependent rewrites, not two.

### The gate finding, run rather than read

The question was whether `xtask ir`'s provenance gate would still hold once
instance copies are in the arena. It does not, and not by a little. Plants of
