materialisation-shaped copies — a template-body subtree copied with
`Src::expanded`, which preserves `Own` — in three fidelities, over the corpus:

```
MATERIALISE-PLANT: green {"copy": 9, "mangled-root": 9, "substituted": 9}
red: copy 165 · mangled-root 163 · substituted 169
```

Of the 174 template-bearing clean-parse files, **163–169 go red**, and the
faithful `makeInstance` shape (only the outermost `declName` mangled) is the
worst of the three. It fails clause 4 on ordinary body statements — 40
`RETURN_STMT`, 40 `BLOCK_STMT`, 30 `PATH`, 20 `CALL_EXPR` — because any subtree
of a template body that does not mention the parameter is copied byte-identical
and wears `Own`. The `substituted` variant fails clause 3 instead: two instances
are structurally *different* `Own` nodes at one `(range, kind)`. Measured over
`lower()`, the friendlier of the two lowerings; `lower_sorted` is worse.

This is not tuning. It is the key space, and it is divergence #24 arriving at
full size.

### The decision, taken here

**A materialised copy keeps `written == Own`, and `TypeKey` grows a fifth field
naming the expansion.**

The rule this repo settled on is "`Own` iff the sole claimant of that
`(range, kind)` in the tree it lives in". Materialisation puts N structurally
different copies of one body node at one `(range, kind)`. So either the copies
are demoted, or the key widens; there is no third option and both gate clauses
say so.

Demotion is the wrong half. `written` has exactly one consumer worth having —
the index an editor answers a position query from — and the 536 unannotated
`auto` hints that motivate it live *inside* template bodies and their instances.
Marking every copy `Donated` empties that index precisely where it was wanted.
The reference has no equivalent problem because its copies are distinct `Fix`
nodes separated by identity; ours would be separated by `ExpId`, which
`arena.rs` forbids as a key on purpose ("an arena index is an address, never a
key"). So the discriminator must be the *expansion* — a stable, meaningful
thing, derivable from the `SrcStack` frame `Src::expanded` already pushes —
rather than an address.

This was also said to settle divergence #24's sorted-path case, "the same
problem one size down". **Refuted the same day** — 201 of 201 colliding keys
there have every claimant at `Expansion::ROOT`, and #24 needs the other of its
two resolutions; see "The fifth field works, does not settle #24" below. It does
correct roadmap §1d: it presents "a fifth `TypeKey` field"
and "an expansion-aware index" as alternatives, where (a) "would cover
`inferType` and `templateTypeCheck` and stop". Measured, the fifth field is
required under both.

What would change this: evidence that an expansion discriminator cannot be made
stable across a keystroke — an editor needs the key to survive an edit — in
which case the fifth field must be spelled as the mangled instance path rather
than an id. And a memory measurement: 23,931 distinct mangled declarations
corpus-wide, times their body nodes, all newly keyed.

### Three other corrections

**Whole-program rooting makes the instance census worse, refuting roadmap §1b.**
`decidedInstances`' error gate (`Template.hs:55,84`) is whole-program and
all-or-nothing, so rooting at the corpus — or at all of `library/` — returns
**zero** templates and zero instances, because one broken file empties the set.
Even restricted to the 233 files that are individually clean, a single root set
decides *fewer* instances (23/47) than the union of per-file root sets (26/49).
The product consequence nobody had written down: the LSP rooting change §2 wants
for the `auto` hints would, done naively, disable the instance census for any
workspace containing one erroring file.

**A donor rule in this journal is half wrong.** It says a substituted argument
subtree "keeps its own `Src`, in the instantiating file, with no frame pushed".
`argAt` is `unNote . unfix` (`TypeCheck.hs:331-337`) — it *discards* the
argument's root note — and `desugarWithNote` then wears the **`TypeParam`'s**
note plus a frame. Measured: the substituted `UnsignedF 8` at a `T value`
position wears `SrcStack(offset 39)`, the template's own `T`. Only the
argument's *children* survive unframed. A port that donates the argument's root
range is wrong at every substitution site. Also worth a donor test: the mangled
`declName` wears the *unmangled* name's range, so its text is not its range's
text and it must be `Donated` while the copied body around it is `Own`.

**Roadmap §1b-i is dead work carrying no withdrawal marker.** It asks for a
driver flag that emits notes for the root module only and calls the donor
differential "worth doing before the next rewrite". The flag shipped
(`--roots-only`); the differential was then built, measured at 93.4% node
agreement, and *abandoned* in favour of a house rule — which is recorded two
entries above under "The donor gate that cannot exist". A reader scheduling from
§1b-i would redo work already tried and rejected.

### Scale

We decide **49 of the reference's 23,931 distinct mangled declarations — 0.2%**.
The gap is not mostly the postponement rule: the three highest-volume templates
are the closure machinery instantiating itself on arguments synthesized by
sub-passes 1 and 2, and sub-pass 1 is unported. `data.closure.core.Closure`
alone has 5,117 distinct argument lists, and `mangle` drops an argument for it
outright (`Mangle.hs:42-43`), so mangling is non-injective by construction and
`deduplicateInstances` is the reference's own backstop. Aggregate node growth
under full instantiation is 1.194× (median 1.008, max **5.06×** on
`test/library/data/hash_table.k`); instance subtrees are 16.7% of the finished
tree; the longest mangled name is 5,040 characters at nesting depth 10.

**Sizing.** Materialisation's Haskell core is 172 lines. This project's measured
Haskell→Rust expansion, code only, is 7×–23× with a median near 13× — 
`captureThis` 9→204, `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` 34→455, `desugarLambdas`
118→968, `decidedInstances` 54→1033, `templateTypeCheck` ~130→911. That puts
materialisation at **1,200–4,000 lines**, so this journal's "1,000–1,500"
estimate sits below the bottom of the band.

The smaller slice that does exist: **the mangler plus `resolve`**
(`Mangle.hs:17-64` + `Template.hs:158-164`), ~600 lines, no types read, and it
puts the instance table under reference grading for the first time — today it is
graded only by a differential between two of our own readings. Its gate is a
**mangled-declaration ledger**: containment (ours ⊆ theirs, `$wrapper$` and
`make_capture` entries dropped by name) plus the conserved quantity "every
instance in `Db::instances` either becomes a ledger entry or is explicitly
declined, never both and never neither". Extract it by brace-matched scan of
*declarations*, never by identifier regex — on `test/library/data/representation.k`
a bare `IdentifierF "…<|…"` match finds 21 names of which **zero** are
declarations; all 21 are references to instances materialised elsewhere, and the
file declares 115. Corpus-wide, mentions outnumber declarations 4.7×. Anyone
counting identifiers is measuring `resolve`, not `instantiate`.

## The fifth field works, does not settle #24, and cannot be keyed on where it is

*2026-08-13, second survey of the same day, run to cost the decision the first
one took rather than to re-open it. Harness preserved at
a scratch directory (not kept).*

**The decision holds, verified by running the gate itself rather than a copy of
its logic.** Instance-shaped copies planted into a fork of the arena in the
three fidelities, then `check_provenance` called unmodified:

| | copy | mangled-root | substituted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4-field key | red 180/180 | red 180/180 | red 180/180 |
| 5-field key | **green 180/180** | **green 180/180** | **green 180/180** |

Same at depth 2 — an expansion of an expansion, which 53% of roots reach. And
the falsification that matters: give two copies of one template the **same**
`InstanceId` and the widened gate goes red 180/180 again, `clause3: 2
structurally different own nodes claim 281..376 FN_DECL`. The fifth field is not
a way of switching the gate off.

The blind spot it creates, stated: with the expansion in the key, clause 4 can
never fire *inside* a correctly-framed expansion — lowered nodes are `ROOT` and
copies are not, so the probe cannot hit. What still bites is a copy that forgets
to push a frame, and two instances sharing one.

### Three claims of yesterday's entry, wrong

**"The same discriminator settles divergence #24 one size down" — refuted.**
`lower_sorted` over `library/`: 94 ok / 30 red with the four-field key, and
**94 / 30 with the five-field key**. Measured directly, there are 201 colliding
keys across those 30 modules; **201 of 201** are the `Identifier` +
`QualifiedIdentifier` pair at a `NAME_REF`, and **201 of 201 have every claimant
at `Expansion::ROOT`**. A discriminator cannot separate two nodes that are both
outside every expansion. This is by construction.

So divergence #24 needs the *other* of the two resolutions it originally named —
demote the inner leaf, because the outermost sorted node is what should answer a
position question — and the two problems take one option each. That correction
matters beyond bookkeeping: the demotion is **independently landable today and
has a real caller the day it lands**, since it is the only thing keeping
`xtask ir`'s provenance and rewrite gates on `lower()` rather than
`lower_sorted()`, which is the lowering the oracle differential grades and the
one every rewrite will eventually run on. Every collision has exactly two
claimants in an ancestor/descendant pair, so demotion clears all 201.

**"Cost today: none — nothing reads `written` but the gate" — refuted.**
`kg_db::instances` reads it twice in production (`:397`, `:709`) and `:709` turns
it into a `TypeKey`. `Db::instances` is reached by `kg dump instances`, so a user
typing a command reaches it.

**"Derivable from the `SrcStack` frame `Src::expanded` already pushes" — half
wrong, and the half that is wrong is a defect in shipped code.**

At the IR end it is derivable and free. At the CST end it is not: every key in
`passes::types` comes from `TypeKey::for_node(file, &SyntaxNode)` and a
`SyntaxNode` has no `Src`, so for ~40 read sites the discriminator would have to
be *threaded through the walk*. Exactly one production consumer keys from an IR
`Src` today (`instances.rs:709-718`).

Worse, the frame **as interned** is not stable. `ExpansionInterner` interns
`{ site, instance, parent }` and `site` is a `FileRange` in the instantiating
file, so any edit above the instantiation re-interns every frame beneath it.
Measured over 177 template-bearing files, inserting one **blank line** above the
deciding site:

```
Own keys inside an expansion:                        134,178
  head entirely above the edit (4-field key unmoved): 27,672
  fifth field changed anyway:                        134,178   ← all of them
control (site held constant):                              0
```

The fix is not to spell the field as a mangled path. It is to **split the
frame**: keep `site` for rendering `while compiling`, and intern the *keyed*
identity on `(instance, parent)` only, with `InstanceId` minted content-addressed
from `InstanceSet`'s existing `(template qualified name, argument key)` pair
(`instances.rs:105-109`) — both text-derived and offset-free, and computed today.

There is a second, independent reason to do that, and it is the one that decides
whether this is affordable. `Foo<uint8>`'s body types are identical whoever
instantiates it, and `Closure` alone has 5,117 argument lists. Only a
content-addressed discriminator lets that inference be *shared*; a site-derived
one forbids it.

### Cost

**The field itself is free.** A fifth field defaulted to `ROOT` at every
construction site, benched back to back: `check` −0.5%, `keystroke` +1.4% — and
`lex` +5.7% and `parse` +3.5% in the same run, two stages that touch no
`TypeKey` at all. Every affected delta is inside the noise floor.
`size_of::<TypeKey>()` 16 → 20 bytes.

**Memory is not the constraint.** A proxy map holding the corpus's 141,797 keys
plus K−1 copies of the 132,225 nodes that sit inside a `TEMPLATE_DECL` (24.6% of
537,553): exactly linear at 28 bytes/entry, 7.3 MiB at K=2 and 14.4 MiB at K=4,
against a measured effective corpus-wide K of about 1.8.

**Time is.** Inference is roughly linear in nodes, so a file pays its own growth
factor, and four `library/` files are **98%+ template body** — their multiplier
*is* their instance count. `keystroke` worst is already 108 ms against a 16 ms
frame, 6.75× over budget before a single copy exists. What keeps it affordable
is dedup, which is what the content-addressed `InstanceId` buys.

### And the recurring failure, already landed a fifth time

`Src::expanded`, `ExpansionInterner`, `ExpansionData` and `InstanceId` have
**zero production callers** — only `src.rs`'s own unit tests. `Src.via` is 4 of
`Src`'s 20 bytes on every one of ~473,000 IR nodes and reads `ROOT` on all of
them. A fifth `TypeKey` field would be the sixth instance: `ROOT` at the one site
that could carry it and `ROOT` everywhere else. So it lands **with**
`makeInstance` and not before, and the two things that can land earlier are the
#24 demotion (which has a caller) and the `ExpansionData` split (which does not,
and should therefore ride along with the slice that mints `InstanceId`).

One more, smaller than the rest and unfixable by any key design: a half-typed
line makes a file error, `decidedInstances`' gate is whole-program and
all-or-nothing (`Template.hs:55,84`), so the instance set goes **empty
mid-keystroke** and every expansion key vanishes regardless of discriminator.
That is a rooting decision, not a keying one.

## `resolve` fires on shapes, not on sites

*2026-08-13, found while porting `Mangle.hs:17-64` and `Template.hs:158-164`.
The slice's own brief — written by me from the materialisation survey — was
wrong about this, and it is the kind of wrong that a port reproduces silently.*

`decidedInstances` is a map from a template's qualified name to the argument
lists decided *for it*, collected by walking use sites. The natural reading, and
the one the brief encoded, is that `resolve` then rewrites **those sites**.

It does not. `resolve`'s guard is `b \`Map.member\` …`, and `b` is a `NotedExp`
whose `Eq` **ignores the annotation** (`Parser/Syntax.hs:593-599`). So the
predicate is "is there *any* decided instance of this template whose argument
subtree is structurally equal to this one", and it fires on every occurrence of
that shape anywhere in the module — **including inside template bodies, where
`decidedInstances` deliberately never collects** (rule 4 postpones an instance
inside another template until that template is instantiated).

Oracle-verified in both directions. `Box<uint8>` decided at a use site also
resolves inside an unrelated template's body. `Box<My>` does not, because the
arguments' scope fields differ and `ExpF`'s field equality is what bounds the
spread. The corpus has exactly one same-module witness
(`test/logic/test_cases_51.k`, `S738<uint32>` at offset 4338) and no
cross-module one, so a port that read the brief and rewrote only the collected
sites would have passed every corpus gate and been wrong.

A second byte-level surprise in the same neighbourhood: **the literal re-stamp
changes the mangled name.** `validateArg` (`TypeCheck.hs:281-283`) narrows an
out-of-range literal argument to its parameter's type, so `W2<300>` under a
`uint8 N` parameter mangles `@44`, not `@300` — oracle-pinned. And because the
stamped key is *structurally* different from the written one, a stamped shape
never spreads: `W2<44>` written by hand in a template body stays unresolved. The
stamp is carried in the decided map and applied to the mangled bytes only; the
tree keeps the literal the user wrote.

The general lesson, which is the reusable part: **a Haskell `Eq` instance that
drops a field is a semantic decision, not a convenience.** `Note`'s does, and
this is the second pass where the difference between "the sites we collected"
and "everything that looks like them" decides what the pass means. Check the
instance before porting any `Map.member` guard.

## Pass 15 is a prerequisite, not a consumer, and one arm of pass 12 is free

*2026-08-13, surveying the four passes marked "not started". Scratch in
a scratch directory (not kept).*

This journal has said, and `status.md` and `roadmap.md` §2 repeated, that the
~110 remaining assertions belong to passes 11, 12, 15 and 17, "all of which need
a tree that only [pass 8's five rewrites] can produce". Measured, that is wrong
in three places, and the most useful correction inverts a dependency.

**Passes 11 and 12 are blocked on pass 15, not on pass 8's rewrites.** Whole
corpus, `kg-oracle --errors --passes N` over 469 roots:

| `--passes` | roots carrying an error | error locations |
|---|---|---|
| 6, 7, 8 | 0 | 0 |
| 9, 10 | 5 | 11 |
| **11** | **351 of 352** | **1,530** |
| 12, 13, 14 | 351 of 352 | 5,123 |
| **15** | **5** | **11** |

Passes 11 and 12 write five thousand error nodes onto essentially the whole
corpus and pass 15 deletes every one of them. The mechanism is an arm nobody
costed: `removeTemplate x | isAbbreviatedTemplate x = SeqF []`
(`Frontend.hs:300-301`) deletes the *leftover original* that
`abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` left beside its template — errors and all. Two
library declarations account for 999 of the 1,530: `inline auto just(auto value)`
(`library/data/optional.k:43`) and `inline auto constant(auto x)`
(`library/data/function.k:41`). Anything importing `data/optional` or
`data/function` inherits them, and `Db::check` runs `frontend_diagnostics` over
every module of the program, so they would reach the scoreboard. **Landing 11 or
12 without a `removeTemplate`-shaped guard is a catastrophe, not a partial
win** — and `kg-db/src/lib.rs` calls pass 15 "rewrite-only", which is true of
the clause and false of its effect. It is the largest single diagnostic
*suppressor* in the frontend.

**One arm of pass 12 is not blocked at all, and it is provable rather than
lucky.** Driving `instantiateTemplates` down its exit path
(`--template-iterations 0`, `Template.hs:55-58`) and comparing every arm against
the unbounded reference over all 2,922 snippets:

| arm | reference | with no materialisation |
|---|---|---|
| **"Too many arguments"** | 8 nodes / 8 assertions | **7 / 7 — invents nothing** |
| "could not deduce all arguments" | 22 / 22 | 571 / 373 |
| per-argument unresolved | 22 / 20 | 319 / 165 |
| "failed to instantiate" | 6 / 6 | **1,713 / 1,270** |
| "undefined template" | 4 / 4 | 40 / 37 |
| pass 11, "unresolved argument" | 5 / 5 | 810 / 363 |

**4,715 invented error nodes and 1,166 assertions the reference accepts would be
newly rejected** — a far stronger proof of the blocked reading than the docs ever
gave, for every arm but one. The exception is structural:
`templateArgsResolved` requires `length params == length args`
(`TypeCheck.hs:324`), so an over-long argument list can never be decided, never
be `resolve`d, and always reaches pass 12 no matter how many rounds run.

**The other three are worth approximately nothing.** Pass 7 `trimExternClasses`
has no `desugarError` in it, changes 2 of 469 corpus roots, and every assertion
it touches already passes — its value is entirely to the C++ backend this port
does not have. Pass 15 delivers **zero** new assertions. Pass 11 delivers
**two**, both `println(clog2(x))` in `basics.k`, and it only gets them by
pre-empting pass 16's `clog2` clause, which this port keeps deliberately silent.
The corrected attribution: **11 → 2, 12 → 49, 15 → 0, 7 → 0**, against a
roadmap that said "~34" for pass 12 and grouped all four as one deferred bundle.

**And pass 15 is already half-ported under other names**, which is the pass-3
pattern arriving again: `facts::reached_only_after_elaboration` covers the
`TemplateF` arm and `passes::undefined_symbols::is_abbreviated_template` is the
other guard. The second is private to a module that has nothing to do with it,
and the next pass that needs it is 11 — so it belongs in `facts.rs` with the
`Frontend.hs:300-301` citation beside the `Parser/Syntax.hs:722-724` one.

### The attribution method, because the obvious one is wrong

Attributing a strict failure to "the first `--passes N` at which an error
appears" gives pass 11 **28** owned assertions. Twenty-six of those are the
transient library errors pass 15 erases. The sound rule is **the first N holding
an error the full frontend also reports**, which gives pass 11 two. Same shape
as the fixpoint survey's false plateaus: a monotone-looking probe over a
non-monotone process reports the first bump, not the answer.

## Materialisation lands, and the donor rule that was true and insufficient

*2026-08-13. `kg_hir::rewrite::instantiate`, 2050 lines, with the `TypeKey`
fifth field. Scratch, including the stability harness, in
a scratch directory (not kept).*

**The decision from two surveys ago held, and the field landed with its first
copy rather than ahead of it.** That was the whole reason to wait: `Src::expanded`,
`ExpansionInterner`, `ExpansionData` and `InstanceId` had **zero production
callers** for as long as they existed, and a fifth `TypeKey` field defaulted to
`ROOT` everywhere would have been the sixth module this repo shipped with
nothing driving it.

**The two defects in shipped code are fixed, and the fix is measured both ways.**
The interner keyed on `{ site, instance, parent }` with `site` a `FileRange` in
the instantiating file, so an edit anywhere above an instantiation re-interned
every frame beneath it. It now keys on `(instance, parent)` alone, with `site`
demoted to rendering data under first-intern-wins — which is `Map.union`'s left
bias (`Template.hs:88`), the same rule that makes a template used at three sites
report at the first in program order. `InstanceId` is content-addressed from
`InstanceSet`'s `(template qualified name, argument key)` pair, both text-derived
and offset-free.

Measured over the whole corpus, blank line inserted above the deciding site:
**0 of 37,056** expansion-keyed `Own` keys change their fifth field. Re-plant the
old interner and the same run reads **37,056 of 37,056**. The instrument is
falsified, not merely green — which is the only reason to believe the zero.

`InstanceId` is a `u64` rather than a `u32` for a reason worth stating: at the
reference's 23,931 distinct instances a 32-bit content hash carries about a **6%**
birthday collision, and a collision here means two instances sharing one frame,
which the widened provenance gate reads as red. The cost of being wrong is a
false failure on a correct program.

### The donor rule was true and insufficient

The brief said: `argAt` is `unNote . unfix`, so it discards the argument's root
note and `desugarWithNote` wraps the result in the **`TypeParam`'s** note plus a
frame. That is correct, and a port can satisfy its wording and still be wrong.

When the substituted argument is a *wrapped* `TypeIdentifier` landing in
`TemplateInstance`-base, `ScopedName`-prefix or `TypeIdentifier` position,
`removeNestedTypeIdentifier` (`Desugar.hs:126-131`) then **discards the very node
that was wearing the `TypeParam`'s note**, and what survives at the site is the
argument's *child* — verbatim, unframed, wearing its own range. Oracle-pinned on
a `ttparam.k` fixture: the surviving `ScopedNameF "Box"` sits at offset 156 bare,
with the `TypeParam`'s note nowhere on the spine.

The general shape, which is now the third instance this week: **a rule about one
pass is only true up to what the next pass in the same walk deletes.** Same class
as `resolve` firing on shapes rather than sites, and as `moveFunctions`' deferral
arms protecting an interior rather than exempting a node.

### One oracle fact nobody would guess

Which of two name-colliding instances `deduplicateInstances` keeps is
**`Map.toList`'s structural order, not program order**. The reference kept
`(bool)->bool` over the first-written `(uint8)->uint8`, because `BooleanF` sorts
before `UnsignedF` in the derived `Ord`. This port takes the caller's list order
and books the difference: observable only in sibling order and in which member of
a collision survives, and no decided corpus instance collides today. It matters
the day one does, and it would be invisible until then.

### Three inert plants, reported as inert

Seventeen plants; three could not bite, and each is kept with its reason at the
site rather than deleted or dressed up as evidence:

* the `Typename` guard (`:113`) is redundant against a lookup that already
  answers `None` for a `Typename` declaration;
* `rewrite`'s third arm (prefix mangling) is **shadowed** — under a bottom-up
  walk the prefix node has already matched arm 2, and disabling it produces
  oracle-identical trees;
* a scope-walk plant cannot bite because every shared scope-bearing node
  reaching it is already `Donated` by the sorted lowering, so `replace` and
  `donate` coincide byte-for-byte today. It is kept as defence against a
  lowering that marks chain wrappers `Own`.

Three of this week's plants were inert and one was nearly reported as evidence.
The rule that caught all of them: **check that a counter moved, not that the
suite is green.**

## Print and reparse works, and the two costs nobody had priced

*2026-08-14. The decision that gates the rest of the frontend, taken by building
the cheaper option far enough to know. Scratch in
a scratch directory (not kept).*

> **The prototype is gone, and this line said otherwise for a week.** It claimed
> `crates/kg-db/src/proto_reparse_infer.rs` was "preserved in the worktree
> `agent-af796fa929e5d23b5`". It was never committed: the branch survives with
> no unique commits, the path is in no reachable commit, no dangling object
> holds it, and the worktree directory is deleted. Two agents went looking on
> 2026-08-14, independently, on a pointer I repeated to both — and a correction
> I sent ("read it with `git show <branch>:<path>`") was wrong for the same
> reason the original was. **A file is preserved when it is committed.** Every
> measurement below survives because it was written down here; the code that
> produced them did not.

Materialisation lands instantiated copies of template bodies into the IR, and
nothing can type them. That blocks `addLambdaWrappers`, `closureCalls`,
`deduceTemplateArgs`' rewrite half, pass 12's other four arms and pass 11 — and,
because the wired passes decline on `Ty::Undefined`, roughly **440 of the 551**
remaining `--strict` failures. Two routes: port the ~3,068-line inference engine
off `rowan` onto the IR, or **print the copy, reparse it, and infer it with the
engine that already exists**.

**Route (b) works, verified end to end against the oracle rather than argued.**
`lower_sorted` → decide `Holder<uint8>` → materialise → print → reparse → infer:
the copied member reads back `Ty::Unsigned(8)` and the copied body's `value + 1`
reads back `Ty::Unsigned(9)`, and the oracle holds `TUnsigned 8` and `TUnsigned 9`
on the same nodes. **The 9 is computed by inference over the copy** — the
`<|$uint@41|>` mechanism one size down, produced with zero engine code written.
Answers hang back on the materialised IR nodes under their own five-field keys,
so provenance never leaves the real `Src` chain.

The fixpoint closes too, and that was the other thing that could have killed it.
Round 2's decided set falls out of running the **existing census** over round 1's
*printed* output; the synthetic site maps back through the side map to the
materialised node; and round 2 then materialises **on the original arena**, with
real ranges and fresh frames. Re-printing every round costs about **1 ms per file
per round** against ~1.1 s of census and inference for the same set — twelve
rounds of printing the whole corpus is noise.

### The brief's foundation was wrong

I wrote that "the round trip proves `kg_hir::pretty` is a faithful IR→source
function at **403/403**". That number is over **`lower`**. Materialisation runs
on **`lower_sorted`**, where the same structural round trip is **188 of 394** as
shipped. `xtask/src/ir.rs:375-378` knew — "a sorted one prints materialised
qualifiers that do not reparse to themselves" — and I quoted the friendly number
at an agent as the ground the whole route stood on.

And the cost I named was the wrong one. The synthetic-range → original-`Src`
side map, which I called "precisely the mapping the journal proved does not
otherwise exist", is **~60 lines** and falls out of the lockstep walk wherever
the shapes agree. The two real costs were never mentioned by anyone:

* **No mangled or synthesized name lexes.** `struct Holder<|$uint@8|> {}` is 18
  parse errors; `$this` and `?lambda0` as identifiers both fail. `<|` never lexes
  at any length, so the 5,040-character question is moot. A **bijective rename
  layer is mandatory**, and because a `Ty` payload can name an instance, it needs
  a reverse substitution over `Ty` as well — bounded, ~100 lines, unprototyped.
* **The printer is deliberately lossy on sorted name forms.** A written `A::b`
  becomes a prefixed `ScopedName` that prints leaf-only. A ~45-line prototype
  patch took sorted fidelity **188 → 365/394** and materialised files from
  6/35 to 25/29, moving no graded gate. A real implementation should print source
  slices at `Own` heads rather than the prototype's heuristic.

### "Donated means synthesized" is false, and it is a live trap

Two guards were tried for the printer and both failed for instructive reasons.
Lexability fails because a sanitised `$` becomes lexable. And **`written == Own`
fails because divergence #24's demotion donates a *written* path's inner links
too** — `donate_inner_claims` marks them `Donated`, so an Own-guarded printer
suppressed every written prefix and reproduced exactly the 188/394 baseline.

#24's own entry is correct about the demotion and says nothing about this. Any
consumer that uses `written` to separate *written* from *invented* gets 0% of
written prefixes. Written down here because the next such consumer will not be
the printer.

### A decline class nobody had counted

`kg_db::instances` **declines every constexpr template argument**. `W<bitsizeof(uint8)>`
and `W<K>` at plain use sites in original source decide nothing, while the
reference decides `W<|@8|>` in **one** round. This caps the multi-round corpus
under **both** routes — `xoshiro.k`'s `<|$uint@41|>` needs the argument fold,
which is `evaluateConstexpr`'s half of `inferExpTree`. This journal's "Scale"
paragraph attributed the 49-of-23,931 gap to the closure machinery and the
postponement rule; it omitted this entirely.

It also decides the routes' relative cost. Under (b) the copy is real source, so
the existing `folded_int`/`ConstEval` machinery applies and the fix is a census
extension. Under (a) the fold must *also* be re-targeted from `ast::Expr` to the
IR — **a second engine port hiding inside the first**.

### The decision

**Route (b).** Not because it is less typing — ~800–1,200 new lines against
3,500–5,000 — but because it reuses the one inference engine whose behaviour the
conformance score already grades. Route (a) *forks* the engine: the CST engine
stays regardless, since it is what every keystroke query runs on, so (a) leaves
two engines that must agree forever, and every future inference fix lands twice
or drifts.

Order: (1) the **sorted** round trip as its own graded `xtask ir` line, with
exact qualifier printing — no heuristics; (2) the rename layer and `Ty`
back-translation, donor-tested; (3) read-back writing five-field keys, wired to
`deduceTemplateArgs`' rewrite half first, the largest strict-failure consumer;
(4) the census constexpr-argument fold, which is scheduled **regardless of
route** since 53% of roots need rounds it currently cannot produce.

What would change it: semantic rather than merely structural fidelity on the
wrapper-mismatch files. Grade type agreement against the oracle over the
shape-equal files before trusting readback there.

*One process note.* The prototype could not find route (b) proposed anywhere in
this repo — because it never was. It arrived in a survey agent's report, I acted
on it, and I never wrote it down. Six days of scheduling rested on a sentence
that existed only in a notification.

## The 109 that were never looked at, and a bucket that was a driver bug

*2026-08-14. Twenty percent of the number this project is sized against had never
been investigated. All 551 snippets, the raw oracle output and the classification
are in a scratch directory (not kept).*

The attribution sweep left 109 assertions in two residue buckets — "the oracle
rejects the snippet at parse time" (92) and "the reference reports nothing" (17).
They were produced as leftovers, not investigated, and I kept quoting 551 as the
completion criterion with a fifth of it opaque.

| bucket | count |
|---|---|
| parse-time name resolution (`Parser.hs` / `Parser/SymbolTable.hs` / `Parser/IO.hs`) | **61** |
| grammar rejection, several symbol-table-driven and surfacing through backtracking | **29** |
| doc-comment lexing, gated on `--parse-docs` | **10** |
| inside the reference's own string/format parser (`Parser.hs:900`) | **2** |
| warning channel (`Error.hs:94`), three promoted by `--Werror` | **7** |
| **sum** | **109** |

Group 1 in detail: const-lvalue 23, template-args-missing 7, ambiguous symbol 7,
import-qualifier conflict 7, type-as-expression 6, undefined symbol 4,
type-as-lvalue 2, redefinition 2, missing import file 2, undefined template 1.
Whole run: 102 + 7 + 442 = 551.

**The split was 102/7, not 92/17.** Ten `doc-comments` assertions were booked
"the reference reports nothing" because the sweep never passed `--parse-docs`.
Not one of the 17 is silent; the reference reports on all of them.

**551 stands. There is no downward correction, and that is structural rather
than lucky.** I had guessed some of these would turn out to be multi-fixture
accumulators — files that are not programs — and that the honest denominator
might be smaller. It cannot be: such a fixture fails as `expected:0`-got-an-error,
and the 551 are 547 "expected `Error 1`, compiled cleanly" plus 4 warning
assertions. **There is not one `expected:0` failure in the entire remainder**, so
no accumulator artefact can hide there. The "69 multi-fixture files" figure I
had in mind is both wrong (it is 73 of 73 under the harness's flags) and
irrelevant — `conformance.rs:250-278` resets the accumulator to the header at
every marker and never hands a whole file to a compiler.

**What is wrong is the attribution table, and it needs a twentieth owner it does
not have.** Parse-time name resolution is not any of the 19 passes. Of group 1's
61, **29 have a `validateProgram` twin** — `checkConstLValue` (`TypeCheck.hs:105-108`)
and the `isType` operand check (`:180-185`) produce identical messages — so pass
19 goes 194 → **223**. The other 32 exist *only* in the parser and symbol table,
and their port-side owner is `kg-resolve` plus the module graph.

**Only 2 of the 109 are genuinely out of reach**, and not permanently:
`interpolated-string::8` and `::13`, raised inside `format` at `Parser.hs:900`
(`expecting 'X','b','d','o','x'` is literally `choiceViaShow [Bin,Oct,Dec,Hex,HexUpper]`).
Both are blocked on the same lexer decision that gates pass 18 — a whole `"…"` is
one token.

### The bucket was partly a bug in our own instrument

`oracle/driver/Main.hs:141` discarded the reference's parse-error bundle and
printed the bare string `PARSE-ERROR`. That one line is why 102 assertions were
known only as an opaque bucket: the information existed, in the reference, and
our wrapper threw it away. Restoring it is two lines — `errorBundlePretty` was
already imported — and it now prints the marker followed by the bundle, so
anything matching the marker still works. Verified: nothing in `xtask`, `crates`
or `oracle` greps for it beyond documentation, and `xtask ir` still exits 0.

**The lesson is about instruments, not about this bucket.** The oracle is the
only thing here whose two sides do not share our lowering, and it had a lossy
path nobody had exercised. A survey that had simply *read* the driver would have
found it in a minute; five surveys ran against it first.

### Cheap work this exposes

* **`checkConstLValue` in pass 19 — up to 22 assertions, ~30 lines.** For an
  assignment whose LHS type `tIsConst`, error. Pass 6 runs before pass 19, so the
  types are there. 13 have a plain-name LHS and are near-certain; 9 have a
  member or array LHS and depend on whether `kg-ty` propagates `Ty::Const`
  through member access, which was not measured.
* **The `isType` operand check in pass 19 — 6 assertions**, already specified at
  `docs/spec/types.md:920-921`, `BitSizeof`/`ByteSizeof` exempt.
* **`--parse-docs` — 10 assertions, and a fifth "shipped with no caller".**
  `parse_docs` is plumbed through `kg-config` and both CLIs and **nothing in the
  parser reads it**. The rule is small (`Lexer.hs:76-88`) but it changes the
  trivia model of a lossless parser: a day, not an hour.

### Two counting traps, both live

The survey's own first sweep dropped the last option of every assertion, because
`Assertion::options.join("\n")` emits no trailing newline and a shell
`while read` loop silently swallows an unterminated final line. It turned an
import-qualifier conflict into a bogus "Can't find file". It moved no bucket
boundary — both are `PARSE-ERROR` — but it would have filed 10 assertions under
the wrong cause.

And the `note:`-inflation trap from the pass-11 sweep has a sibling:
`imports::63` prints **four** `path:line:col:` headers for **two** diagnostics,
because each is repeated inside an `In imported file:` wrapper
(`ExtendedError.ImportError`, `Error.hs:60`). Counting header lines overcounts
here exactly as counting `note:` blocks did there.

## `Own` is neither "synthesized" nor "rewritten", and a printer found out twice

*2026-08-14. `sorted trip: 403/403` from a baseline of 188/394, no heuristics, no
residue booked.*

The print-and-reparse route needs `kg_hir::pretty` faithful over `lower_sorted`,
where it started at **188 of 394**. It now reads **403/403** on the graded line,
and the gate is falsified rather than asserted: break the printer and it reads
193/403, names 210 files and exits 1.

The mechanism is what I proposed — print the source slice at the head of a node
the lowering made, leaf-only in member position. **The guard I proposed was
wrong, and wrong in the direction that would have poisoned the next step.**

`Rewriter::replace` hands a replacement the replaced node's `Src` **verbatim**
(`rewrite/mod.rs:101-104`), which is faithful — it is the reference's `renote`.
So a `resolve`-mangled mention wears the *written* occurrence's `Own`, ROOT head
while its leaf spells the mangled name, and an `Own`-guarded slice prints the
**unresolved** spelling back. The printer would have silently undone the rewrite.

The boundary that actually holds is `ModuleIr::lowered_len`: a fresh arena index
means rewrite-made, and it bounds the whole subtree. Measured — disabling the
`Own`, `via` and `file` clauses individually moves neither the corpus count nor
any test; disabling `lowered_len` turns the masking test red.

This matters beyond the printer, and immediately. The **rename layer is the next
step** and it rewrites names in place with `Src` kept verbatim. Without
`lowered_len` this printer would un-rename them on the way to the parser, and the
whole route would fail in a way no structural gate could see.

So `written == Own` has now been mistaken for two different things in two days:
"this node was synthesized" (refuted when divergence #24's demotion turned out to
donate *written* qualifier links) and "this node was rewritten" (refuted here).
It means **sole claimant of this `(range, kind)`**, which is what it has always
been defined as in `src.rs`, and both refutations were found by a consumer
building on the wrong reading rather than by anyone reading the definition.

### Two corrections to the shape of the fix

**`FunctionCall` needed slicing, not just name heads.** The const-function
substitution (`Parser.hs:776-777`) replaces a callee with the initializer's copy,
so the written callee name exists **nowhere** in the IR and its leaf re-sorts in
callee position to a bare `TypeParam`. Only the call's own slice closes it —
taken over a booking, because that cause names no unported pass and a booking
that cannot shrink is a suppressed failure.

**A slice must refuse when it would drop written text.** A method callee's head
is the `NAME_REF` alone, so slicing it drops a written `<…>` argument list — four
of the six residual files. The refusal fires when any `Own` descendant pokes
outside the range, and the structural fallback then has to restore the written
`template` keyword (`obj.template Go<uint32>()`) or an unresolved member's
instance collapses.

Both predicted residue classes — "member-position" and "wrapper-normalisation" —
closed exactly, so the line landed with nothing suppressed. The
donor-range-length heuristic that reached 365/394 was passed without a heuristic.

### Eleven plants, three inert, two that exposed pinning gaps

Three plants could not bite and are recorded as inert with the measurement: two
guard clauses subsumed by `lowered_len`, and a `TemplateInstance` arm whose only
outermost corpus occurrence prints identically either way.

Two more initially fired **nothing** — and that is the useful part. Removing the
`ScopedName` arm left the corpus at 403/403, because no corpus file reaches it;
it is pinned instead by the reference's delayed-error shape
(`Parser.hs:720-721`), and its test's doc says the test exists *because* the
corpus cannot. Removing the `NamedValue`/`QualifiedIdentifier` arm moved the
corpus 403 → 347 with **no test red at all** — a real gap, closed by adding a
value-position read before the plant was counted.

That is now nine inert plants across five slices this week. The rule that catches
them every time: **check that a counter moved, not that the suite is green.**

*One claim of mine refuted in passing:* threading file text into the printer does
not touch the `format` bench stage. That stage runs `kg_fmt::format_file`;
`kg_hir::pretty` is in **no** bench stage and its only caller is `xtask ir`.

## Pass 19's two parser twins, and what the written tree cannot know

*2026-08-14. `checkConstLValue` and the `isType` check landed in pass 19;
conformance 2055 → **2085**, strict 551 → **521**, all thirty movers attributed,
none regressed.*

The measurement the slice was gated on came back stronger than hoped:
`Ty::Const` propagates through member and array access for **22 of 22** corpus
assignment shapes — `tMember (TConst a)` re-wraps its hit (`Type.hs:940`) and
`tElementLValue (TConst a)` is `TConst $ tElement a` (`Type.hs:949`) — so the
"13 near-certain plus 9 unmeasured" split dissolved and the whole clause is one
`type_of(lhs).is_const()`.

Two survey claims did not survive contact:

* **The isType six are not operand-check shapes.** The journal said the 29 had
  a `validateProgram` twin in `checkConstLValue` plus "the isType operand check
  (`TypeCheck.hs:180-185`)". For the const 23 the twin is real. For the isType
  six, the reference rejects all of them in its *parser* — `expression` checks
  `isType` on every result (`Parser.hs:823-828`) — and the pass-19 operand
  check, which only visits `UnaryF`/`BinaryF`/`FanOutF`/`MuxF`/`ParamIntF`
  operands, reaches none of the six as written. What landed is both: the three
  `expression` positions the corpus pins (statement, `static assert`, array
  dimension) plus the literal operand set. That decided a *different* seven
  than the survey's six — `type-check::4,14,15,16` fell to the operand arms
  unasked; `higher-order-functions::54` and `template-argument-deduction::68`
  are declined (below).

* **`const-correctness::20` was mis-bucketed, in our favour.** The survey's
  const-lvalue class keyed on parse-error bundles and listed 0–19. `::20` — a
  `const` *member* on a non-const object — is invisible to the parser twin
  (the base symbol is not `Const`-declared) and is the one corpus assertion
  the reference reports from `checkConstLValue` itself, whole-lvalue spelling
  and all. Our clause produces the byte-identical message. 22 expected, 23
  landed.

**The recurring hazard has a name now: the reference type-checks the
*rewritten* tree, we check the *written* one.** Twice the 1,768 `expected:0`
assertions caught a faithful-looking port firing on legal code the reference
never sees at pass 19: `evaluateConstexpr` folds a *comparison of two types*
to a `BoolLiteral` by subtyping (`evalBinaryType`, `Constexpr.hs:245-251`) —
`library/base.k:52-55` compares `decltype`s to function types, 620 false
errors across the library — and `index_t<10> == uint4`
(`type-constexpr::38-41`) is a type on one side that our table leaves
`TUnresolved`. The landed rule fails toward silence: a type operand in a
comparison is reported only against a **literal** other side, the one shape
the corpus pins (`uint32 == 4`). Oracle runs, not reasoning, drew this line —
the same session's reasoning had first "corrected" the mux test to accept
`mux(1, uint32, 2)` on a fold theory the oracle refuted in one invocation:
mux *arguments* are each their own `expression`, so the parser rejects the
type before any fold can eat it.

Declined, with owners: `const-correctness::18` (`c.Foo(x)` — a method-call
receiver is parsed as an *lvalue*, `Parser.hs:732`; not an assignment);
`higher-order-functions::54` (`Do<uint32>` as argument — class-vs-function
template is `namedValue`'s symbol lookup, `Parser.hs:783-792`); both belong to
the parse-time symbol table port in `kg-resolve`, alongside the 32 the survey
already assigned there. `type-check::13` and `template-argument-deduction::68`
sit inside uninstantiated template bodies, which the reference's desugar never
reads (`Frontend.hs:298-299`) — only its parser rejects them, and a pass-19
port that fired there would invent a pass the reference does not have.

Falsification: seven plants, each confirmed by a counter that moved — the two
clause switches (5 unit reds + the 30 strict movers), plain-path-only scope
(member test red alone), exemption removal (`bitsizeof` accepts red), dropped
`TType` arm (alias red), comparison stand-down removal (4 accepts red), and an
unconditional-report plant that also turned two `navigate` tests red — the
invented-diagnostic failure mode, caught by tests that were not even mine.

## The census asks the fold, and the class the brief called total measured small

*2026-08-14, task #37. Scratch in a scratch directory (not kept).*

**Silence 2 is lifted by asking, not rewriting.** `constexprResolved`
(`Constexpr.hs:385-390`) accepts `W<bitsizeof(uint8)>` or `Foo<uint32, K>`
only because `evaluateConstexpr` (`Inference.hs:50`) rewrote the argument
first. Both readings of `templateResolved` — `instances.rs` over the IR,
`Cx::instance` over the CST — now ask `kg_db::fold::ArgFold`, which is
`ConstEval` over the same `FileScope` passes 6/16/19 fold with, plus one
widened question: `sizeOf = tWidth . typeOf` (`Type.hs:462`) answered from the
module's own `TypeTable`, because `FileScope` answers no type question. The
IR side reaches the CST expression through `Src::head`'s range, `Own` nodes
only. Keys, stamps and `validate`'s clauses all read the *folded* value —
`W<8>` and `W<bitsizeof(uint8)>` are one instance, `W2<K>` for `K = 300`
under `uint8` is `uint8:44`, and the subtyping clause's message shows the
folded literal's minimal type (oracle-pinned: `uint4` for a folded `8` under
a `bool` parameter).

Numbers: instances 233/26/49 → **233/28/53**, conformance 2085 → **2087**
(the two movers are `syntax::type-check::27` — `Foo<int<32>, 10==10>` — and
`::35` — `Foo<float32, -5>`, both expected-Error, both now rejected by
`validate` on a fold-resolved instance), strict 521 → **519**, differential
232 → 269 resolved instances with the two readings agreeing on all 403.

**The brief's framing — "declines every constexpr template argument" — was
true as a mechanism and misleading as a population.** Measured over all 480
corpus files, per-file rooted: the fold unlocks **4** distinct instances
(three `TestLimits` — negative and hex literal arguments, `UnaryF Neg` — and
`count_t<bytesizeof uint32>`, oracle-pinned `@4`). The remaining candidate
declines partition as: **122** `optional<decltype(…)>` sites — *not* this
class; `eval DecltypeF` is `expFromType . typeOf` (`Constexpr.hs:308-309`),
the type-dependent-rewrite class; **42** `index_t<qualified-or-imported
const>` sites — the fold class proper, blocked on `FileScope` being one file
(the whole-program `ConstEnv` seam `scope.rs` already documents); **12**
literal-argument tails (`factorial<5>`, `AddN<1>`, `FIFO<…>`) declined by
`t.resolved()` on nodes the table never typed — a minimal `factorial<5>`
fixture decides here and the oracle materialises `factorial<|@5|>`, so these
are table blind spots, not fold misses. Also small: arity 12 (the
`deduceTemplateArgs` rewrite), silence 4 × 35, silence 3 × 6.

**Do not lift `t.resolved()` for literals without the postponement analysis.**
The conjunct is doing two jobs: masking table blind spots (the tails above,
a real miss) and standing in for `inferExpTree`'s FunctionF postponement
(`Inference.hs:55-59` — a function with function-typed parameters keeps its
whole body `TUnresolved`, so the reference's round 1 does *not* decide
literal-argument instances written inside one). A literal bypass would decide
both. Separating them means porting the postponement predicate; until then
the tails stay booked.

**A fold-decided instance is not handed to `resolve`/`instantiate`.**
`DecidedInstance.folds` marks the positions whose reference subtree is the
folded value, and both `xtask ir` builders skip any instance carrying one:
the mangled bytes must come from the value (`W2<|@44|>`, `W<|@E@b|>`), and
`mangle_args`/`makeInstance` walk the written tree — a `Path` argument would
mangle as its *name*. Lifting the skip needs `DecidedSite` to carry the fold,
which is a `kg-hir` change deliberately left out of this slice. Also declined
on purpose: an aggregate-valued constant (`Foo<A>` for `const` struct/array
`A`) — its resolvedness in the reference comes from the `TemplateInstanceF`
arm's *splice* (`Constexpr.hs:133-151`), and deciding without the splice
silences `validate Auto InitializerListF{}` and mis-renders `validateType`.

One prior-session claim corrected on the way: the prototype
`proto_census_constexpr_arg_probe` was never committed — the branch survives
with zero unique commits, no dangling object holds the file — so its `bs.k`
measurement is unverifiable and was re-derived from scratch here.

## The boundary is observable: the ABI loaded, the reference recorded

*2026-09-17. Roadmap item 6, steps 1 and 2 of
[`ParseTree_Integration_And_Test.md`](history/ParseTree_Integration_And_Test.md);
`docs/spec/abi.md` is the contract every claim below cites.*

Two crates and a driver, in the order they were proven, and four
decisions the plan left open or got wrong.

**`kg-backend-sys` loads the library; it does not link it.** The plan and
§14.4 assume the reference's shape — the executable linked against
`libkanagawa-backend` and finding it by rpath. Linking would have made the
C++ build a build-time input of the workspace, on CI and on every machine
without it, behind a cargo feature nobody would enable. Instead bindgen's
dynamic-loading mode generates one function table (`KanagawaBackend`),
filled by `dlopen` of a path (`KG_BACKEND_DIR`, beside the executable,
or `../kanagawa-build/dist/bin`), and `ParseStages` — declared, never
defined, §1 — is an `Err` in that table rather than a load failure. The
workspace builds everywhere; only a `kg build` that runs needs the dylib.
`kg-abi-gen` is the one place that finds the headers and configures
bindgen, shared by the sys crate's `build.rs` and the interposer's, so the
two cannot describe different ABIs. One header does not parse as C:
`internal_tests.h` opens an *unguarded* `extern "C"`, so its one
declaration is restated in the wrapper.

**The spike passed on the first run that compiled.** `tests/smoke.rs`:
`InitCompiler` accepts a 520-byte `Options` we filled (§3.4's widths
pinned field by field, `--max-block-ram`'s `-1` reaching `size_t` as the
same two's complement the Haskell `poke` produces, the three never-written
fields and every padding run zeroed), hand-built nodes go in, and
`Codegen` on an empty root runs §12.3's whole-program sequence to
`ExtractDeviceConfig`, which reports Error 84 for a program with no
device module — the failure the spike was *for*, since it proves steps
1–5 of the sequence ran. bindgen requested layout tests and emitted none
for these headers; `tests/layout.rs` asserts every size and the offset
after each of §3.2's seven padding runs instead.

**The interposer sees depth 0 only, on macOS, and that is the region that
matters.** §5 and §14 design around backend-internal recursion reaching
the shim — true under ELF interposition, where every call through the
PLT resolves to the preloaded symbol. Mach-O's two-level namespace binds
the backend's calls to *its own* definitions, so the shim, installed by
rename-and-shim (the executable, the real library renamed `-real`, the
shim under the real name, in `target/ptrace/bin/`), records exactly what
the Haskell front end issued and nothing else: 4,679 calls for a
one-function file, every one at depth 0, `Codegen` last. The depth
counter stays for Linux. The forwarders are generated from bindgen's
output parsed with `syn`, type-directed as §14.3 tables it, with two
corrections to the table: a typedef'd enum arrives as `pub mod _Name`
plus `pub use _Name::Type as Name`, both spellings; and an unknown type
is still a build error, which is how the first build found that.

**The options line is fields, not a hash.** §14.1 hashes the 520 struct
bytes; the reference's bytes are not reproducible — `alloca`, three fields
never written, seven padding runs (§3.2) — so the hash would differ
between two runs of the same command. `#options` renders the fields by
name (`Debug` of the two inner structs, the strings, the file list) and
the call line says `<opts>`. Likewise `Location._valid` on the wire is
whatever the `alloca` held — `Types.hsc` pokes five fields — and
`SetLocation` forces it true (§6.1), so a differ must not read it.

**Traces are a cache, not fixtures.** The plan committed every root's
trace under `test/ptrace/`. Measured: one root is 216 KB, 40 KB gzipped,
and the syntax corpus alone is 2,922 programs — and the reason for
freezing (a rebuilt reference should show as a diff) is served by a
stamp: `target/ptrace/traces/STAMP` hashes the executable, the real
library and the shim, and a change clears the store. Each program is
keyed by its text and flags; `cargo xtask ptrace` replays hits and
records misses, the way `target/oracle-cache/` does for `kg-oracle`.

**The reference confirms the backend codes.** For every syntax assertion
the recorder runs the snippet exactly as `syntax-test.py` would — the
snippet alone, that test's effective flag list, a subfolder as working
directory — and keeps the process's output beside the trace. An
`expected:<n>` with `n ≠ 0` that the front end accepts is confirmed when
the reference's own run prints `Error <n>`: **99 of 99 in `basics.k`**,
which is the store becoming the ground truth `conformance` books as
undecidable. The first run said 20 of 153 and every miss named the wrong
snippet's error, because eight workers shared one
`syntax_test_temp_file.k` in one directory as the runner does; one
directory per assertion, and the numbers were the corpus's.

**An indeterminate `bool` looked like a data race.** The first whole-corpus
run had 50 programs whose trace ended mid-walk with a line like
`#options 00036040 0 SetLocation2 <opts> -> -` and a process killed by
SIGABRT, on files the unshimmed reference compiles cleanly. `SetLocation2`
rendering `<opts>` — a variant only an `Options` argument produces — and
earlier `SetLocation2 - -> -` lines meant the shim's own `Raw` enum was
being decoded as the wrong variant: `Location._valid` is a C `bool` the
reference never writes (`Types.hsc` pokes five fields of an `alloca`), so
the byte is stack garbage, and a Rust `bool` holding anything but 0 or 1 is
undefined behaviour that the niche-packed `Option<Location>` turned into
another variant, then a `String` that never existed was freed. The shim
reads that byte as a byte now. Whole corpus, second run: **3,270 programs,
2,422 walked, 0 crashed, 241 of 241 backend codes confirmed**, 666 s cold
(the library roots are large — `float32.k` alone is 252,000 calls — and
the store is 127 MB gzipped).

What this does not yet do: nothing on our side writes a trace. Step 3 —
the lowering from the twin's IR to the post-desugar tree §11.2 describes,
and a `Backend` trait whose first implementation writes this format — is
where the frontend's remaining gaps become counts, and it starts on the
roots the reference walks with no template in them.

## The walk exists, and 580 programs tell the backend exactly what the reference tells it

*2026-09-17, later. Roadmap item 6, step 3 of
[`ParseTree_Integration_And_Test.md`](history/ParseTree_Integration_And_Test.md):
`kg-ptbridge` and `cargo xtask ptdiff`.*

**The walk is `ParseTree.hs` arm for arm, and the rewrites are done on the
way out.** `kg-hir`'s `Exp` mirrors `ExpF` constructor for constructor, so
`parse` (`ParseTree.hs:63-175`) ports line by line, in `cataM` order —
children in `ExpF` field order, then `setSrcLocation`, the constructor,
`SetNodeType` for an integer or enum type (`:50-55`). What the reference's
passes had rewritten by then, this port answers as queries, so each is a
clause of the walk with its citation: templates deleted and nested
sequences spliced (`removeTemplate`, `Frontend.hs:298-302`), `auto` spelled
from the type table (`deduceAuto` and `expFromType`, `Type.hs:1595-1660`),
names unqualified or fully qualified (`resolveNames`, `redundantNameScope`,
`Frontend.hs:160-167,273-291`), every string token decoded and a hole-less
one a plain literal (`interpolatedStringPre`, `Parser.hs:886-893`),
constants folded by asking `kg-db`'s evaluator per expression
(`evaluateConstexpr`, through a public `ModuleFold` door), a constant's
enum or function initializer copied from the module that declares it with
its own notes (`Constexpr.hs:252-260`), a void `return f()` split into a
nested `Seq` nothing flattens (`returnVoid`, `Frontend.hs:293-296`), a true
`static assert` left as an empty list wearing its note (`staticAssert`,
`:393-398`, pass 16 — after pass 15's flattening), an enum constant's
missing value the previous one plus one (`reifyEnums`, `:195-208`),
`decltype` the operand's type spelled out (`Constexpr.hs:304-305`). The
`Backend` trait and its two implementations are generated from the headers
like the interposer's forwarders; `Trace` writes `kg-pttrace` lines with
ids minted in call order, and `ParseAppendList` and `ParseEnumValue` return
an argument rather than a new node — measured over the recorded corpus,
where a new id would have put every later id off by one.

**`ptdiff` is the instrument, and it ranks the work.** Three readings per
program — exact, structural (locations blind), first divergent call — and
two histograms: first divergences by `(theirs, ours)` function pair,
declines by reason. Each round of this session was: run it, dump the top
program's two traces, read twenty lines, port the clause, run it. Over the
276 `basics` programs the reference walks, the count went 0 → 231 → 233
structurally identical (base library included); over the corpus, 476 → 580
of 2,421. Conformance stayed 2489/2489 throughout.

**Pass 8's output is what the walk reads.** The route's rewritten IR was
never exposed — `Elaboration` held tables and twin parses, and the tree the
copies live in was dropped at the end of `elaborate_module`. It is kept now
(`RewrittenModule`): the last round's *renamed* IR, so the side map's pairs
still name its nodes; the walk spells a name through `renames.original_of`
and reads a minted node's type through its twin partner's key in the
synthetic file, where the read-back had refused it for being `Donated`. A
module the route never targets is walked through the syntactic rewrites
alone (`rewrite::pipeline`, which is where `moveFunctions`' `main@Bar`
names come from). This is what turned the `println<|$uint@32|>` copies from
the reference's into ours.

**Two things the differential caught in the frontend.** `kg_config`'s
`.options` module was built from the parser library's defaults
(`optimize = -1`), not the compiler's (`2`): every `const auto optimize`
deduced `int1` where the reference deduced `uint2`. The five backend options
now ride in `Settings::backend` and every driver sets them. And the
loader's `redundant_imports` calls `compiler.device.schema` redundant in
`hardware/config.k`, which uses `MemoryType::LUT` and
`MemoryInitFileType::Mem` from it — a false `redundant-import` warning no
conformance assertion happens to test, found because the reference wraps
its parser seed in a `Warning` per redundant import and the seed then
survives pass 15's flattening as an empty list in the trace. The seed is
implemented and disabled (`KG_PTBRIDGE_SEED`) until the loader's marking is
right; 155 programs wait on it.

**What the 1,626 first divergences are, ranked.** Foreign instances the
route cannot mint — a `Closure<…>` whose argument is a `$wrapper$` closure
type, landing in `data.closure.core` before `make_capture0` (502);
instances with a string-literal argument, `fmul32<|$stringliteralmock@3|>`
(158); the seed (155); copies missing or extra at a module's end and
instance names that differ (`BinaryOpsLiteral<|@32|>` against
`AndLiteral<|@0@32|>`, 400 between four rows); `parseInstanceType` before a
materialised class (53); a `TypeIdentifier`'s scope, which the reference
takes from the use site and this lowering from the declaration (43); and
three typing gaps in `kg-ty` worth their own rows — a `switch` selector
shadowed by a later `case` local (33), an explicit enum value under a doc
comment (35), a written type's use (32). Every one of these is a count that
falls when its row is done, and none is the walk's.

**Exact agreement is a separate campaign, and it is positions.** Of the 580
structural agreements, 0 are exact, and every first mismatch is a
`SetLocation2`: the reference's end position is the *next token's* start
(trivia included), a `module` name's span starts at the keyword, a
declaration's excludes its doc comment, a sorted name's minted segments all
wear the whole name's span, `FunctionModifier` and `ModuleDecl` have no
position at all (pattern-synonym constructors, `TH.hs:65`). Positions reach
the backend only as error locations, so structural agreement is what
`Codegen`'s output depends on; the exact reading is for the day the
backend's messages are compared.

## `kg build` compiles, and the backend grades the walk end to end

*2026-09-17, last. Step 5 of the plan: the real backend behind the
walk, and a gate that reads what it says.*

**Both binaries compile through `libkanagawa-backend`.** `kg build
--backend sv|none|trace` and the compat `kanagawa` — the frontend, then
`compile` (`ParseTree.hs:31-41`) through `kg-ptbridge`'s real
implementation, `Codegen` last, the backend writing to the process's
stdout as it does under the reference. A program the frontend rejects
never reaches `InitCompiler`; a program the walk declines exits 1 with the
node kind named on stderr — loud, so upstream's runner counts it; a backend
error is the backend's own line and exit 1. On the three programs tried by
hand — a clean one, a recursion (Error 37), an assignment to a string
(Error 77) — the output is the reference's to the byte, file names
included now that they are canonical as `Parser/IO.hs:105` makes them.
With no backend on the machine (`KG_BACKEND_DIR=none` pins that for the
tests) the compat binary is the frontend-only run it was.

**`cargo xtask backend` is the end-to-end reading.** For every recorded
program it spawns our `kanagawa` with the reference's exact flags in the
same directory and compares what `syntax-test.py` reads — the first
`Error N` on stdout and the exit code — with the reference's recorded run.
One process per program, because `InitCompiler` is once per process
(§12.1). Numbers, first run: **3,270 programs; 1,621 agree; of the 2,422
the reference walked, the backend says the same about 912.** The rest:
1,312 declined by the walk (the `ptdiff` classes, as they were), 161 where
both sides reached the backend and it answered differently — 55 of them
`Error 5` and 48 `Error 32` on programs the reference compiles, the walk
having emitted something the reference did not — 51 frontend
disagreements (`errors`' territory), and **125 crashes**: a C++ exception
thrown out of a `Parse*` call, which `Rust cannot catch` and aborts on. The
reference never sees those because it never makes those calls; they are
divergent walks feeding the backend what it asserts on (`safe_cast` in
`SetNodeType`, §6.2), and each one is a `ptdiff` divergence first.

**`repoint` fell from 25 to 15, and that is the honest direction.** The
frontend-only binary exited 0 on every program it could not lower, which
upstream's runner read as passing every `expected:0` assertion. Now a
declined walk exits 1 and the runner stops the file there. The number to
watch is `backend`'s 912, per assertion; `repoint` is per file and will
climb back as the declines fall. The CI ratchet sits at 57 failing files,
exactly where it is.

**What the first `kg build` of an exported design needs.** No structurally
exact program in the corpus exports a class, so nothing has produced a
`.sv` yet: the exported designs are whole files under `test/` whose import
closure holds the instances the route still declines (`base.k`'s, first
of all — `file::library/base/system.k` declines at one). That is the same
work list as before, read from the other end.

## An abbreviated function is a template, a hole is a name, and the seed was never the walk's

*2026-09-17, night. Roadmap item 6, the first three rows of `ptdiff`'s work
list read from the other end: `ptdiff` 580 → 721 structural, `backend`
912 → 948 of 2,422; conformance, strict, errors and the tests unchanged.*

**The top three rows were one mechanism, and it was the frontend's.** The
example under `ParseFunctionModifier / ParseNamespace` was a `println(s[1])`
whose `debug/print.k` module the walk emitted *empty* where the reference
walks a `println<|$string|>` copy. `kg dump twin` on the snippet said "no
module was elaborated": `declares_a_template` looked for written `template`
declarations and `inline void println(auto x)` is not one until
`abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` runs (`Function.hs:288-308`, sub-pass 7 of
`Template.hs:71-81`). Three ports, each a clause the reference already had:

* the route elaborates a module that declares an abbreviated function
  (top level or a class member), and phase 1 indexes the synthesized
  template off a fork `rewrite::abbreviated_function_template` alone has
  touched — the pass is **not idempotent** (the leftover it keeps beside the
  template is still abbreviated, and a second application mints a second
  template), so the fork is for the index and `handed` gets the one
  application `pipeline_tail` always made;
* the deducing pass's rewrite half deduces a call to an abbreviated
  function as the reference does after the rewrite — one `typename x$T`
  per `auto` parameter, in `autoParams`' order, bound whole by
  `Deduction::bind_typename` (clause 15, `Type.hs:1572-1573`) because the
  lossless CST still says `auto` and `deduceType _ TAuto = return ()`
  binds nothing from it. The diagnostic half asks for nothing new: its
  arity verdict (`Cx::deduce_abbreviated_call`) was already the base run's
  whole report, and `with_deduction` takes a flag so the two halves cannot
  drift;
* `decomposeInstance` (`Type.hs:1454-1456`): the parser wraps a callee in
  `TemplateInstance … (Seq [])` only when the symbol *is* a template
  (`Parser.hs:669-674,694`), so an abbreviated function's callee reaches
  `deduce_rewrite` bare, and the rewrite mints the instance at the
  identifier's own note instead of filling one. Found by the same-file
  probe materialising nothing while the cross-module one worked — the
  foreign path never needed the callee node.

Probed against `kg-oracle --errors` before the tests were written: a
conversion inside `Pa(auto x)`'s body, called with a `uint32`, is reported
at the body with the call as its `while compiling` note, in one file and
across an import. Two tests in `elaborate.rs` pin both.

**A hole is a name, and the walk parses that much.** The next decline was
`interpolation hole` (36 → 68 once every `println` copy walked, since its
body is `__print("{x}\n")`). The lexer keeps a whole `"…"` as one token
(divergence #15), so the walk had declined every string with a hole. A

children of `InterpolatedStringF`); each is `NamedVariable
(ScopedIdentifier (BaseList (Identifier x)))` as `resolveNames` leaves a

**The seed was never the walk's, and enabling it moved 140 programs.** The

**What the histogram says now.** String-literal template arguments

* **The twin fold.** `fold:int<N>` (119) was mostly `uint<(N > 1) ?

## The copies the reference makes, and in its order

*2026-09-18 and 19. Roadmap item 6, `ptdiff`'s work list read top down:
`ptdiff` 890 → 1065 structural, `backend` 1114 → 1315 of 2,422;
conformance 2489 → 2491, strict 116 → 114, `errors` 552 → 553 agree at
the same 24; three commits.*

**`resolveNames` reads the tree it walks.** The 148-program row
(`@helper@return_type_polymorphism` then `Fn_T<|$bool|>`, where the walk
spelled the bare copy) was `postDesugar symbols` (`Frontend.hs:63`): the
list runs bottom-up, so the map is taken after `instantiateTemplates` and
`removeTemplate` — a copy is declared in it, a template is not — and a
function is spelled with its declaring scope wherever it is called. The
walk asked the program's item map, which has no copies. `post_symbols` is
`getSymbols''` over every module's walked IR in program order, keys in
original names; the not-found hack for names inside copies went with it.
`ptdiff` moved 4, `backend` 46 — a copy called unqualified from inside
another copy is a call to nothing, and the backend said so.

**A folded argument is the literal it folds to.** The census has recorded
`folds` since 2026-08-13 and every consumer skipped an instance that had
one: `hal::fmul32<config::hal_device_family, 3>` in the device library
(164 programs, every one that reaches `hardware.dsp`) and
`T1<x>` over `const auto x = lutmul(2, 3)` (82). `evaluateConstexpr`
rewrote those arguments before `decidedInstances` keyed them
(`Inference.hs:50`), so `canonical_args` now mints each folded position as
its literal before `resolve` and `instantiate` read the list, and the
five "no folds" filters became one `materialisable`. A string mints as the
hole-less token `interpolatedStringPre` would have made a `StringLiteralF`
of, which needed the mangler's `$stringliteral` arm (`Mangle.hs:57`) and
`tArg`'s `TStrArg` — both "declined, zero reachable" since August, and
reachable the day the census let a string through — and the text
unmanglers to read one back (`fmul32<mock, 3>`). The string's end is the
next `@` or `$`; the mangle has no terminator, and a string holding either
is misread. The corpus's are device family names.

**`static for` unrolls in the copies.** `literal-operand.k`'s
`BinaryOpsLiteral<N>` loops `static for (const auto x : 32)` over
`AndLiteral<x, N>()`; the reference unrolls a loop whose variable reaches
a constant position into one `$xN` scope per iteration
(`Constexpr.hs:48-121`) and decides 128 more copies from the literals.
Ported as `kg_hir::rewrite::static_for`, run by `static_control` after
each round's `instantiate`. Five things had to move with it, each found by
the next divergence rather than by reading:

* the fold environment could not see an iteration's index — `scope_at`
  was the enclosing declaration's key, blind to blocks — so it now replays
  the scope stack's qualifier off the item tree, as pass 9 does; and the
  twin's fold had been using the *base* module's environment over the
  twin's text, coherent only while nothing looked a local up by offset;
* `validateArg` rewrites a literal argument before the instance is keyed
  (`TypeCheck.hs:280-284`), so a folded `0u5` under `auto x` is `0` —
  `0u5 - 16` does not type as `0 - 16`;
* copies came out in the census's *string* key order, `@10` before `@2`;
  `Map.toList` orders by `ExpF`'s derived `Ord`, which `kg_hir::order`
  ports (the enum mirrors `ExpF` constructor for constructor, so the index
  is the declaration order; a `Name` compares as its string —
  `Hashed`'s `Ord` ignores the hash, hashable-1.5.1.0). One test encoded
  the old order and was corrected against the oracle;
* the dispatch's `static if (N > 0 && ((N - 1) & N) == 0)` needs
  arithmetic to decide. The first cut folded arithmetic and muxes *in
  place* and `xtask ir`'s type agreement caught it: the reference types a
  node before it folds it, and a `const auto` over `TestDiscard ? N / 4 :
  N` keeps the mux's supertype. Only comparisons of literals fold in
  place now; a predicate or a limit is asked for its value
  (`static_value`, over `evalBinary`'s table lifted out of kg-const as
  `fold_binary_values`). A negative result never folds in place either:
  the printer spells `-10`, the twin reparses a unary minus, and the side
  map pairs by constructor — `template-instance-identifiers.k::37` went
  silent until that was found by bisection;
* rounds after the first rewrite the *reparsed* twin, and the printer
  cannot spell `$x0` or `DeclareUninitConst`; `restore_decorations`
  carries every block path and declaration flag back from the previous
  round through the side map.

And one frontend verdict the unroll made reachable: pass 16's `clog2`
check fired inside the mux case `index_t<0>`'s selector does not take
(`uint<(0 > 1) ? clog2(0) : 1>`, `static-for.k::16`); `evaluateConstexpr`
deletes that case first (`Constexpr.hs:311-315`).

**What moved and what did not.** `literal-operand` went from its fourth
call divergence to agreeing past call 13,000; its remaining program
diverges on an abbreviated template row. Not kept, and recorded: a
non-dependent loop stays a `StaticFor` rather than becoming the
`UnrolledFor` the reference makes — the walk emits both as
`ParseUnrolledFor` and an `UnrolledFor` cut the twin's side map at the
loop (`deduce: Unresolved` 26 → 39 before it was reverted).

**Left, measured.** `xtask ir`'s type agreement reads 29/32 over 3,587
types (30/32 over 3,379 before): `memory<exp2m1_row, 512>` in
`numeric/float32.k` — a foreign alias copy the fold work now makes — reads
back as its concrete `const [[memory]] exp2m1_row[512]` where the
reference holds it inside `TInstance … ["@data@memory","memory"]`. The
backend reads integer types only, so the walk does not see it. The work
list now: the closure machinery (522, next entry), an abbreviated
template that is also written (85), copies of different templates in the
reference's order at a module's end (83), `TypeIdentifier`'s use-site
scope (72), `kg-ty`'s `switch` selector (47).
