## A captured lambda is its closure copy, and every round rewrites our own tree

*2026-09-19. Three commits: the `Closure` copy, `closureCalls`, and the
round redesign. `ptdiff` 1065 → 1107 structural, `backend` 1315 → 1332 of
2,422 (2044 of 3,270 overall); conformance 2491 → 2492, strict 114 → 113,
`errors` 553 → 554 agree at the same 24 disagreements.*

**The `Closure` copy is made in the round the lambda is desugared.**
`desugarLambdas` writes `cast<Closure<decltype(f), f, C>>(make_captureN(…))`
and the reference decides that `data.closure.core::Closure` instance in the
same round; the census postponed it, because `decltype(f)` of a *function*
bound nothing (`named_type_at` took only types). Three pieces: a function's
type travels as a `Type` shape and `canonical_args` evaluates a `decltype`
argument to it (`Constexpr.hs:304-305`); `mint_ty` spells an
attribute-free function type (`expFromType`, `Type.hs:1632`); and the
resolved mention, which prints as the copy's alias and which the twin
would type as the capture struct the alias's body names, is told apart by
`closure_leaves` — the twin's import view hears that the alias *is* the
closure, with the instance as its face (`infer AliasF`,
`Type.hs:1175-1177`), so deduction still reads its three arguments.

**`closureCalls` reads types, so it runs a round late.** `Do(x)` on a
copy's `Closure<…>` parameter becomes `f(cast<Capture>(Do), x)`
(`Closure.hs:19-26`), which needs `Do`'s type — only a twin has it. The
reference's order agrees: the copy is made at a round's end and the
sub-pass list runs at the next one's start (`Template.hs:77`). The round
gate stays open while such a call is pending (`closure_calls::pending`).

**Later rounds rewrite our tree, not the reparse.** Until today, round
two and on censused a twin and then rewrote *that twin's* IR, and a
`restore_decorations` step carried back what the printer could not spell
— block paths, declaration flags. It could not carry back a hoisted
lambda's qualified capture type, an iteration's frame, or a node's own
position, and each of those surfaced as a round that decided nothing or a
diagnostic that went home to the wrong place. Now every round rewrites
`Round::ours`, the tree the twin was printed from, and translates each
twin range the census and the deduction read into that tree's
coordinates (`TwinSites`: the twin node at the range, its side-map
partner, the partner's head *and* frame). What fell out:

* one shared `ExpansionInterner` for all rounds, so a frame minted in round
  two means the same in round four; `carry_home` runs once, over the last
  round, with no range translation down through the rounds —
  `home_range` and `translate_down` went;
* a `Site` is `(head, via)`, and an unrolled `static for` iteration is a
  frame of its own (`ExpansionData::iteration`, which `copy_frames` hides,
  since the reference notes no frame for an iteration) — without it the
  128 `AndLiteral<x, N>()` mentions in `literal-operand.k` were one site;
* of the several twin nodes at one range the `TemplateInstance` is asked
  first, then a `ScopedName`: a copy's substituted argument at the same
  range names the template's node, not the copy's (`callbacks.k::41`).

**A site is still not a node.** A donated head is shared: `desugarLambdas`
mints `make_capture1(y)` and the hoisted function's mention in the
`Closure<decltype(f), f, C>` beside it under the capture list's one
range. The deduction of `make_capture1<uint32>` then rewrote *both*, and
round three carried `__kg_m0<|$uint@32|>` — the lambda, instantiated with
the capture's argument — so the `Closure` never resolved and
`a_captured_lambda_is_its_closure` went silent. A deduction is a call's,
so `deduce_rewrite` now rewrites a callee only; `resolve` already fires
only on a `TemplateInstance`. The rule for any new rewrite over
`Round::ours`: key by site, then check the node is the kind the decision
is about.

**Carrying at a refused pair: one direction only.** A refused pair's
roots stand at the same position, but the two trees disagree about the
node, and the twin's verdict there may be its own misreading —
`C<typename T::Foo>` prints `Foo`, which the reparse reads as a value
that pass 9 finds undeclared (`template.k::40`). The other direction is no
misreading: `makeCapture`'s `NamedValue` of a captured type alias
(`Function.hs:146-157`) is typed as its name, `TType t` (`Type.hs:1240`),
exactly what the reparse's `TypeIdentifier` is typed. So `carry_home`
admits a refused root when ours is a `NamedValue` and the twin a
`TypeIdentifier`, and nothing else (`lambdas.k::22`). The same refused
roots count as minted for the twin's parser-rule exemption, so that the
capture is judged by the argument check, not as "Invalid use of a type as
an expression" (`Parser.hs:823-828`), which the reference's parser never
sees there.

**A frame from another module is not a frame of this twin.** The base run
reports pass 12's LT verdict with a `while compiling` at the template's
declaration — read off a *helper's* twin, `RewrittenModule::homes` maps it
back. The importing module's twin reported the same verdict, unframed,
and its copy is seeded ahead of the base run's, so the dedup kept the
unframed one and `Db::frontend_diagnostics`' merge let it replace the
base's. Three changes: `carry_home` counts a diagnostic as framed only by
a label in its own twin and passes a foreign label through; the dedup
keeps the framed copy of two identical reports (`passes::dedup_reports`);
and only a framed carried diagnostic displaces the base's identical one,
a seam one yields. `a_closure_parameter_left_unbound_is_the_lt_verdict`
goes red with either of the last two cut.

**The bench, interleaved.** Keystroke on `wide_to_narrow.k` reads 447 and
454 ms against 542 and 543 for the tree before the redesign, run
alternately on one machine. Rewriting our own tree does less than
rewriting a reparse plus restoring its decorations. Both are above the
390 ms `status.md` recorded before the closure work; the rounds the
`Closure` copies open are the likely cost, unmeasured.

**Left.** The top `ptdiff` row is still the closure machinery (342, down
from 399): the reference's walk opens `data.closure.core` with its
`Closure` copies, and ours has none there. In
`return-type-polymorphism::16` the copy is over
`main@$wrapper$@data@optional$is_valid<|$uint@32|>` — the wrapper
`addLambdaWrappers` makes for `Go(is_valid<uint32>, 10)`'s function
argument — whose round-by-round path through our route is not yet
traced. Then `same_types`'s `$fun`
attributes in a mangle (201), an abbreviated template that is also written
(88 + 85), `TypeIdentifier`'s use-site scope (66), `kg-ty`'s shadow and
`switch` rows (48).

## Two gates wrote into the reference, and a root read twice

*2026-09-19, same night. `backend` 1332 → 1347 of 2,422 (2044 → 2059
overall), 123 → 109 backend disagreements; `ptdiff` unchanged.*

**`../kanagawa/` had 163 files it should not have.** `git -C ../kanagawa
status` lists 163 untracked `*PathLength.pdrpt` reports under `test/`,
one of them 33 MB. A compile that reaches `Codegen` writes its reports
into the working directory (`kanagawa.cpp:145-158`), and both `xtask
ptrace` (running the reference) and `xtask backend` (running ours) ran a
whole-file program in the file's own directory. 157 are from the
2026-09-17 recording; 6 are from tonight's `backend` run, which is how it
was found. Nothing tracked was modified. The fix is in the program list
both gates share: a whole-file program now runs in
`target/ptrace/work/file/<its directory>/` and names its file by absolute
path. Re-recorded, the reference's trace for
`test/interface/another_exported_class.k` is byte-identical below the
header and its report lands under `target/`. The key hashes the
argument, so a `ptrace` run re-records the 348 whole-file programs once;
`risc-v.k` alone takes over twenty minutes in the reference. The stray
reports are left in place: the reference tree is read-only to this work,
cleanup included. `git -C ../kanagawa clean -n -- '*.pdrpt'` lists them.

**The compat binary read `library/base/system.k` twice.** `kanagawa
system.k`, run in `library/base` as the reference's runner runs it, took
the root as `system.k` and `base.k`'s import of `base.system` as
`/…/library/base/system.k`: two `FileId`s, two modules, and the backend's
"Duplicate function: @base@system::cycles". `ptdiff` could not see it —
it joins the working directory and the argument, so its walk always had
one absolute path. The reference knows every file by `canonicalizePath`
of where it was found (`Parser/IO.hs:104`), roots and imports alike, so
the legacy CLI now canonicalizes the roots it reads and the import
directories it hands the loader. The VFS stays lexical on purpose (its
doc comment: ids must not change when a file appears or disappears under
a long-lived server). The modern `kg` CLI still keys a root by its
spelling, which is how it prints paths relative to the shell; `kg build
system.k` in `library/base` would read the file twice the same way.
Recorded in `gaps.md`, not fixed: canonical identity with relative
display is a renderer change of its own.

## A generic lambda's `Closure` copy, and one copy is one type

*2026-09-19, same night. `ptdiff` 1107 → 1114 structural; the closure
row 342 → 332. Every other gate unchanged: conformance 2492, strict 113,
`errors` 554/63/24, `backend` 1347, `xtask ir` as before.*

The reference makes every `Closure` copy in `data.closure.core`, and a
generic lambda's too: `kg-oracle --typed` on `lambdas.k::2` holds the
copy's instance as `[("FunctionType", TTypeArg (TFunction … TAuto
[TStruct …, TAuto])), ("fn", TNameArg TTemplate ["Go@?lambda0"]),
("Capture", …)]`. Ours made none, for three reasons in a row, each found
by `KG_ELAB_TRACE` (which now also prints what each program pass hands
an owner, and every shape an owner declines to mint):

* the twin's symbol map poisoned the hoisted function's name, which
  `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` declares twice — the template and the
  function it keeps (`Function.hs:288-291`). The reference's
  `HashMap.fromList . reverse` keeps the first of a key (`Symbols.hs:42`):
  the template. `passes::types::insert_function` keeps a template a
  function declaration follows; every other duplicate is still poisoned;
* the census took a function-name argument only when its type was a
  resolved function. A name typed `TTemplate` is now a function shape when
  it names a top-level *function* template. The first cut took any
  template and minted `memory` — an alias template given to a
  template-template parameter — as a function; `T3<16, memory>` then said
  "Type name not in scope" in four programs;
* the owner could not spell `auto`: `expFromType TAuto = Just AutoF`
  (`Type.hs:1615`) is now `mint_type`'s first arm.

Making the copy exposed two more differences:

**A generic closure is a closure.** `infer AliasF` reads only the
instance's three arguments (`Type.hs:1175-1177`), so the copy is a
`TClosure` whatever its function. The reference's recorded walk of
`closures.k::28` has `Go<|$uint@4@…Capture@main@?lambda0|>` and
`main@?lambda0<|$uint@4|>`. The test that pinned that program's clean
compile said "unresolved", which was the right answer for the wrong
reason; it is renamed and re-documented, same expectation. A guard that
kept a generic closure untyped turned that into "Could not deduce all
arguments" in eight programs, which is how it was found out.

**One copy is one type.** `Go(uint32 -> uint32 Do, …)` given `[](auto x)
-> uint32 {…}`: the formal's `Closure<(C, uint32) -> uint32, f, C>` and
the argument's `Closure<(C, auto) -> uint32, f, C>` are one copy in the
reference (the function type mangles to nothing, `Mangle.hs:42-43`), and
every mention is typed from that copy's note, so the conversion is `s ==
t`. Each of our twins types its own mention from its own instance, so
kg-ty's clause 19 now says so directly: same function, same capture,
same copy (`higher-order-functions.k::35`).

**Which of two colliding instances is the copy.** The same collision
decides the copy's *display*: the lambda's `-> uint7` in the reference,
the formal's `-> auto` in ours (`return-type-polymorphism.k::23`, which
this change broke before it fixed it). The reference decides the lambda's
instance in round one and the formal's, inside `Go`'s copy, in round two,
and `deduplicateInstances` keeps the first sibling. An owner here is
handed both at once, so `InstanceSpec::round` carries the reference's
round (one more per copy frame the mention stands in, `Template.hs:86-90`)
and `instantiate` orders by round, then by argument. Tests:
`closure_copy_tests`, both red under their named mutation.

## A wrapper copies what was written

*2026-09-19, same night. `ptdiff` still 1114 structural, and 191 programs
diverge later than before, none earlier (a per-program diff of `--verbose`
runs): most of the closure row's programs now agree through their wrapper
copies and stop at a copy the next piece makes. Every other gate
unchanged.*

`addLambdaWrappers` reads no type for a function: `wrap q` looks the name
up (with templates left out of the map, `Template.hs:79-80`) and, for a
`Function`, copies the declaration's written parameters and return type
into the lambda (`Function.hs:389-390`). Ours asked the type table, which
types an abbreviated function nothing, so the helper's `compose2(increment,
add)` in the 133 `higher-order-functions.k` programs was never wrapped.
`Wrap::written_signature` now reads the declaration where the table has
no function type: each written parameter type as its declaring module's
table reads it, `auto` as `auto`. (A function *modifier* is not an
attribute: `inline` declined every candidate until that was separated.)

Three spellings followed, each read off the reference's recorded walk and
`kg-oracle --typed` (a namespaced fixture, `scratchpad/wr/`: `TNameArg
TTemplate ["@h", "$wrapper$inc"]`):

* a wrapper hoisted to a namespaced module's top level is that
  namespace's — `@@helper@higher_order_functions@$wrapper$…`. The census
  now qualifies a bare function name declared at the module's top level
  with the module's namespace (`getQualifiedName`);
* but the wrapper's own *name* uses the mention as the parser left it:
  `makeQualified` rewrites an import's name to its declaration's
  qualified name (`Parser.hs:687`) and leaves a local one alone, so one
  call makes `$wrapper$@numeric@int@operator$increment` and `$wrapper$add`;
* the instance's display reads the producer's `TNameArg` (the reference's
  qualified name) rather than the minted alias, whose `.ns::name`
  spelling is for the mangler alone.

Test: `a_wrapped_abbreviated_function_is_its_modules_and_its_written_
signature`, red under each of the three mutations it names.

## The list runs every round

*2026-09-19, same night. conformance 2492 → 2493, strict 113 → 112,
`errors` 554 → 555 agree (62 silent, 24 disagreements), `backend` 1347 →
1352 of 2,422; `ptdiff` 1114 structural. `xtask ir`'s type agreement now
reads the reference at two iterations: 29/33.*

The reference applies pass 8's whole list to the whole program every
round (`Template.hs:37-81`, `foldr` over wrappers, lambdas, abbreviated
templates, `moveFunctions`, …). Ours ran it once, before round one. Three
pieces of the per-round list landed, each found by following
`higher-order-functions.k::1` one divergence further:

* **A round that typed a closure opens the next.** `compose2(increment,

*re-exports* (`data.function` reaches `data.closure.core` through
`data.closure`), which `leaf_spellable` refuses. It takes
`higher-order-functions.k::1` from call 41 to 51 — `compose2`'s lambda's
`Closure` copy is made — and falsely rejects 185 programs. The copies it
lets a module spell by their alias are typed as their capture struct in
importing twins, which needs `infer AliasF` for every importer (the
`closure_copy_names` of the entry above, re-tried here), and the closure
types then disagree on spelling one copy's function — `[@ns, name]` in
one reading, the single alias `mint_shape` mints for `.ns::name` in the
other — so clause 19 compares `last()` of different shapes. That
normalisation is the next piece before the widening can land; neither is
in the tree.

**A size folds in the type fixpoint, as the reference's does.** `ptdiff`
1119 → 1213 structural, `backend` 1372 → 1472 of the walked (crashes 111 →
88), conformance 2493 → 2494, strict 112 → 111; `errors` and `ir`
unchanged. Four pieces, one program's worth (`helper/constexpr.k`, whose
module every `constexpr.k` assertion imports, and which was declined
outright before):

* `evaluateConstexpr` is a `cata` (`Inference.hs:47-50`): by the time a
  `BinaryF` reads `typeResolved a && typeResolved b` (`Constexpr.hs:172`)
  a compound operand has already been folded. The literal it became wears
  the folded node's note — `bitsizeof`'s is `TUnresolved`
  (`Type.hs:749-750`) — so the reference folds the node above a round
  later, once `inferIntLiteralType` has typed it; the fixpoint reaches the
  same literal either way. `eval_binary` now folds first and counts an
  operand that folded to a value as resolved, and only a compound one: a
  written literal or a name is the node it was, and the environment's
  answer for it stands (`folding_stops_while_a_type_is_unresolved` holds).
  So `T3<bitsizeof S2 == bitsizeof S1 + bitsizeof bool>` (`constexpr.k:26`)
  decides.
* The type table's own fold (`Declarations::folded_value`) could read no
  width: its environment is the file scope, whose `bit_width_of` is `None`,
  so `int<16 - bitsizeof(S1_t) - …>` — S3's last field — stayed
  `TUnresolved`, and S3 with it. The reference types it the round `S1_t` is
  typed. A round here cannot read the table it is writing, so each rebuild
  hands `Declarations` the widths its predecessor's table holds for the
  file's `bitsizeof`/`bytesizeof` operands (`fold::KnownWidths`). One
  round later than the reference, and the same fixed point: a round that
  changes nothing hands the next one the same widths, and the loop stops
  there either way. `bytesizeof(S3)` is `2`.
* `folded_literal_type` types a folded expression as its literal only when
  every leaf is untyped — a `PATH` that folds to an untyped constant — and
  `bitsizeof S3`'s one leaf is a struct. A `bitsizeof` folds to
  `untypedIntLiteral` whatever its operand (`Constexpr.hs:271-275`), so its
  subtree now counts as one untyped leaf, and `const auto S3_size =
  bitsizeof S3` is `const uint5` where the walk declined `deduce:
  Unresolved`.
* `withUnmangledName` asks an alias's *type* (`ParseTree.hs:64,177-178`):
  `using C_t = C<2>` hands the backend `"C<2>"`. The table types the
  mention as the copy's own class (`Class([@helper@constexpr, C<|@2|>])`)
  where the reference holds the `TInstance`; nothing but an instance
  reaches a copy, so the copy's mangled leaf spells it.

The first piece alone took `ptdiff`'s declines from 225 to 127 and the
backend's **crashes from 111 to 269**: 157 `constexpr.k` programs whose
import had been declined now walked, and `helper/constexpr.k` handed the
backend an unfolded `ParseSizeOf` where the reference has `2` — a segfault,
not a verdict. The rest of the list closed that, but it also named a class
of crash: a number the backend reads as a number (an array dimension, an
integer attribute) that the fold here missed. `max_threads(C_t::x)` over an
import (`constexpr.k::126`, the fold is one file wide) and a non-`const`
member as a dimension (`constexpr.k::166`, which the reference's frontend
rejects and ours does not) both segfaulted. The walk now declines either
(`fold:attribute`, `fold:array dimension`) — the reference never hands the
backend anything but a literal there. Every crash the first piece added is
gone, and 23 older ones with it.

A procedural trap, written down because it cost a wrong reading: the
mutation script restored each file with `mv` from a copy made *before* the
mutation, which carries the older mtime, and cargo then kept the mutated
build — every mutation after the first ran over its predecessor's. Touch
the restored file.

**A re-exported namespace is spellable, and a `Closure` copy is its
closure to every module.** `ptdiff` unchanged at 1213 structural, but 143
programs now diverge later than they did and none earlier — 128 of them
`higher-order-functions.k`, from call 41 to 51: `compose2`'s own lambda's
`Closure` copy is made, with the reference's name. Conformance, strict,
`errors`, `ir` and `backend` (1472) unchanged. The re-export widening
tried and backed out on 2026-09-19 lands, with the three things it was
waiting on:

* `leaf_spellable` counts a namespace an unaliased import *re-exposes*
  (`visibleSymbols` is `exposed ∪ reExposed ∪ diffs`, `SymbolTable.hs:
  148`). `data.function` imports nothing; the base library's `module
  data.closure` re-exposes `data.closure.core`, two hops, and the
  reference reaches it by qualified names the parser wrote. Alone this
  falsely rejects 189 programs — the two below close all of them.
* `infer AliasF`'s closure arm (`Type.hs:1175-1177`): an alias whose own
  note is a `Closure` instance is `TType (TClosure fn FunctionType
  Capture)`, for every module that names it. Our twins typed a spelled
  copy as the capture struct it aliases, so `twice`'s copy's capture of
  a closure parameter was "Invalid conversion from `Closure<…>` to
  `…::Capture`". The instantiate report now lists each `Closure` copy
  with its note (`closure_copies`), the twin's environment carries them
  by the print's spelling (`Imports::with_closures`), and kg-ty's alias
  arm types such an alias as the closure, the note's instance as its face.
  Two instances can make one copy — a function type mangles to nothing —
  and the note kept is the first, the copy `deduplicateInstances` keeps;
  keeping the last displayed `-> auto` for `-> uint7` and cost eight
  structural programs (`return-type-polymorphism.k::23`) until it was
  turned around.
* One closure, one function path. A function handed to a copy's owner is
  minted as an alias for `.ns::name` (the mangler's spelling); a closure
  read over that alias named the function `[alias]` where the deciding
  twin's reading says `[@ns, leaf]`, and clause 19 compares by leaf. The
  pool now records the path an alias for a qualified spelling denotes
  (`RenamePool::alias_qualified`, its leaf the twins' own spelling), and
  `closure_leaves` names the function by it. And a function the deciding
  module's own route hoisted — `$wrapper$inc`, in no item tree — named
  bare by a deduction is its module's namespace's, the rule
  `function_named_at` already applies to a written argument
  (`qualified_own`); the owner had minted `…@$wrapper$inc…` where the
  reference has `…@@h@$wrapper$inc…`.

qualified alias in kg-ty's `closure_instance` too (a `SymbolEnv` hook),

**A copy that became a template is deduced again.** `ptdiff` 1258 →

`template <typename T> inline T Fn_T_auto(auto x)` is a template whose
function is abbreviated too. `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` leaves a
template alone (`Function.hs:310`), so round one binds `T` from the
declared type and makes `Fn_T_auto<|$bool|>` — a plain function with an
`auto` parameter, which the next round's `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate`
makes a template, and whose call the next round's `deduceTemplateArgs`
deduces again: `Fn_T_auto<|$bool|><|$bool|>`. Three things were missing:

* the calling module had no second round: nothing it wrote mentioned a
  template by the round gate's reckoning. `calls_a_templated_copy` asks
  whether it calls a copy some twin now holds as a template;
* `resolve`'s `names_template` compared the mention's base, unaliased,
  against the template's dotted leaf as written — for a template that is
  itself a copy, the print's alias. Both by name now;
* the display: the reference's walk names the second copy by its first
  instance, `"Fn_T_auto<bool>"` — the first round's note is the one the
  declaration keeps — so `unmangled` reads the name through its first
  mangle only (`first_instance`). `return-type-polymorphism.k::7`'s
  `"reinterpret_cast<bool><uint4>"` row (24) is this display too.
