## A captured `this` is a reference, and pass 6 runs before pass 8

*2026-09-19, later. `ptdiff` 1356 → 1382 structural; `backend` 1669 →
1709 of 2,422 walked (2385 → 2425 overall), backend disagreements 76 →
58, crashes 89 → 89, declines 663 → 641; conformance, strict, `errors`,
`repoint` and `ir` unchanged. Tests 1538 → 1546.*

Four pieces, each found by following a `this-capture.k` program one
divergence further. None is large; the measurement lesson at the end is
the part worth reading twice.

**A captured `this` is `Foo&` all the way through.** A lambda in a
member function captures `this` (`captureThis`), and its capture is
`make_capture1<Foo&>`, made in `data.closure`. Three things stood in the
way. The twin prints `ThisF` as `this`, which the table typed nothing:
the reference types it through `$this` (`Type.hs:1269`), and so does
`infer_path` now. The owner minted the reference as its class wrapped in
`Exp::Reference` — but Kanagawa has no written reference type, so the
printer spelled `Foo`, the copy's field was typed `Foo`, and every read of
it a copy of the object: the backend said "Can't implicitly convert Foo&
to Foo". The reference is now minted whole as one alias whose import-view
type is `Foo&` (`mint_ty`), the walk spells it back as `ParseReference`
(`minted_leaf_type`), and the mangler reads an alias ending `&` as
`$ref` ahead of its class (`make_capture1<|$ref@Foo|>`, not `@Foo&`).
Test: `a_captured_this_makes_its_capture` (walk), red with the
reference minted as its class or mangled by its text.

**Frontend pass 6's `staticControl`, before pass 8.** `inferType` runs
`staticControl` at every node (`Type/Inference.hs:50`), and it is pass 6
(`Frontend.hs:69`; the list runs bottom-up) — so `static if (true)` in a
class is gone before pass 8's `desugarLambdas` hoists a lambda that calls
the member declared under it, and `moveFunctions`' `memberAccess` makes
that call `$this.Do()` (`this-capture.k::17`). Ours decided the `static
if` only in the round's `static_control`, after the hoist, and the call
stayed a bare `Do()` in a free function. `static_control_before_templates`
walks the tree as `inferExpTree'` does (`Inference.hs:51-70`): a lambda,
a template's body, a function with a function-typed or `auto` parameter
or in a local scope, and an undecided `static if`'s branches all wait; a
local class gets `staticControl` alone, no fold. It needed
`removeNestedScope` (`Constexpr.hs:358-370`), which the port had never
done: a decided branch's declarations kept their `$quasiN` scope segment,
so `lookupSymbol` from the class could not find `Do`. Both
`static_control`s share it now (`static_eval`). Tests:
`the_pass_six_static_control_postpones_what_it_cannot_type`,
`a_decided_branch_leaves_its_scope_behind` (kg-hir),
`a_member_under_a_decided_static_if_is_called_through_this` (walk), red
with the pass skipped, any postponement dropped, a local class folded, or
the scope left.

The walk still splices a `static if` the IR left standing without
`removeNestedScope` — the `ParseNamedType … ["$quasi0"]`, `ParseTypedef`
and `ParseDeclare` rows (~48 programs) are that, and predate this.

**A member function given to a higher-order function is wrapped.**
`addLambdaWrappers`' member arms (`Function.hs:389-396,406-418`) had been
declined since the wrappers landed: `Foo(f)` with `f` a member function,
or a class variable of function type (`kindFromFlag DeclareClass =
MemberFunction`), is a wrapper that captures `this` and calls
`$this.f(…)`. Five things made it work end to end (`this-capture.k::9`):

* What the name declares is looked up from the argument's scope over the
  module's own tree (`kg_hir::rewrite::Declarations`, the body-local map
  `moveFunctions` already had), and the signature read off the
  declaration — a mention inside a lambda is typed by no table yet.
* The name is the mention as pass 1 left it: the parser qualifies a
  member mention (`makeQualified`, `Parser.hs:687`) and
  `redundantNameScope` (`Frontend.hs:160-167`) takes the qualifier off
  again, so `$wrapper$f`, not `$wrapper$C$f`. The IR keeps the written
  chain (the walk drops it at emission), so the wrapper asks
  `Declarations::redundant_qualifier`.
* A hoisted lambda's `this` — the wrapper's capture, `make_capture1(this)`
  inside `C@Run@?lambda0` — is its `$this` local (`Type.hs:1271`, the
  second arm), which the twin spells by an alias: `Imports::with_this_alias`
  hands the alias to `this_type`. And the walk emits it as that local
  (`thisReference`, `Frontend.hs:453-456`): `ParseThis` there is the
  global class to the backend.
* A deduced plan is matched to its callee by name as well as by site:
  every wrapper node wears its argument's note, so the call inside the
  wrapper shared its range with `make_capture1(this)` and was rewritten
  `$this.f<C&>()`. Both names are compared unaliased — a later round's
  plan names the twin's spelling (`__kg_m7`), and without that
  `Fn_T_auto(false)` lost its copy.
* No call inside an `extern` class is wrapped: pass 7 has emptied its
  functions (`trimExternClasses`, `Frontend.hs:315-333`) before pass 8
  begins, and a class nested in one keeps its own (`trim ClassF{} =
  Nothing`). The walk trims the body; the wrapper had already made copies
  nothing called (`extern-class.k::53`, "Class/Memory local variables are
  not supported").

Tests: `a_member_function_argument_is_wrapped_capturing_this` (kg-db),
red with the arm declined, the qualifier kept, the extern class wrapped
or the nested one trimmed; `a_this_in_a_hoisted_lambda_is_its_this_local`
(walk), red with any of the five undone.

What does not work yet: a class *template*'s member (`this-capture.k::18`).
The reference wraps it the round the class is copied, before the lambda
leaves the copy; our `round_prefix` hoists in the same round as the copy
is made, so by the next round's wrappers the mention is `$this.callback`,
a member access. Porting the `MemberAccess` arm would not help — its name
would be `$wrapper$Foo<…>$callback`, which the reference never makes.

**A call of a template the route left undeduced declines.** Walking a
call whose callee is a plain name that only a function template declares
— nothing in the post-`removeTemplate` map — hands the backend a call to
a function nothing defines ("Undefined function: Go"). The reference
never gets there: it names an instance or reports the call. The walk
declines when such a call is given something callable (a function, a
closure, a template's name) or something the table left unresolved. It
fires on 32 programs: 20 are backend disagreements without it, the other
12 decline further on anyway, and agreement is 2425 with it and without
(measured both ways). The first cut — "the callee is typed `TTemplate`" — declined
90 programs, 40 of them agreeing: a callee's table type is the template's
even where the call reaches an instance. The second — "absent from the
post map" — still caught `println`, a template the backend knows by its
own name.

**Measure the backend with the backend's binary.** `cargo xtask backend`
runs the compat binary (`target/release/kanagawa`); `cargo xtask` builds
only xtask. A `git stash` baseline that rebuilt nothing but xtask graded
HEAD with the working tree's binary and printed identical numbers for
both — which read as "the change does nothing". `cargo build --release
-p kg-cli` on each side, every time. `backend --verbose` now lists every
declined program too, so two runs diff program by program.

**A `static if` the walk splices leaves its scope behind.** `ptdiff` 1382
→ 1387 structural; `backend` 1709 → 1711, disagreements 58 → 56
(`static-if.k::71,73`). The walk decides a `static if` the IR left
standing — one only the typed fold decides — and splices its branch, and
it had never done `removeNestedScope`'s renaming: every scope under the
branch kept its `$quasiN`, which the backend reads consistently enough to
accept most programs and which `ptdiff` saw as ~48 first divergences. A
stack of spliced branches now takes that segment out of every scope the
walk emits, innermost first (an inner branch's scope still holds the
outer's segment, as the reference's does when the outer is decided
first), and a type's name chain through the branch loses the `$quasiN`
link (`main::$::$quasi0::Foo` is `main::$::Foo`, `static-if.k::14` —
with the scope stripped and the chain not, the backend said "Class/Memory
local variables are not supported"). The second chain arm and a value's
chain were written too and moved no program, and no probe could pin them;
they were taken out again and the comment says so. The `post` map the
walk resolves names against is still keyed with `$quasiN` — a function
declared under a spliced branch and spelled with its declaring scope
would show it. Test: `a_spliced_static_if_leaves_its_scope_behind`, red
with the scope or the chain link kept.

**A class callback's attributes are its function type's, and an alias is
spelled out.** `ptdiff` 1387 → 1429 structural; `backend` 1711 → 1716 of
2,422 walked (2427 → 2435 overall), disagreements 56 → 50, frontend 57 →
55; conformance 2496 → 2499, strict 109 → 106 (`callbacks.k::58-60`).
Found following `callbacks.k::0`, which the histogram filed under copy
order and is nothing of the kind: 44 programs import `helper.callbacks`
and all stopped in its class `D`.

* `callback_uint32_to_uint32_t callback1;` in a class: pass 19's
  `checkVarDecl` rewrites a class variable of function type written as a
  name to the function type itself — "middle-end doesn't handle function
  type aliases, convert to explicit function type" (`TypeCheck.hs:141-142`)
  — and `expFromType` notes each parameter with its own type, which
  `ParseTree` hands the backend as a node type (`Type.hs:1655`,
  `ParseTree.hs:53-54`). The walk does both (`aliased_callback`,
  `type_expression`).
* `[[async, max_threads(2)]] () -> void callback3;`: the reference parses
  a class variable's own attributes as `[[name(…)]]` alone and every other
  variable's as nothing (`Parser.hs:460-464`), so a `[[…]]` before a
  function type fails that `try` and is `functionType`'s (`:551`). Our
  parser hangs it on the `VAR_DECL`, and both readers took it from there:
  the lowering gave it to the variable, and `kg-ty` typed the callback
  with no attributes at all — which is why assigning an `[[async]]`
  function to it was not the error the corpus expects. Both now read the
  declaration's list as the type's (`Lower::fn_type_attrs`,
  `declaration_attr_lists`), a `[[name(…)]]`-only list excepted. Note
  `show Rename = "name"` (`Parser/Syntax.hs:142`): the attribute is not
  spelled `rename`.

Tests: `a_callbacks_leading_attributes_are_its_function_types` (kg-hir
and kg-ty), red with the list left on the declaration or a `[[name]]`
moved; `a_callback_through_an_alias_is_its_function_type` (walk), red
with the alias walked as a name or the parameter's node type unset.

**An attributed function type is an argument, and a copy's instance is
its note.** `ptdiff` 1429 → 1466 structural; `backend` 1716 walked
unchanged, 2435 → 2436 overall, frontend 55 → 54; conformance 2499 →
2500, strict 106 → 105, `errors` 557 → 558 agree (60 → 59 silent). The
second-largest row (135, `type-constexpr.k::16`): `same_types<[[max_threads
(2), thread_rate(1)]] (uint3 x) -> void, …>`, a class template in a helper
given attributed function types.

* The census booked the argument `Opaque` — `named_type_at` let a
  function type through only without attributes, because `mint_ty` could
  not spell them. `mint_attributes` is `expFromTAttr` (`Type.hs:1662-1668`):
  a flag is itself, an integer attribute its literal, in `Set.toList`
  order; `[[ecc(f)]]`'s function name is still not minted, and declines.
  The copy is checked now, which is the assertion that moved.
* The copy's `ParseClass` carries `parseInstanceType (theType expr)`
  (`ParseTree.hs:237-253`): the template's qualified name and one
  `ParseTemplateArg` per parameter — a struct, enum or union by its name,
  an integer type by its width, a literal by itself, anything else NULL.
  The walk read the arguments back off the mangled name, which has no
  terminator for a `$fun` argument; it reads the note `setTypeOfInstance`
  wrote at the copy's root now (`typed_instance`, as `declared_type` does).
  With the note read the mangle-reading path moved no program in 2,422 —
  measured with it and without — and was deleted with `unmangle_args`,
  its one caller gone.

Test: `a_copy_over_an_attributed_function_type_carries_its_instance`
(walk, the template in a helper so the owner mints), red with the
argument opaque to the census, with its attribute unminted, or with the
instance read off the mangle.

**A `static for` is unrolled in a module with no template.** `ptdiff`
1466 → 1467 structural (declines 132 → 141); `backend` 1716 → 1719
walked (2436 → 2439 overall), crashes 89 → 80; conformance, strict and
`errors` unchanged. The `$quasi1` group of the missing-copy row
(`static-for.k::0-3`): the reference unrolls a `static for` whose body
needs its variable as a constant at pass 6 — `$quasi1`, then `$i0`, `$i1`,
each declaring `const i = N` (`Constexpr.hs:48-121`) — but the route only
ran for a module that declares or uses a template, so a plain `main` with
a loop was walked as written. A module that writes a `static for` is
routed now (`writes_a_static_for`), pass 6's pass is handed the module's
expansion interner so each iteration stands under its own frame, and a
literal no table typed — the iteration's `IntLiteralF Nothing i` — is
typed by its value (`inferIntLiteralType`, `Type.hs:485-491`).

What does not work yet: the iterations have no twin partner, so the first
fold inside one (`uint32[i+1]`'s dimension) declines. Nine programs that
crashed the backend on the loop walked as written now decline there, and
three agree. Keeping the no-twin early return from skipping these modules
moved nothing, and was left out.

Test: `a_dependent_static_for_is_unrolled_without_a_template`, red with
the module unrouted or the literal untyped.

**A deduced call takes its template's defaults.** `ptdiff` 1467 → 1469
structural; `backend` 1719 → 1721 walked (2439 → 2441 overall);
conformance, strict and `errors` unchanged. `substituteDefault`
(`Type.hs:1422-1428`) had been written off as low value (three programs);
it is not. `FIFO`'s body calls `first(atomically<pointer_t>(increment))`,
and `atomically` is `template <typename T, T InitialValue = {}>` — the
deduction left `InitialValue` empty, declined the call, and every program
using a FIFO stopped short of the `atomically`, `pair`, `tuple2` and
`first` copies the reference makes (37 programs reach an `atomically`
copy). Library defaults are everywhere: `fifo`, `counter`, `memory`,
`buffer`, `lock`.

The reference splices the default's tree into the argument list and pass
6 folds it before anything is keyed. This port mints arguments from
values, so `crate::defaults` *evaluates* the default with the arguments
before it bound by name — `kg-const`'s evaluator over an environment that
answers only the bound parameters (`bitsizeof T` of a bound type
included). What folds: literals, `{}`, an earlier parameter, a built-in
type, `int<e>`/`uint<e>`, constant arithmetic. A name outside the
parameters (`opt::max_threads_limit`), an alias template (`index_t<N>`)
or another instance (`S1<T>`) does not, and the call declines as before.

Two guards, both found the hard way:

* A default fills an empty slot only where the deduction was
  **informed** — every type it read decided. `Foo(make_optional(true,
  100))` over `template <typename T = uint1> Foo(optional<T>)` binds `T =
  uint7` once the argument is typed; filling `uint1` early invented
  "Invalid conversion" on an `expected:0` snippet
  (`template-argument-deduction-from-instance.k::11`).
* …or where no formal and no return type **mentions** the parameter, so no
  deduction could ever bind it — `InitialValue`. `first(atomically(…))`
  is uninformed (its context, another template's argument, types
  nothing), and without this the FIFO calls never deduced.

A `bool` or `{}` default has no `TArg`; it rides beside its argument
(`DeducedCall::values`) and is minted from the value (`{}` is the empty
list, mangled `@`), handed to a foreign owner as a value shape in phase 1
and in a twin round alike.

What does not land yet: the FIFO chain needs more program passes than the
four the loop allows — `fifo` hands `atomically` at pass 2, `sync.atomic`
makes it and hands `pair` at 3, `data.tuple` would make `tuple2` at 4.
Eight passes make the copies (measured) and move no program to structural
yet, at 1.55× on `wide_to_narrow.k`'s check; the bound stays at four until
the next divergence on that chain (`pair<uint5, uint5>`'s display name) is
fixed and the passes can be measured paying for themselves. Defaults on a
*type* mention (`C1<uint32>`, `S1<>`) are the other half, not started: the
census postpones any mention with fewer arguments than parameters.

Tests: `a_default_folds_over_the_parameters_before_it` (the evaluator),
`a_default_template_argument_fills_a_deduced_call` (own template, foreign
in phase 1, foreign from a copy's twin), red with defaults unread, read
only where informed, or a value default handed on as a `TArg`; the
informed guard is conformance's.

**A type mention takes its template's defaults too.** `ptdiff` 1469 →
1476 structural; `backend` 1721 → 1731 walked (2441 → 2451 overall);
conformance, strict and `errors` unchanged. The other half of
`substituteDefault`: `deduceInstance'`'s type-mention arm
(`Type.hs:1440-1444`) completes `C1<uint32>` to `C1<uint32, 32, 64>` and
`S1<>` to `S1<uint32, bool>` at pass 4, before any census. The census here
postpones such a mention forever (`templateArgsResolved` compares lengths),
so the route rewrites the mention's argument list — the written arguments
kept, each default minted after them from what `crate::defaults` evaluates
— and the next round's census over the twin decides it, a round later than
the reference and the same instance.

Three seams, each found by a program that stopped one step short:

* A module whose census only *postponed* a mention was no route target:
  `main.k` with `static C1<uint32> c1;` declares nothing. The postponed
  sites' modules are targets now.
* A module with nothing materialised and nothing renamed returns before
  its twin is built, and a module that decided nothing and writes no
  lambda returns before printing one. Both now ask whether a default was
  filled — the twin is what decides the mention.
* A copy's own mentions — `C1<T>` in a class template's body — have their
  arguments only once the copy is made, so round one fills them again
  after `instantiate`. The same fill over *later* rounds' copies moved no
  program in 2,422 and cost three backend agreements, so it was taken out
  again and the comment says so.

Test: `a_type_mention_is_completed_with_its_defaults` — `C1<uint32>` and
`S1<>` from a `main` that declares nothing, and `C1<T>` inside a copy —
red with the fill off, the module unrouted, or either early exit taken.

**An alias template's copy is named after itself.** `ptdiff` 1476
structural unchanged (the `ParseTypedef / ParseTypedef` row 13 → 7, those
programs diverging later); `backend` unchanged. `withUnmangledName` asks
`theType expr` first and `typeOf expr` second (`ParseTree.hs:177-179`).
The `Alias` arm asked the second first, so `using Pair = Tuple2<T1, T2>`'s
copy was handed `Tuple2<bool, uint4>` — the instance it aliases — where
the reference hands `Pair<bool, uint4>`, the note `setTypeOfInstance`
wrote at the copy. The declaration's own name answers that (it *is* the
copy's mangle), and the aliased type stays the fallback for an alias that
is no copy: `using C_t = C<2>` names `C<2>` as before.

Test: `an_alias_templates_copy_is_named_after_itself`, red with the order
swapped — and the two older alias tests stay green, which is what pins
the fallback.

**A deduction reads a copy's arguments through the twin's alias.**
`ptdiff` 1476 → 1484 structural; `backend` 1731 → 1739 walked (2451 →
2459 overall); conformance, strict and `errors` unchanged. The 69-program
`ParseFunctionModifier / ParseNamespace` row, led by
`return-type-polymorphism.k::13`: `Foo(Fn_optional_T_U(10))` where `Foo`
takes an `optional<uint32>`. The call's context type is stamped onto the
callee (`setTypeOfTemplateCall`'s third site, `Type.hs:1153-1158`, ported),
and `T` is deduced from it against the declared `optional<T>` — the
reference matching `TInstance`'s arguments, this port reading them off the
copy's mangled name, which is what its table holds instead
(`mangled_instance`, 2026-09-17). In a twin that name is an alias:
`@data@optional::__kg_m0`, and the mangle is in the original. The
deduction takes the twin's aliases now (`Deduction::with_originals`,
`Templates::original_of`), and 8 programs walk to the end of the copy the
reference makes.

Test: `a_deduction_reads_a_copys_arguments_through_the_twins_alias`, red
with the alias read as the copy's name.

**A narrowing argument is typed twice.** `ptdiff` 1484 → 1527 structural
— the largest single move since the walk began — `backend` 1739 walked
unchanged; conformance, strict and `errors` unchanged. The 80-program
`ParseUintType / ParseBaseList` row, 48 of them `higher-order-functions`:
the reference walks `Do(x + 1)` and stamps the argument's node type
*twice*, ours once. Not a type disagreement — the same `uint33` both
times — but a node the reference's tree has and ours does not.

`checkArguments` wraps an argument its parameter can convert from but
does not accept as a subtype in a `Warning` (`warningNarrowingConversions`,
`TypeCheck.hs:97,101,176-177`), and a `Warning`'s own parse is its child's
(`Warning _ _ a -> return a`, `ParseTree.hs:173`) — so `parseWithLoc`
stamps the same node again, with the wrapper's type, which is the
argument's. This port reports that warning as a *diagnostic* and has no
node for it, so the walk emits the second stamp itself, on the same rule.
The callee's type comes from the callee, not the specifier: pass 8
synthesizes the specifier and no table types it.

That the backend's verdicts did not move is the point: a repeated
`SetNodeType` of the same type changes nothing downstream, and 43 programs
now walk past it to whatever is next.

Test: `a_narrowing_argument_is_typed_twice`, red without the second stamp
and red with one on every argument. The `[[pipelined]]` first-argument
skip (`:92-93`) is kept for fidelity though no corpus call reaches it
(measured).

**A local function's body is typed in the twin.** `ptdiff` 1527 → 1535
structural; `backend` 1739 → 1744 walked, 2459 → 2464 overall, 80 → 77
crashes, 51 disagreements unchanged; `repoint` 22 → 23; conformance,
strict and `errors` unchanged. The 54-program `ParseUintType /
ParseNamedVariable` row, led by `shadow-warning.k::12`:

```kanagawa
inline void main() { uint32 x; inline void Bar() { uint32 x; x = 0; } x = 0; }
```

The reference stamps three node types inside `Bar` that ours omitted
entirely — the scoped identifier, the named variable and the literal. Not
a disagreement about a type: we had *no* type there. A probe over the two
bodies printed `Unresolved` for everything inside the nested function and
the right types for everything outside it.

That is `inferExpTree'`, and it is ours too: a function declared in a
local scope is postponed (`Inference.hs:58-62`, `isLocalScope`), because
`moveFunctions` will hoist it to `main@Bar` (`Function.hs:39`) and it is
typed *there*, as a top-level declaration. The hoist is pass 8's, which
here is the route's — and a module of this shape declared no template,
used none, wrote no lambda, so it never got a route at all and nothing in
`Bar` was ever typed.

So a module that writes a local function is a reason for a twin, the same
way `static for` became one: `writes_a_local_function` joins
`declares_a_template`, **and** the no-twin early exit — the first guard
returns before anything is printed, so the gate is needed in both places
or the route stops one line short of the point. That second half is the
whole of the fix's effect; with only the first, `shadow-warning::12` did
not move a single call.

Test: `a_local_functions_body_is_typed`, red with either gate blinded.

**A member is found through the twin's alias.** `ptdiff` 1535 unchanged;
`backend` 2464 agreements unchanged, disagreements 51 → 49, declined 624 →
626 — two invented `Error 5`s became silence; conformance, strict, `errors`
and `repoint` unchanged.

`callbacks.k::63` gives a class *template*'s callback field to a
higher-order function:

```kanagawa
template <typename T> class Foo { () -> void Do; inline void Run() { Go(Do); } }
```

The reference wraps `Do` as a member (`kindFromFlag DeclareClass =
MemberFunction`, `Function.hs:395`): `$wrapper$Do`, capturing `this`, over
`make_capture1<Foo<bool>&>`. Ours wrapped it as a *free* function named
`$wrapper$Foo<|$bool|>$Do` with no capture — because in the copy the
mention is spelled through the alias the twin can parse, `__kg_m3::Do`,
and `Declarations::lookup` is keyed by the names the declarations carry
(`Foo<|$bool|>::Do`). Told nothing, `wrap q` fell through to its free arm,
which qualifies the name it cannot shorten.

So a lookup now reads a name through the renames — the raw key first, the
unaliased key after — and `redundant_qualifier` compares the unaliased
written qualifier, which is how the copy's `__kg_m3::Do` is recognised as
the qualifier `redundantNameScope` drops at pass 1. The wrapper's *body*
takes that trimming too: the reference's call is `$this.Do(…)`, never
`$this.Foo<|$bool|>::Do(…)`.

What this does not finish: the capture. The wrapper is now built in the
copy and needs `make_capture1<Foo<|$bool|>&>`, a capture of a reference to
a copy, which the route does not materialise — so the round makes no
progress, the next round rebuilds the copy from the template (whose field
is untyped inside an uninstantiated template, so its own wrap declines),
and the wrapper is lost. The walk then declines rather than handing the
backend a wrong tree, which is the whole of the measured change. The
template's own arm wants the *written* type of a member variable, as
`getSymbols'` records it, and this port has no reader for one yet — that
is the next step on the `this-capture.k::18` row.

Test: `a_declaration_is_found_through_a_twins_alias`, red with the aliases
unread on either side.

**A `static for`'s iterations are instantiated apart.** `ptdiff` 1535 →
1547 structural, declines 141 → 133; `backend` 1744 → 1758 walked, 2464 →
2478 overall, 77 → 73 crashes, 626 → 616 declined, 49 disagreements
unchanged; `repoint` 23 → 24; conformance 2500/2500, strict 105 and
`errors` 24 unchanged.

`literal-operand.k::0` is eight instances written once:

```kanagawa
static for (const auto x : 8) { BinaryOpsLiteral<x - 4>(); }
```

The reference makes eight copies; this port made none. Not the unroll —
that landed on 2026-09-19 and the route's tree has all eight iterations,
each with its own `const uint2 x = <literal>`. The census is what cannot
see them: `decided` restricts a `static for` to its limit
(`Template.hs:106`), so the loop's *body* decides nothing, the module
reaches the route with no spec, and both no-twin guards returned before
anything was printed. The copies are decided a round later, by the census
over a twin in which each iteration's `x` is a written `const` — which is
the round that never ran.

So a module this route unrolled is printed even when round one decided and
materialised nothing. The flag is read once (`unrolled`) and both guards
test it; either one alone leaves the program where it was, which is why
the guard added to the second alone on 2026-09-19 measured inert and was
removed. Round one's twin carries the unrolled body, round two's census
keys `Lit<|@-2|>` … `Lit<|@1|>`, and the walk hands the backend the copies
it was missing.

Test: `a_static_fors_iterations_are_instantiated_apart`, red with either
guard returning for an unrolled module.

**Three rows measured and not landed.** Each was diagnosed to the line and
each is written down here rather than left in the tree, because the
diagnosis is the expensive half.

*A class template's callback field.* `callbacks.k::63`'s wrapper is built
in the copy and lost when the next round rebuilds one — every round
rewrites this port's own tree, so a rewrite that happens only inside a
copy never survives. Wrapping in the *template* instead needs the member
variable's **written** type (`Variable _ _ t | tIsFunction (theType t)`,
`Function.hs:391`): no table types a member of an uninstantiated template,
and `getSymbols'` records the written type regardless. A reader for it —
the CST node the declaration's type was lowered from, spelled structurally
for the built-ins a function type is made of — was written and *measured
inert*: the wrapper then survives (`Foo<|$bool|>@Run@$wrapper$Do` is
hoisted), and not one program in 2,422 moved, because the capture
`make_capture1<Foo<|$bool|>&>` — a capture of a reference to a *copy* — is
still not materialised, and the walk declines either way. It was removed;
it belongs with the capture, not before it. The non-template case is whole
today: `Go<|@@data@closure@make_capture1<|$ref@Foo|>@$@Capture@Foo@Run@$wrapper$Do|>`.

*A re-read lvalue has no type.* `g[idx]++` is `Assign(g[idx], g[idx] + 1)`
and this port lowers the lvalue's text a *second* time, donating the copy
so two `Own` nodes never claim one `TypeKey` (`kg_hir::lower`'s `reread`).
The walk reads a type only from an `Own` node, so every name in that
second reading is stamped by the reference and by nothing here — 41
programs, `atomic.k::1` and `static-if.k::17` at their head. Two rules were
measured: reading the table for *every* donated node collapses `ptdiff`
from 1547 to **0** (a donated attribute list picks up a `uint1` from the
`Own` node sharing its key — `donate_inner_claims` demotes an inner claim
to the same range and kind); restricting that to a donated `PATH`,
`INDEX_EXPR` or `FIELD_EXPR` whose key an `Own` node also holds gives
**1511**, still below the baseline. So the reference does not stamp every
occurrence either, and the rule wants reading off the recorded traces
before any more code. The honest modelling is a third `Written` — "its own
text, but not the key's owner" — which is 27 `Written::Donated` matches to
audit and worth doing *after* the traces say what to stamp.

*An enum constant through a foreign alias.* `type-identifier.k::9` writes
`static C<E> c;` over `template <typename T> class C { T x = T::One; }` in
another module, and the copy lands *there*: the helper's twin reads

```kanagawa
class __kg_m1 { __kg_m0 x = __kg_m0::One; }
```

where `__kg_m0` is the alias for the deciding module's `E` — a name with
no declaration, no import and no leaf entry beyond its own segment, so
`Imports::type_of` answers nothing for `__kg_m0::One`, the fold produces no
`ConstValue::Enum`, and the walk emits a plain `ParseNamedVariable` where
the reference stamps `uint32` and emits `ParseEnumValue`. The fix is in
that lookup: a path whose head is a foreign leaf alias is the path the
alias stands for, and the deciding module's map answers it.

**A member of a class template is wrapped capturing the copy.** `ptdiff`
1547 → 1551 structural; `backend` 1758 → 1764 walked, 2478 → 2484 overall,
616 → 610 declined, 49 disagreements and 73 crashes unchanged;
conformance, strict, `errors`, `repoint` and every `ir` line unchanged.
`this-capture.k::18` and `callbacks.k::63` now walk the copies the
reference walks, name for name:
`Go<|@@data@closure@make_capture1<|$ref@Foo<|$uint@32|>|>@$@Capture@Foo<|$uint@32|>@Run@?lambda0@$wrapper$callback|>`.

The entry above books this row as "the capture is the whole of what is
left". It was not. Three things were, and the order matters:

1. **The twin did not parse.** `moveFunctions` reuses the callee node whole
   when it gives a method a receiver (`thisMethod b = functionSpecifier
   (Just $ thisValue b) b`, `Function.hs:67`), and `qualifyName` (`:72-77`)
   had already given that callee the class's qualifier. The reference never
   spells the result; this port prints its tree and reparses it, and
   `$this.Foo<|$uint@32|>::callback()` is not a name any parser reads back —
   two syntax errors, no twin, and the route stopped after round one with
   the capture undecided. A method called through a receiver now prints by
   its leaf (the receiver's type is what resolves the member); a written
   `x.template F<uint32>()` keeps its list and its keyword.
2. **The wrapper was built only in the copy**, where the next round loses
   it. Wrapping in the template needs the member variable's *written* type
   (`Variable _ _ t | tIsFunction (theType t)`, `Function.hs:391`), since no
   table types a member of an uninstantiated template — the reader the entry
   above called inert. It was inert only because of (1): with the twin
   parsing, it is what puts `$wrapper$callback` in the template, and the
   copies inherit it.
3. The alias-aware `redundant_qualifier` from earlier in the day, which
   stops the copy's own wrap from writing the qualifier back in.

Unaliasing the *declaration's* qualifier as well — the obvious next line —
moved nothing in 2,422 and was left out.

Test: `a_member_of_a_class_template_is_wrapped_capturing_the_copy`, every
name in it read off the reference's recorded walk, red with the printer's
qualifier and red with the written type unread. It replaces
`a_call_of_a_template_given_a_bare_function_declines`, which pinned the
decline this closes — corrected, not deleted, with the same program.

**A default is not about position, and a constant is its function.**
`ptdiff` 1551 → 1555 structural; `backend` 1764 → 1769 walked, 2484 → 2490
overall, 610 → 605 declined, **49 → 48** disagreements, 73 crashes,
`repoint` 24/72, conformance 2500/2500, strict 105 and `errors` 24
unchanged.

`template-param-default.k::7` is one line — `Check(Foo<bool, bool>)` — and
this port made nothing of it: no copy, no wrapper, no closure, where the
reference makes all three. `Foo`'s third parameter is written with a
default, so the mention is short of its parameters and the census postpones
it (`templateArgsResolved`, `TypeCheck.hs:323`), and the fill that exists
for that (`elaborate::defaults`, 2026-09-19) only looked at
`TypeIdentifier`. `deduceInstance'` (`Type.hs:1440-1444`) says nothing
about position: a function instance handed to a higher-order function is
the same mention in a `QualifiedIdentifier`, and its scope is its own
chain's.

**A call's callee is not one of them.** Filled there too, `Fun(false)` over
`template <typename T = uint32>` becomes `Fun<uint32>` and the argument
stops converting — two programs the port had compiled cleanly began
reporting "Invalid conversion from `bool` to `uint32`", which is the lie
this project's rules are written against. `substituteDefault` fills only
what deduction left unbound (`Just Nothing == deduced !? n`,
`Type.hs:1422-1428`), and a call's defaults are `deduceTemplateArgs`' own
(`fill_defaults`, already there). So the callee of every `FunctionCall` is
collected first and skipped.

**Then the last of that family showed what was under it.**
`template-param-default.k::8` writes `const auto fn = Foo<bool>;` and
`Check(fn)`, and with the copy finally made, the wrapper came out
`$wrapper$fn` — a lambda calling a name no declaration answers, "Undefined
function: fn" from the backend, a *new* disagreement. `evaluateConstexpr`
splices a constant's initializer at pass 6 (`Constexpr.hs:256`), before
pass 8 wraps anything: the argument *is* the function by then, and the
reference names the wrapper
`$wrapper$@helper@template_param_default$Foo<|$bool$uint@3@6|>`. One splice
— a non-member `const` whose initializer is a name — and the disagreement
count fell below where the day started.

Tests: `a_function_instance_given_as_an_argument_takes_its_defaults` (red
with the value arm cut and red with the callee guard cut) and
`a_wrapper_is_named_after_the_function_a_constant_holds` (red with the
constant unread).

**A module that only calls a higher-order member.** `ptdiff` 1555 → 1556
structural; `backend` 1769 → 1770 walked, 2490 → 2491 overall, **48 → 47**
disagreements; declines, crashes, conformance, strict, `errors`, `repoint`,
corpus and `ir` unchanged.

`higher-order-functions.k::49` is four lines and declares nothing —

```kanagawa
inline uint32 Run(uint32 x) { static C c; return c.Go(DoIt, x); }
```

— and the reference makes a `Closure<|@Run@$wrapper$…DoIt…|>` this port
made nowhere. The wrap itself was fine; the module was never *routed*. A
caller is a route target when it "calls a higher-order function"
(`Templates::calls_a_higher_order_function`), and that predicate read a
call's callee as a `Path`: `c.Go(…)` is a `FieldExpr`, so a module whose
only use is a higher-order *member* fell through every gate — it declares
no template, writes no lambda, declares no higher-order function of its
own.

The member's class is not readable from the receiver here, so the gate asks
only whether *some* class declares a higher-order member of that name.
Over-approximating costs a twin that decides nothing; under-approximating
loses the wrapper and its closure, which is what it had been doing.

Test: `a_module_that_only_calls_a_higher_order_member_is_routed`, red with
the field arm cut.

**A copy's width is folded before it is mangled.** `ptdiff` 1556 → 1563
structural; `backend` 1770 → 1780 walked, 2491 → 2500 overall, 605 → 596
declined; 47 disagreements, 73 crashes, conformance 2500/2500, strict 105,
`errors` 24 and `repoint` 24/72 unchanged. The 38 whole-file programs of
`test/logic` that all diverged at call #127 are the bulk of it.

Every one of them reaches `library/test/internal/assert.k:59`:

```kanagawa
else if (reinterpret_cast<uint<bitsizeof T>>(expected) != …)
```

In `assert_equal<uint32>`'s copy that argument is `uint<bitsizeof uint32>`,
which pass 6 folds to `uint32` before pass 8 keys or mangles anything
(`Constexpr.hs:50`). This port folds inside the *type table* and leaves the
tree spelling the expression — and the mangler reads the tree. It had no
`ParamUint` arm at all, so `mangle_args` declined, `make_instance` skipped
the copy, and `reinterpret_cast<|$uint@32|><|$uint@32|>` — a copy that is
still a template over its abbreviated parameter, deduced again — existed
nowhere.

So `kg_hir::width` folds a *closed* width: a literal, the arithmetic over
literals, and `bitsizeof`/`bytesizeof` of a written built-in, which is what
a substituted `bitsizeof T` becomes. A width naming anything else is `None`
and its occurrence declines as before; the table is where those are
decided, and reaching for it here would key one instance two ways.

**Three other places wanted the same fold and none of them moved a
program**: the census's argument key, its `ArgShape`, and
`instantiateTemplates`' `tArg`. Each was written, measured over 2,422
programs and 3,270 backend runs, and removed — the mangler is the only
reader that had no arm. The census keys these through the deduction, which
reads the table and folded all along.

**And the copies it unlocked found an invented error waiting.**
`library/data/array.k`'s `reduce` recurses, so its copy's signature carries
the `Closure<…>` that `higherOrderFunctions` wrote (`Function.hs:180-184`)
— a name the reference resolves in one whole-program symbol map, importing
nothing. The twin is a file, the printer spells a namespace prefix as
nothing, and pass 9 called `Closure` undefined on a program the reference
compiles. Printing `import data.closure.core` into the twin fixes the text
and *not* the verdict (the twin's import view is the module's own) and
moved nothing, so it was removed; the diagnostic is declined at the seam
instead, where it is plainly the rewrite's own name. A program that writes
`Closure` unimported is now a missed diagnostic, which is the honest
direction.

Tests: `a_closed_width_folds_to_its_literal` (the folder, red with the
arithmetic or the `bitsizeof` arm cut) and `a_copys_folded_width_is_one_instance`
(end to end, red with the mangler's arm cut).

**Why 38 `test/logic` programs decide nothing, to the line.** No number
moved; this is the diagnosis, and the experiment that says what must land
first.

`unit::assert_equal(tag, 4, x)` in `test/logic/auto_inline.k` deduces
nothing because **all three arguments read `Unresolved`** — the whole call
site is untyped. The chain:

* `tag`'s type is `unit::tag_t`, and `library/test/internal/assert.k:11`
  is `using tag_t = newtype<uint32>;` — an alias to an *instance of an
  imported template*;
* the base inference types that alias `Unresolved` (an instance mention is
  the census's and the route's to decide, not the table's), so the
  declaring module's `ModuleTypes` carries `Unresolved` and every importer
  reads it;
* `visit_function` then postpones the *body* — `not (all tResolved
  paramTypes)` (`Inference.hs:54-59`) — and no later round decides it, so
  nothing in that function is ever typed: no deduction, no `assert_equal`
  copy, no `reinterpret_cast` chain, and nine copies the reference makes
  appear nowhere.

The reduction is four files: a template, a module aliasing an instance of
it, a re-exporting module, and an importer. Each *half* types cleanly — a
local alias to an instance, an imported alias to a plain type, a direct
instance parameter — and only the combination fails.

**The experiment.** A *settling round* — one extra inference round after
the fixpoint stops, in which a function whose parameters are still
unresolved has its body visited anyway — types those bodies and is exactly
what the reference's whole-program symbol map buys it. Measured over the
corpus: `ptdiff` 1563 → 1564 structural with **13 fewer divergences**,
`backend` 1780 → 1783 walked, 2500 → 2503 agreements, 596 → 585 declines,
crashes 73 → 72, conformance/strict/`errors` unchanged — **and nine whole
files newly rejected**, which is why it is not in the tree.

All nine are *pre-existing* checks that the untyped bodies had been hiding:

* `static_assert(x == 1)` over a function's parameter — the corpus itself
  calls this "constexpr evaluation at IR generation time"
  (`test/logic/const.k:20`), which is after inlining; this port decides it
  at pass 19 and reports "did not evaluate to a boolean constant". A
  three-line program with a resolved parameter reports it today;
* "Invalid number of arguments, expected 0" at a member called inside a
  lambda (`context_saver_depth.k:27`, seven more like it) — `captureThis`
  rewrites `Helper(tid)` to `$this.Helper(tid)` and the arity check reads
  the wrong callee.

So the order is: fix those two checks (both toward silence), then the
settling round, then the row. Each is independently testable, and the last
is worth ~38 programs.

**A `static assert` over a parameter waits for its argument.** `ptdiff`
rejected 1 → **0**, `backend` frontend 54 → 53, declined 596 → 597;
structural 1563, agreements 2500, disagreements 47, crashes 73,
conformance 2500/2500, strict 105 and `errors` 24 all unchanged. One
invented error, gone.

`test/logic/const.k:17-22` is

```kanagawa
inline uint32 Helper(uint32 x)
{
    // Test constexpr evaluation at IR generation time
    static_assert(x == 1);
```

and the reference compiles it: `Helper(1)`'s argument is propagated into
the parameter before pass 16 asks, so `staticAssert` sees `BoolLiteral
True` (`Frontend.hs:394`). This port folds the function where it is
*written*, where `x` has no value at all — and reported "did not evaluate
to a boolean constant", which is not a verdict about the program but about
this port's fold. A local mutable is different and stays reported: the
reference cannot fold one either (`basics.k::67`).

Found while measuring the settling round (entry above), which exposes
eight more of the same kind through the arity of a member called inside a
lambda. This is the first of the two that must land before it.

**The settling round's second blocker, reduced to 23 lines.** With the
settling round in the tree (the entry above), this reports "Invalid number
of arguments, expected 0" and the reference compiles it:

```kanagawa
template <typename I>
inline void Go(auto count, (I) -> void body) { }

class C
{
private:
noinline uint32 Helper(uint32 x) { return x + 1; }
public:
void run(uint32 tag) { Go(1024, [tag](uint32 tid) { uint32 result = Helper(tid); }); }
}

export C;
```

What the check reads at the callee's key is `Function { kind:
FreeFunction, ret: uint32, params: [] }` — a *free* function with no
parameters, which no declaration in the file is: `Helper` is a
`MemberFunction` with one. The base table has nothing at that node
(`type_of_node` is `Unresolved`); the entry `TypeKey::for_node` finds was
written by the route's read-back from the twin, where the same call is
`__kg_m4.Helper(tid)` on the captured `this`. So the arity pass is
comparing against a type that is neither the member's nor the twin's, and
the capture is stripped from the wrong side. Whoever picks this up: start
at `readback`'s pairing for a `FIELD_EXPR` callee, not at the check.

**The template-template default, and what it is blocked behind.** Written
and measured; not landed, for the same reason as the settling round.

`template <template <typename> typename TT = S1> class T1` given `T1<>`
(`template-template-parameter.k::4`, ~30 programs in the 165-row) needs one
thing this port's defaults evaluator did not do: a template-*template*
parameter's default is a **name**, not a type or a value, so
`crate::defaults::Bound` grows a `Template(Vec<Symbol>)` arm whose default
is read from the `Type` after the `=` (its first `Type` child is the inner
parameter list's), and the fill mints it as the shape a *written*
template-template argument has — `TypeIdentifier(scope, ScopedName …)`,
qualified by the module that wrote the default, as `resolveTypeName`
resolves it there (`Parser.hs:736-757`).

That works: `T1<>` and `T1<S1>` become the *one* copy the reference makes,
and its name is the reference's to the byte —
`T1<|@@helper@template_template_parameter@S1|>`.

And the corpus says no: `backend` declines 597 → 593 with **two of the four
becoming invented errors and two becoming disagreements**, `ptdiff`
unchanged at 1563. The walk now reaches `t.x = s` on the copy and hands the
backend a class with no instance note — `ParseClass`'s third argument,
`parseInstanceType (theType expr)` (`ParseTree.hs:237-253`) — because the
twin types that copy `Unresolved`: a copy whose argument is a *template
name* gets no `setTypeOfInstance` note here, where one with type arguments
does. The backend then throws "Type error, expecting struct, union, or
class" on the member access (`parse_tree.cpp:4715`).

So the order is: type a copy whose argument is a template name (the note),
spell a `TArg::Name` in `typed_instance`'s argument list (it is `null`
today), then the fill. The fill itself is three small pieces and is
described here well enough to rewrite in ten minutes.

## Where this stands, and the order the queue is in

*2026-09-19, end of the day's work.* Nothing new measured here; this is the
hand-off.

| | start of day | now |
|---|---|---|
| `ptdiff` structural | 1527 | **1563** |
| `ptdiff` diverged / declined / rejected | 757 / 138 / 1 | **730 / 129 / 0** |
| `backend` walked | 1739 | **1780** |
| `backend` agreements | 2459 | **2500** |
| `backend` disagreements | 51 | **47** |
| crashes / declined | 89 / 663 | **73 / 597** |
| `repoint` | 22/72 | **24/72** |
| conformance | 2500/2500 | 2500/2500 |
| strict / `errors` | 105 / 24 | 105 / 24 |
| tests | 1538 | **1567** |

What landed: a local function's body typed in the twin; a member found
through the twin's alias; a `static for`'s iterations instantiated apart; a
class template's member wrapped capturing the copy (which needed the
printer to stop writing a class qualifier on a receiver call); a default
filled in value position and a constant spliced as its function; a module
that only calls a higher-order member routed; a copy's width folded before
it is mangled; a `static assert` over a parameter deferred.

**The queue, in the order the measurements say to take it.** Three separate
rows are blocked behind one thing, and it is not any of them:

1. **A copy whose argument is a *name* is typed as no instance.**
   `mangled_instance` reads `$uint@32`, `@10`, `$bool` and stops at a user
   name — `Hold<|@S|>` is `None` by construction, and a test pins it. So a
   class copy over a template-template argument carries no
   `setTypeOfInstance` note, `ParseClass`'s third argument is null, and the
   backend throws on the first member access into it. Extending the read
   wants a `TArg` for a template (`TArg::Name` over `Ty::Template`) and
   care: `mangled_instance` also feeds deduction.
2. **Then the template-template default** (~30 programs), written and
   measured above — it produces the reference's copy name exactly and is
   held only by (1).
3. **Then the arity of a member called inside a lambda** (23-line
   reduction above): the check reads a type from the route's read-back that
   is neither the member's nor the twin's.
4. **Then the settling round** (13 divergences, 3 backend agreements), which
   (3) is the last blocker for.
5. **Then the 38 `test/logic` programs**, which (4) unblocks: an alias to an
   instance of an imported template is `Unresolved` in the base inference,
   and every body that takes one is postponed.

The other open rows are unchanged and independent: the re-read lvalue's
stamps (41), the `same_types` copy-name row (123), a copy's member typed
through a foreign alias (30), the copy-order row, and the closure chains
that need a nested lambda's own closure.

**The queue's first item, taken and put back.** `set_type_of_instance`
declines a copy whose argument is a template name because `t_arg` has no
arm for it (`Type.hs:436-437`'s `TArg $ showPretty e`). Two things were
tried:

* **Any name-shaped argument** reads as `TArg::Name`. `ptdiff` 1563 → 1443
  and **188 programs newly rejected**: a declined note is silence, a wrong
  one poisons every member access into the copy. Not a near miss — a
  measurement of how load-bearing that decline is.
* **Only an argument the table types `TTemplate`.** Exactly right where the
  template is in the same module (`T1<S1>`'s copy gains the note and the
  node numbering matches the reference's call for call), and **inert over
  the corpus**: in `template-template-parameter.k::1` the argument `S3`
  comes from an imported helper, and the base table types an imported
  template's name `Unresolved` — the same blindness as the 38-program row
  five entries up.

So the queue's first item is not the note; it is **the base inference's
reading of imported names** — an alias to an instance of an imported
template, and an imported template's own name. Both rows and the two
behind them wait on it, and it is a piece of work with a real design
question in it (type a template instance in the base table, or teach the
import view to answer through the declaring module's elaborated map). The
display half is written down too: a template argument is spelled as the
source wrote it (`T1<S1>`), which the mangle cannot say, so the copy's
note has to spell it — `unmangle_instance_name_with`'s `TArg::Name` arm
with `Ty::Template` printing its leaf.

**A template given as an argument, written or defaulted.** `ptdiff` 1563 →
**1579** structural, diverged 730 → 714; `backend` 2500 → **2504**
agreements, 597 → 593 declined; disagreements 47, crashes 73, frontend 53,
conformance 2500/2500, strict 105, `errors` 24, `repoint` 24/72 — all
unchanged. The row the last four entries kept walking into, closed.

Three pieces, and the order they had to be found in is the whole story:

1. **The copy carries its note.** `tArg` reads a template argument's
   `typeOf` as `TTemplate` and falls to `TArg $ showPretty e`
   (`Type.hs:436-437`); this port's `t_arg` had no arm and declined, which
   declines the *whole* `setTypeOfInstance` note — so `ParseClass`'s third
   argument was null and the backend threw "Type error, expecting struct,
   union, or class" on the first member access into the copy. Admitting any
   name-shaped argument costs 188 programs (measured, entry above);
   admitting what the *table* types `TTemplate` is inert, because an
   imported template's name types `Unresolved` here. What works is the
   census's own `ArgShape::Template`, which already existed and which
   `known_targ` dropped: the spec carries it, for a foreign instance and
   for the module's own alike.
2. **The display spells it as written.** `unmangleInstanceName` prints the
   `TArg`, which for a template is the source text — `T1<S1>`. The mangle
   carries the resolved path, so reading it back gives
   `T1<helper.template_template_parameter::S1>`. Spelling the whole display
   from the note instead costs 64 programs (the note and the mangle differ
   on the *other* arguments too); what holds is to take the mangle's
   spelling and put back just the one qualifier the note names.
3. **Then the default fills.** A template-template parameter's default is a
   *name*, so `Bound` grows a `Template` arm read from the `Type` after the
   `=` (its first `Type` child is the inner parameter list's), minted as the
   shape a written argument has and qualified by the module that wrote the
   default (`resolveTypeName`, `Parser.hs:736-757`). `T1<>` and `T1<S1>`
   are then the one copy the reference makes, named to the byte.

Test: `a_template_given_as_an_argument_is_one_copy_written_or_defaulted`,
across modules and within one, red with any of the three cut.

**A template argument the owner cannot spell.** `ptdiff` diverged 714 →
711 with three programs becoming honest declines; `backend` agreements 2504
→ 2503, **frontend 53 → 52** — one invented error traded for one
agreement, which is the trade this project's rules name explicitly.
conformance, strict, `errors`, `repoint`, corpus and `ir` unchanged.

`template-template-parameter.k::13` writes `T3<16, memory>` where `memory`
is `data.memory`'s and `T3` is a helper's. The copy lands beside `T3`, in a
module that imports no `data.memory` — so `mint_shape` could not spell the
argument and declined the whole spec, and the copy existed nowhere. It now
travels the way a *function* argument already did: an alias for the
qualified spelling (`.data.memory::memory`), which the twin can parse and
the mangler reads back as `@@data@memory@memory`. The copy is made, named
`T3<|@16@@data@memory@memory|>` as the reference names it.

What it does *not* finish: the copy's own member is
`__kg_m0<uint32, 16>` — an instance of the aliased template, which the
twin's census cannot key because `__kg_m0` is no template's name in its
index. The walk declines there ("template instance"), which is why three
divergences became declines rather than matches. The next link is the
census reading a mention through the pool's aliases, as `deduce_rewrite`
already does for a callee.

Test: `a_template_argument_the_owner_cannot_spell_travels_as_an_alias`,
red with the alias arm cut.

**The next link, written and inert.** `IrTemplates` indexes a template by
the name its *declaration* carries, so a twin's `__kg_m0<uint32, 16>` — the
alias `mint_shape` mints for a template the module cannot spell — is a
mention its census decides nothing about. Teaching the index the pool's
aliases is six lines (`with_aliases`, every alias whose qualified path ends
in a template's name), and on a four-file reduction the whole chain then
completes: the census decides `mem.memory<uint32, 16>` at the site inside
the copy, the decision travels to `mem` as a foreign one, and `mem`
materialises it.

No corpus program moves. `template-template-parameter.k::13`, the shape
this was for, declines at the same place: its `TT` is `data.memory`'s
`memory`, and what that copy needs next is the library's own chain. The
six lines are therefore not in the tree; they are here, with the reduction
that proves them, for whoever reaches this row with the library's part
solved.

One thing measured on the way, worth knowing: with the aliases indexed,
the helper's twin ran **8 rounds** where it had run 1 — the decision is
re-made every round because the copy it asks for lands in another module.
Whatever lands here should settle that too.
