## The settling round, measured whole and not landed — and the two bugs it found

*2026-09-20.* The queue's items (3) and (4) — "the arity of a member called
inside a lambda", then "the settling round" — taken together, because (3)
is only observable with (4) in the tree. Both are written, both are
measured over the whole corpus, and **neither is landed**. Two *other*
defects they exposed are, and they moved the numbers on their own.

**What the settling round is.** `Inference.hs:58` postpones the body of a
function whose parameters are not all resolved, on the premise that a later
round resolves them. Where the type never resolves — an alias to an
instance of an *imported* template, `using tag_t = newtype<uint32>` — no
round ever does, so nothing in that body is typed at all (the diagnosis is
three entries up, "Why 38 `test/logic` programs decide nothing"). A
*settling* round relaxes that one guard once the ordinary fixpoint has
stopped. `Round` grows a `settling` flag and a `postponed` flag; the loop
turns settling on when a converged round had postponed something, and the
patch is in `scratchpad/settling.patch`.

**What it is worth, measured on this tree** (one settling round; letting
the fixpoint continue afterwards is the second figure):

| | before | settling | +loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ptdiff` structural | 1583 | **1584** | 1584 |
| `ptdiff` diverged / declined | 707 / 132 | 704 / 134 | 703 / 135 |
| `backend` agreements | 2506 | **2509** | 2509 |
| `backend` crashes / declined | 73 / 592 | 72 / 590 | 72 / 590 |
| `ir` elaborated roots | 34 | **48** | 48 |
| `bench` keystroke, worst | 578 ms | **1313 ms** | 1519 ms |
| `bench` check, worst | 94.8 ms | 95.0 ms | 128 ms |

conformance 2500/2500, strict 105 and `errors` 24 throughout.

**Why it is not in the tree.** Three reasons, in the order they decided it:

1. **The keystroke worst case goes 578 ms to 1313 ms**, and `check` does
   not move at all. The cost is not the extra round: it is that fourteen
   more roots now *elaborate*, and `Db::elaboration` runs on every
   `diagnostics`. The worst file changes from `wide_to_narrow.k` to
   `test/library/data/fifo/transpose.k`, whose whole-program `kg check` is
   0.40 s either way. This is the shape `CLAUDE.md`'s bench rule exists
   for.
2. **It is not the reference's algorithm.** The reference types those
   bodies in pass 8's *inner* `inferType`, over the materialised tree
   (`Template.hs:71-81`); a settling round types them at pass 6 over the
   unmaterialised one. Every type it computes there is a guess about what
   pass 8 will conclude — which is exactly how the two bugs below surfaced
   as *invented errors* rather than as missing ones.
3. **It does not buy the row it was scheduled for.** The queue said "worth
   ~38 programs"; `test/logic/auto_inline.k` diverges at the same call
   (#127, `ParseFunctionModifier / ParseNamespace`) with it and without it.
   The `ParseFunctionModifier / ParseNamespace` row goes 38 → 67 under it,
   which is programs arriving from *earlier* divergences, not leaving.

The principled route for that row is the one the queue's first item names
and this does not attempt: the module that declares `tag_t` materialises
`newtype<uint32>`, and the importing module's table reads the copy through
the declaring module's elaborated map. Then the ordinary fixpoint resolves
the parameter and no round has to be relaxed.

**The stamp that must not cross the seam** — written, red only under the
settling round, in the same patch. `setTypeOfTemplateCall`
(`Type.hs:1120-1129`) plants a synthetic `TFunction FreeFunction mempty t
mempty` on a callee a round could not resolve, so the expected type can
flow backwards into it; its parameter list is empty whatever the callee's
arity is, and its only reader is deduction's third source
(`Type.hs:1479-1480`). Pass 8's twin fails to resolve what the user's
module resolves — `captureThis` rewrites `Helper(tid)` to
`$this.Helper(tid)` and the twin spells the receiver `__kg_mN.Helper` on a
capture whose type is a `decltype` declared inside `run`, which nothing at
the twin's file scope can link — so the twin stamps `Helper`, and the
read-back carried the stamp home onto the *written* callee's key. Pass 19
read it as a nullary free function: "Invalid number of arguments, expected
0" on a program the reference compiles (the queue's 23-line reduction).
The fix is a `stamped` set on `TypeTable` and a skip in
`kg_hir::readback::read_back`; it is **inert over today's corpus** (every
gate byte-identical with and without it), so it belongs with the settling
round rather than ahead of it.

**A local declaration hides a file-scope constant from the fold** — landed.
Found by running the corpus under the settling round and reducing
`test/logic/test_cases_2.k:129`, and then **pre-existing**: the reduction
fails on `main` with no settling round at all.

```kanagawa
inline void A() { uint3[16] x; static_assert(bytesizeof(x) == 6); }
const uint3 x = 2;
```

`FileScope::lookup_const` walked outward until a *constant* turned up,
which steps straight past the local `x`, folded it to `2` and typed it
`uint3` — so `bytesizeof` said "undefined for a type with bit size of 3".
`lookupInScope` searches one map holding every symbol
(`Symbols.hs:83-87`) and `eval (NamedValueF x)` then asks whether what it
found is a `const` with an initializer (`Constexpr.hs:286-293`), so the
walk stops at the innermost declaration of the name whatever kind it is.
`FileScope::resolved_key` is that walk and the three callers go through
it. `ptdiff` 1579 → 1580, `backend` frontend 52 → 51.

**A lambda hoisted out of a member finds its own capture** — landed. Found
the same way, from `test/logic/string.k:797`, and also pre-existing.
`?lambdaN$capture` is the name `desugarLambdas` gives every capture alias,
so a module's twin declares it once per lambda and the printer spells a
hoisted function's parameter type by its leaf alone;
`Declarations::alias_leaves` disambiguates by the scope the function was
hoisted out of, and the map behind it knew only **top-level functions**.
`moveFunctions` defers inside a local class (`Function.hs:84-128`), so a
class declared in a function is hoisted first and a lambda inside one of
its members after — `Interpolation@ClosureClass@test@?lambda0`, whose
parent is the member `test`. The longest top-level-function prefix of that
is `Interpolation`, so the capturing lambda's parameter was typed as
another lambda's `make_capture0::$::Capture` and pass 9 called its own
fields undefined. `hoisted_parents` is now `hoisted_scopes`, over top-level
functions *and* the member functions of top-level classes, returning the
scope path. `ptdiff` 1580 → 1583, `backend` 2503 → 2506 agreements, 596 →
592 declined, 47 → 48 disagreements (one program that was declined now
walks and disagrees).

Two things measured on the way and **not** kept, because nothing pins them
and the corpus cannot tell them apart from what is there: asking
`alias_leaves` *before* the imports rather than after (it is the more
defensible order — a `__kg_mN` is a rename local to one twin — and it is
inert: 1583/707/132 either way, `string.k` clean either way), and sorting
the `alias_leaves` candidate lists (`FxHashMap` is not randomised, so the
order is already reproducible).


## The base map read `Unresolved` and the twin knew better

*2026-09-20, later.* The queue's item 1 — "the base inference's reading of
imported names" — taken the way the entry above said it had to be taken:
not by relaxing pass 6's guard, but by letting the twin's answer reach the
module that asks. `ptdiff` structural 1583 → **1590**, diverged 707 →
**695**; `backend` agreements 2506 → **2514**, walked 1786 → **1794**,
declined 592 → 584. conformance 2500/2500, strict 105, `errors` 24,
corpus, `repoint` 24/72 and `ir`'s exit code unmoved.

**The bug was three lines old and in plain sight.**

```rust
pub(crate) fn overlay(&self, extra: &ModuleTypes) -> ModuleTypes {
    let mut names = (*self.names).clone();
    for (k, v) in extra.names.iter() {
        names.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
    }
```

The doc above it says "the elaborated twin's names … **on top of** the base
map". `or_insert` is the other way round: the base wins every collision, so
`extra` could only ever contribute keys the base did not have. For
`tag_t` the base *has* the key — with `Unresolved` on it, because an
instance mention is the census's and the route's to decide, not the
table's — and the twin has the copy. Every importer read the `Unresolved`.

The rule that replaces it is `resolveTypeOf`'s, one level up
(`Type.hs:1037-1048`): a key the base left unresolved takes the twin's
answer, a key the base resolved keeps it. Monotone, and it cannot
un-decide anything.

**Two more pieces, and the order they had to be found in.** Neither moves
a number alone, and the first one measured *worse* on its own:

1. **The census's shape must fold a substituted width.** `assert_equal`'s
   body is `reinterpret_cast<uint<bitsizeof T>>(expected)`; in the
   `uint32` copy that is `uint<bitsizeof uint32>`, and pass 6 folds it to
   `uint32` before pass 8 keys the instance (`Constexpr.hs:50`,
   `Frontend.hs:69`). `kg_hir::width::folded_width` is that fold and the
   *mangler* already used it — `written_builtin` still required a bare
   literal, so the argument shaped `Opaque` and the copy was never handed
   to `type.coerce`. With it, `test/logic/auto_inline.k` walks from call
   #127 to call #510.
2. **A module with nothing to rewrite still needs a twin.**
   `elaborate_module` early-returns when a module has no specs, no decided
   instance, no lambda, no wrapper, no local function and nothing
   unrolled — and `a::fail(tag, 3u32)` in a module that writes nothing
   else is exactly that. Its twin is the only table that resolves
   `a::tag_t` to the copy, so without one the call deduces nothing however
   many rounds run. `calls_a_known_template` is the predicate, syntactic
   by necessity: the `using` set beside it is built from the calls the
   *base* table could deduce, which is the set this is trying to grow. It
   both routes the module and keeps `elaborate_module` from early-returning
   on it, and the second half is what the test turns on. Worth `ptdiff`
   1583 → 1590 and `backend` 2506 → 2514 together with the overlay.

**Measured and dropped on the way.** Re-running the deduction over each
pass's elaborated tables — a second `collect_deduced` in the program-pass
loop — reads well and is **inert**: `elaborate_module`'s own per-module
deduction already covers it once the module has a twin, and every gate was
byte-identical with and without. It also carried a hazard worth writing
down, because the next person will reach for the same idea: a
partly-explicit deduced call at a site the *census* already decided spells
its written arguments with no scope at all (`expFromType`'s
`typeIdentifier []`, `Type.hs:1648`) where the census spells them with
their own, so admitting both makes two copies of one instance under two
names and mangles the call site to the one nobody declared
(`initializer-list.k::42`, `Error 5 Undefined function`). Dropping the
spec is not enough — the call has to leave the *rewrite* list too, since
`elaborate_module` reads that list to spell the call.

**Two costs, and they are the next two pieces of work.**

* **The worst-case keystroke goes 578 ms → 1289 ms**, and `check` does not
  move (94.9 → 94.9 ms). Fourteen more roots elaborate and
  `Db::elaboration` runs on every `diagnostics`; the worst file changes
  from `wide_to_narrow.k` to `test/library/data/fifo/transpose.k`, whose
  whole-program `kg check` goes 0.40 s → 1.42 s. The cost is the
  reference's own fixpoint: `transpose.k` now runs all four program passes
  (28, 61, 104, 130 decisions handed) where it ran two with four. The
  lever is that **phase 2 re-elaborates every target module on every
  pass**, and a module whose foreign specs and predecessors are unchanged
  cannot produce a different twin. `MAX_PROGRAM_PASSES` is not the lever:
  at 2 the corpus falls to 1429 structural and 2292 agreements.
* **`ir`'s `type agreement` goes 30/34 → 21/38**, on one cause. Five roots
  fail, four of them newly, and all four read
  `type.newtype::newtype<|$uint@32|>` where the reference reads
  `type.newtype::newtype<uint32>`. That is not a spelling difference the
  gate should forgive: the reference's `pretty (TInstance t x as)` prints
  `template<args>` (`Type.hs:402-406`), so it holds a `TInstance` where
  this route brings home a plain struct named after the copy. An alias to
  a copy needs `setTypeOfInstance`'s note, the way a written instance
  already gets one. Three roots that used to fail now pass, so the
  denominator moved too.

**The reduction, for whoever takes either of those.** Four files —
`type/newtype.k` with the template, `helper/a.k` with `using tag_t =
newtype<uint32>` and a `fail` template taking one, `main.k` calling
`a::fail(tag, 3u32)` — and the whole chain is observable end to end: the
copy lands beside its template and `bool b = x` inside it is an `Invalid
conversion` carried home with the call as its `while compiling` frame. It
is `a_twins_resolved_name_beats_the_base_maps_unresolved_one`.

**`MAX_PROGRAM_PASSES` is four, measured.** Taken while looking for the
keystroke back: at **3** the corpus falls to 1508 structural and 2394
backend agreements; at **4** it is 1590 and 2514; at **6** it is *byte
identical to 4* and the worst-case keystroke goes 1289 ms → 1951 ms. So
the cut is in the right place and is not the lever.

The lever, measured the same hour: phase 2 re-elaborates all 29 target
modules of `transpose.k` on every pass, and the specs that change arrive
**early** in the order — the first module whose owned-spec count moves is
index 7 on pass 1, index 5 on pass 2, index 4 on pass 3. A positional
"skip everything before the first change" is therefore worth about a fifth
of it. What would be worth the rest is per-*import* dependency tracking —
re-elaborate a module only when a module it imports changed — and the
obstacle to that is `twin_roots`, which `elaborate_module` is handed whole
and may index a copy from any earlier module's twin, not only from an
import. Establish that dependency before building on it.

## The note that fixes the types and costs the walk

*2026-09-20, later still.* The `type agreement` fall the entry above
records has **one cause, now confirmed by fixing it**, and the fix is in
`docs/patches/instance-notes-in-the-twins-map.patch` rather than in the
tree, because it costs the walk more than it buys.

**The cause.** `setTypeOfInstance`'s note (`Type.hs:426-440`) is written
here onto the *arena* key of a copy's declaration and lands in the module's
own elaborated table. It does **not** land in the map the module hands its
importers: that map comes from inferring the twin's text, where `struct
__kg_m48 { uint32 unwrap; }` is a plain struct. So `using tag_t =
newtype<uint32>` reaches every importer as a struct named after the copy,
and renders `type.newtype::newtype<|$uint@32|>` where the reference renders
`newtype<uint32>` — its `pretty (TInstance t x as)` builds the display from
the *arguments* (`Type.hs:402-406`).

`ModuleTypes::thread_instances` is the fix: `setTypeOf`'s own `TInstance`
threading (`Type.hs:1050-1058`) applied after the twin's inference, since
the reference writes the note before `inferType` and this route infers the
twin whole. `instance_notes` re-keys each arena write under the name the
twin gives the declaration.

**It works, exactly.** `ir`'s `type agreement` **21/38 → 34/38**.

**And the walk falls with it**: `ptdiff` 1590 → **1498** structural,
diverged 695 → 789; `backend` 2514 → 2492 agreements, frontend rejections
51 → 54. Restricting the threading to aggregates — `pretty` falls through
a `TInstance` over a function, an error or an unresolved inner, and this
port's `Ty::Instance` does not — recovers most of it and not all: 1585
structural, 2496 agreements, `type agreement` 33/38. The row that moves
first is `ParseUintType / ParseBaseList`, 30 → **145** unrestricted: an
alias template's `using U = uint32` copy wrapped in an instance stops
reading as an integer.

**What it actually needs**, and this is the reusable part: the reference's
type predicates see **through** `TInstance` — `tIsStruct`, `tIsClass`,
`tIsInt` and their siblings all fall to `maybeInner`
(`Type.hs:607-640`), `tConcrete` unwraps it (`:596-597`), and `<:` and
`tIsConvertibleTo` unwrap both sides (`:326-327,359-360`). This port's
`Ty::Instance` is not transparent that way at the sites the census and the
walk read, so the moment a copy's declaration wears one, argument shapes
that used to read `Struct` read `Opaque` and instances are keyed
differently. `named_type_at`'s `concrete()` is one such site and fixing it
alone moves nothing, so the campaign is to find them all — `rg
'Ty::Struct\(' crates/kg-db crates/kg-ptbridge` is where it starts — and
only then to thread the note.

Until then the gate's number is honest about a real gap: our copies are
not instances to the modules that import them.

## A hoisted lambda inside a copy keeps its pre-hoist scope, and why the fix is not in

*2026-09-20, last.* The row the roadmap names — `static-if.k::47` and 28
others, where the reference's `ParseNamedType` scope is the single hoisted
name `foo<|…|>@?lambda0` and ours is the chain `["foo<|…|>", "$",
"?lambda0"]` — is **diagnosed to the line**, and the one-line fix is
`docs/patches/hoisted-lambda-scope.patch`, not in the tree.

**The cause.** `newScope` re-roots a scope under `getQualifiedName e`
(`Function.hs:48-50`), and `move_one` builds that from the item's name
*as the arena holds it*. A copy's lambda reaches `round_prefix` already
wearing the pool's alias — `?lambda0` is `__kg_m4` by then — while the
`declScopeName` of everything inside it still spells `?lambda0`, because
`kg_hir::rename` renames declaration **identifiers** and not scopes.
`KG_MOVE_TRACE` says it outright:

```
move_one parent=foo<|…|> item_qualifier=[foo<|…|>,$]
         item_qname=[foo<|…|>,$,__kg_m4] new=[foo<|…|>@?lambda0]
```

`mangle` un-aliases for the *name* (hence the correct `new`), and
`item_qname` did not, so `stripPrefix` matched nothing and the second arm
never fired. The base case works for the same reason it has to —
`Run@?lambda0` wears no alias, and its parameter's scope is `[Run@?lambda0]`
in our tree today.

**The fix works and costs four.** Un-aliasing the name in `item_qname`
(or stripping either spelling — measured identical) takes
`ParseNamedType / ParseNamedType` 29 → 23 and `ParseFunction /
ParseFunction` 30 → 27, and `static-if.k::47` from call #1419 to #1431.
`ptdiff` structural does **not** move: 1593 either way. And `backend`
agreements go 2514 → **2510** — four `higher-order-functions` programs
(67, 68, 83, 84) that agreed before now report `Error 32 Unknown symbol:
x`. Declines are unchanged, so those four walked before and walk now; the
extra re-rooting makes a name the backend then cannot resolve.

**Where to look next.** The `x` in question is the parameter of the
wrapper `rewrite::higher_order` made — `Foo<|…|>@$wrapper$@helper@
higher_order_functions$DoIt`, a name that already holds `@`s. Its
declaration and the uses under it both re-root (checked in
`KG_ELAB_DUMP_IR`'s output), so what breaks is something the *prefix
chains* carry rather than the `scope` fields: `qualifyName` builds those
before the partition and `modifyDeclScopeName` never touches them. Read
those two against the reference's `qualifyName`/`fixScopedName`
(`Function.hs:69-82`) before landing the one-liner.

`KG_ELAB_DUMP_IR=1` is new and is how the above was found: it prints the
tree the backend walk is handed, annotated with every node's
`declScopeName`.

## Three copies the owner could not spell, and one it could not fold

*2026-09-20, evening.* Four small rows off the `ptdiff` work list, each
diagnosed from the recorded traces and each landed with its own test.
`ptdiff` structural 1590 → **1595**, diverged 695 → **689**; `backend`
agreements 2514 → **2516**, walked 1794 → **1796**, disagreements 48 →
**46**, frontend rejections 51 → **50**. conformance 2500/2500, strict
105, `errors` 24 and the corpus unmoved throughout.

**A nested copy's template argument is spelled off its own note.** A
template named as an argument is spelled as the source wrote it
(`TArg $ showPretty e`, `Type.hs:436-437`), and the mangle carries the
resolved path instead — so the qualifier has to come back off the note.
`unqualify_template_arguments` read the note of the copy being *named*,
and the display nests: `check_scalar_return_type<uint32,
helper.memory::read_mem<uint32, memory>>` spells the inner copy's own
arguments inside itself, and `memory` is the inner one's template
argument, whose note lives in another module. Collected over the whole
program once, from every copy the walk's symbol map holds, longest
spelling first.

**A hoisted name is one identifier, and the mangle cannot say so.**
`mangleName` joins `parent @ child` into one identifier
(`Function.hs:39`), and the mangle prefixes *every* segment with `@` — so
a one-segment `Run@Fn4` and a two-segment `Run::Fn4` mangle identically.
`unmangle_text` has no symbol map and reads the two-segment one; the
reference reads its map (`unmangleQualifiedName`, `Type.hs:180-187`) and
prints `Go<Run@Fn4>`. The walk has a map of its own, so a split spelling
whose joined form **is** a declared name is un-split. A module namespace
is not at risk: it mangles `@@a@b`, a different branch of `unmangle_leaf`.

**A root file's template is a template-template argument too.**
`mint_shape` mints an alias for a name the owner cannot spell, from the
name's *qualified* spelling — and a root file carries no module header, so
`let ns = namespace?` declined the whole spec and the copy existed
nowhere (`T4<bool, Foo>`, `template-template-parameter.k::15`). The
reference resolves it because `getSymbols` is one whole-program map
(`Frontend.hs:40`); the alias now stands for the bare name, which the
mangler reads back as `@Foo`, the byte the reference writes. The program
becomes an honest *decline* rather than a divergence — the next link is
`Foo<false>` inside the copy — and one invented error goes with it.

**An enum a root file declares folds inside a foreign copy.** `static
C<E> c;` over `template <typename T> class C { T x = T::One; }` puts the
copy in the *helper*, whose twin then reads `__kg_m0::One`. No import
connects the two modules, so neither the constant nor the type reached the
alias: `Db::foreign_constants` walks the import graph, and so does
`Imports`. Both halves are the same shape and both were needed —
`FileScope::constants_under` seeds the twin's fold with the enum's
constants under the alias, and `Imports::type_of` types a constant of an
enum a minted alias names as the enum. With the fold alone the walk
emits the value but no node type and `type-identifier.k::9` still
diverges (1593 structural, 2514 agreements, 75 crashes); with both it is
identical to the reference but for positions.

**Two rows read and not taken**, with what was learned:

* `same_types<…>` over two attributed function types (2 programs of the
  123-row). The reference's mangle is a `cata` over the **written**
  argument tree (`Mangle.hs:27-64`), so `[[max_threads(2),
  thread_rate(1)]]` and `[[thread_rate(1), max_threads(2)]]` mangle
  differently — written order, not `Set TAttr` order. This port's mangler
  is the same cata and gets it right for a *local* instance; a foreign one
  is re-spelled from `ArgShape::Type(Ty::Function)`, whose `TAttrSet` is
  sorted. Carrying the written order would mean a per-argument field on
  `ForeignSpec`, beside `scopes`.
* `Foo(E::X)` over `enum E : uint3 { X = 0b111 }` (11 programs,
  `conversion-warning.k::4`). The reference's argument is the bare
  literal `7`, stamped `uint3` twice, with **no** `ParseEnumValue` —
  where the same `E::One` in an *initializer* does get one
  (`type-identifier.k::9`). `eval (NamedValueF x)`'s `EnumConstant` arm
  (`Constexpr.hs:286-293`) produces `EnumValueF` in both, and
  `ParseTree.hs:90` walks every `EnumValue` the same way, so something
  between them replaces it in argument position. Find that before
  changing the walk.

## The walk had no type where the reference had one, five times

*2026-09-20, night.* Five rows of the `ptdiff` list, all of one family:
the reference's tree carries a type this port's does not, because
`inferExpTree` types a node *before* its own fold and this port infers
over a CST that has neither the synthesized node nor the fold. `ptdiff`
structural 1598 → **1655**, diverged 686 → **628**; `backend` agreements
2516 → **2545**, walked 1796 → **1825**, crashes 73 → **44**.
conformance 2500/2500, strict 105, `errors` 24, corpus and `ir` unmoved.

**A decided `static if` inside a function is decided.** Two halves:
`Round::visit`'s splice asked whether any *child* of the node is dead, and
`dead_static_if_branches` records the branch **inside** the `ELSE_BRANCH`
wrapper — so every decided `static if` with an `else` missed the splice
and *nothing* in its live branch was ever typed. And
`dead_static_if_branches` skipped a `static if` under a `FN_DECL`
outright, on a reasoning about module-level maps that had nothing to say
about types. A class or a template still stands down — a copy's predicate
is the twin's — and the predicate now folds at its **own** scope. Worth
1600 → 1603 together, 1601 and 1600 apart.

**A re-read lvalue is its own text.** `x++` is `Assign(x, x + 1)` and the
lvalue's text is lowered twice; the copy was `Donated`, which says both
"no position" and "no key", where only the second is true.
`Written::Reread` is the third case the earlier survey asked for, and
every existing `== Own` / `!= Own` test keeps its meaning. **It moves
nothing alone** — the *operator* the lowering synthesized has no key
either, since `Binary Add` stands at the lvalue's range with the lvalue's
kind. `set_node_type` gains a third fallback beside its two: the operands'
types through `kg_ty::width::t_binary_op`, the same rule `kg_ty::infer`
runs. Together 1603 → **1629** and `backend` crashes 72 → **44**.

**A narrowing initializer is stamped twice**, as a narrowing argument
already was — `checkVarDecl`'s `initValueCheck warningNarrowingConversions`
wraps the initializer and the reference's walk types the wrapper too. The
guard that decides it is **not folded**: an initializer `evaluateConstexpr`
folds is a literal by the time `checkVarDecl` sees it, and
`checkConversion`'s literal arm judges it by `inferIntLiteralType` of the
value, not by the table's type for the written expression.
`helper/constexpr.k`'s `C<2>` members are 72 programs of exactly that, and
stamping them cost 1629 → 1557 before the guard; with it, 1642.

**An enum value converted to an integer is its value**
(`TypeCheck.hs:155-156`), at a call argument and at a variable's
initializer — the two `checkConversion` sites the walk has a target type
for. `Foo(E::X)` on a `Foo(uint2)` is the bare literal `7`, where the same
`E::One` initialising an enum-typed member keeps its `EnumValue`. 1595 →
1598 → 1600. `checkReturn` is the third site and is not wired: the walk
would have to carry the enclosing function's return type and no corpus row
asks for it.

**A negated literal is typed by `tNeg`.** `inferExpTree` is
`evaluateConstexpr . unfix . inferExpType` bottom-up (`Inference.hs:47,50`),
so a node is typed before its own fold and keeps that note: `-1` is `tNeg
(inferIntLiteralType Nothing 1)` = `int2`, not the folded `-1`'s `int1`.
`infer`'s folded-literal shortcut covered `PREFIX_EXPR` unconditionally
and cannot simply stop — `bitsizeof e` and `clog2 e` have no
`inferUnaryOp` rule, so their note stays unresolved and the folded
literal's type is what a later round writes, and dropping `PREFIX_EXPR`
costs 1642 → 1551. `inferUnaryOp` **first**, the shortcut only where it
has no answer: 1655.

**The shape to take from this.** Every one of the five is the same
question asked at a different node: *what did the reference's tree hold
here that a CST cannot?* The instruments that answer it are the recorded
trace either side of the divergence — `ptdiff --dump` — and
`KG_ELAB_DUMP_IR`, which prints the tree the walk is handed with every
node's provenance. Four of the five were found by reading twenty lines of
trace; none needed a reduction.

## Two displays and a grammar, and the mangle that cannot be read back

*2026-09-20, late.* Three more rows off the list. `ptdiff` structural 1655
→ **1671**, diverged 628 → **612**; `backend` agreements 2545 → **2554**,
walked 1825 → **1834**, frontend rejections 50 → **41**. Everything else
unmoved.

**A callback's initializer is a function specifier.** `() -> void
callback = c.void_F_void;` reaches the reference's backend as a
`FunctionSpecifier` with `c` as its receiver: `methodSpecifier`
(`Parser.hs:730-735`) resolves the receiver's type *at parse time* and
builds one, which this CST cannot. The walk makes the distinction
instead, and the **grammar** is what decides it rather than the member's
own type — a callback's initializer is a function specifier wherever it is
a member of something. Worth 1655 → 1663 and nine frontend rejections.

**An alias template named as an argument is spelled as written.** `tArg`
reads a `TypeIdentifier` whose type is no `TType` and falls to `TArg $
showPretty e` (`Type.hs:436-437`), so the reference displays
`Foo<callback_T_to_R_t>` where the mangle reads back
`Foo<helper.callbacks::callback_T_to_R_t>`. The *note* cannot say which
argument that was — it holds the aliased type, not the name — so the
program's own alias templates are the source, collected beside the
template names. And the fixups had a door they did not reach: an alias's
display comes from `aliased_instance` when the alias's own name carries no
mangle. Neither half moves alone; together 1663 → 1671.

**Read and not taken: `main@?lambda0` inside a mangle** (27 programs,
`template-argument-deduction.k::188`). Both sides mangle the copy
identically —
`Foo<|$uint@32@@data@closure@core@make_capture0@$@Capture@main@?lambda0|><|$uint@4|>`
— and the reference *displays* `Foo<uint32,
data.closure.core::make_capture0::$::Capture, main@?lambda0>`.
`unmangle_leaf` cannot read the leaf, because `?` is not in its word
charset, so `unmangle_text` leaves the whole mangle raw and `unmangled`
falls to the note — whose template path's leaf is the *first* copy's
mangled name, giving `Foo<|…|><uint4>`. Adding `?` to the charset is
**measured at 1671 → 1551**, and would not be enough anyway: the
component is `@main@?lambda0` where the reference prints one segment, and
a `@main@?lambda0<|$uint@4|>` elsewhere prints without its arguments. What
this row wants is `unmangleQualifiedName`'s actual rule
(`Type.hs:180-187`) — each prefix looked up in the symbol map, spelled as
an instance only where the map says it is one — which this port
approximates by the name's *shape*. Start there, not at the charset.

## The default that named an instance, and the alias that named a scalar — 2026-09-20

The last entry's work list ended on `template-param-default.k::31` with one
sentence: `kg dump instances` says the program decides **nothing**. It does,
and here is why, and the two changes that follow from it.

`helper/template_param_default.k:59` is

```
template <typename T, auto N = 10, typename U = index_t<N>>
using A2_t = S1<T[N], U>;
```

and the third default is neither a type nor a bare template name. It is a
*mention of an instance*. `crate::defaults::Bound` had `Type`, `Value` and
`Template` and no fourth case, so `default_argument` declined; and because an
undecided default stops the module, the decline took the whole program with
it. That is not a small failure mode: a single unspellable default and the
program's census is empty.

`Bound::Mention { segments, args }` carries the written head and one `Bound`
per written argument, each evaluated the way the surrounding defaults are —
through `env.ty` for a type, `ConstEval` otherwise. `elaborate::defaults`
mints it back as an `Exp::TemplateInstance` over the same qualified chain the
`Template` arm builds, which is now a `qualified_chain` helper the two arms
share. Deduction refuses a `Mention` exactly as it refuses a `Template`:
neither is a type, and guessing one keys an unrelated instance.

The corpus totals did not move — `ptdiff` 1672, `backend` 2554 — and the row
did: `::31` went from call #1102 to #1142, having decided `idx<10>` and
stopped at `S1<|$array$uint@7@10$uint@4|>`. That is a *link*, not a win, and
the discipline for a link is a test that pins it. `a_default_that_names_an_
instance_is_decided` asserts the materialised counts of a four-line
reduction; cut the `Mention` arm and the report list is **empty**, which is a
sharper red than the count it asserts.

Then the link itself. The fill mints `__kg_m0 = idx<|@10|>`, the next program
pass hands `A2_t<uint7, 10, __kg_m0>` to `h`, and `h` declined it —
`KG_ELAB_TRACE=1` prints the reason in one line:

```
File(FileId(1)): declined h.A2_t at …: cannot mint Opaque
```

`arg_shapes` gave `ArgShape::Opaque` to any argument that was not a written
built-in and not a named struct, union, class, enum, array or function. An
alias naming a *scalar* is none of those, so it travelled as nothing at all.
What should travel is the scalar: the reference's key holds the expansion,
`A2_t<uint7, 10, index_t<10>>` mangling `$array$uint@7@10$uint@4`. A written
built-in never reaches that arm — `written_builtin` takes it first — so the
arm is exactly the named case, and it is three lines.

    conformance  2500/2500 -> 2501/2501, undecidable 422 -> 421
    --strict     105 -> 104
    ptdiff       structural 1672 -> 1677, diverged 611 -> 607

The conformance line is the one worth reading twice. An assertion left the
*undecidable* bucket and passed. That bucket is the honesty mechanism, and
the only way to shrink it is to decide something that was undecided — which
is what a missing copy always is.

## The constants that needed a width — 2026-09-20

`constexpr.k::31` is `T3<(S3_size / 8 == S3_size >> 3)>`, and eighteen rows of
that file sat behind it. `kg dump instances` decided nothing for any of them.
Bisecting the argument found the whole of it in one line of the helper:

```
const auto S3_size = bitsizeof S3;
```

`(K == 8)` over `const uint32 K = 8;` folds. `(J3 == 64)` over `const auto
J3 = 64;` folds. `(J == 64)` over `const auto J = bitsizeof S;` does not, and
neither does the same constant with a written type — so it was never about
`auto`. It is about `bitsizeof`.

`FileScope` answers `bit_width_of` with `None`. It has to: a struct's layout
is the type table's to know, and the table is inferred *from* the fold. So
the constant declined, and `Db::foreign_constants` carried the decline to
every importer, and a template argument that does not fold decides no
instance.

The reference has no ordering to trip over here. `inferType` is a single
catamorphism — `inferExpType`, then `evaluateConstexpr`, then `staticControl`
at every node (`Type/Inference.hs:50`) — so `sizeOf e = tWidth (typeOf e)`
reads a type the same pass wrote a moment earlier. There is no stage at which
the fold exists and the types do not.

Here there is, and the answer is not to remove it but to run the fold a
second time on the other side of it:

* `FileScope` remembers where each declined *variable* constant's initializer
  is — range, kind, and the scope its names resolve from.
* `Db::late_constants` folds those again through `ModuleFold`, the module's
  own parse under its own converged table. Memoized on the scope by pointer,
  so a rebuilt scope invalidates it outright.
* `Db::module_instances` lays the result — and its imports' — under the
  census's environment. That is where the value is first missed.

One round, not a fixpoint: a constant whose initializer needs a width *and*
another such constant still declines. No corpus program needs two, and a
second round costs a `FileScope` rebuild per module to buy nothing measured.

The rule that matters for anyone extending this: **`Db::file_scope` must not
read any of it.** `file_scope` is what `infer_module` folds with; a table
built from a scope built from that table is a cycle, and the memo would hide
it as a stack overflow in an unrelated query.

    ptdiff   structural 1677 -> 1684, diverged 607 -> 600
    backend  2554, 44 crashes, 1834 walked — flat
    bench    keystroke 1282 ms — flat

## Where the missing copies actually are — 2026-09-20

With those landed the top of the `ptdiff` table is 172 rows of
`ParseIdentifier / ParseBaseList`: a copy the reference makes and we do not.
Grouping them by the template whose copy is missing is the useful reading,
and it is not evenly spread:

| 25 | `tuple2` | 13 | `Foo` | 10 | `optional` | 8 | `pipelined` | 7 | `c1` |

`tuple2` is `sync/atomic.k`'s `pair<T, T>`, reached through `data.fifo`, and
it reduces to nine lines with no library in them:

```
template <typename T1, typename T2> struct tuple2 { T1 first; T2 second; }
template <typename T1, typename T2> using pair = tuple2<T1, T2>;
template <typename T> inline pair<T, T> atomically((T) -> T modify) { … }
…
auto p = atomically<uint5>([](uint5 x) -> uint5 { return x; });
```

Written `pair<uint5, uint5>` works: the twin makes `struct __kg_m1` and
`using __kg_m0 = __kg_m1`, both copies, in two rounds. Calling `atomically`
with a *named function* works. Calling it with a **lambda** does not, and the
trace says why in two lines:

```
round 2 File(FileId(0)): postponed "atomically<uint5>"
DEDUCE-FAIL "atomically": deduced slot 1 of ["T", "__kg_m0", "modify"] -> Some(Type(Unresolved))
```

`higherOrderFunctions` has rewritten `atomically` in its owner's twin to three
parameters, and the call writes one. The other two are deduction's to supply,
and deduction binds the middle one — the capture type — to `TUnresolved`.
The argument it is deducing from is
`cast<Closure<decltype(__kg_m1), __kg_m1, __kg_m2>>(make_capture0())` with
`using __kg_m2 = decltype(make_capture0())` beside it, so what is unresolved
is the type of a `decltype` of a call to an `auto`-returning library function
whose return type is a struct *declared inside its own body*.

That is gaps.md's row 2 — "the `Closure` copies materialised in
`data.closure.core`" — seen from the deduction end rather than the walk end,
and it is worth writing down that the two are the same gap. The reduction
above is the smallest repro found so far and needs no library at all once
`make_capture0` is written out by hand; it belongs in whatever session picks
this up.

The `ParseIdentifier / ParseIdentifier` bucket (118) is **not** one mechanism,
and the previous entry's reading of it was too generous. Its largest members
are `higher-order-functions` (47) and `constexpr` (18), and sampling them
shows the same missing-copy story in a different disguise: where a copy is
absent our walk emits the *next* identifier, so the pair of names differs
without either being wrong about names. Only the `same_types` head of it —
four rows — is really about spelling, and it is the written attribute order a
foreign spec loses to `TAttrSet`'s ordering. Fixing that is four rows, not a
hundred and eighteen. Size a bucket by its mechanism, not by its count.

## Four passes, six passes, eight passes — 2026-09-20

The obvious explanation for the library-closure chain is that it is simply
longer than the budget. It is a long chain — `FIFO<uint32,32,…>`'s copy is
made in pass 1, its `using pointer_t = index_t<Size>` decides `index_t<32>`
which `type.stdtype` makes in pass 2, `atomically<pointer_t>` would decide in
pass 3 and `sync.atomic`'s copy would decide `tuple2<uint5,uint5>` in pass 4 —
and `MAX_PROGRAM_PASSES` is 4.

It is not the budget. Six passes and eight passes are both **byte-identical**
to four: `ptdiff` 1684 in all three. The fixpoint has converged; it has
converged on the wrong answer.

Where it stops, measured on `local-classes.k::14` (`import data.fifo`) with
four traces — the census's candidate drops, `deduceTemplateArgs`' bail-outs,
the twin names each module hands the next, and the twin text per round:

1. The census declines every one of these calls with an **arity mismatch**,
   which is by design (`resolve_guard`'s "silence 1"): `atomically` has three
   parameters after `higherOrderFunctions` and the call writes one, `first`
   has two and the call writes none. They are deduction's, not the census's.
2. `deduceTemplateArgs` over the twin declines `atomically` every pass with
   **`written arg "__kg_m20::pointer_t" not a type: Unresolved`** — the
   *written* argument, before any deduction happens.
3. And yet the same name's **declaration** is typed. The names map
   `data.fifo` hands on carries `__kg_m20::pointer_t = Type(Unsigned(5))` in
   two passes of three, and `type.stdtype`'s carries
   `__kg_m25 = Type(Unsigned(5))` — the copy of `index_t<32>`, whose width
   `uint<mux(true, 1, (clog2 32))>` folds correctly (checked on its own: it
   is `uint5`).

So the declaration is typed and the *mention* is not. That is the link, and
it is one question: `type_of_node` on a qualified member-alias mention inside
a template argument list.

A nine-line reduction with no library in it gets one pass further and shows
the shape of the answer:

```
module st { idx }
template <auto N> using idx = uint<(N > 1) ? clog2(N) : 1>;

module f { F, atomically, inc }
import st
inline auto inc(auto v) { return v + 1; }
template <typename T> inline T atomically((T) -> T modify) { … }
template <auto Size> class F { public: using pointer_t = idx<Size>;
    inline pointer_t get() { return atomically<pointer_t>(inc); } }
```

There the mention *does* resolve — but only in the **second** program pass
and the **third** round of it, and the failure then moves on to slot 1, the
closure's capture type, which needs `Closure<…>`'s own copy. Each link costs
a pass, each pass is a whole-program re-elaboration, and four are not enough
for the real chain while eight change nothing: the difference between the
reduction and `data.fifo` is what to find next.

Two smaller things fell out of the same afternoon and are worth not
re-deriving:

* A **function template** named as an argument — `atomically<pointer_t>(inc)`
  over `template <typename T> inline T inc(T)` — is spelled `inc<>` in the
  copy, and `wrappers::written_name` reads a `ScopedName` chain, so no
  wrapper is made. Seeing through an empty `TemplateInstance` gets the name
  and the wrap still declines further down, at the signature. It is also
  **not a corpus shape**: `numeric/int/operator.k`'s `increment` is
  `inline auto increment(auto a)`, abbreviated, and that one wraps fine. Left
  alone rather than landed on a shape nothing exercises.
* A use of an **alias-template instance** types as `Unresolved`, always —
  `Id<uint8>` over `template <typename T> using Id = T;` included. That is
  faithful: `infer TemplateInstanceF{} = TUnresolved` (`Type.hs:1268`). The
  reference gets a type only because `resolve` has already rewritten the
  mention to its materialised copy. Any temptation to "just substitute" here
  is a divergence from the reference's tree, not a shortcut.

## What the closure deduction is actually waiting for — 2026-09-20

One more reduction and one clause of the reference settle what the previous
entry left open. Splitting `atomically` into its own module — three files,
`st` with the alias template, `at` with the higher-order function, `f` with
the class template that calls it — reproduces `sync.atomic`'s failure
exactly: `at` materialises **nothing**, as `sync.atomic` does under
`data.fifo`.

The chain has two links, and the reductions separate them.

**Link one, the written argument.** `atomically<__kg_m20::pointer_t>` needs a
type for its written argument. In the two-module reduction it arrives in the
*second* program pass, third round; in the three-module one, likewise; in
`data.fifo` it never does, and that is the difference to chase.

**Link two, the actual.** Once the written argument resolves, the deduction
fails on slot 1 — the closure's capture. The reference says why, exactly:

```haskell
deduceType (TypeIdentifier _ (TemplateInstance a b)) (TInstance _ a' b')
    | getQualifiedName a == a' = zipWithM_ deduceArg (toList $ unfix b) (map snd b')
```

(`Type.hs:1532-1533`.) The **formal** is a written tree — `Closure<(__kg_m0,
T) -> T, modify, __kg_m0>`, the parameter `higherOrderFunctions` wrote
(`Function.hs:355-359`) — and the **actual** must be a `TInstance`. Nothing
else in `deduceType` matches a template-instance formal against an unresolved
actual except the clause below it, which binds every argument to
`TUnresolved`.

So the capture is deducible only once the *actual's* `Closure<…>` mention has
become an instance type — which in this port means its copy is materialised
in `data.closure.core` and the mention wears the alias. `data.fifo` gets
that far (`__kg_m23 = Closure<|…|>` is in its alias list); the three-module
reduction does not, because its `Closure` argument still contains an `auto`
from the abbreviated `inc`, and a key with `auto` in it decides nothing.

That is the whole shape of gaps.md row 2, and it is two independent
questions, not one:

1. why `__kg_m20::pointer_t` — a member alias of a copy, typed
   `Type(Unsigned(5))` in the names map its own module hands on — has no type
   at the *mention* inside a template argument list; and
2. how a `Closure<…>` whose arguments are not yet decided reaches
   `Ty::Instance`, which is what `deduceType`'s only usable clause requires.

Neither needs more program passes. Both were chased with four traces and a
nine-line reduction apiece, and the reductions are the thing to keep.

## The alias that stayed behind — 2026-09-20

Link two of the previous entry, chased to a line of the printer.

The three-module reduction plus `-I …/kanagawa/library` (a `kanagawa.toml`
with `[project] import-dirs`) makes the census speak plainly:

```
CENSUS postponed Closure shapes [Opaque, Opaque, Opaque]
```

All three arguments of `Closure<decltype(__kg_m1), __kg_m1, __kg_m3>` are
opaque, which is one cause, not three: `__kg_m3` has no type, so
`decltype(__kg_m1)` has none either, because `__kg_m1`'s own parameter is
typed `__kg_m3`. The twin reads

```
inline uint5 __kg_m1(__kg_m3 __kg_m4, uint5 v) { … }      // module scope
class __kg_m2 { … inline pointer_t get() {
    using __kg_m3 = decltype(make_capture0());            // inside the body
    return atomically<…>(cast<Closure<decltype(__kg_m1), __kg_m1, __kg_m3>>(…)); } }
```

`__kg_m1` is at module scope and `__kg_m3` is inside a function body. The
first cannot see the second, and `data.fifo`'s twin has exactly this shape.

**The reference does the same thing and gets away with it.** `moveFunctions`
hoists `Function`, `Template`-of-`Function` and `Class` and *not* `Alias`
(`Function.hs:121-127`), so the capture alias stays in the body there too —
`kg-oracle --tree --passes 8 --template-passes 4` on the same reduction shows
`AliasF { declScopeName = ["@data@function", …], declName = "?lambda0$capture" }`
left where it was. What the reference does differently is **spell the
reference to it in full**:

```
ScopedNameF … "@data@function" … "constant" … "$" … "?lambda0$capture"
```

— the chain `qualifyName`/`fixScopedName` builds when `moveFunctions` moves a
declaration away from what it names (`:35`, and this port's
`rewrite::move_functions` module comment).

This port builds that chain too (`lambdas::capture_type_ident`) and then
**prints the leaf**. `pretty.rs`'s `ScopedName` arm suppresses a prefix
except for five named cases — a resolved instance, a member instance, an
import alias, a written qualifier — and a synthesized function-body scope is
none of them. So a chain the reference needs becomes `__kg_m3`, a name
nothing at module scope declares.

Two ways out, and the choice is the next session's:

* **Print the chain.** Add the case, and the pool must then alias the whole
  chain rather than its leaf — as it already does for
  `__kg_m16 = data.closure.core::make_capture0::$::Capture`, which is the
  same shape reached from the other side. This is what the reference does.
* **Hoist the alias with the function.** Simpler, and a divergence in the
  *position* of a synthesized declaration — which `xtask ir`'s lambda ledger
  is blind to by construction, so it would need its own pin.

Neither is a one-liner and both are measurable: `ptdiff`'s top bucket is 172
missing copies, of which `tuple2` (25), `optional` (10), `pipelined` (8) and
`async_then_void` (4) are this chain.

One warning for whoever picks it up: a reduction of this needs the real
library on the import path. Without it our own `higherOrderFunctions` rewrite
still mints `Closure<…>` and `make_capture0()` into the twin, the census
reports `dropped Closure (no template)`, and the failure looks like a
different bug. And do not name your test module's function `atomically`:
`sync/atomic.k` declares one, `IrTemplates::build` marks a name declared in
two modules ambiguous, and the census then drops *that* too.

## Four rows, and one that invented an error — 2026-09-20 later

Four landings after the pass-budget entry, each small and each measured.

**An instance in qualifier position takes its template's defaults.**
`fill_type_defaults` reached a mention through its `TypeIdentifier` or
`QualifiedIdentifier` wrapper, and a prefix has neither — it is a bare
`TemplateInstance` under a `ScopedName`. `C<uint32>::addr` therefore stayed
one argument short of `template <typename T, template <typename> typename TT
= A>`, the census declined it on arity, and the module elaborated **nothing
at all**. The same program written `static C<uint32> bar;` filled and made
both copies. Filling at the prefix is idempotent by construction: `desugar`
is bottom-up, so the wrapper above an already-filled instance sees a full
list. **+22 backend agreements** — the largest single move of the day, from
three lines.

**A template-template parameter's kind may mention a bound parameter.**
`resolve_kind` declines any kind mentioning a parameter other than as a bare
name, because its other caller uses the answer *as a type*. The
template-template arm discards the answer, and `(T) -> uint32` with `T` bound
to `bool` is decidable. Then the same arm again for a *value*: `uint<N>`
beside `auto N`, where no `Ty` binds an `auto` and the argument's folded value
is what says the kind is decided.

**A template name two modules declare resolves through the imports.**
`IrTemplates` is keyed by simple name across the whole program and books such
a name ambiguous. That is right for two declarations one module can see, and
wrong for `a1.b1.c1.c1::c1` beside `a1.b2.c1.c1::c1`, which no module imports
both of. The census printed its verdict in one line —
`CENSUS dropped c1 (no template)` — and the consequence was larger than the
mention: with nothing decided there, `a1.b1.c1.c1` never became a *target*,
so the module that owns the template was never elaborated at all.

**And the one that went back.** The same rule has a second half in the
reference: an import with an alias contributes its names *only* under the
alias (`findInImport`, `SymbolTable.hs:276-278`), so `a1<5>` beside
`A5::a1<bool>` is `a1.a1`'s and not ambiguous. Filtering aliased imports out
of the visible set moved `diverged` 591 → 590 and **rejected 0 → 1**: with
`a1<5>` decided, `imports.k::36` reached `templateTypeCheck`, which resolved
the *alias-qualified* `A5::a1<bool>` by its leaf alone, found `a1.a1`'s
`template <auto N>`, and reported "The type can't be used as an argument for
non-type template parameter" on a correct program.

An invented error is the one outcome this port trades nothing for, so the
half went back. It is right, and it is blocked behind a bug the ambiguity was
hiding: `template_type_check` resolves an alias-qualified mention by simple
name. `Templates` already carries `visible_through_import` and
`with_visible` for exactly this question; nothing on that path asks it yet.
That is the next step of this row, and it has to land *before* the alias
filter, not after.

## The type the language cannot spell — 2026-09-20 later

`memory.k::17` is 32 programs, and it is the print-and-reparse route meeting
its first genuinely *unspellable* type.

```
template <typename T, auto N>
using memory_ecc = [[memory, ecc(make_ecc<T>)]] T[N];
```

with `T = uint32[10]` is an attributed array of an array. The grammar gives an
attributed array exactly one dimension — `memoryAttr type3 "[" e "]"`,
`Parser.hs:529` — and `type3` admits a path, a built-in and a `decltype`, none
of which the substituted element is. There is no parenthesised type. Checked
rather than assumed: `kg-oracle --errors` on
`using C = [[memory]] uint32[16][10];` rejects it at the second `[`, the same
token this parser rejects it at.

The reference never has to spell it. `instantiateTemplates` substitutes into a
tree. This port prints the twin and parses it back, so the substitution has to
survive text — and it did not:

```
== library/data/memory.k
materialised 2  foreign 2  ...  twin parse errors 6
pairs 0  refused 0  read back: written 0 absent 0 ...
```

**A twin that does not parse abandons its whole module.** `data.memory` lost
six copies to one alias, and with them `make_ecc`, `make_optional` and
everything downstream of its twin. The cost of one unspellable copy was not
one copy.

So the twin's parse takes any number of dimensions on an attributed array
(`kg_parser::Parser::twin`, reached only through `kg_syntax::parse_twin`,
which only the elaboration calls). Divergence #31, and it is narrow by
construction: no source can write the shape and the source parser still
refuses it, so no source program's verdict moves.

**And that alone rejected three correct programs.** With the module unlocked,
`memory.k::17`'s `static assert(decltype(read()) == ecc<uint32[10]>)` began to
*fail*. The type was flat — `TArray attrs uint32 [16, 10]` — and `tElement`'s
ECC clause reads the **last** dimension (`Type.hs:930-935`), so `mem[0]` was
an array where the reference has `ecc<uint32[10]>`. The reference's
substitution leaves the shape nested, `TArray attrs (TArray [] uint32 [10])
[16]`, and the inference nests it here for the same reason. An attributed
array of more than one dimension is *always* a nested one, because the
grammar has no other reading of it.

The lesson is the ordering. The parse relaxation on its own is a regression —
three `expected:0` programs rejected — and only with the nesting is it a gain.
`ptdiff`'s `rejected` column is what said so, within one run of landing it;
without that column the conformance number would have moved the other way and
the cause would have been two changes away.

    conformance  2501/2501 -> 2502/2502, undecidable 421 -> 420
    --strict     104 -> 103
    ptdiff       1693 -> 1695 structural, diverged 591 -> 589

## A string's holes are expressions — 2026-09-22

Divergence #15 said an interpolated string had to stay one token because
"`Event::Token` can only merge raw tokens, never split one". That was true
and beside the point: a *lexer* that splits needs no split event. What the
lexer had declined to know was where a hole ends, and that takes brackets,
not the expression grammar — a mode stack of string and hole frames, and a
brace count inside a hole (`Lexer::string_piece`). `"a{x}b"` is now
`STRING_TEXT "a`, `{`, `x`, `}`, `STRING_END b"`; a string with no hole is
still one `STRING`. The parser builds `INTERPOLATED_STRING` /
`INTERPOLATION` / `FORMAT_SPEC` (`Parser.hs:883-903`), each hole an ordinary
expression, the format kept as the tokens before the hole's `}` so pass 0
keeps judging it character by character where the reference does.

**Two landings, because the second half was a different question.**

*The tree* (8df1d80). Everything a CST node gets, a hole now gets: pass 9
judges its names like any other (its text scanner is gone, and so is the
import-use scan's), inference types it, rename rewrites a name used in it
rather than refusing. Every gate was byte-identical. One self-report moved
the wrong way — `ir`'s carried-home line, 62 → 65 raised — and the A/B
said why: pass 9 now judged `N` in `{replicate<N-2>("-")}` inside a *copy*
(risc-v's trace, `bank/schedule`'s `Banks`), because the twin printer copied
a string's text verbatim, unsubstituted. Declined, so invisible; still a
false error waiting for the day it is carried.

*The IR.* `Exp::Interpolated` holds the reference's segments — the text
before each hole, and the hole's expression, `=`, alignment and format —
with the holes as ordinary children, so every rewrite reaches them and the
printer prints them from the tree. A hole-free string stays
`Exp::InterpolatedString`, which is what `interpolatedStringPre` makes of it
anyway. The backend walk walks each hole as a node, in `cataM` order (every
hole's expression, then its alignment, before the list opens), echoes
`{x=}` for a name (`showPretty` of anything else declines rather than guess
its spacing), and fills a missing precision from `sizeOf` as
`updatePrecision` does — which the old walk never did: it sent 0 for `{x:x}`.

    carried home   62 -> 46 raised (65 after the tree alone): copies print substituted
    oracle diff    116/124 -> 122/124 node-for-node; the "diverge at an
                   interpolated string" booking is gone, so a divergence
                   there now fails the gate
    ptdiff         1696 -> 1726 structural, declined 138 -> 110
    backend        2587 -> 2617 agreements, 1864 -> 1893 walked;
                   hole declines 100 -> 0 (one echo shape left in ptdiff)
    everything else unchanged: conformance 2503/2503, strict 102,
    errors 24, corpus, fmt-check, 1590 tests

**What the walk had been leaning on.** Two programs went structural →
diverged, `statement::11` and `auto-placeholder::22`, both at `print<uint1>`'s
`__print("{x}")`. The old hole walk typed a local by its *declaration*; the
new one asks the table, and the table had nothing — the twin's inference
never decides `static if (decltype(x) == string)` in that copy, so it walks
neither branch, and nothing in the live one is typed. The reference decides
it and types the branch. So a name the table left untyped that is a local
of the enclosing function is typed by its declaration
(`Walker::local_type`, `typeOf (NamedValueF a) = typeOf a`), and both came
back with no program moving the other way. It is a fallback over a real gap
— an undecided `static if` in a copy leaves its live branch untyped for
*every* expression in it, not just names — and the gap is the thing to
close, in the twin's `dead` ranges.

**Left.** Pass 18 still reads holes through its text scanner; asking the
table at the hole's own node is what lifts its declines. An echoed hole
over anything but a name declines in the walk. And an attribute string
with a `{` — `stringLiteral` reads it as text — is one `LITERAL` over split
pieces; no corpus attribute writes one.

## A `static if` over a type, decided where the reference decides it — 2026-09-22

`unit::fixture<Foo>()` gates 46 corpus programs (every test that runs
`unit::test<1>(unit::fixture<…>())`), and all 46 declined at the same
place: `deduce: Unresolved` at `library/test/unit.k:162:8`, the `auto`
return of `fixture`. (That location is new too: the compat binary's decline
line printed a raw `FileRange { file: FileId(88) … }`, and now prints
`path:line:col`.) The body is

```
static if (decltype(Fixture::run) == () -> bool) { return []{…}; }
else { return [](unit::tag_t tag){…}; }
```

and the chain to the answer had four links, each its own bug.

1. **The predicate is over types, and nobody folded it after typing.** The
   twin decides its `static if`s once, *before* inference, with a constant
   folder that cannot see a type; `staticControl . evaluateConstexpr .
   inferExpType` (`Inference.hs:47`) folds after typing. `type_table` now
   re-decides through the converged table (`fold::typed_env`, which already
   had `evalBinaryType`) and, when that decides something new, resumes the
   fixpoint over the extra dead ranges. `print<uint1>`'s `decltype(x) ==
   string` decided at once; the fixture's did not, because —
2. **`Foo::run`'s type was `Unresolved` where the twin looked.** Its
   parameter is `unit::tag_t`, an alias to `newtype<uint32>`: resolved only
   by the *root's* twin, and the root walks after `test.unit`. Each program
   pass rebuilt `finished` from the base maps, so `test.unit`'s twin could
   never see it. A pass now starts from the previous pass's overlaid maps,
   and the loop goes on while they still gain resolved names
   (`ModuleTypes::resolved_count`, which an overlay can only raise).
3. **The twin knew; the tree did not.** A typed decision lived only in the
   table's dead ranges, so the IR kept the `static if`, `moveFunctions`
   kept deferring the lambda inside it, and no `Closure` copy was decided.
   Each round now hands the previous twin's typed verdicts to
   `staticControl` over the tree (`static_control_with`, keyed by the
   `StaticIf`'s `Src` — an id does not survive `resolve` rebuilding the
   node), a pending verdict keeps the route going for one more round, and
   `round_prefix` hoists the lambda the splice exposed — which is the
   reference's own order: `desugarLambdas` inside the `static if` on one
   iteration, `moveFunctions` after `inferType` spliced it, on the next.
4. **The hoist re-rooted the declaration but not its uses.** After a
   round's rename, a chain spells the parent by its alias (`__kg_m51`) and a
   declaration's scope spells it as declared (`fixture<|…|>`), so
   `fixScopedName` and `removeNestedScope` compared two spellings and matched
   nothing. Both now compare un-aliased — and that is the half
   `docs/patches/hoisted-lambda-scope.patch` was missing: the patch
   re-rooted *declaration* scopes and cost four `higher-order-functions`
   programs a wrapper parameter the backend could not find; the chain half
   alone costs the same four for the mirror reason. Together they agree, and
   the patch is now in the tree (`move_one`'s `item_qname_original`).

Two things the links exposed, both fixed:

* **An invented error, reproducible without the library.** A member of a
  class-template copy another module made — `call<helper<4>>` copied in `h`,
  its `f.run()` naming the root's `helper<|4|>` — read `Undefined`, because
  `Declarations::method` treated every miss on a copy as "no such member".
  It is that only where the copy is seen; the member is now looked up in
  every module's map (`Imported::in_any_module`) and an unseen copy is
  unknown. HEAD reported "Symbol name not in scope: `run`" on a program the
  reference accepts (`tests/elaborate.rs`,
  `a_member_of_a_copy_another_module_made_is_not_missing`).
* **A pass-8 verdict must not reach pass 7.** `static if (bitsizeof
  Foo<uint32> == 32) extern Invalid;` is decided by pass 8, and what it
  splices is invisible to `externClasses`, which ran first
  (`extern-class.k::49`). Typed verdicts apply to statements — a `static if`
  inside a function body — and never to declarations.

And one that is not: `local-classes.k::15,16` (and
`higher-order-functions.k::126`) declined before and now walk to a backend
error. In the copy of a *local* class's member template, the lambda's `x` is
spelled `main@Foo::x` where the reference captured `$this.x` — hoisting the
local class out of `main` first re-roots its member references, and the
lambda's later hoist no longer sees them as members. Pre-existing; the
closure used to hide it by never being decided. No agreement was lost.

each found by following one program (`test/logic/auto_inline.k`) until the

   (`Cx::literal_fits`). Two narrowings came out of the gates, not the
   design: a literal `validateArg` would reject makes no copy in the
   reference (`c.Bar<uint16, 6>(true)` over `T x`, `T = bool`,
   `elaborate::seam_tests` went red), and a fully written call has nothing
   to deduce and is the census's to decide from the written list, which
   re-stamps `10` as `uint8` (`function-template.k::13,14,16` went
   structural → diverged, the copy's `N` typed `uint4`).
2. **The declared closure type was read in the wrong file.** `test`'s
   function-typed formal, `(__kg_m12, unit::tag_t) -> void`, is a node of
   `test.unit`'s twin, and `closure_function_type` asked the *caller's*
   table about it — which never typed it, so the check was undecidable and
   the call declined. A finished twin now keeps its table (`TwinRoot::
   types`, `Round::types` an `Arc`), `Templates::with_tables` hands them to
   the check, and a formal is read in its own file.
3. **`x || true` never folded.** `evalBinaryBool _ True Or` is guarded on
   `tIsBool (typeOf x)`, which kg-const asks as `operand_type` — and no
   environment answered it, so `((tag & mask) == tag) || … || (param::tag
   == 0 && …)` in `test_case` (`library/test/unit.k:75`) stood. `WidthEnv`
   now answers it from the table.
4. **A twin's local constants were folded before its table existed.**
   `const auto T = Flags << (bitsizeof id_t + bitsizeof group_t)` needs a
   width; the twin's file scope declined it, and nothing retried.
   `fold::refold_declined` re-folds a twin's declined constants against its
   converged table until nothing new folds — the per-twin `late_constants`.
   The retry had to learn the declared type's cast too
   (`castIntegralConstexpr`; `DeclinedInit` carries the type's node), which
   `late_constants` had silently skipped: `const uint4 c = 20` re-folded to
   `20`, not `4`. `const auto` keeps the literal, as the reference does.
5. **`cast<id_t>(1)` never folded.** Two gates: `int_cast_target` read only
   a spelled `uintN`, and the `typeResolved` gate (`every_name_is_a_known_
   constant`) refused any named type. `WidthEnv` answers both from the
   table — a type-position subtree counts when the table resolved it, every
   value name still asks the file scope (`WidthEnv::names_resolved`).
   The file scope itself is unchanged: it cannot see a type.
6. **A qualified alias displayed as its spelling.** A function handed to a
   copy's owner is aliased by the spelling `.test.unit::f`; `unrename_ty`
   read an alias back to that spelling, so a `Closure` copy's `TNameArg`
   displayed `.test.unit::fixture<…>@?lambda1`. It now reads back the path
   the pool recorded, each segment un-aliased.

Where it stops: the walk reaches the backend, which says `Error 24 …
Class/Memory local variables are not supported` at `unit.k:63` — the walk
diverges one call earlier, where the reference makes a `make_capture1<…>`
copy in `data.closure` for `test`'s wrapper and this port does not. That is
the "missing copies" row, reached now from a program that used to stop four
links before it. Four programs move from declined to that backend
disagreement; none moves the other way.

    ptdiff   1732 -> 1735 structural (3 up, none down)
    backend  2629 -> 2632 agreements, 1904 -> 1907 walked; 513 declined
    errors, conformance, strict, corpus, fmt, ir: unchanged (24; 2504; 101)
    tests    1592 -> 1594

Found on the way and not fixed: `static assert(5000 == cast<id_t>(5000))` is
"static assertion failed" in the reference (`scratchpad/ca/c.k`) and silent
here — pass 16's typed fallback is limited to type comparisons by design,
each widening needing its own oracle evidence. This is that evidence for a
cast through an alias; no corpus assertion needs it yet.

**The pass budget, measured again.** The wrapper `test` builds around its
closure (`make_capture1(fn)`'s `Closure`) is decided in `test.unit`'s fourth
round of the *fourth* program pass, and handed to `data.closure.core` with no
pass left to make it. Six passes make it: `auto_inline.k`'s first divergence
moves from call #521 to #3259 (a hoisted lambda's name mangled without its
module namespace, `test<|…|>@?lambda0` where the reference has
`@test@unit@test<|…|>@?lambda0`). But the whole corpus gains one backend
agreement, and the worst keystroke goes 1384 → 2038 ms; eight passes are
identical to six. The budget stays at four. What would make a fifth pass
affordable is the lever this journal has named since 2026-09-20: phase 2
re-elaborates every target module on every pass.

## The copy-order row: a leaf spelled through an alias — 2026-09-22

The roadmap's third queue item — "`higher-order-functions.k::7` emits one
module's two `Closure` copies in the opposite order … the comparison
unaliases, and what it compares after that is where to look" — is one line
of `ExpOrd::name`. The two `Closure` copies differ in their capture type, a
leaf the owner's twin cannot spell (`mint_leaf`), whose alias's original is
the type's *spelling* — and that spelling is itself written through the
alias of the copy it belongs to: `data.closure::__kg_m61::$::Capture` for
`make_capture1<|$uint@32|>`'s. Un-aliasing the leaf gave that text, and the
comparison then ordered two captures by the order their copies were minted
in. `ExpOrd::name` now reads each `::` segment of such a spelling back too,
so `make_capture1<|$bool|>`'s capture orders first, as the reference's key
does. (Re-spelling the leaf from an un-renamed type fixed the order too, and
broke the mangle and the walk, which read the spelling's segments as
names; the comparison is the only reader that wanted the other form.)

    ptdiff  1735 -> 1742 structural (9 up, 2 down: `higher-order-functions.k
            ::65,66`, where the reference orders two captures by the
            `ScopedName` chain's *scope* field first — a leaf has one
            identifier and no chain to compare; they matched by mint order)
    backend 2632 (unchanged — order moves no verdict); every other gate unchanged

## A module path is one lexeme — 2026-09-22

`dotSepName` (`Parser/Lexer.hs:230-233`) is `lexeme $ try (ident' … \`sepBy1\`
char '.')`: characters, no space inside, and a `try` around the whole. This
parser rebuilt the name from `IDENT . IDENT` tokens with trivia allowed
between them, so `import a1 .a1` imported `a1.a1` where the reference imports
`a1` (and fails to find `a1.k`), and `import a1. a1` parsed where the
reference fails the whole name at its start, "expecting module name"
(`imports.k::117-119`). `module_path` now joins a dot only glued on both
sides, a `-` part likewise, and reads a glued dot with no glued component
after it as the `try`'s failure — the error at the name's start.
`Parser::nth_glued` / `nth_glued_back` are the two adjacency questions the
character-level lexemes need.

    conformance 2504/2504 -> 2507/2507, strict 101 -> 98
    errors      24 disagreements (unchanged), 562 -> 564 agree, 55 -> 52 silent

## `Foo<…>` is a template only if the parser already knows one — 2026-09-22

`prefixedScopedNameAndSymbol` (`Parser.hs:652-690`) reads `<` as a template
argument list only when `findSymbol` returns a template *at that point of
the parse*; otherwise `Foo` is a name and `<` the comparison. This parser
decides `<` by lookahead alone, so it accepted three shapes the reference
rejects (gaps.md A4): a template declared later in the module
(`function-template.k::17`), a plain function (`::8`), and a template the
module declares inside a braced top-level `static if` — a block, so a scope
(`dependent-template.k::7`). `not_a_template_yet` (pass 9's parse-time half)
now reports each, "`Foo`: undefined template", booked against the
reference's parse error (divergence #7).

Two false positives on the first run fixed the shape of the rule, and both
are in its doc comment. `Do<a && b>(10)` over a *variable* `Do` is `(Do < a)
&& (b > 10)` and compiles (`helper/dependent_template.k`), so only a single
argument that cannot extend a comparison — a type, a literal, a bare name —
is judged; `Foo < uint32 > (10)` is no expression and `Foo < N > (x)` a
non-associative chain. And an *unbraced* `static if (c) template …`
declares into the module (`static-if.k::34`).

    conformance 2507/2507 -> 2511/2511, strict 98 -> 94
    errors      24 (unchanged), 564 agree, 52 -> 48 silent
    backend     2632 -> 2639 agreements (frontend 40 -> 37: programs whose
                reference verdict is this rejection)

**And the receiver half.** `recv.M<…>` without `template` is a member
template only when the parser can find `M` in `recv`'s class
(`Parser.hs:668-680`): not when `recv`'s declared type is a `typename`
parameter — the dependent name `template` exists for
(`dependent-template.k::4`) — nor when `recv` is declared only inside a
block the call is not in (`::2,11`). `receiver_not_yet_a_class`, same shape
guard. Conformance 2511 → 2514, strict 94 → 91, silent 48 → 45, backend
2639 → 2642; gaps.md A4's "`template` keyword on a dependent member" and
"a template declared under `static if`" are both closed by the pair.

**An initializer list is not a fold.** Pass 10's `fold_divergent` guard stays
silent over any subtree the file-scope folder can fold, since the
reference's tree would hold a literal there. `{1, 2}` folds here to an
aggregate value, but `evaluateConstexpr` has no clause for an initializer
list — the reference keeps it — so `{1, 2} + 4`'s "Invalid operands to
binary expression: `{uint1, uint2}` and `uint3`", which kg-ty already
computed, was never reported (`initializer-list.k::35`). The list and a
designator are now skipped; their elements are still judged. Conformance
2514 → 2515, strict 91 → 90, errors agree 564 → 565.
