## The audit, acted on — 2026-09-23

`docs/history/audit-2026-09-22.md` (2026-09-22) was a read-only assessment with fourteen ranked
recommendations. This entry records what landed, what was decided on the
way, and what was deliberately left. The code changes are one commit each;
the reasons are here.

| Audit item | Landed | Note |
|---|---|---|
| D1, `g(x < y, z > -1)` | `a6c15be` | a binding-aware re-read in `kg-syntax`: a `<` after a name the tree proves a value is marked a comparison and the file parsed again |
| D2, D3, D4, §4.3 | merge `aa73019` | the language server: queued invalidation, `catch_unwind`, cancellation, coalescing, in-order and tiered publication |
| D5 | `26a12f2` | strings reach C as `withCAString` pokes them — low byte, stop at NUL — on both sides of `ptdiff` |
| D6 | not done | see below |
| D7, D8, §6.3 ratchets, §7 | merge `6f8a735`, blessed `1352c88` | per-item ratchets in `baseline.json`; `gates.sh` is red on any regression |
| D9 | `d8917c9` | one spelling of `data'closure'core'Closure`; the closure's *alias* stays apart |
| §6.2.1 pass budget | `5b14f67` | batch runs to the fixpoint; the editor keeps four |
| §6.3 oracle flags | `82f7270` | all 834 must-reject snippets graded |
| §6.3 fuzzing, reduction | merge `c32a349` | `fuzz --differential`, `reduce` |
| §6.4 step 1 | `1924fd3`, `d8917c9`, `be5f6fb` | one alias predicate, one closure path, one registration index for "what did the parser bind this name to" |
| §4.5 | `7a3982f` | stale self-descriptions, dead `TyInterner`, a scratch path |
| §9 | `dcb307a`, `45ac8a1` | `status-md` renders the headline; this journal's index |

**The pass budget.** Measured before deciding: 111 of the 304 library and
test files need five to ten program passes to converge, none approaches
the guard of 64, and running every batch path to the fixpoint moves the
backend gate by one agreement and costs it 30 s. The four-pass bound stays
where latency is the point — the server and the keystroke bench — and an
elaboration that stops at a bound says so (`kg check` prints a note, the
server logs it). Correctness first, and the bound as an explicit, visible
trade in the one place it belongs.

**What the ratchets caught on their first run.** `repoint` blessed in a
worktree disagreed with main on 21 tests (+11/-10) while its total moved by
one — the "9 up, 2 down" case the audit described, in its first hour.
Main's runs agree with each other exactly; the runner is not
location-independent. CLAUDE.md now says to bless from main only.

**What the differential fuzzer found.** Seven false alarms on its first
run — shapes we reject that the full reference compiler accepts — and nine
more on the second, once every snippet was gradable. Nearly all are one
fact: `parseSymbol p` runs the whole declaration parser and registers the
name afterwards (`SymbolTable.hs:194-207`), and the parser rewrites each
name to what `findSymbol` finds uniquely at that point. So a variable's
initializer does not see the variable, a plain function's body does not see
the function (a function *template*'s does — probed), a parameter's type
sees only earlier parameters, a template's parameter list does not see the
template, and a local declared later in a block is not yet there. The first
fix was a per-reference ancestor walk in kg-ty; it fixed its targets and
*introduced* a false alarm (`Foo x;` before `Foo Foo = …`), which the
second fuzzer run found and a session-start build confirmed was new. The
replacement is the index `Declarations` now builds in the walk that files
every declaration (`Registered`: key, scope region, registration point),
queried once per reference through `SymbolEnv::type_of_symbol_as_parsed`.
It is exact where the text is in parse order and deliberately off in a
twin, whose text is re-sorted and whose hoisted functions lose qualifiers.
Four false alarms remain open, each in a lookup of its own (gaps.md §G).

The lesson is the one CLAUDE.md already states for gates, applied to
fixes: a fix's specification is a hypothesis. A differential instrument
that grades the mutated neighbourhood of a fix, not just its repro, is what
caught the regression.

**Left, and why:**

- **D6, the backend in a worker process.** 42 corpus programs abort with
  "Rust cannot catch foreign exceptions". The xtask gates already isolate
  each program in its own process; for `kg build` the right shape is a
  worker process, and it is a design of its own (how the walk's trace is
  shipped, how a decline is reported). Next in line after the fuzzer's
  open rows.
- **§4.2 memoized per-module base check, early cutoff, once-per-program
  `Templates::of`.** Performance; `Templates::of` is deliberately
  per-module (it swaps in every other module's twin). By the
  correctness-first rule this waits until the frontend is complete, and
  the pass budget no longer depends on it.
- **§6.4 steps 2–5, inference on the IR.** Scheduled deliberately, per the
  audit, once the strict curve flattens.
- **Backend codes folded into `conformance`.** `conformance.rs` is the
  scoreboard and off-limits; the combined number, if wanted, belongs in the
  ratchet's summary, and is the owner's call.
- **The output gate (§6.1 rung 6).** No walked program exports a class yet,
  so it would be empty; it is also where the owner's decision below bites.
- **§8 developer layers** (diagnostic sub-codes, a real renderer, code
  actions, the VS Code untitled scheme, a loud formatter failure). Not
  started.

**A decision for the owner, from §6.1:** does output parity for `kg build`
mean byte-identical `.sv`, or identical modulo source locations? That
choice decides whether span agreement (divergence #25, 93.4%) is a gap to
close or a booking.

## The backend's crashes were the walk's untyped nodes — 2026-09-23

At the start of the day 42 corpus programs aborted inside
`libkanagawa-backend` ("Rust cannot catch foreign exceptions"). Every one
was a call sequence the reference never makes, and almost all were the same
thing: **a node reaching the backend without the `SetNodeType` the
reference gives it**, where the table left it unresolved and the walk's
fallbacks fired only for nodes the table had never keyed. One family at a
time, each with a walk test proven red:

| Shape | Reference clause | Crashes cleared |
|---|---|---|
| an enum based on an alias (`enum Foo : DWORD`) | `checkEnumBaseType` respells the base as its integer type (`TypeCheck.hs:201-203`) | 12 (`enum.k`, the RISC-V ISA) |
| an unsuffixed literal the table left unresolved (a declaration in a spliced top-level `static if`) | `inferIntLiteralType Nothing i` | 20 |
| `x++`/`x += y` over a `static if` local or a folded constant | `inferBinaryOp` over the operands' types | 3 |
| a folded `byteoffsetof` dimension | the fold's untyped literal, typed next round | 1 |
| a value argument `validateArg` stamped (`Bar<int32, -10>`) | `inferIntLiteralType (Just t)` | 1 |
| a product and its `return` in a hoisted local function | `inferBinaryOp`; `tUnConst $ typeOf a` | 1 |
| `default = { f };` | `checkDesignatedInitializer` (`TypeCheck.hs:69-71`) — a frontend error we lacked | 2 |

The walk's `operand_type` is now "the reference's type for this node,
recursively": the table's when it resolved one, else the literal rules, a
folded name's literal, a local's declared type, `inferBinaryOp` over the
operands. It patches over inference gaps in the one place the backend reads
types; the gaps themselves (why a spliced `static if` block leaves its
literals unresolved) remain inference's to close.

Two frontend clauses fell out of following the chain further:

- **`removeNestedScope`** (`Constexpr.hs:358-370`): a decided `static if`'s
  braced branch loses its `$quasiN`, so `const uint32 y = 10;` inside one is
  the file's `y`. The constant folder now iterates fold → decide → re-key →
  fold. `static assert(y == 11)` over it was silent; it now fails as the
  reference's does.
- **A fold keeps a typed operand's type** (`typedIntLiteral $ inferBinaryOp
  op a b`, `Constexpr.hs:200-202`). The stamp was asked of
  `ConstEnv::binary_op_type`, which no environment implemented, so every
  such fold was untyped — `0u16 << 16` lost its `uint32`.
  `ConstEnv::binary_value_type` answers from the folded operands with
  kg-ty's width algebra (`infer_binary_op_values`). Keeping the type exposed
  the clause that drops it again: `validate Auto (IntLiteralF _ i) =
  IntLiteralF Nothing i` (`TypeCheck.hs:283`), which a copy decided inside
  another copy never applied.

And the `unit::test` chain the budget entry described moved: a closure now
names its function by the declaration's qualified name (`TNameArg` is
`getQualifiedName`, so `@test@unit` in front of a hoisted lambda), and
`validateArg`'s stamp now reaches a *deduced* call's written value
arguments (`test_case<Test, Group, Flags>` over `flags_t Flags` is `0u16`).
Five whole files (`counter.k`, `auto_inline.k`, `initializer_list.k`, two
export-class tests) got the reference's backend verdict.

**The ratchet earned its keep three more times.** The first cut of the
deduced-call stamps cost five programs (their walk now reached an untyped
shift and declined); the first cut of the typed fold re-folded without
widths in the twin and cost the same five; the auto-strip was needed
because the typed fold cost `literal-operand.k::0`. Each showed as "N newly
failing" while the totals looked fine or better.

Merged from worktrees the same day: the backend in a worker process (D6;
`kg build` and `kanagawa` record the walk, decline before touching the
library, and replay into a worker whose C++ exception is exit 3 naming the
call — `xtask backend` counts it a crash), and `evaluateConstexpr`'s
argument splice (`Constexpr.hs:133-151`): an alias argument is mangled as
what it names, a const function variable as the function.

    session start -> now:
    conformance 2515 -> 2518/2518, strict 90 -> 87,
    errors 24/565/44 (742 graded) -> 28/614/81 (834 graded),
    ptdiff 1742 -> 1780, backend 2643 -> 2689 (crash 42 -> 1), repoint 27 -> 29

The last crash, `memory::19`, is an internal error the backend catches

## One library copy, four links, 62 programs — 2026-09-23 (later)

The backend's largest decline bucket was `deduce: Unresolved at
library/data/function.k:66:8` — 114 programs, one site: `compose2`'s `auto`
return, in the copy `helper/higher_order_functions.k`'s own
`compose2(increment, add)` makes. Every program importing that helper
walks the copy, and the copy's return type — the closure over its
lambda — never resolved. Following it took four links, each a real
divergence with a test red without it:

1. **A closure argument was spelled as its show.** The copy's
   `make_capture2(f, g)` is deduced over two closures; `data.function`
   cannot spell `data.closure.core::Closure`, so `mint_leaf` minted an
   alias whose original was `show_unmangled(closure)` — `[capture]
   function` — and the mangler read the copy's name back as
   `make_capture2<|@@[data@closure@core@…] …|>`, a function nothing
   declares. A closure is now spelled as its copy (`typ (TClosure _ _ _
   s) = typeIdentifier' s`, `Type.hs:1633`), and the call names the copy
   `data.closure` actually holds.
2. **The copy lives in a module `data.function` does not import.**
   `data.function` imports nothing; its lambdas reach `data.closure` only
   through what `desugarLambdas` mints, and the reference looks such a
   name up in its one whole-program map. A twin now answers an alias that
   names an instance (`<|`) from the one module whose elaborated map
   declares it (`Imports::copy_anywhere`) — unique hits only, aliases being
   minted once per program.
3. **The hoisted lambda's capture parameter** is the copy's own local
   alias, told apart from every other copy's `?lambda0$capture` by the
   function the lambda came out of. The lookup took the scope's first
   segment as that function, which in a namespaced module is the
   namespace: the disambiguation had never worked in the library. Nothing
   in the walk reads that parameter's type (the corpus measures the same
   either way), but the lambda's body does — "Invalid conversion" inside
   `compose`'s lambda was silence (`kg-oracle --errors` agrees now).
4. **Two `static for` loops declaring one name.** Walking further exposed
   three crashes (`test/logic/test_cases_{13,22,27}.k`,
   `parse_tree.cpp:1266`, `assert(_type)`): the type table keys leave
   `$quasiN` out, so both loops' `x` land on one key, which `insert`
   poisons, and every `x + 1` went to the backend untyped. The key stays;
   a poisoned local is now resolved by position — the innermost block that
   contains the mention and declares it before it — which is what the
   block's `$quasiN` scope gives (`Declarations::in_its_block`). In a twin
   too: the printer reorders declarations, never a block's statements.

And one unrelated clause on the way: a **template-template parameter's
default fills a deduced call** (`Fn1()` over `TT = S1` is `Fn1<S1>`,
`tArg e@QualifiedIdentifier{} = TNameArg`), minted as `TArg::Name` typed
`TTemplate`, which `shape_of_targ` hands a foreign owner as
`ArgShape::Template`. A special arm in `deduce_rewrite` turned out to be
unneeded — the `TNameArg` chain decides the same copy — and was cut.

    backend 2689 -> 2751 agree (crash 1 -> 1, declined 513 -> 451)
    ptdiff structural 1780 -> 1796

The bucket is 38 now, at `data/function.k:75` — `bind1st<…>`'s
`<uint4>`-suffixed copy, whose instance type stays unresolved: the next
link.

A process note: `3c2e170` (designated initializers) was committed after

`fb0112d` fixed them. Every commit since runs `cargo test --workspace`

## A copy spelled as a copy — 2026-09-23 (evening)

The backend's decline reasons were cut at 60 characters, so the verbose
list could not name a site; `xtask backend --verbose` now prints each
`DECLINED` line whole (the histogram still buckets on the first 60). The
largest site was then plain: 35 programs at `library/control/loop.k:136`,
`static pipelined<I, decltype(body)> loop;` in a `pipelined_for` copy
whose `body` is a closure.

- **The census left a closure argument opaque.** `named_type_at` took
  named, array, scalar and function types; a closure — or its
  `Closure<…>` instance face — fell through, the shape was `Opaque`, and
  an opaque instance is never materialised. It binds as its copy now.
- **The copy's name came back wrong, twice.** `mint_leaf` gave a type the
  twin cannot spell an alias whose original is its display text. For a
  closure the display is `[capture] function`, and its unmangled name
  does not mangle back either (a closure's function type is dropped,
  `Mangle.hs:42-43`); for any other copy named through a round's alias,
  the display *is* the alias, which the pool aliased again — the walk
  unaliased once and handed the backend `__kg_m53`
  (`test/logic/nested_atomic.k`, and `long_class_name.k`'s standing Error
  27). A copy now always takes the qualifier chain with its own mangled
  leaf, the shape a spellable type already had, and the alias registered
  for the leaf is the one the printer gives the copy's declaration. This
  replaces the display-spelling fix of the morning, which unmangled
  whenever it could parse the arguments and so worked only by accident.
- **`expFromType` spells with no scope** (`typeIdentifier []`,
  `Type.hs:1648`): the `decltype` arm of `canonical_args` minted with the
  use site's.
- **A `decltype` position is a splice** (`eval (DecltypeF _ x) =
  expFromType x (typeOf x)`, `Constexpr.hs:304-305`): its minted tree is
  typed by no table, so the copy had no `setTypeOfInstance` note until
  the census's shape stood in, as it already did for spliced aliases.

And one guard, in the walk: **a type naming a copy that no walked tree
declares is declined** (`undeclared copy`). Walking further had exposed
`test/interface/external_class_template.k`, whose `Computer<32, 6>` —
an `extern` class template with a string default — is mentioned and never
made; the backend's "Left of . in a method call must be an object" was an
error on a program the reference compiles. The guard costs one agreement,
`type-constexpr.k::17`, and that agreement was luck: its mention and its
copy disagree on a function type's attribute order (the owner mints from

written order for both), and the backend accepted a static of an
undeclared class only because nothing uses it. Blessed as given up, the

Measured and dropped on the way: handing every module the whole

## `typeResolved` is about the type — 2026-09-23 (late)

`constexpr.k::139-143` — `static assert(!(b && (i == 4)))` under `const
bool b = false` — compile in the reference, and the walk declined each
at its `static assert`: the predicate did not fold. The clause that folds
it was ported long ago (`evalBinaryBool`, `x && false → false`,
`Constexpr.hs:238-242`), and never reached. `eval (BinaryF op a b)` is
guarded by `typeResolved a && typeResolved b` (`Constexpr.hs:172`), and
the table-aware fold environment answered that for a value node with the
file scope's gate — every name a known constant — which a runtime `i ==
4` never passes. `typeResolved` asks whether the node's *type* is
resolved (`Type.hs:1003`), and the table knows: a value node it types
resolved is resolved. What that admits is exactly what exists for
runtime operands — the absorbing `&&`/`||` and `&`/`|` identities, and a
`mux` with a constant selector picking a runtime arm, as the reference
picks it.

    backend 2771 -> 2783 agree (12 newly, 0 given up), ptdiff 1800 -> 1812
    conformance, errors, strict unchanged

Then typing `make_capture0` in a module that imports no `data.closure`
(`docs/gaps.md`). The first cut was right and bought 13 programs, and
made 11 false alarms out of a closure-identity bug the unresolved types
had been hiding — `atomically(constant(true))`'s closure met itself as
two, one side naming the lambda by the owner's *qualified* alias
(`[__kg_m54]`), the other by its path (`[@data@function, __kg_m3]`). It
was reverted, the bug fixed (a qualified alias names its path wherever
a closure's function is read), and the fallback re-landed. What it then
exposed — `closureCalls` missing a local class's members in a copy — the
walk now declines instead of handing the backend a call through a
variable. Net: +1 agreement, one fewer backend disagreement, no false
alarm, and ~30 programs that now fail at the next honest link rather
than at the first.

## A hoisted class sees its function — 2026-09-23 (night)

`control.async`'s `async_then_void` declares `using task_t =
decltype(task);` and a local class whose `exec(task_t task, …)` calls
`task()`. `moveFunctions` hoists the class; the twin prints it at module
scope, where the scope walk from inside `exec` never passes through the
function's body, and `task_t` resolved to nothing — so `task` was no
closure, `closureCalls` left `task()` alone, and (since the afternoon's
guard) the walk declined it. The reference resolved every name where it
was written. The walk now does the same for anything hoisted: its own
scopes exhausted, it looks in the function's body, then the function,
before the module (`hoisted_scopes` learned hoisted classes, which it had
mapped only for lambdas). +9 agreements.

The rewrite then named functions the backend did not know, twice over: a
generic lambda called through its closure (the reference calls its
deduced copy), and a closure function named across modules without its
namespace. A guard — a call of a hoisted lambda's function no walked tree
declares is declined — keeps both honest. Asked of every mangled name it
declined 17 programs the backend compiles (`post` does not index every
copy a call may name); asked of `?lambda` names only, none.

    backend 2784 -> 2793 agree, disagreements 29 -> 28, ptdiff 1812 -> 1817

## `Closure`'s `fn` is a function type once substituted — 2026-09-23 (night)

The largest decline site, 18 programs at `sync.atomic`'s `(T) -> T
modify`, was `data.fifo`'s `atomically<pointer_t>(increment)`: the copy's
`Closure<(C, uint8) -> uint8, wrapper, C>` parameter was decided, then
rejected by the template type check — "Expected a constant expression of
type `(C, uint8) -> uint8` but the argument type is `(C, auto) ->
auto`". `Closure`'s `fn` is a *value* parameter declared `FunctionType
fn`; `resolveTemplateParamType` substitutes that to a `FunctionType`
before `validate` runs (`TypeCheck.hs:357-372`), and `validate
typ@FunctionType{}` lets a template through (`tIsTemplate`, `:270`) —
and a generic `increment`'s wrapper is one. The value arm now hands an
expected function type to the `FunctionType` arm (`function_arg_verdict`),
and that arm reads a function with an `auto` parameter as the template it
is the leftover of.

Tracing it took `KG_ELAB_TRACE=1`, which is the instrument for "why is
this copy not made": the census decided the instance, the site
translated, `resolve` never saw it in `decided` — because
`templateTypeCheck` had struck it first. A fallback for sites under a
refused side-map pair was written on the way and measured unnecessary
(the corpus is identical without it); it was cut.

The copies now reach their call — `modify(state)`, which names the
generic wrapper where the reference calls its deduced copy — and the
walk declines there, honestly, widened to `$wrapper$` names.

    backend 2793 -> 2798 agree, 0 given up; ptdiff 1817 -> 1818

And one round more: a round that rewrote a call through a closure now
asks for the next, where the call — naming the closure's function, which
may be a generic lambda — is deduced to its copy, as `deduceTemplateArgs`
does right after `closureCalls` in the reference's round. `lambdas.k::2,
15, 33` agree (+3). The same call from `sync.atomic`'s copy to a wrapper
the calling module declares is still declined: that module elaborates
later, and `sync.atomic`'s template index cannot see its twin yet
(`docs/gaps.md`).

## Each pass starts from the last pass's twins — 2026-09-23 (night)

Phase 2's program passes each rebuilt `twin_roots` from nothing, so a
module saw only the twins of modules before it in this pass's dependency
order. `sync.atomic`'s copy of `atomically<uint8>` calls, through its
closure, the generic wrapper that the *calling* module's elaboration makes
— a module later in the order — and on every pass `sync.atomic`'s
deduction read that module's source, where no wrapper exists. The
reference's rounds run over the whole program at once
(`Template.hs:50-62`). Each pass now starts from the last pass's twins,
each replaced as its module is redone; the deduction finds the wrapper a
pass later and the copy calls the wrapper's copy.

    backend 2801 -> 2815 agree (0 given up), ptdiff 1818 -> 1819
    "call of an undeclared function" declines 23 -> 3

## A twin that did not parse — 2026-09-23 (night)

Ten programs declined at `fold:decltype` in
`test/syntax/helper/higher_order_functions.k`, whose global `const auto
add_and_increment = compose2(increment, add)` mints capture aliases the
walk types through the module's twin — and the module had no twin: `kg
dump twin` reported `twin parse errors 1`. The helper's `closure<void,
uint32>` copy substitutes `T = void` into `(T) -> R`, and the printer
wrote `(C, void) -> uint32`, which neither parser accepts. The reference
never prints it; its *type* drops a `void` parameter (`typeOf p == TVoid
= Nothing`, `Type.hs:1352-1353`), and so does the printed twin now. One
unparseable copy cost the whole module every twin type it had.

    backend 2815 -> 2825 agree, ptdiff 1819 -> 1828, conformance 2520 -> 2521,
    errors agree 616 -> 617, silent 79 -> 78

The copy that now parsed spoke, and first in the wrong place:
`higher-order-functions.k::209`'s `Do()` in `GoVar`'s copy is "expected 4"
at the `)` (146:19) and this port said 146:16. `closureCalls` conses the
closure's cast onto the arguments but keeps the *list's* note (`renote
(cons cast) c`, `Closure.hs:19-26`), so the arity check anchors at the
first argument the call was written with — the minted cast is skipped
(`conversion.rs`). That made it silent rather than right: no twin node
starts at a `)`, and the carry home declines what is not start-aligned.
A `)` is the one unaligned position that is still exact — the call it
closes ends there on both sides — so the carry pairs it by the call's end
(`twin_diagnostics.rs`, `closing_paren`). Mutation-checked both halves:
the anchor lands on `Do` with the cast counted, and the report vanishes
with the `)` carry off.

`twin parse errors` in `kg dump twin`'s header is worth a corpus-wide
look: a module that loses its twin loses everything elaborated in it.

## A gate that slept — 2026-09-23 (night)

The gate run for `a9eaea9` read 13229 s where ~790 s is usual — tests
3715 s, codegen 900 s — every stage stretched by the same factor, and a
`timeout -s KILL 400` afterwards let a process reach 2031 s of wall clock
with exit 0. The Mac was sleeping while the gates ran: wall-clock readings
taken across an idle stretch measure the lid, not the compiler.
`scripts/gates.sh` now holds idle sleep off with `caffeinate -i -w $$`
while it lives. Time a single program with `/usr/bin/time -p` (user
seconds) under `caffeinate -i`, never `date` arithmetic.

What it hid, measured that way: `test/library/data/array.k` through our

CPU at `3c2e170` and 84 s at `990135b` and `a9eaea9`; the reference
compiles the whole program, backend included, in 23 s wall / 53 s CPU.
The trace shows `reduce`'s recursion minting a fresh closure per level
(`Closure<decltype(__kg_m747), __kg_m747, __kg_m1>` and on) through eight

## The machine ran out of memory — 2026-09-23 (night)

The user reported the machine out of memory after this session's runs.
The kernel log kept no jetsam record I could read, so the culprit is not
named; what was measured afterwards, sampling the whole process tree
every half second (`scratchpad/memwatch.py`), is what the gates cost when
green. `scripts/gates.sh` peaks at **17.3 GB**: `xtask ptdiff` 7.5 GB (a
plateau of ~0.8 GB per worker thread's `Db`, not growth), `xtask ir`
5.7 GB, the `query` test binary 4.2 GB, and the heaviest compile
(`test/library/data/array.k`) 1.8 GB beside a 0.6 GB backend worker.
`xtask backend` alone peaks at 5.5 GB. Beside that the session had run
three 1.8 GB compiles at once and a second `backend`, on a machine other
sessions were building on. Nothing bounded any of it. A program whose
elaboration does not converge is bounded only by count (64 passes × 8
rounds, no bound on copies per round), and eight run at once.

Three bounds now, each several times the largest normal reading and
each tested by tripping it:

- `bounded::run`: every child a gate spawns (backend, ptrace, repoint,
  the oracle) runs in its own process group and is killed past 8 GB or
  900 s, summed over the group so the backend worker counts. The kill is
  the group's, so the worker goes with it. `KG_CHILD_MEM_MB=500 xtask
  backend --filter test/library/data/array.k` reads `CRASH … killed at 565
  MB resident`. The unit test is red with the sampling off (the time bound
  fires instead) and with only the leader killed (the drain waits 30 s on
  the grandchild's pipe).
- `bounded::watch_self`: each xtask process exits 99 past 16 GB.
  `KG_XTASK_MEM_MB=300 xtask ptdiff` stops at 720 MB with the message.
- `gates.sh`'s watchdog: below 10% free system-wide it lists the run's
  largest processes and kills its descendants — by parent pid, since the
  process group of a non-interactive caller is the caller's. It exits with
  the script. Exercised with the floor at 101%.

What stays open: the compiler itself has no bound on growth, only on
passes and rounds. A copies-per-program cap that reports exhaustion, as
the pass guard does, is the in-compiler form of the same guard.

## Output parity, decided and graded — 2026-09-23 (night)

**The owner's decision (`docs/history/audit-2026-09-22.md` §6.1): output parity for `kg build` is
identical output modulo source locations.** Location agreement is kept as a
second ratchet that may only rise, not a gate to reach first. What decided
it was measured before the question was asked: the reference's `.sv` puts a
`// file.k:line:col` comment on 88 of 372 lines of the smallest exported
class, and our compiler's `.sv` for it differed from the reference's
*only* there (`13:5` for the body where the reference says `14:9`, the
`return`) and in the header's command line. `_types.sv`, `RtlMap.json` and
the path-length report were byte-identical. Byte-identical parity would
have made divergence #25 (93.4% span agreement) a gate to close before
anything else; modulo locations grades the logic now.

**Two things that were wrong on the way.** The compat binary handed the
backend its full `argv[0]` as `_cmdArgs`, so every generated file's second
line differed. `legacy::cmd_args_string`, which does it the reference's
way (`unwords (getProgName : args)`, `Main.hs:36-40`), existed with tests
and no caller on the compile path: the recurring failure again. And the
compat binary refused `-o`: `cmdargs` auto-assigns short flags per mode,
which `docs/spec/cli.md` §11 Q1 had marked UNVERIFIED. The reference's own
`--help` answered it: `-j` and `-o` in `compile`, seven letters in `pretty`.

**`cargo xtask output`.** Of the 2166 programs whose `ptrace` run reaches
`Codegen`, the reference writes RTL for 274 (a program writes files only
for what it exports). Both compilers run each in the same directory with
the same arguments, since the report holds the source file's absolute path
and the `.sv` header holds the command line. The reference's side is
stored, keyed by both reference binaries, the whole `.k` tree, the
program's text and flags, and the directory. Recording it took 20 minutes
and peaked at 13.7 GB (`risc-v.k` alone at 7.5 GB, killed at the 900 s
budget; the reference itself cannot build it inside that). Replaying it
takes two minutes under 4 GB. The normaliser learned three location
places by running it, each now a unit test that is mutation-checked:

- the trailing comment, in four shapes: `a.k:14:9`, `a.k:14:{9,16}`,
  `a.k:12:5, :14:9`, and the call-site chain `{{a.k:9:5 <- 'callee'(a.k:20:3)}
  <- …}`, whose quoted names are any text. Outside the quotes every word
  must be a `.k` file, a number or `<-`, so prose naming a place is code;
- the path-length report's `relativePath` and `range*` columns, named by
  its header row;
- the digits after "line: " and " at line " in an assertion's `$fatal`
  text. Its call-trace frame's function name is still compared.

**First reading:** 153 of 274 identical modulo locations, 23 of them byte
for byte; 29 differ, 83 declined by the walk, 1 failed
(`local-functions::34`, a P0 item), 8 the reference itself fails once asked
for RTL. Location comments agree on 37193 of 83861 lines. The 29 are two
families, both real:

- **The call-trace name (~19).** An assertion's frame names its function
  as the backend was told it. We pass the mangled
  `pipelined_for<|$uint@10@@data@closure@make_capture2<|…|>…|><uint10>`
  where the reference passes the display form `pipelined_for<uint10,
  data.closure::make_capture2<…>::$::Capture, …>`. This is `ptdiff`'s
  `ParseFunction / ParseFunction` row (57) seen from the other end.
- **Static-instance numbering and module names (~11).**
  `__static_instance_7__control_loop__pipelined_for___uint_1` where the
  reference has `_0` and `uint_4`, and an extra `typedef uint1`: the
  order and set of instances the walk hands over.

What the gate cannot see is written in its module doc: a program the
reference writes nothing for and ours writes something for (ours never
runs there), and anything that is not a file under `out/`.

## P0, second batch: qualifiers the backend could not find — 2026-09-24

The other eight valid programs the backend refused were all one kind of
fact: a qualifier the reference has already rewritten by the time it walks.

- **A qualifier that names a type alias is the aliased class.**
  `bar_t::foo_t` under `using bar_t = Foo<uint32>` reaches the backend as
  `Foo<|$uint@32|>::foo_t`. The parser keeps the alias as the written
  qualifier and resolves through it only for lookups (`Parser.hs:667-668`).
  Bisecting `kg-oracle --tree` over `--passes`, `--template-passes` and
  `--template-iterations` put the substitution in the first instantiation
  round, not in any template pass, and `removeNestedTypeIdentifier`
  (`Desugar.hs:122-127`) is the shape it leaves. The walk now emits a
  qualifier naming an alias of a class by the class's own path.
  `using.k::39` and `template-instance-identifiers.k::35,36,39` agree.
- **The twin printer dropped two qualifiers.** A rebuilt scoped name prints
  leaf-only unless an exception proves the qualifier. The "written
  qualifier" exception demanded the whole chain be written, so `Bar::Zero`
  in a class template's copy, whose `Bar` the parser qualified with the
  class (`makeQualified`), printed as a bare `Zero`: no fold, no `EnumValue`,
  "Unknown symbol: Zero" (`enum.k::51`). Only the immediate qualifier needs
  to be written now; it prints by its own rule. And a template parameter
  substituted as a qualifier (`T::B2` in `C<Bar>`) is the site's chain,
  wearing the site's expansion where everything a rewrite made inside the
  template shares the copy's. Printed as the type now (`enum.k::56`).
- **A member variable named through its class from outside it** (the lambda
  of a local class's template method copy, `local-classes.k::15,16`) is a
  `memberAccess` rewrite this port's `moveFunctions` missed, and is
  declined. The first cut declined any class-qualified member and cost 438
  programs in one gate run: inside the class `resolveNames` unqualifies it
  (`Frontend.hs:277`), which the walk does too. The guard is now only for a
  qualifier that is not a prefix of the use's scope; two existing walk
  tests pin that.

    backend 2828 -> 2835, backend errors 17 -> 9 (all 9 are programs the
    reference's frontend rejects); ptdiff 1829 -> 1836; repoint 30 -> 31

## P0, third batch: method references and a bound on growth — 2026-09-24

- **A member access naming a method is a method reference.**
  `deduceTemplateArgs`' first clause (`Type.hs:1390-1391`) rewrites
  `MemberAccessF a b`, typed `TUndefined` (a method is no field) on a
  class-typed `a`, to `FunctionSpecifierF (Just a) (Class::b)`, and
  `resolveNames` drops the qualifier. `auto callback = d.c[1].u32_F_u32;`
  is the shape: a callback initialized with another object's method. As a
  member access the backend answered "Type error" on five programs the
  reference compiles (`callbacks.k::5,22,26,27,29`); the walk now emits the
  specifier. The rewrite belongs in pass 4 of the IR, not the walk; it is
  here because the walk is the one consumer, and the IR's inference does
  not type the node `TUndefined` to key on.
- **An alias bound on the elaboration** (`ALIAS_GUARD`, 5000;
  `Db::set_alias_guard` for tests). Counts bounded passes (64) and rounds
  (8) and nothing bounded how much one round makes. Measured first: the
  corpus's most is `test/library/data/array.k`'s 1039 names (1.8 GB),
  `risc-v.k`'s 360. A template whose copies double per level (`F<N>` calling
  `F<2 * N>` and `F<2 * N + 1>`) makes 255 in eight rounds; past the bound
  the rounds and passes stop and the elaboration reports exhaustion, as the
  pass guard does. A template recursing one copy per level is *not* such a
  thing: `MAX_ROUNDS` ends it and the next pass converges, which the first
  test caught.

    backend 2835 -> 2840 (frontend disagreements 35 -> 30); ptdiff 1836 -> 1841

## `fifo.k:64`, the fuzzer's false alarms, and two runaways — 2026-09-24

**`atomically<pointer_t>(increment)`** was the decline 16 corpus programs
shared. The spec reached `sync.atomic`, which made the copy
`atomically<|$uint@5…|>`; the *call site*, in `FIFO`'s copy, named
`atomically<|@@data@fifo@FIFO<|…|>@pointer_t…|>`. A deduced call keeps its
written arguments as written (`Type.hs:1407`), and the reference mangles
`$uint@5` because its inference rounds splice an alias argument to its type
before the instance is keyed, the rule `instances::arg_splices` already
applies to a written instance. `deduce_rewrite` applies it now to a
deduced call's explicit arguments that name a type the table types as a
scalar, an array or a function (which only an alias can be).
`local-classes.k::14` agrees; the programs behind it move on to their next
decline (`control/loop.k:279`, a `decltype` of a lambda capturing a
closure).

Two other changes looked necessary on the way and were not: merging the
two views of a generic wrapper (`TTemplate` against a function type with
`auto` in it) in `mint_shape`, and falling back to the census's shape
where the fold has no type for a member alias. Each made the owner's
trace cleaner, and with the splice in place neither changes a verdict:
reverted, since code no test pins is a claim nobody checks.

**The fuzzer**, re-run with its seed, found its own runaway first: the
probe server keeps one `Db` for every mutant and grew to 10 GB. It now
drops the `Db` past `KG_PROBE_DB_MB` (2 GB), and the server process has a
budget of its own (`KG_PROBE_MEM_MB`, 4 GB) the worker replaces it under.
Of the nine false-alarm buckets, two were fixed:

- `uint2 Fn_T_T = Fn_T_T(10);` calls the imported template: the variable is
  not registered until parsed whole. `Binders` now keeps where a local's
  declaration ends and does not let it shadow before that. The reproduction
  needs the real helper's imports, so the test is on the rule itself.
- `{boolConst:b3}` in `inline void boolConst()` names the imported constant:
  a plain function's body does not see the function. Silence.

Three buckets the full reference rejects in its backend (booked, not
false alarms); the `GoVar`/`DoIt` wrapper shape (18 mutants) stays open.

**The hang.** A `static for` of 65535 iterations with a lambda in each
(the reference's own frontend runs past its limit too) took `kg check`
past 11 GB. Two causes: `moveFunctions` checked every scoped name against
a *list* of the moved items, re-un-aliasing each entry per check —
quadratic, now a set built once; and past that, the unrolled body itself
is a million nodes every later pass pays for. `static_for::UNROLL_NODES`
(2^20 nodes, iterations times body) leaves a bigger loop standing, as an
unfolded limit does. The corpus's largest literal limit is 128. The input
now checks in 0.27 s and 18 MB.

    backend 2840 -> 2843; everything else unchanged

## An enum constant as a template argument — 2026-09-24

`Types<Base::RV32I>::Decoded` (`processor/risc_v/internal/decoder.k:200`)
was the top decline site, nine programs, and none of its three facts was
about RISC-V. Probing variants in the walk tests isolated it quickly: an
integer argument worked, and `Types<Base::RV32I>` failed even used directly
with the enum declared locally.

1. **The route counted an enum value unmintable.** The census folds the
   argument to `ConstValue::Enum`, and `materialisable` required every fold
   to mint as a literal — so the instance was decided and silently never
   made. `kg dump instances` (the census) listed it; `KG_ELAB_TRACE` said
   nothing at all, which is itself worth noting as a hole in the trace.
2. **The reference keeps the name.** `eval (NamedValueF x)` over an enum
   constant is `EnumValueF x v` (`Constexpr.hs:258-259`), and `mangle
   (EnumValue x _) = x` (`Mangle.hs:39`): the copy is
   `Types<|@@processor@risc_v@isa@Base@RV32I|>`, named by the constant as
   the parser qualified it where it was written. The site now wraps its
   written name as `EnumValue { name, value }`, and the census qualifies an
   enum shape by the enum type's own path, so the owner mints the same name.
   Without the qualification the owner made `Types<|@Base@RV32I|>` beside it
   and the backend answered Error 24.
3. **A copy prints the constant by its name** (`src (EnumValue a _) =
   pretty a`, `PrettyPrint.hs:98`), `Base::RV32I`; this port printed the
   value, which no copy folded against the enum.

The first cut mangled any `NamedValue` by its name, which the reference
never sees at that point. `C<T::Foo>` with `T` a class (a type named as a
value; the reference rejects `template.k::41`) then made a copy that took
the backend down with SIGSEGV. Only the census knows a position folded to
an enum, so the rewrite happens there, where the census's fold says so.

## Two fold clauses the copies were missing — 2026-09-24

The fold declines cluster by test, and the two largest clusters were one
fact each.

- **A copy's `static if` over an imported constant** (`static-if.k::63-70`,
  8 programs). `static if (True)` in `C<uint32>::Run`, `True` from the
  helper: the copy's literal `staticControl` cannot fold a name, so the
  branch stood, the lambda in it stayed local (`moveFunctions` defers
  inside a `static if`), and the walk met a `decltype` of a local function.
  `typed_static_ifs` already hands the next round the verdicts the twin's
  typed fold reaches; it passed over every `static if` inside a class,
  because `facts::decided_static_ifs` was written for a module's own text,
  whose callers read verdicts at module scope. A twin's class copies are
  where a copy's `static if`s stand: `decided_static_ifs_within(…, true)`.
- **A copy's literal dimension** (`template-argument-deduction.k`'s
  helper, 11 programs). `T[N+1]` in a deduced copy is `uint4[(10 + 1)]`;
  the reference's `evaluateConstexpr` walks `11`. The twin's fold keys its
  values by ranges, and a copy's printed parenthesis does not line up with
  the node that asks. The walk now folds literal arithmetic itself where
  the backend needs a number, an array dimension or an `int<N>` width, and
  nowhere else, since elsewhere `2 + 1` is walked as the operation the
  reference walks.

Also removed: a `KG_DBG` trace line in `walk.rs` that `262213e` committed by
mistake.

    backend 2851 -> 2872; ptdiff 1841 -> 1859

## Two more folds the walk could not reach — 2026-09-24

- **A constant whose initializer needs a width** (`const auto x = bitsizeof
  Foo; static assert(x == 1);`, `type-identifier.k::3-7`). The file scope
  declines `bitsizeof` for want of a table; the census resolves such
  constants from the converged table (`Db::late_constants`, and its
  imports' through `foreign_constants_with`), and `Db::module_fold`, the
  walk's folder, did not. Probing narrowed it in four programs: a direct
  `bitsizeof Foo == 1` folded, and `x = bitsizeof uint8` through a constant
  did not, whatever the declaration order.
- **A conditional whose arms are comparisons of constants**
  (`template-argument-deduction.k::41-44`). The reference folds bottom-up,
  so by the time it asks `typeResolved` of the mux its arms are `true` and
  `false` and it is a `bool`; this port's table types a comparison of two
  constants unresolved (the folder's business, `Type.hs:1182-1188`), so the
  mux was refused. `eval_mux` now treats it as resolved when an arm is such
  a compound and every arm folds to one kind. The first cut applied it to
  literal arms too and broke `folding_stops_while_a_type_is_unresolved`,
  which pins the blanket guard (`Constexpr.hs:295-296`): a mux of literals
  the environment calls unresolved is a real type error, arms of two kinds.
  The narrowed rule keeps that test and adds one of its own.

The remaining `fold:static assert` and `fold:int<N>` declines are mostly
programs the reference *rejects* (a `static assert` over a runtime value, a
`bool` as a width): our frontend's silence there, P3, not a fold.

    backend 2872 -> 2880; ptdiff 1859 -> 1867

## A parameter typed by an earlier one — 2026-09-24

Of the 185 "template instance" declines, 153 are programs the reference
accepts, and the `template` test family led them (17). Most of that family
is one clause: `resolveTemplateParamType` (`TypeCheck.hs:349-362`)
substitutes the earlier arguments into a value parameter's written type
before the argument is validated. The census's `resolve_kind` declined
every value parameter whose type mentioned another parameter, so
`template <typename T, uint<bitsizeof T> N>` decided no instance at all.
`substitute_dependent_kind` now folds the shapes that are decidable here:
`uint<…>`/`int<…>` and arrays, with widths and dimensions over literals,
earlier value arguments, `bitsizeof`/`clog2` of bound types and values,
and arithmetic; and the same inside a function-typed parameter's positions
(`(uint<bitsizeof T>) -> void F`). An alias template (`index_t<N>`) and a
class member alias (`T::Foo::X`) still decline.

    backend 2880 -> 2894; ptdiff 1867 -> 1874; output equal 154 -> 156

## An alias template as a parameter's type — 2026-09-24

The follow-up the entry above left open. `template <auto N, index_t<N> M>`
(`template.k::7,32-35`) types `M` by `type.stdtype`'s `using index_t =
uint<(N > 1) ? clog2(N) : 1>`. `substitute_dependent_kind` is now a small
scope walker (`Dependent`) that expands an alias template's instance — a
resolved `TemplateInstance` or the still-written `Path` with arguments —
by reading its body in the alias's own module with its parameters bound,
and folds the ternary (`mux(c, f, t)`, `Constexpr.hs:311-313`) and
`bytesizeof` (`template.k::25,26`).

Two readings of the reference decide which values a type sees.
`validateArgs` (`TypeCheck.hs:222-228`) resolves each parameter's type
over the *written* arguments (`resolveTemplateParamType symbols template
args`), and converts each argument to its type only in its own position.
So a nested alias instance converts its arguments before its body reads
them — `Foo<T, 100>` with `N` an `index_t<bitsizeof(T)>` under `T =
uint6` is `index_t<4>`, and the program's `static assert(N ==
cast<uint2>(101))` holds (`template.k::33`, which the first cut rejected)
— but a later parameter of the instance itself reads the earlier argument
unconverted. A first draft converted at the instance level too; the
reference text says otherwise, and it came out.

    backend 2894 -> 2901; ptdiff 1874 -> 1876

## Nine silent programs, five mechanisms — 2026-09-24

The backend gate's `FRONTEND` rows are programs whose verdicts differ
before the backend: 31 of them, nine where the reference rejects and this
port exits 0. Read one at a time, they came apart into five mechanisms:

- **A warning printed beside an error.** The reference prints warnings only
  from `codegen` (`Main.hs:84-97`), which a failed frontend never reaches;
  the legacy binary printed them first, and the error bundle after them
  lost its `Error 1:` header. 17 `imports.k` rows were this. `--Werror`
  also owes its own line, `Error 1: Warnings treated as errors`
  (`all-warnings-as-errors.k::1,2`).
- **`default = e;` counted as a syntax error.** The frozen `SyntaxKind`
  vocabulary has no `DEFAULT_INIT`, so the parser wraps one in `ERROR`; the
  symbol map read that as the reference's `ErrorF` and set `$errors`, which
  stands pass 9 down for the *whole program* — any undefined name in a
  file with a `default` went unreported until the backend's "Unknown
  symbol" (`callbacks.k::89`). `kg_syntax::is_default_init` names the one
  shape, well-formed only, and the three readers ask it.
- **A class member of function attributes is a function.** `classVariable`
  admits only `[[name]]` (`Parser.hs:462`); `[[reset]] (bool) -> void
  callback;` falls through to `function MemberFunction` and fails at the
  `;` (`callbacks.k::81`). Probing the neighbours found a false divergence:
  `[[pipelined]] (bool) -> void cb;` on a *local* is a variable of an
  attributed function type (`funcTypeAttr`), which our rule was reporting
  as a function; it now reaches the reference's "Expected 'const'".
- **A `typename` parameter as an array dimension** — `brackets expression`
  (`Parser.hs:529,535`), so `T[N]` is the parser's "Invalid use of a type
  as an expression" at `N` (`template-argument-deduction.k::68`), inside a
  template where pass 19 does not look.
- **A type for a function-typed parameter.** `validate _ _ | tIsType`
  precedes the `FunctionType` clause (`TypeCheck.hs:266-269`); ours listed
  every non-type kind but the function one (`type-check.k::45`).

Left: `template.k::27` (the census now substitutes the dependent kind,
pass 12 does not — the two should share it), two parse-time shapes whose
message is megaparsec's (`function-template.k::19`,
`template-template-parameter.k::23`), an export list naming an undefined
symbol in an imported file (`imports.k::63`), and `extern-class.k::51`.

    backend 2901 -> 2929; strict failing 84 -> 79; errors silent 78 -> 73;
    conformance 2521 -> 2526; repoint 31 -> 32

## A template-template argument its template cannot spell — 2026-09-24

`T4<bool, Foo>` with `Foo` in the root file, `T3<15, memory>` with
`memory` from `data.memory`: the helper declaring `T3`/`T4` imports

`leaves`). The copy's `TT<uint32, N>` is then `__kg_m0<uint32, 15>`, which
nothing past the mangler understood. Four readers now do:

  (`IrTemplates::alias_template`), so the instance is decided and handed
  to its owner;
- `resolve` recognises the alias as the decided template's name and
  mangles the path's leaf under its namespace prefix — `data.memory::
  memory<|$uint@32@15|>`, the name the owner declares its copy under, where
  it had been `.data.memory::memory<|…|>`, a copy nobody declared;
- the twin's sorter reads the alias as that template
  (`sorted::twin_sorted`'s `templates`), so the mention pairs with the
  copy's instance node and a diagnostic raised there is carried home;
- pass 8 looks through it to the template's list — the reference's
  "Invalid argument for template parameter `B`" at the helper's
  `TT<false>` for a `Foo<uint32 B>` (`template-template-parameter.k::17`).

The first gate run caught what deciding more instances exposes. `ttp::17`
became our `uint<false>` width error inside the copy the check should have
refused (hence the last two readers), and a namespaced variant written as
a test did the same until pass 8 followed a qualified alias too. And

reported a type as an expression in *any* attribute, where the reference
has no such clause in `validateProgram` at all — the error is its parser's
`expression`, which only an `intAttr` argument is (`Parser.hs:173-177`;
`ecc` is an `identAttr`). The arm now judges the seven integer attributes.

A sorter tweak dropping the alias hit's scope was written, measured
unnecessary (the instance node pairs either way; only the base's subtree is

## A width that can never fold — 2026-09-24

`unresolved ParamUintF{}` (`Frontend.hs:405`) rejects any width still
unfolded at pass 16. Pass 16 here reports only what it can prove, and an
unfolded width here usually means "not known yet". Two shapes are "never":
an expression of literals alone, which nothing later can change —
`uint<1 && 1 && 1>` and `uint<false >= true == true>` meet no arm of
`evalBinary` (`Constexpr.hs:176-216`: `&&` on integers, `>=` on booleans)
— and a mutable name, which `eval (NamedValueF x)` never replaces.
`facts::only_literals` is the first; `certainly_runtime` the second.

Wiring the second in broke `constexpr.k::116`'s `uint<bitsizeof x>` over a
mutable `x`: `runtime_names` asks whether a node sits under a written type
by walking its ancestors up to the expression, and for the expression's
own root that walk starts above it — inside the `uint<…>` — so the root
`bitsizeof` was skipped as "under a type" and `x` read as a value. Every
earlier caller passed a statement's expression, where the question never
arose.

    conformance 2536 -> 2542; errors silent 63 -> 57; strict failing
    69 -> 63; backend 2947 -> 2953

## Roadmap 3: a copy's round is the round that decided it — 2026-09-24

`Map.toList` orders one template's copies by round, then key
(`Template.hs:120`), and static instances are numbered in that order, so
`__static_instance_N__` in the RTL is only right when each copy's round is.
`InstanceSpec::round` was the copy depth of the deciding mention — one per
copy it stands in — and that is wrong exactly when a copy is decided late.

`kg-oracle --template-iterations 1..4` on `test/logic/test_cases_17.k`
shows why: `fixture<Test500>` is decided in iteration 2 and
`fixture<Test501>` in 3, not 1. A class argument is resolved only when all
its fields are (`tResolved (TClass _ xs) = all (tResolved . snd) xs`,
`Type.hs:1027`); `Test500` holds `Foo500<uint32, 2>`, typed once its copy
exists, and `Test501` holds `Foo501<uint32, 2>`, which holds
`Bar501<uint3, 1>` — one more round. Every lambda `Closure` inside the
fixture copy is decided a round after the copy, 3 and 4.

Our twin rounds already hold `fixture<Test500>` to round 2 and
`fixture<Test501>` to round 3; what was missing was carrying that into the
copy. Two changes:

* `ExpansionData::round` — the copy's frame records its spec's round
  (ordering data, like `site`: not identity, first intern wins), and a
  mention's round is its innermost copy frame's plus one
  (`elaborate::reference_round`).
* `elaborate::twin_round` — a twin's decision of an own-text mention the
  *base census postponed* (`Round::held`) is dated by the twin's round `k`.
  Nothing else is: the first cut dated every own-text twin decision by `k`
  and lost `higher-order-functions.k::59,183`, where the reference decides
  the wrapper's `Closure` in iteration 4 and ours in twin round 5, while a
  deduced `compose2` is a round early here. A twin's rounds are a clock
  only for what the base census held.

`test/library/numeric/int/multi_word.k` matched briefly under the first cut
and does not now; it was never structurally equal — the reference decides
four of its twelve `tuple2` copies in round 2, a separate timing question.

    output 169 -> 174 (test_cases_17, 23, 31, 35, 38); ptdiff 1901 -> 1904;
    tests 1756 -> 1757

## What a wrapper's closure waits for — 2026-09-24

The top `ptdiff` row (`ParseIdentifier / ParseIdentifier`, 126 programs) is
mostly closure copies in another order: `Closure` against `Closure` (15),
`data.closure` against `data.closure.core` (19), `make_capture1` (10),
`make_capture1/2` swapped (11). One template's copies sort by round, then
key (`Template.hs:120`), so each is a round the port dates differently.
Three timings, each read off `kg-oracle --template-iterations N`:

* **A capturing lambda's closure is a round after its capture.**
  `scratchpad/cap/a.k`: in a method, `make_capture1<C&>` is iteration 1 and
  the lambda's `Closure` 2; inside the copy `Tpl<uint8>` (1),
  `make_capture1<uint8>` is 2 and the `Closure` 3. The closure's third
  argument is `decltype(make_captureN(…))`, typed only once the call beside
  it is deduced. `make_capture0` is no template and adds nothing — which is
  why `fixture<Test50x>`'s `[]` closures were right at copy + 1. Landed:
  `elaborate::captures` adds the round.
* **A wrapper's closure is decided in the iteration that wrapped it.** The
  reference's `addLambdaWrappers` runs first in an iteration (`foldr ($)`
  over the pass list applies the last, `Template.hs:71-80`), and that
  iteration's census decides the new `Closure`; this port's wrapper reaches
  a census only through the next twin, a round late (`Go3(bind1st<…>, 10)`,
  iteration 4 there, twin round 5 here, `higher-order-functions.k::59`). A
  call in a lambda's body is wrapped a round later still: inference skips a
  `LambdaF` (`Inference.hs:55`) until `desugarLambdas` has made it a
  function (`this-capture.k::9`).
* **A deduction over closures is two rounds after them.**
  `compose2(increment, add)` in `helper.higher_order_functions`: the
  wrappers' closures are iteration 1, `compose2`'s copy 3 (its lambda's
  closure, capturing, 5) — `deduceType` binds a closure only as a
  `TInstance` (`Type.hs:1532`), a round after the copy exists. The port
  deduces it in its base pass, round 1.

Dating wrappers correctly (tracked per head, by the round that wrapped them)
fixed `this-capture.k::9` and broke `higher-order-functions.k::59, 67, 68,
83, 84, 92`: with the wrapper late, those programs' order had been right
only because `compose2` was early by the same margin. The two go together
or not at all; the wrapper half is not landed, and the deduction half needs
the round of the closures a deduction reads, which the census's shapes do
not carry yet.

    Every gate unchanged with the capture rule landed (ptdiff 1904, backend
    2995, output 176): the programs it dates are held by the other two.

`ParseFunction / ParseFunction` (40 programs) was mostly one question:
which declaration gets a display name. `withUnmangledName` asks the
declaration's own type — a `TInstance` gets `unmangleInstanceName`, anything
else `NULL` (`ParseTree.hs:177-180`) — where the walk judged by the name's
shape: a plain template name before the mangle. Both directions were wrong:

* A copy of a hoisted generic template — `Run@?lambda0<|$uint@32|>`,

  `closures.k::28`). Where the table holds an instance note at the
  declaration, it now decides. Its *absence* decides nothing: inference
  overwrites some copies' notes with the function type (`compose2<|…|>`),
  and taking "resolved, not an instance" as "no instance" lost 117 programs.
* A wrapper hoisted out of a copy — `Run<|$uint@32|>@$wrapper$Do<|…|>` —
  wraps the callee the copy had already resolved, and is a function in the
  reference (`::57,58,103-109,149-155`); this route makes it by

  a `$wrapper$` whose parent segment holds a mangle — gets no display. The

  full of `@`s, and splitting inside it cost `compose2` its display on the

## A template name two modules declare — 2026-09-25

`imports.k::36,37,107,114` missed whole copy chains — `a1<5>`'s copy names
`b1<5>`, whose copy names `c1<5>` — because the census decided nothing at

(`SymbolTable.hs:272-278`) it did not have:

* An aliased import answers a bare name nowhere: the alias is stripped off

  census stripped a leading import alias or namespace and then searched by

  decided `A5::a1<bool>` as `a1.a1`'s `a1`, a wrong copy where the old
  ambiguity had declined; the candidate now carries what it stripped

* A module's own import alias qualifies whatever else shares its simple
  name: a nested `Bar::Foo` beside `import a1.a1 as Foo` does not answer

no `bitarray` copy at all. `template <auto Size, auto WordWidth, …,
template <typename, auto> typename Memory = memory> class bitarray`,
mentioned as `bitarray<Size, WordWidth>` inside a class whose `Size` is a
`const auto`. The reference completes the list at pass 4
(`deduceInstance'`, `Type.hs:1440-1444`); `fill_type_defaults` declined it
three separate ways, each alone enough:

* **The default's module.** `Memory = memory` is written in
  `data.bitarray`, but `memory` is `data.memory`'s, which that module
  imports; `resolveTypeName` (`Parser.hs:736-757`) qualifies it by the
  declaring module, `@@data@memory@memory`. Both the mention rewrite
  (`defaults::qualified_chain`) and a call's defaults
  (`deduce_template_args::fill_defaults`, which also needed the
  elaboration's `Templates` to carry `with_visible`) qualified it by the
  *writer*, `@@data@bitarray@memory`, a name nothing declares.
* **A class constant.** `Size` is no literal and the base table types it
  `uint11`, not a value: `bound_argument` now reads `ArgFold`'s folded value
  at the node first (round one only; a copy's mentions wait as before).
* **The homonym.** `data.bitarray.banked` declares a `bitarray` of its own
  and imports `data.bitarray`'s as `ba`, so `Templates::located` answered
  neither. `defaults::homonym` resolves the mention the way the census now
  does: a pass-1 qualified mention by its namespace, an unqualified one by
  the writer's own declaration first, then its imports
  (`SymbolTable.hs:249-259`); `Templates::located_in` is the per-file index
  it reads.

bitarray.k now diverges at #554 (a `uint1` where the reference walks
`bool`, not yet read), banked.k at #141: a `tuple2<optional<bool>[1],
optional<bool>[1]>` made by `atomically` inside `vec::sharded_map`'s
lambda under `static for` — the unrolled static-for lambda gap, not this.

Tried and dropped: peeling nested alias instances in `named_type_at`
(`concrete.concrete()`), which moved nothing measured.

Left: a twin round's `Templates` (`elaborate.rs`, the round-2 and later
indexes) still has no `with_visible` — its files are synthetic ids the
visibility map is not keyed by — so a call's template-template default
inside a copy is still qualified by its writer.

Every total is where it was — each program still diverges later on —
so the gain is two programs' first divergences, #92 -> #554 and #92 -> #141,
and three copies the reference makes that were missing. Two walk tests pin
it (`a_homonym_mention_short_of_an_imported_default_is_completed`, red with
any of the three pieces removed; `a_calls_template_default_names_the_module_declaring_it`).

## An initializer list's elements, converted to their fields — 2026-09-25

`Foo({E::X, false})` on a `Foo(S)` whose first field is an `int2`: the
reference walks the bare `3`, typed `uint2` twice (`conversion-warning.k::6`,
the recorded walk). `checkConversion'` (`TypeCheck.hs:161-177`) leaves a
list that is a subtype of its target whole; otherwise it checks each
element against the type it initializes (`tInitializedType`,
`Type.hs:293-304`). So the `EnumValue` clause (`:155-156`) turns an enum
element meeting an integer field into its literal, and an element that
narrows is wrapped in a warning and stamped a second time. The walk applied
both only at the argument or initializer itself.

`Walker::conversions` now walks the list against the target: the nodes an
enum is walked as its literal at, and the positional elements a warning
wraps. A designated element is checked with `errorNarrowingConversions`
(`:157`), as is a declaration whose list starts with a designator (`:130`),
so neither is ever stamped as a warning. The element nodes carry no type
here; each element's `TPositional`/`TDesignator` is read off the list's
`TInitializer`.

`{E::X, false}` for a `uint2` field *is* a subtype (`TEnum _ uint2 <:
uint2`, `Type.hs:328`) and keeps its `EnumValue`, which the test pins too.

The same family, landed next: `Do(Foo::One)` on a `uint3` parameter over a
`uint16` enum (`conversion-warning.k::15`). The converted literal is judged
by `inferIntLiteralType 1 = uint1`, which does not narrow, where
`call_arguments` judged the table's `uint16` and stamped twice. An argument
that folds to an integer, or an enum value meeting an integer parameter, is
now judged by its value, as a declaration's initializer already was
(ptdiff 2035 -> 2036).

    ptdiff 2031 -> 2035 (conversion-warning::1,2,6,
    template-argument-deduction::217); all else unchanged; tests 1772 -> 1773

## `static if (true)` with no `else` — 2026-09-25

`static-if.k::15`: `template <typename T> struct Foo` and `Foo<bool> foo1;`
under `static if (true)` in `main`. The reference copies `Foo<|$bool|>` into
`main.$`: inference's `staticControl` has put the branch in place of the
statement (`Constexpr.hs:43-44`, `Inference.hs:50`), `removeNestedScope`
took the branch's `$quasi0` out of every scope under it, and `decided` runs
over the spliced tree. Ours made no copy, for three reasons stacked:

* **The inference.** `InferFile::dead` held the branches `staticControl`
  deletes, and the walk treated a `static if` as decided only when a dead
  range lay inside it. `static if (true) { … }` with no `else` deletes
  nothing, so it looked undecided and its branch was never typed.
  `InferFile::live` now lists every decided statement. This alone fixed
  `static-if.k::32`.
* **The census.** `scan`'s `static if` arm is `decided`'s, condition only,
  which is right for the `static if`s inference left standing. A literal
  condition is one it did not leave standing, so the census now scans the
  branch it keeps. A literal only: a predicate the table folds, like
  `decltype(Fixture::run) == () -> bool` in a `unit::fixture` copy, is
  spliced a round later on our side. Scanning its branch a round early named
  a hoisted lambda outside its copy (8 programs lost, `test/logic/`).
* **The key.** `local_templates` keyed the template under its written scope,
  `main.$.$quasi0.Foo`. `own_templates` reads the spliced tree, whose scope
  is `main.$`. The walk now drops a spliced branch's segment at its depth.

    ptdiff 2036 -> 2038 (static-if::15, ::32), backend 3008 -> 3009;
    all else unchanged;
    tests 1774 -> 1775

## A folded enum value keeps its expression's type — 2026-09-25

`enum Foo : int8 { E2 = -128 }`: the reference walks `-128` typed `int9`,
`-1` in an `int1` enum `int2`, `-2` `int3` (`enum.k::27,33,37`, the recorded
walks). `evaluateConstexpr` leaves `IntLiteralF Nothing v` under the
expression's *own* note (`Constexpr.hs:117-283`), and the expression was
the negation of a `uint8`. The walk minted the literal typed as a bare
literal, `int8`. It now takes the table's type of the written value, and
falls back to the bare literal only where the table left it untyped.

With it, `enum.k::44`: `const uint8 count = Foo::B;` over `B = -1` turns the
enum into its literal (`TypeCheck.hs:155-156`), `int1` into `uint8`, a
narrowing stamped twice. The declaration path judged a folded enum value as
no conversion at all; it now judges it by its literal, as the call path
does.

Left in the enum rows: a substituted enum argument in a copy
(`enum.k::14,15`), whose name and literal both wear the parameter's note,
`int32`, where ours walks `EnumValue` with the literal typed `uint1`.

    ptdiff 2038 -> 2042 (enum::27,33,37,44); all else unchanged;

## A member call's name, typed as its method — 2026-09-25

`result = _obj.increment(_idx + 1);` with a `uint33` argument for a `uint32`
parameter. The reference stamps the argument twice, since `checkArg`'s
narrowing wraps it in a warning (`scheduling.k::5`, the recorded walk). Ours
stamped it once: `call_arguments` found the callee `() -> uint32`, arity 0
against 1, and left the formals unread.

The name had that type from `setTypeOfTemplateCall`'s stamp
(`set_type_of_template_call`), which the port also applies to a plain
function's name, and whose comment claimed "a stamp nothing reads". For a
member call the walk reads exactly that name. In the reference `b` of
`FunctionSpecifierF a b` is a resolved `QualifiedIdentifier`, typed by
`typeOfSymbol` of the method, so no stamp lands on it. Here the member
access resolves only once the class's members are known, and by then the
round-one stamp sat on the name. The FIELD_EXPR's own resolution now types
its name as the method (`method`, `Type.hs:1222`), overwriting the stamp.
A name typed as a function already takes no further stamp. A member
template's access is `TUnresolved` and keeps its stamp for deduction's third
source.

A guard in the stamp itself was tried first. It fixed nothing, because the
stamp had already landed, and was redundant once the name is retyped, so it
was dropped (proven by mutation).

    ptdiff 2043 -> 2047; all else unchanged; tests 1777 -> 1778

## An unrolled dimension over the induction variable — 2026-09-25

`static for (const auto i : 2) { uint32[i+1] a; }`: in iteration `$i0` the
reference walks the dimension `1` typed `uint1` (`static-for.k::0,1`, the
recorded walks); ours typed it `uint2`, the table's type of `i + 1`. The fold
of two untyped literals leaves an untyped literal under the *original* note
(`Constexpr.hs:76`), and that note had no type when `staticControl` copied
the body: the loop is unrolled at its own node (`Constexpr.hs:48-54`),
before the `const auto` it declares is typed, so every expression over the
induction variable was still unresolved. The next round types the literal
as a bare literal.

The rule is narrow on purpose. A blanket "a folded dimension is a bare
literal" broke `enum.k::42`: `bool[count]` over `const uint8 count` keeps the
constant's typed note (`castIntegralConstexpr`, `Constexpr.hs:283`). So only a
dimension that names an iteration's induction variable qualifies; each
mention is qualified by the iteration's scope, `…::$i0::i`
(`fixScopedName`, `Constexpr.hs:105-108`), which is what
`Walker::mentions_induction_var` looks for.

The other 17 of that `ParseUintType / ParseUintType` row each look like a
different mechanism (`literals.k::35` 4/5, `local-functions.k::16` 32/4,
`test_cases_15.k` 2/32, …), not yet read.

    ptdiff 2047 -> 2049 (static-for::0,1); all else unchanged; tests 1778 -> 1779

## M1: inference on the IR, in shadow — 2026-09-25

`kg-sem` transcribes `inferType` (`Type/Inference.hs`) onto the IR. The
IR mirrors `ExpF` constructor for constructor, so the rules of `infer`
(`Type.hs:1174-1340`) map almost line for line; the arithmetic under them
is `kg-ty`'s substrate-free `width`/`subtype`, unchanged.

Three details decide whether it is the reference or an imitation of it:

* **The fold rewrites in place, under the node's own note.** `-128` keeps
  `int9` (the negation's type). `1 + 2` is `TUnresolved` by `Type.hs:1182`,
  folds to a literal, and is typed `uint2` *as that literal* the next round.
  The engine writes the node's expression in its own arena (a fork), and
  leaves the `TypeMap` entry alone.
* **Declarations are read from the round's snapshot.** The reference builds
  its symbol map once per round, so a declaration typed later in a round is
  seen the round after.
* **The one discarded subtree is rolled back.** A function whose
  parameters are functions keeps its original note, `Inference.hs:55-56`,
  through `TypeMap`'s journal.

`cargo xtask sem` runs it over every library and test root and compares each
reachable `Own` node with the CST table: 95.9% of 2.26M nodes agree at first
run. The groups read so far are the CST engine's deviations, and are listed
in the plan's progress note. The next step is a classifier that books each
known CST deviation with its reference citation, so the gate's count of
unexplained disagreements can ratchet down to zero.

## M1 complete: the reference arbitrates — 2026-09-25

Agreement with the CST engine is the wrong target for the IR engine: the
CST engine deviates from the reference in known ways (above), and the IR
engine should match the reference, not them. `cargo xtask sem --oracle`
asks the reference directly. `kg-oracle --typed --passes 6` prints every
node's type after `inferType`. `f_constructors_typed` reads it back as
`(constructor, range, type)`, the typed sibling of `xtask ir`'s
`f_constructors_noted`, and each disagreement is settled by the reference's
type at the same constructor and range (falling back to the start, as spans
agree for only 93.4% of nodes).

Result over the corpus: 1258 disagreements settled for the engine, none for
the CST engine, none for neither. The gate fails on any verdict against the
engine and runs beside `ir` in `scripts/gates.sh`. It was proven
load-bearing by removing the function-template rule, which gives 10
verdicts against the engine on `test/library/data`.

The engine fixes the arbiter found:

* an unsorted `Path` (a name the sorter could not sort) is `TUnresolved`;
  typed `TUntyped` it made every call through it "Undefined function";
* `getName b` of `FunctionSpecifierF (Just a) b` is the qualified name's
  leaf. Without that, no method call was ever typed;
* the sorter's import view does not flag an imported function template, so
  `bind2nd` reaches inference bare where the reference's parser wrapped it
  in an empty `TemplateInstanceF`. `type_of_symbol` gives the wrap's
  `TUnresolved` until the view carries template shapes (single-source D2.1).

    tests 1788 -> 1790; every other gate unchanged

## M2: the engine types the copies — 2026-09-26

Run over the elaborated program's final trees, the engine typed 44% of the
nodes inside copies as the twin reads them. Three inputs the reference
hands a copy were missing, and each moved the number:

* **`setTypeOfInstance`'s note** (`Template.hs:122-139`) on each copy's
  declaration: 44 → 63%. Round one's writes were merged into the table and
  dropped. Every round's now rides on `RewrittenModule::instance_notes`.
* **The minted leaves' types**: 63 → 65%. A type the owner cannot spell is
  minted as an `__kg_mN` alias whose type sits in a side table
  (`Imports::with_foreign`). In an IR world the minted node carries its
  type; here the engine is seeded from `RewrittenModule::leaves`.
* **The un-renamed tree**: 65 → 95%. The rename layer renames identifiers,
  never scopes, so a copy is `__kg_m12` at its mentions and
  `make_capture1<|…|>` in the scopes of what it declares. Nothing resolves
  across that until the identifiers are read back.

Then two comparison fixes, both toward honesty:

* A node a fold orphans (`uint<bitsizeof T>` rewritten `uint5` drops its
  folded child) is not compared, since no walk meets it.
* A difference only in a `TInstance` note is counted apart.

The remaining disagreements that the oracle settled went to the engine:
the reference's hoisted lambdas are `LambdaFunction`, and its `Closure`
copy keeps an `auto` parameter. They are booked as the twin's deviations
by class. The report is 98.8% inside copies, and it is a report, not a
gate: M3 switches the walk and lets the reference-graded gates judge.

## The frontend made fast, and exactly — 2026-09-27

*2026-09-26/27. No scoreboard number moved; every elaboration is
identical to the one it replaced, on every corpus root, which is the whole
claim. `docs/plans/performance.md` has the plan and the measurements.*

With the twin gone the program-wide loop was the frontend, and its cost was
the testing loop's: `array.k` 17 s, `risc-v.k` 26 s, `scripts/fast.sh walk`
6.5 minutes, the full gates 20. Two days later: `array.k` 3.0 s,
`risc-v.k` 6.1 s — 9× the reference's own frontend (plan §11) — the walk
tier 79 s, workspace tests 35 s at rest.

**Every optimisation is exact, and it is the tools that say so, not the
argument.** Three of them, kept:

- `cargo xtask infer-identity` elaborates every corpus root twice —
  inference incremental, and walked whole (`KG_INFER_FULL=1`, the fixpoint
  as first written, kept as the reference) — and compares fingerprints
  that carry every fixpoint's unresolved count *iteration by iteration*
  (`Report::infer_trace`). The first incremental version ended identical
  on all 304 roots and still drifted mid-fixpoint; only the trajectory saw
  it.
- `KG_INFER_CHECK=1` runs a whole-walk iteration beside each incremental
  one from the same state and names the first differing node with its path
  and owners. It found the three facts the design had missed: the tree is
  a DAG (a folded constant shares its initializer's children), a
  declaration can be read before any walk owns it, and a shared node read
  live must wake a later sharer in the same pass.
- `infer-identity --dump DIR` writes each root's fingerprint, symbols
  spelled out, for `diff -r` against a baseline worktree's — the check for
  a change that moves both inference modes alike (the in-place rewrites,
  the collector, `desugar`). Build the worktree with `KANAGAWA_ROOT` set.

Each mechanism was then broken on purpose and the tools had to go red
(178–304 roots each); the two that stay silent on the corpus — the
between-fixpoint type journal and the mid-pass notice's child ownership —
are kept because the argument needs them, and cost 3%.

**The rewrites append, so ids are stable for the loop.** Every pass
appends into its module's own arena (`*_in_place`); only inference
rewrites a node in place, and it journals what it overwrote. That is what
lets the incremental walk's units — declarations, statements and calls,
keyed by root node — live across fixpoints, with the passes between them
seen through a type journal, new nodes, and every symbol-map lookup
remembered and re-asked where a rebuilt map differs.

**The gates replay the backend.** `kg_ptbridge::cache`, keyed by the whole
recording, compared byte for byte; `gates.sh` re-runs one hit in 20. A run
the gates would kill for its budget is killed by `kg` first and kept —
`risc-v.k`, which the reference takes 44 minutes and 13.4 GB to compile,
had cost every backend run 15 minutes — and is never re-verified, since
which budget stops it depends on load (the milestone run of 2026-09-27
found that the hard way).

**No doc tests.** There were none, and rustdoc cost 49 s of every
workspace test run; `doctest = false` everywhere, examples are unit tests.

## The foundation survey — 2026-09-27

*Read-only: nothing was built or run, no number moved. Three readings in
parallel — the crates and the data model, the query layer and the tools,
the gates and the backend bridge — with the claims the plan now leans on
read again by hand. What it changed is
[`history/sprint-parity.md`](history/sprint-parity.md)'s revision of the same
date.*

**The sprint had a target without a mechanism.** A keystroke of 400 ms was
W5.1's, by "memoized import interfaces" and a cancellable refresh. The
query layer has neither. An edit that changes the green tree makes a new
item tree (`ItemTree` cannot be compared, and `Item::range` would move
under any comparison that kept it), a new `Program`, a lowering of every
module (`sorted_program` is memoized nowhere) and the loop from its first
round; nothing in `kg-db` or `kg-sem` can be cancelled. The design for
the firewall was already written — `spec/resolve.md` §11.2, §11.6 — and
never scheduled. It is W7 now, behind `edit-identity`: a warm `Db` after
an edit against a fresh one.

**Three ways a missing instrument graded green.** `sem` returns four
zeros without `kg-oracle` and passes; `ir`'s oracle differential prints
"skipped"; and the compat binary, finding no backend library, compiles
frontend-only and exits 0 — its third candidate path is compiled in
relative to the crate, which a worktree does not have beside it. The last
is the likely mechanism of the 21 `repoint` tests a worktree's baseline
disagreed on (2026-09-23, "reason unmeasured"): `87d5d63` saw the same
fall to 32/72. Not re-measured here; W0.4 does.

**Identity by text, three times.** An instance is keyed by its arguments'
rendering and read back by about a dozen parsers of mangled names; a
diagnostic's message decides whether the pass-9 checkpoint closes
(`passes/mod.rs:172`) and merges the two engines' reports
(`db.rs:1534`); four environment variables change what the compiler
decides, outside every memo key. `single-source-of-truth.md`'s
`xtask lint`, the ratchet against the first, was never written.

**Locations are not only comments.** The backend prints them in its
errors (`errors.h:110`), maps them in its debug symbols, and under
`--code-coverage` builds names from them (`ir.cpp:2210-2218`). "Identical
modulo locations" stays the bar; the plan's §8 has the cost, and W6 a
gate on the backend's message text, which nothing compared.

**Where a reading was wrong.** `kanagawa/` is a git checkout (`98a2d8c`,
six commits past the `8e0a3fb` the removed workflow pinned and
`spec/diagnostics.md` was extracted at), not a bare tree; and
`kg-db/src/instances.rs`, which reads as dead — `kg dump instances` and
`xtask ir` are its only callers — is the register's independent second
reading, to go at M6 with the lines that grade it, not before.
