## What the loop leaves, and five programs the guard cut short — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W0.1, W0.2, W0.6. `cargo xtask loop-left`; the oracle driver's
`--loop` mode.*

**The metric was measured under the wrong settings, and counted the wrong
thing.** `Report::left` read 3964 over 155 roots, and `risc-v.k` 1039
under `xtask`'s settings against 141 under the compat compiler's. The
first is `bench::rooted_settings`: `mini-base.k` and `test/syntax` on the
import path — the syntax tests' environment, not the one the reference
compiles the corpus's programs in. Under it `risc-v.k` is *rejected*
(`make_optional` not in scope, 16 errors) and its leftovers are an
aborted program's. The metric now uses the recorded compile's flags
(`--import-dir library`, the default base), the same `ptdiff` and
`backend` use.

And the reference leaves instances too: a `TemplateInstance` inside a
non-template declaration that no round's census reaches survives pass 8
in its tree exactly as in ours. `data/cache.k`'s seven leftovers are the
reference's seven, name for name. So a raw count cannot reach the plan's
"0 on every program the reference compiles". `loop-left` spells both
sides' leftovers by the reference's own `getScope|getQualifier|getName`
and compares multisets: of our 2701, 2557 were the reference's.

**The rest was the guard.** The reference's round count is the smallest
`--template-iterations R` whose pass-8 tree equals the fixpoint's — the
budget counts down one per deciding round and at zero runs the same pass
list and `deduplicateInstances` as the round that decides nothing
(`Template.hs:52-57`), so the property is monotone and the driver
searches it (about ten frontends a root, cold: 485 s for the corpus, then
replayed from the oracle cache). It agreed with ours on every root but
five, and on those five the reference took 33, 33, 34, 36 and 51 rounds
where `ROUND_GUARD` stopped us at 32. Its comment said the corpus needed
at most 12; `budget.rs` said `array.k` took 31. The five held 143 of the
144 instances only we left. `data/string.k`, "at the guard" in the
plan, was a real count of 34, not a loop that does not converge.

With the guard at 128 — the reference has none — rounds agree 321/321
and leftovers 320/321, and the five programs agree through the real
backend (`backend` 3210 → 3215). What is left is one instance, W1.2's.

**What it overturns.** W7.5b's premise, that the port pays the round
floor more often than the reference: it takes the same number of
rounds. The keystroke's cost is the cost per round (W7.5a, W5.3–W5.4).

**The oracle driver computes, the reference decides.** `--loop` is ours
(`oracle/driver/Main.hs`): it calls the reference's `frontend` with
different `templateIterations` and compares the trees with `Note`'s own
`Eq`, which ignores notes. It changes nothing the frontend computes; a
rebuilt driver re-keys the whole oracle cache, so the first `errors` and
`ir` after it run cold.

**A mutant that survived its own restore.** `mutant.sh` put the original
file back with `cp -p`, old mtime and all; the last build had been of the
mutant, and cargo does not rebuild a source older than its artifact. The
rebuild after a `loop-left` mutant finished in 0.04 s with the mutant
still compiled in. The restore now touches the file.

## The query layer measured before it is changed — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W0.5, W7.1, W7.5a, W7.5c. `kg_db::stats`, `cargo xtask
edit-identity`, `bench --filter phases`, `KG_LOOP_PROFILE`, `cargo xtask
loop-modules`. No number a user sees moved; the cross-build dump against
`0aa5e1a` is identical on all 304 roots.*

**What an edit recomputes, counted.** Every memo now counts its hits and
misses and times its misses exclusive of what they asked for. The answer
for today's layer is short: any edit that changes a green tree — a body,
a signature, an import, a library module's body — misses one item tree,
then `program`, `looped`, the sorted lowering of *every* module and every
module's `file_scope`, and the loop runs from round one. Base inference
is the exception that already works: it re-infers the edited module and
only those whose imported maps changed. `crates/kg-db/tests/memo.rs`
pins each edit's line, so each mechanism W7 lands shows as that line
changing.

**The keystroke was measured on a program the reference rejects.** The
bench's `keystroke` stage builds its `Db` from `rooted_settings`
(`mini-base.k`, `test/syntax`), under which `risc-v.k` has 16 errors —
the 1.46 s the sprint started from. Under the recorded compile's
settings a `risc-v.k` body edit costs 1.82 s in the editor (four rounds)
and 5.6 s at the fixpoint, 72% and 90% of it the loop.

**`edit-identity` is the gate every memo lands behind.** A `Db` kept warm
across the corpus, as an editor's is, against a fresh one after every
edit and every undo: diagnostics, the loop's fingerprint, every table.
Green today (348 roots, 1123 edits) because nothing is skipped; red on
every edit kind when the item-tree memo ignores its parse. Its first run
made no library-body edit at all: the first import a module "has" is the
implicit base, `base.k`, which declares no function, and the edit
quietly found nowhere to land. It now takes the first *written* import
that has a body, and the run reports how many of each edit it made.

**W7.5a's hypothesis was wrong.** The plan read the round's floor as
walks of library modules that gained nothing. Measured: those visits are
most of the visits and 5% of `risc-v.k`'s loop. The time is inference,
the three whole-program symbol maps each round rebuilds, the prefix
passes, and the few modules that did grow — walked whole for the nodes
they gained. A pass that skips a module is worth 5–10% on the programs
that matter; one that visits only what changed inside a module, or
symbol maps patched rather than rebuilt (W5.4), is where the floor is.

**W7.5c: a library module's state depends on the root through its
copies' dating.** What a library module wrote comes out identical under
two roots (all but one node's type in one module per pair). The copies
two roots both ask of it do not: 57 of 90 shared copies decided in
different rounds for `array.k` against `vector.k`. The round is part of
the result (copy order, and the earliest round a mention inside a copy
can be decided), so the per-module memo of `ir-elaboration.md` §3.2 would
not be exact. W7.5d starts from that.

**A dump diff that lied, and why.** The first cross-build diff differed
on nine roots: the new build had been run with `--kanagawa-root
../kanagawa` and the baseline with an absolute path, and `infer-identity`
collected its roots under the path as given, so a library root that
imports what imports it was loaded twice under two file ids. Both
`infer-identity` and `sem` now canonicalize the root first; the gates
always passed an absolute one.

## Cancellation, and where its latency was — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W7.2. `kg_base::cancel`; `bench --filter cancel`.*

**Unwinding, not a `Result`.** A cancelled computation must write no memo
and must not need every signature between a checkpoint and the caller to
change. Each memo in `Db` is inserted after its value is computed, so an
unwind that passes through a query writes nothing for it — salsa made the
same choice for the same reason. `resume_unwind` runs no panic hook, and
no memo lock is held at any checkpoint (each is read into a temporary and
released), so the database an unwind leaves is sound: the server keeps
the project instead of evicting it as it does after a real panic. What a
finished sub-query memoized stays; it answered its own inputs correctly.

**Where the time went.** The first checkpoints — between rounds and
between passes — left 203 ms: the sorted lowering and base inference
had none, and nor did the root module's single visits late in the loop.
Per-module checkpoints and a strided one inside the rewriting and
inference walks brought it to 48–71 ms, growing with how far the check
had run. The growth was the unwind itself: dropping `risc-v.k`'s
elaborated program, millions of nodes, on the caller's thread. A
cancelled `Program` now hands its memory to a thread that frees it, and
the worst case is 14–32 ms.

**A token stack per thread.** Code that holds no `Db` — the rewriting
walk in `kg-hir`, the CST passes — checks the tokens of every computation
the thread is inside (`kg_base::cancel::scope`): the query's, raised by an
edit, and the request's, raised by `$/cancelRequest`.

## The resilience gate, first and empty — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W3.0. `cargo xtask resilience`, `xtask/src/resilience.rs`.*

**What "error-recovered" is, counted.** The plan's 76 is every corpus
`.k` whose whole-file parse reports an error: 73 `test/syntax/*.k`
snippet accumulators, `test/syntax/imports/a1/…` and the two
`tools/chkdoc/contexts` templates — all snippet files; no whole program
fails to parse (`xtask corpus` holds that). An accumulator is what an
editor holds mid-edit, a file of fragments, so it is the right corpus;
64 mutants of `xtask fuzz`'s broken-buffer mutators (the byte-level
ones — `difffuzz`'s are grammatical and would mostly still parse),
redrawn until they fail to parse, are laid over clean files as
overlays, the way an unsaved buffer reaches the `Db`.

**What the editor reads today, and what is compared.** Hover is
`Db::definition_at` then `Db::type_of_definition` (the CST table at the
declaration node), completion `Db::completions_at` with each candidate's
detail the same way; both filtered by `hover.rs`'s `shown`. Only the
type-reading half moves at M6, so the IR side shares the name
resolution and is asked only for types: it answers where it holds a
node, in the reference's own rendering, and says nothing otherwise. A
member list (`s.`) is read off the CST type of the base, so it is "no
answer" on the IR side until that is ported. The gate is blind to name
resolution (a wrong jump agrees with itself), to hover ranges, and to
signature help and inlay hints.

**The reference is in the ledger.** Every graded answer is a `cst` item
(`file@offset KIND name = answer`), a pass set: while the migration
runs, any change in what the editor says — whichever engine made it —
is named, and neither the IR's progress nor a CST change can hide
behind the other. `ir-only` (the IR has a type the reference does not)
is a fail set on purpose: an answer nobody adjudicated is blessed, not
assumed. The verdict is the ratchet alone, as `loop-left`'s is: a
first reading is blessed, and from then on an item that got worse is
red — the engines already part on real programs (`sem` measures
where), so "no disagreement" could not be the rule.

**Its first run found a bug in the editor.** `--jobs 1` and the default
parted on 107 completion lists: `names_in_scope` sorted imported names
by `SymbolPath`, which compares interned ids — numbered in the order the
`Db` first met each name — so the order a client showed (its
`sort_text`) depended on what else the session had opened. It sorts by
spelling now (`complete.rs`, a test proven by reverting the sort). The
`CLAUDE.md` rule held: a verdict that differs between `--jobs 1` and
the default is a `Db`-history bug, not the fan-out's.

**Proven before it grades anything.** No `baseline.json` section exists
until the main checkout blesses one, so the proof ran in a throwaway
copy of the tree with its own blessed baseline: the CST hover typed at
the declaration's parent (2690 `cst` items left), the IR side answering
`bool` everywhere (2604 `disagree` and 2368 `ir-only` entered), and
every imported completion name upper-cased (965 left) are each red; the
IR side echoing the reference is green with 2687 improvements. Runtime
~1.5 s over 8 threads, 7 s on one, under 1 GB.

## One position index, and what the IR answers through it — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W3.5. `kg_hir::position`, `Looped::index`, `Db::ir_type_of_definition`.*

**Ranges order the nodes, not the tree.** The index holds the `Own`
nodes at `Expansion::ROOT`, in the module's own file, reachable from
the root — `Donated` wears a donor's text, `Reread` stands where an
`Own` node already does, a copy's node is the body seen through one
instance, and an unreachable node is one a rewrite replaced. The loop's
rewrites move nodes (a method out of its class, a lambda's body into a
function) without changing their `Src`, so the tree's shape says little
about where a node's text is; its head says everything, and every `Own`
head is a CST node's range (`lower.rs`'s `own_src`), so the ranges nest.
"Innermost" is the smallest range holding the offset, and between equal
ranges — a `NamedValue` over the `NAME_REF` lowered with it — the node
deeper in the tree. Sorted by start, then end descending, each entry
keeps the nearest entry enclosing it; a query is the last entry
starting at or before the offset, then up that chain to the first that
holds it. The test fixtures lower *sorted*, as `kg-db` does: the
unsorted lowering keeps a path as one `Path` node and donates nothing
inside it, so against it the donated-node test had no donated node to
skip.

**What the IR answers, and where it cannot.** Through the index the
loop's final tree types 958 of the 1716 hovers the CST engine types, the
same way every time; it contradicts none. It types 519 the CST engine
cannot — template instances the loop elaborated (`newtype<uint32>`) —
and those are `ir-only`, unadjudicated. The 758 it cannot answer are
mostly declarations its tree no longer holds: a snippet accumulator
redefines `main` and `Main` dozens of times and the loop keeps one
(`a_declaration_the_loop_dropped_has_no_ir_answer` pins the shape), and
a mutant can break a declaration the lowering then does not keep. That
is the corner §2.6's balance point asks about, measured: the editor on
the IR engine alone would lose the type of every redefinition in a
buffer. Completion disagrees on 9 lists — `basics.k`'s `auto y = x <<
amt` (`int63` in the CST table, `uint63` in the loop) and
`constexpr.k`'s redefined `c`. Blessed as the gate's starting state on
2026-09-27 with those nine held by its `disagree` fail set: the `c` is a
redefinition the reference rejects, so neither engine is right; the
shift's signedness is open, for the reference to settle.

## The sorted lowering, memoized by what it read — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W7.3. `kg_db::sorted::SortedMemo`; `ImportSymbols::compared`;
the `sorted module` counter. The cross-build dump against `69c878c` is
identical on all 304 roots.*

**The plan's key was a reading of what the graph could reach; the memo
keys on what the lowering asked.** `kg_hir::lower_sorted` takes a parse,
a file id, the interner and an import door, and the door is the only
input that crosses modules. So the memo records every distinct question
the lowering put to the door and the answer it got, and a lowering is
reused when its parse is the same `Arc` and each question, asked again,
reads the same. It is the salsa argument in small: a deterministic walk
that gets the same answers asks the same next question. Nothing has to
enumerate "per module the graph can reach": a question never asked cannot
have changed the result.

**The fingerprint moves with a body edit, and is read.** The plan left
that open. `kg_hir::sort::fingerprint` hashes the whole declared tree,
body included, because it stands for `nub`'s equality — symbol trees with
notes ignored (`SymbolTable.hs:229-237`, `Parser/Syntax.hs:594-599`). It
is observable: a root that is itself `module lib` and declares the
`twice` it imports resolves the call (the two are one) until `lib.k`'s
body changes, and then the name is ambiguous and stays bare
(`memo.rs`, `an_imported_body_edit_can_re_sort_an_importer`). With the
answers compared whole, `risc-v.k`'s library body edit re-lowered three
modules of 50, the root among them — one answer of its 982 differed, by
fingerprint only — and `array.k`'s four of 39, 41 of the root's answers
differing by token only (a local added to a body moves every later
`ItemId`).

**Read only where `nub` weighs two hits.** `SymTab::one` is the only
reader of a hit's token and fingerprint, and it reads them only for an
answer that met another hit. The lowering now says so
(`ImportSymbols::compared`, a no-op by default); an answer never compared
is checked on its count, shapes and scopes, which are all the rest of
what the lowering reads of it. That took `risc-v.k`'s library body edit
to one module, and its lowering from 0.18 s (every module) through 0.14 s
(answers compared whole) to 0.006 s.

**What the instruments see.** `edit-identity` turns red with the answers
left out of the key — on one root of the quarter run, `config.k`'s
import edit — and with the parse left out. It is blind to the finer
parts: its four edits never change an importer's answers without
changing the importer's text, except through the library body, whose
answers differ by fingerprint or token and are never compared. So three
`memo.rs` tests are the instrument there, each red under its mutant: the
fingerprint left out of a compared answer, the shape left out of an
uncompared one, and `nub` never reporting. The token has no test: two
hits of one declaration share a fingerprint, so a token decides `nub`
only between hits that have none — an unharvested key. It stays in the
comparison.

**An `UPDATE_EXPECT` run in a worktree rewrote the main checkout.**
`expect-test` finds the file to rewrite from the *outermost* ancestor
directory holding a `Cargo.toml` unless `CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR` is set, and
a `.claude/worktrees/` checkout sits inside the main one. The snapshot
lines went into `kgrust/crates/kg-db/tests/memo.rs` while the worktree's
own copy stayed stale and its tests still passed (they compare against
the compiled literal). Run it as `CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR=$PWD UPDATE_EXPECT=1
cargo test …` from a worktree.

## A diagnostic's kind, and the verdict switches as settings — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W8.1 and W8.2. `kg_diag::DiagnosticKind`, `kg_hir::ErrorNote`,
`kg_config::Verdicts`. `lint` message-test 4 → 0, env-verdict 5 → 0;
every other ledger unchanged, and the cross-build `infer-identity
--dump` identical to `2a64ce7`'s on all 304 roots after each.*

**A kind has to be set by every emitter of its family, not only by the
one a test was written against.** `Db::check` seeds the CST run with
what `kg_sem::check` raised inside the copies (`run_whole_program(…,
carried)`), so the pass-9 checkpoint and `deduceAutoTypes`' return arm
see the loop's "Could not deduce all arguments" and "static if
predicate" diagnostics beside the CST passes' own. A text test caught
both; a kind test catches only a kinded one. So `kg_sem::check`'s two are
kinded too, as are pass 4's and pass 12's LT verdicts and pass 16's
`static if`. The conflicting deduction is carried on the IR — `reconcile`
marks its table entry and `Cx::arg` writes the kind into the
`Exp::Error` — because its text travelled that way.

**`kg_sem::check`'s round test cannot be shown load-bearing, and was not
before.** Every conflict node is minted by `Mint::new_note`, which
donates, so `written` is false and the node is raised whatever `round`
says; the mutant `round = false` survives every test and gate. The kind
test is kept as the rule for an `Own` conflict, with a comment saying no
program reaches it.

**The gates no longer see the verdict variables.** They were read inside
the compiler, so `KG_LEFTOVERS=1 cargo xtask conformance` graded the
leftover verdicts. They are now settings (`Settings::verdicts`), read
from the environment by `kg`, `kanagawa` and `kg-lsp` only; a gate's own
`Db`s are built by `conformance::settings_for`, the scoreboard's, and
grade the defaults. A compiler a gate spawns (`backend`, `output`,
`repoint`) still reads them. `xtask` says so on stderr when one is set.
W1.4's gate — "no `expected:0` gains an error with the leftovers on" —
therefore needs the switch passed explicitly, which is the scoreboard
owner's change to make. `KG_LEFTOVERS` had also been an `env_flag!`, read
once per process: a `Db` could not have changed it; `set_settings` now
does, and `a_verdict_switch_is_a_setting_every_memo_sees` holds it.

**`KG_SEM_ONLY=1`'s `ptdiff` reading is the default's** (the baseline
build, `2a64ce7`, which still read the variable): exact 0, structural
2373 — the same set — diverged 44, declined 5. The walk's fall-through to
the CST table decides nothing `ptdiff` can see (sprint W3.6's first
condition); no program was found for a unit test of the switch's
threading, which shares `ModuleCtx::with_switches` with the seed's.

## W2 row 1: four silences that were waiting upstream — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W2, the table's first row. `scripts/fast.sh walk`: strict
failing 34 → 30, `errors` silent 28 → 24, `backend` declined 46 → 42.*

**The row's premise was wrong.** It read as `deduceAuto`'s rewrite half
left unported. Pass 17's two function clauses (`deduce_auto.rs`,
`function`) were already written, keyed on what the passes before it
leave in the sink — the LT verdict at the returned call, the `static if`
predicate's error — and both silences were those verdicts missing, not
pass 17's. The other two were pass 19's, not 17's.

- `return Fn_T_N();` in `inline auto Run()` over a `T[N] Fn_T_N()`: pass
  4 treats a call in a `return` as one the context may yet inform, and so
  declines the LT verdict. The reference stamps only a *typed* function's
  top-level returns (`Type.hs:1161-1166`, guarded `t /= TAuto` at
  `:1121`); a bare-`auto` function's type is its return's, so nothing
  informs the call. `context_expects_a_type` now says so.
- `static if (decltype(main) == () -> bool)` as the first return-bearing
  statement of `inline auto main()`: `main`'s type is the `static if`'s
  (`returnExp StaticIf{} = True`, `Type.hs:1211-1217`), so the predicate
  never folds. Pass 16 reports that cycle (`asks_the_type_it_decides`);
  even `(… == …) && false` stays standing in the reference, which is not
  claimed.
- `static Foo<(uint32) -> auto> foo;` over `class Foo { using callback_t
  = T; }`: `check AutoF` (`TypeCheck.hs:51`) fires *in the copy*, at the
  written argument. A struct field `T x;` instead reports its own
  variable verdict and not the `auto`, and a function template that never
  uses `T` compiles — so the error is the copy's, not the argument's,
  and `kg_sem::check` asks it only over a copied alias.

**A substituted argument is in a copy without saying so.** The loop's
copy of `Foo<(uint32) -> auto>` holds the argument's nodes with their own
`Src` — `Own`, `via` the root — so `Cx::in_copy` is false at the `auto`
while true at the class around it. The check carries the enclosing copy
down the walk (`Cx::copies`); any later check on substituted arguments
needs the same.

## The redundant-import seed is a fact of the walk — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W1.3. `ptdiff` structural 2384 → 2395; nine of the eleven were
"ordering" rows the plan booked to copy order.*

**`checkRedundantImports` puts a node in every file, and the backend walk
sees it.** Each file's `Seq` starts with an empty `Seq` wrapped in one
`WarningF redundant-import` per import still `Redundant` when the file
ends (`Parser.hs:234-240`); bare, pass 15 flattens it away; wrapped, the
walk emits a `ParseBaseList` for it. So an import we credit that the
reference does not — or the reverse — is a `ptdiff` divergence, not only
a warning. `kg-db/src/imports.rs` had over-approximated uses on purpose
("a missed warning is undecidable, an invented one breaks `warning:0`");
that trade priced in the scoreboard and not the walk. It now aims at
exact and keeps the superset only where the file cannot say.

**What the reference looks up for a member.** A method call is
`methodSpecifier`: the receiver's type name `T` (`resolveTypeName`,
through member accesses, indexing and an alias), then `T::Go`
(`Parser.hs:729-757`) — never `Go` alone, so an import exposing a free
`Go` is not credited by `foo.Go()`. A field access (`access`,
`Parser.hs:811-819`) and a designator (`:863`) parse `identifier` and
look nothing up. A class body is a scope like a block for what it
declared earlier (`findInScopes`), a member function's body included. An
instance's name is its template's (`getName (TemplateInstanceF a _)`).

**A header moves the seed.** `moduleDecl` returns `Seq [ModuleDecl …]`
(`Parser.hs:188`), so `checkRedundantImports`' `ModuleDecl` clause
(`:234`) is never the one taken for a file: the `Seq` clause seeds the
outer list, and the seed is walked before the namespace's name.

**How it was found, for the next one.** `kg-oracle --roots-only --passes
1 --tree F.k | grep -c 'WarningF redundant-import'` is the reference's
redundancy verdict per file — `--errors` prints no warnings — and
without `--roots-only` it counts the imported modules too, which is
where `imports.k::43`'s warning lives (`a1/a6.k`).

**A false "caught" from `scripts/mutant.sh`.** In zsh an unquoted `$C`
holding a command is not word-split: `mutant.sh … -- $C` ran a command
named `cargo test …`, which does not exist, and reported the mutant
caught. Every mutant here was re-run with the command written out, and
`target/mutant/last.log` read for the test's own assertion.

## The interface firewall, keyed on what inference read — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W7.4. `kg_db::passes::types::ImportsRead`; `Db::file_scope`,
`Db::infer_module` and `Db::late_constants` re-keyed. The cross-build
dump against `4778c7b` is identical on all 304 roots.*

**The plan's design was a reading, and half of it was wrong.** It had
the base tables keyed on the direct imports' converged maps by pointer,
the cutoff lost only because a re-inferred module hands out a new
pointer, and the fix a comparison by value. The first half is so: a
library body edit re-inferred every importer of the edited module
(`risc-v.k` 4 of 50 modules, `array.k` 11 of 39) and rebuilt every
module's fold environment, which was keyed on the program's pointer.
The fix is not. A module's map holds every declaration it files,
function locals included (`f::$::x`), so a body edit that declares a
local makes an unequal map — measured with a probe, on `memo.rs`'s lib
and on `array.k`'s root body and signature edits (`risc-v.k`'s, and both
bench files' library body edits, land where the map was equal — inside
a template, whose body `TemplateDecl` does not file). `Ty`'s `==` ignores a
parameter's name (`Type.hs:126-129`) and an importer's table holds the
function type it was handed, names and all. And an importer reads maps
that are not its direct imports': `Imports::type_of_def` types a
re-exported hit off the map of the module that *declares* it. With
pointers every one of those was covered by accident — each edit renewed
every pointer downstream — and a value comparison of the direct
imports would have kept a stale importer the first time a re-exported
declaration changed type.

**So the key is what was read.** The model is the sorted lowering's
(W7.3): the fixpoint reaches other modules through one door, `Imports`,
whose answer cache already held every distinct question with its
answer. The memo keeps that cache and is valid while each question,
asked again of the new program, reads the same — by `Ord`, which sees
the parameter names. A module that asked nothing the edit changed
keeps its table; a local no importer can ask for moves nothing.

**Two inputs no key named.** The fold environment (`FileScope`) is
built from the module's tree *and its imports' constants*; the old doc
comment called the table "a pure function of the module's item tree"
and was exact only because the scope was rebuilt on every program. It
is now keyed on the tree and the imported constants by value, with the
program's pointer as the cheap check, and hands back its old `Arc` —
which the base table keys on. `late_constants` was keyed on the scope's
pointer alone and folds against the module's type table (its roots in
no key either); with the scope surviving program changes that would
have gone stale the first time an imported struct changed width. It
now keys on the table too. Each has a `memo.rs` test red under its
mutant.

**What the instruments see.** `edit-identity` — whole, 348 roots and
1123 edits — is green, and its quarter stays green with the importer's
reads left out of the key and with the imported constants left out:
its four edits never change what an importer reads. The unit tests are
the instrument, as they were for W7.3's fingerprints: an imported
signature, a parameter's name, a constant's value under an unchanged
type (`uint32`, not `auto` — an `auto` constant's width is its
literal's, which the door answers for, and the first version of that
test pinned the door instead of the environment and survived the scope
mutant), and an imported struct's width through a late constant.

**What it bought.** Little time: base inference and the scopes were
~24 ms of `risc-v.k`'s 1.7 s library-body keystroke and are now ~1 ms;
the keystroke is the loop's. `Db::program` still moves with every item
tree, and with it `looped` — which reads every body and would rerun on
a body edit whatever the program's key. The plan's third layer, the
program keyed on a `ModuleInterface`, is left for W7.5d: §11.2's
interface maps names to `ItemId`s, which a local declared above them
moves.

## W2 rows 8–11: a driver's flag, a parser choice the lowering denied, and `nub` — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W2, rows 8 to 11, in a worktree beside rows 6–7. `scripts/fast.sh
--lint walk` / `loop`, cumulative: conformance 2580 → 2587, strict failing
25 → 15, `errors` silent 19 → 15 (agree 678 → 682), `ptdiff` structural
2384 → 2391, `backend` agree 3233 → 3246 (declined 28 → 18).*

**`--Werror` is the driver's, and the scoreboard's seam is the snippet
protocol.** `Main.hs:93-99` fails a clean frontend on its printed warnings;
the CLIs already did, `Db::check` never did, so `all-warnings-as-errors.k`
and `callbacks.k::10` were strict failures with a correct compiler binary.
`Db::check_snippet` — the whole-run protocol the scoreboard calls — now
returns a clean program's warnings as errors under the flag, kinds kept, so
`errors` still grades the first warning's position and message.
`Db::check` is unchanged: `Db::instances`' error gate reads it.

**A warning is not an error to `errors a`.** Conversion's `poisoned`
counted every sink entry as `null (errors a)` does; `errors` lists `ErrorF`
only (`Error.hs:88-92`). It never mattered until pass 19 had a warning
inside an expression — `initializer-overrides` on `{.x = 10, .x = 11}` —
and then it hid the conversion error beside it.

**Row 9's unsorted paths were a parser alternative the lowering said did
not exist.** `field_member`'s comment held that `.member<args>` outside a
call never parses (`notFollowedBy templateArgs`, `Parser.hs:812`); that is
the *lvalue* parser. The expression parser tries `methodInstanceSpecifier`
before `value` (`Parser.hs:766-770,849`), so `obj.template Go<uint32>` as a
value is a `FunctionSpecifier` with its receiver — `kg-oracle --tree
--passes 0` shows it — and the loop, handed that, makes the instance with
no change of its own. `dependent-template.k::12` (a conversion the
reference reports on the same shape) came with it, a row-6/7 silence.

**`resolvedFuncParams` needs the program, so pass 2 now has it.** An
alias-typed callback (`using Callback = (uint32) -> uint32`) makes a
higher-order template in the reference (`Function.hs:133-141`); the IR's
pass 2 read the written type only. `kg_sem::pass1::heads` builds the
program's symbols (only when some module declares an alias of a function
type or of a name) and `higher_order::apply_with` copies the alias's
`FunctionType` across arenas (`ExpArena::deep_copy_from`). The walk test
that used the alias shape for the "call of a variable" decline had said
"when it closes, this needs another call no rewrite reaches"; the
replacement, `decltype(g)`, is a program the reference *rejects* and this
frontend accepts — the decline is what keeps that silence from compiling.

**A certain leftover: a type for a template-template parameter.**
`templateArgsResolved` asks `tIsTemplate` of such an argument
(`TypeCheck.hs:323-329`) while `unresolveArgError` asks
`templateArgResolved`, which a type passes (`Frontend.hs:423-426`), so the
instance is never made and pass 12 says "Failed to instantiate template"
(`template-template-parameter.k::36,37`). A type argument is final, so the
loop's check asks that one arm without `KG_LEFTOVERS`. Its `Ty::Type`
guard (rather than the reference's full `not tIsTemplate`) is a silence
margin no unit test can show load-bearing: no program leaves an instance
with a template argument standing that the reference makes. The two other
#32 silences (`constexpr.k::132`, `template-argument-deduction.k::143`)
are pass 12 at the module's own text, which the loop's check does not
judge even with `KG_LEFTOVERS=1`; closing them needs a module-text verdict
that the CST run drops when its pass-9 checkpoint closes
(`Frontend.hs:42-52`), since the loop cannot see that flag.

**Row 11's premise was false: not the walk.** The `dsp.k` "backend
disagreements" were parse-time ambiguities (`checkSymbols`' `findSymbol`,
`SymbolTable.hs:228-237,261`): a device's `hardware.dsp` as the root
exports `fmul32` while `base.k` imports `mock`'s. The first port reported
every such name and swapped the two disagreements for two others:
`arria-10-gx-1150`'s and `stratix-10-nx-2100`'s declarations are *textually
`mock`'s*, and `nub` compares trees with notes ignored
(`Parser/Syntax.hs:594-595`), so to the reference they are one
definition. The decision now reads the sorted lowering's position-free
fingerprint — the same one the sorter's own `nub` uses. The
library-acceptance test had asserted every library file compiles; the
reference rejects these two, and the test now names them. The same check
closed `imports.k::63`, a row-7 one-off.

## W2 rows 6–7: the parser's table, and five one-offs — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W2, rows 6 and 7. `scripts/fast.sh walk --lint`.*

**Row 6: a class's members are in its table before its body is.**
`class_` parses each class twice: once under `lookAheadSkippingMemberBody`
to collect every member for which `isTemplate m || isType m || isVariable
m`, then for real with those seeded into the scope (`Parser.hs:316-329`).
So inside a class, a variable, alias or nested type member shadows a
module-scope template of the same name *wherever the member is written*,
including the alias being declared: `using Foo = Foo<10>;` in a class is
`Foo < 10 >` and a parse error (`using.k::37`), where the same line at
module scope reads the template, because `parseSymbol` registers a
declaration only once it is parsed. Member *functions* are not seeded: a
later one is not in the table, and the reference then reports "Undefined
template" from the frontend instead — left silent here. Struct fields
are no symbols at all (`memberVariable` is `noted`, not `symbol`).

The other two shapes are the table's kind checks: a template template
parameter's default goes through `templateSpecifier`, which wants a
template (an alias, a plain struct, or a template declared later all
fail), and a function template instance is no `typeSpecifier` (`isType`
of a function template is `False`). All three are `PARSE-ERROR`s, so the
`errors` gate books them "parse-time table", not agree.

**Row 7: five one-offs, and one comment that was wrong.** `kg-hir`'s
`field_member` said "`.member<args>` outside a call never parses in the
reference". It does, as a *term*: `methodInstanceSpecifier` runs before
`value` (`Parser.hs:765-769`), and a member spelled with `template` and
arguments is a `FunctionSpecifier (Just obj) (TemplateInstance …)` — a
method named as a value, `{.callback = obj.template Go<uint32>}`. Lowered
that way, two accepted programs walk that the walk declined as unsorted
paths (`dependent-template.k::9,10`) and the rejected one converts
(`::12`).

`memory.k::19` is pass 10's, on a node the text does not have: `mem[0]
+= 10` is `Assign lval (Binary Add lval 10)` noted at the lvalue, and the
CST pass has no `Binary` there to find a `TError` on. The loop's IR has it
(`kg-hir` synthesizes it), and its type is the reference's message word
for word. `x++`'s `Binary` has no note at all in the reference, and an
ill-typed one crashes it (`bool b; b++;` → `Prelude.undefined`,
`Error.hs:199`) — left silent.

**`nub` ignores notes.** `findSymbol`'s ambiguity test is `nub` over the
answers (`SymbolTable.hs:231`), and `Eq (Note n f a)` compares the
expression alone (`Parser/Syntax.hs:593-595`). Two files declaring the
same module name therefore declare *one* symbol wherever their
declarations are equal token for token: under the default device,
`device/arria-10-gx-1150/hardware/dsp.k`'s export list is clean (its
`fmul32` is `device/mock/`'s exactly) and `agilex-7-f-023`'s is "`fmul32`:
undefined symbol" (one literal differs) — both files sitting in `library/`
and both walked by the gates. Only the export list's check counts answers
by namespace for it; the other ambiguity reports compare declarations by
identity, which can only over-report where two same-named modules declare
equal symbols — not seen in the corpus.

**Where the reference reports an undefined qualified name.** Three nodes
carry the verdict, and each has its own note (`Frontend.hs:97-102`,
probed 2026-09-27): a value's `QualifiedIdentifier` is `copyNote`d from
its scoped name, whose note is the *last* identifier, so `Foo::Bar` and
`B::NOPE` are reported at the last segment and named by it; a callee's is
re-`noted` over the whole path by `freeFunctionSpecifier`, so `Foo::Bar()`
is at `Foo` and still names `Bar`; a type's `TypeIdentifier` stays quiet
under `not (hasErrors x)` and the innermost undefined `ScopedName` speaks,
so `M::Nope n;` over an alias `M` is "Type name not in scope: `M`". A
module path is never a qualifier — `findInImport` matches a namespace
(`@m@n`), not its dotted spelling — so `m::n::K` is undefined even when
`K` exists, and named `K`. This port had named the head for all three.

## W1.3's type-width rows: four mechanisms, none of them the walk — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W1.3. `ptdiff` structural 2402 → 2409, diverged 19 → 12;
`output` equal 264 → 265.*

**Every row's first divergent call was a `ParseUintType`/`ParseIntType`
width or an alias spelled out, and not one was the walk's typing.** Each
came from the loop's tree or types, four ways:

- **`validateArg` sees through `TInstance`.** Its re-stamp asks
  `tIsSigned (theType typ)` and `sizeOf typ` (`TypeCheck.hs:281-285`),
  both of which look through `TConst` and `TInstance`. The census matched
  a bare `Unsigned`, so `template <fifo_index_t I>` with `using
  fifo_index_t = index_t<N>` substituted `0` unstamped — `uint1` against
  the reference's `uint2`. `T N` under `T = UInt<16>` is the same
  (`test_cases_24.k`'s `N - 1`: `int17` in the reference, since `10u16 -
  1` is typed, where the unstamped `10 - 1` is an untyped `9`).
- **Unroll a round late, as the reference does.** Per node the reference
  runs `inferExpType`, `evaluateConstexpr`, `staticControl`
  (`Inference.hs:50`). `2*N-1` folds `2*N` in one round, and the
  subtraction waits for the product's literal to be typed (`typeResolved
  a`, `Constexpr.hs:172`); only then is the limit an `IntLiteral`, the
  `const auto` variable typed `constIndexType`, and the loop unrolled with
  that type. The IR engine's unroll read the limit's value through the
  arithmetic and so unrolled while the variable was still untyped — each
  iteration's copy then typed by its own literal. The unroll is shared
  with the CST-side passes (`for_twin`), which fold nothing in place and
  still need the value read; the switch is that flag.
- **A typed fold is typed by the nodes.** `typedIntLiteral $
  inferBinaryOp op a b` (`Constexpr.hs:200-202`) reads the operands'
  *notes*, and a folded operand keeps the note it had: `-1` is the
  negation's `tSuper uint1 int1 = int2`, not the literal's `int1`. So
  `-1 << 8u16` is `int10`. `kg_hir::constexpr::binary` computes the type
  from the values alone and is right only when note and literal agree;
  `kg-sem` now re-types with its own `inferBinaryOp` port.
- **A spliced alias is a copy.** `resolve e'@TypeIdentifierF{}`
  (`Constexpr.hs:149-151`) splices an alias body into a template argument
  over a persistent tree. Sharing the body's children within one module
  let the next round's resolve of `word_t` inside the argument rewrite
  `using cache_line_t = word_t[WordCount]` itself. The constant-aggregate
  arm beside it still shares within a module; no row shows it, so it was
  left alone.

**The instrument, for the next row.** `ptdiff --dump` shows where; a
snippet shows why, and both compilers trace an arbitrary file: ours is
`kg build --no-manifest -I <lib> --backend trace -o ours.trace F.k`,
the reference's is `target/ptrace/bin/kanagawa --place-iterations=1
--import-dir <lib> F.k` with `KG_PTRACE_OUT=theirs.trace` (the shim
`cargo xtask ptrace` lays out). Strip the `Location` lines and the two
`#` headers and `diff` them: each of the four above reduced to a
ten-line program this way, and each unit test was read off one.
`kg-oracle --no-base --passes 9` shows the mangled names the stamp
decides.

## Eight mechanisms behind twelve ordering rows — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W1.3 (and W1.2's one decline). `scripts/fast.sh --lint loop`:
`ptdiff` structural 2402 → 2412, diverged 19 → 9; `backend` agree 3254 →
3258; `output` 264/274 +0/−0; everything else +0/−0.*

**The first differing call named the wrong layer every time.** Each row's
first divergence was a `ParseIdentifier` against something, which reads as
copy order; none of the nine was. Four were an instance the loop never
made, three a value spelled differently in the walk, one the
redundant-import seed, and the ninth pair a walk rule wider than the
reference's. Finding the cause took the structural diff of both dumps from
the module that parts, then the reference clause — never the first call.

**GHC's `show :: Float` is not Rust's shortest round trip.** The mangle
had declined a float argument on purpose (a wrong byte invents a name), so
`Foo<float32, 1.0>` was never made: the loop re-decided it for 128 rounds
and the walk declined. `F32Bits::haskell_show` ports `formatRealFloat
FFGeneric` over `floatToDigits` (Burger–Dybvig, GHC's strict boundary
tests and round-half-up last digit). Against a compiled GHC 9.6 sweep
(every exponent's boundary mantissas and a stride over all 2^32 patterns,
544,923 values) it agrees on all; Rust's `{:e}` digits differ on 1,171 of
them — `2^25 × 1.5` is `5.0331648e7` to GHC and `5.033165e7` to Rust —
so the bespoke formatter is load-bearing beyond the `1.0`/`1` spelling.

**Folds the IR had declined.** `cast<float32>(n)` reinterprets the low 32
bits (`castWord32ToFloat . fromIntegral`, `Constexpr.hs:332`) and a float
into an integer type is its bit pattern (`:337-343`); `~` over an enum
value wraps to the enum's base and keeps an untyped value untyped
(`:262`, `Type.hs:732-744`); an enum constant whose value is an enum value
nests it whole (`isIntLiteral` sees through `EnumValue`, `Type.hs:1087`).
Each had been a deliberate decline from M1's shadow port, none measured
against a program.

**`checkReturn` converts one level deep.** `renote (fmap $ renote
checkReturn) $ body e` (`TypeCheck.hs:76`) reaches the statements directly
in a function's body: `return Foo::Off;` there is the bare `1`, the same
statement inside an `if` keeps its `EnumValue` (`kg-oracle --passes 19`).
The walk now carries the conversion for those statements only.

**The seed again: a path's first name.** `Bar::Zero` resolves `Bar` with
no qualifier through `findInScopes`, so a class's own `enum Bar` answers it
and `[Bar]` never reaches the imports; only `[Bar, Zero]` does. The scope
rule had been applied to one-component paths only.

**`resolve` is by key, program-wide — and that was the round order.**
`risc-v.k`, `accumulating.k` and `pipelined.k` each parted at a copy
declared a round late. Read with a temporary per-decision print of the
census (site, `via`, the frame's round) against `kg-oracle
--template-iterations N`: `decode_instr`'s copies are made in the
reference's rounds on both sides (3 at 5, 11 at 6), but the
`reinterpret_cast<bool>` in their bodies was decided here a round after
the reference. The census cannot read those bodies yet — `custom_decode`'s
`Closure<…>` is unresolved, and `inferExpTree'` does not type a function
whose parameters are not (`Type/Inference.hs:56-58`; the reference's
`--notes` shows the body's `bool` still `TUnresolved`). The reference does
not need to read them: `resolve` renames every `TemplateInstance` in the
program whose arguments are a decided key (`Template.hs:158-159`) — the
same shape decided at `risc-v.k`'s own call renames the mention in the
decoder's *template* that round, and every copy is made from the renamed
body. `resolve.rs` already spread a key by fingerprint, but only from the
deciding module's own sites: its 2026-08-13 measurement found no
cross-module witness, before the program-wide loop existed. The loop now
seeds every module's pass with the round's keys. A three-file oracle
fixture shows it (`rc<bool>` in `h`'s template `dec`, renamed by `main`'s
call); `accumulating.k` closed, the other two moved on to new mechanisms:
`risc-v.k` to a class member initializer naming a member declared *later*
(`.custom_decode = CustomDecode` in `ProgramTest`, which the parser's
scope does not hold yet, so the reference binds the enclosing `Tests`'s
`CustomDecode`), `pipelined.k` to a type argument displayed through its
alias (`pair<uint32, uint32>`, ours `tuple2<…>`).

**`dependent-template.k::16` ("deduce: Unresolved") is the parser.** In
`AmbiguosSyntax`'s `else` branch `Do` is a variable at parse time, so the
reference parses `Do<a && b>(10)` as `(Do < a) && (b > 10)`
(`kg-oracle --passes 1`), folds it to `true` and deduces `Go`'s `bool`.
This parser commits to template arguments and the lowering leaves the path
unsorted (`ArgsOnNonTemplate`), so `Go`'s return type never resolves.
Closing it needs the call re-read as a relational chain under the
reference's precedence — a parser/lowering change, not the loop's.

**Reading `--template-iterations N`.** The tree printed at `N` is `N`
rounds' `instantiate . resolve` and the `inferType` after them, then the
next round's pre-census passes (the driver's `--template-passes` defaults
to all of them, `Template.hs:62-64`) — the tree the next census reads. So
a mention written `<uint1>` at `N` was deduced before round `N + 1`'s
census. Eleven runs over `risc-v.k` cost 6.5 minutes.

## Pass 12 at a module's text, admitted past pass 9 — 2026-09-27

*Sprint W1.4. `kg_sem::check::Checked::late`, `Looped::late_for`,
`run_from_10`'s `late`. Every decidable assertion passes: conformance
2602/2602, `--strict` failing 0, `errors` silent 0.*

**The reference's pipeline has one flag and two setters.** After pass
1's `checkPar`, only `undefinedSymbols` (pass 9) sets it
(`Frontend.hs:86-87`); passes 10–19 are `pass`/`passPar`, so they all run
or none does. The loop's verdicts inside copies can seed the CST run
because no CST pass judges those nodes; a verdict at the module's own
text cannot, because the same text's pass 9 is the CST passes' — a
leftover instance beside an undefined name is reported by the reference
as the undefined name alone. The seam is to carry those verdicts apart
and let the CST run admit them where pass 12 sits in its own order:
after its pass-9 checkpoint, before its pass 12 and pass 17.

**Why it waited.** Admitted, the verdicts are exactly as right as the
loop's leftovers at the text. `loop-left` grades roots only; on the
snippets, four `expected:0` programs gained errors until W1.3's name
rows made the instances the reference makes (a float argument mangled as
GHC shows it, `cast<float32>` folded, `~` over an enum folded). So a
parity item and a verdict item landed in that order, the verdict parked
on a branch meanwhile.

**The `KG_LEFTOVERS` measurement that preceded it.** With the switch
set, the compilers `backend` spawns changed no verdict on 3270 programs:
the copies' arms no longer invent errors (the round guard and W1.2
removed the causes), and they close nothing — the silences were at the
module's text, which the switch never reached.

## The compat binary's command line, against the reference binary — 2026-10-09

*Sprint W8.6. `kg_cli::legacy::{help, run}`, `xtask/src/cli.rs`;
divergences #34–#38.*

**`cmdargs`' help is portable exactly, and its source is on this
machine.** `~/.cache/cabal/packages/hackage.haskell.org/cmdargs/0.10.22`
holds the version the reference links; reading it settled what the
reference's help screens only suggested. Four rules no screen states:
flags are listed in the order of the *data declaration's* fields
(`Options.hs`), not of the `CmdArgs.hs` record literal (`mode_` reads
`fields`); a flag without a `groupname` takes the previous field's
(`assignGroups`), which is why `pretty --help` lists `--indent` under
"Compiler"; short letters are assigned per mode, a non-`explicit` flag
getting the first letter of each of its names that no other flag of the
mode holds or wants (`--backend` wants `b` and `t`, so neither
`--base-library` nor `--target-device` gets a letter in `compile`); and
the wrap counts a column's two leading spaces against its first line, so
a line that would end at column 79 of 80 still breaks. A derived name is
lower-cased (`asName`): the reference's flag is `--dump-ir`, and this
binary had accepted `--dump-IR`, which the reference refuses. A mode
word is any unambiguous prefix (`kanagawa l a.k` is `list-deps`). The
port reproduces all 17 graded command lines byte for byte but for the
version on its first try, and `flags::tests::short_letters_are_cmdargs_own`
re-derives every letter by the rule.

**A file not found is not a diagnostic.** `parseFile` *throws*
(`Parser/IO.hs:83`), nothing catches, and GHC prints `kanagawa: Can't find
file: …` and the import dirs on stderr; this binary printed an `Error 1:`
on stdout, and two tests asserted it. Probing the reference corrected
both. The base library is looked for first, so a missing one is the
first exception.

**`--template-iterations=N` is exactly `N` of our rounds.** A round here
is the pass list, the census and `instantiate` (`kg_sem::elaborate`), and
the reference's recursion is the same three, so the bound needed only
`PassBudget::AtMost(0)` to mean zero rounds instead of one. Three probe
programs at 0–3 rounds agreed with the reference on exit code and first
error; one of them shows the gap a bounded loop exposes: the reference
adds pass 10's "Invalid conversion from `unresolved`" where a call's
callee was never instantiated, and this compiler stops at the first
error (`known-divergences.md`, "Not yet implemented").
`--frontend-passes` is a debugging aid for the reference's own frontend —
`--frontend-passes=5` on a two-function program crashes its backend walk
with `Prelude.undefined` — and is refused here below 19, as is
`--template-passes` below 9 under a count.

**What the gate is built on.** `cargo xtask cli` reads the reference
build's `CTestTestfile.cmake` rather than reimplementing upstream's CMake
functions: whatever `ctest -R '^cli\.'` would run, with this binary
substituted and the build's test directory redirected to a scratch one,
fixtures honoured, `cmake -E` done natively, and a command it does not
know failing rather than skipping. The golden is configured afresh from
the checked-in template. Against main's binary from before this item it
read 6/25, so it can see what it was built to see.

**Found, not fixed: the diagnostics' blank lines** (#38, open). Diffing
whole streams rather than first errors: the reference prints a file's
diagnostics as one megaparsec bundle — a blank line between consecutive
ones — and `putStrLn` adds one after `exitErrors` and after each warning
bundle; this binary prints none of them, and an excerpt of a CRLF line
drops the CR the reference keeps. No gate compares a whole stream, so
nothing had seen it.

## The last corpus rows: three mechanisms, and parity on every graded program — 2026-10-10

*`repoint` 72/72, `ptdiff` 2422/2422 structural, `output` 266/274 with
nothing differing — the other eight are programs the reference itself
fails on or runs out of memory compiling.*

The milestone run at `8f5939b` (S3 and S4 together) found `repoint` at
71/72, thirteen files past its baseline: W1.3's rows and W1.4 had moved it
and no milestone run had blessed it. What was left on the corpus was three
rows, and each was a mechanism of its own.

**The walk re-ran pass 1 inside copies** (`risc-v.k` #394963). Since
`8c21699` `kg_sem::pass1` runs `redundantNameScope` on the IR before the
loop, once, as the reference does; the walk still ran it a second time at
walk time, a leftover of the twin's era. Inside a copy that second run
asked the parse-time table about the copy's scope (`Tests::P<|@3|>`),
which the table never held, so the lookup fell back to the enclosing
scope, found the enclosing class's `CustomDecode`, judged the written
qualifier redundant and dropped it — and pass 16's `resolveNames` then
re-resolved the bare name to the copy's own member. The reference binds
`.custom_decode = CustomDecode` to `Tests::CustomDecode` because the
parser meets the initializer above `ProgramTest`'s own `CustomDecode`
(`Parser.hs:686-688`); a C++ reader would call that a bug in the test, and
parity is parity. The walk now runs pass 16 only.

**A copy keeps each node's note** (`memory/pipelined.k` #38677).
`desugarWithNote` (`Desugar.hs:91-94`) copies a template body with every
node's own type (`n' <> n`, `Typed`'s `Semigroup` keeps the left one).
Ours minted copies untyped and re-inferred them from their text, which is
the same answer except where the text and the note disagree — and
`expFromType` makes exactly such nodes: a deduced `pair<uint32,
uint32>[2]` is spelled `tuple2<|…|>[2]` but its element is noted
`TInstance … pair …` (`Type.hs:1631,1638,1647`). `pipelined_last`'s `auto
count` makes its instance a template again, so the deduced `T` reached
`FIFO<T, …>`'s `memory<T, 32>` only through a copy of a copy, and the
instance was shown `memory<…tuple2…>`. Bisected to the `auto` parameter
with six twenty-line programs traced against the reference binary
through the `target/ptrace/bin` shim (`KG_PTRACE_OUT`) — a way to record
the reference's walk of *any* program, not only the corpus's. The copy
walk now allocates each copy `for` its original, and `carry_types` gives
it the original's type; `infer-identity` 304/304, every ratchet +1/−0.

**`Do<a && b>(10)` is a relational chain when `Do` is no template**
(`dependent-template::16`). Our parser is context-free and commits to the
angle list; the reference parses one only where `findSymbol` finds a
template (`Parser.hs:669-680`), so over the `else` branch's variable `Do`
the text is `Do < a && b > (10)`. Because `opsTemplate` keeps `<`, `>`,
`<<`, `>>` off the argument's top (`Parser.hs:913`) and every operator
left there binds looser than the relational level or tighter than it, the
reference's reading is reachable from the committed tree without a
reparse: `Do <` takes the argument's leftmost operand below its looser
operators, `> (10)` its rightmost. The lowering does that only where it
is the whole reading — one argument with a looser operator at its top,
one call argument, no attribute, and no operator or postfix around the
call that could take `Do` or the call argument first; everything else
keeps the committed tree, as before. The nodes headed at the path are
`Donated`: the path's text still holds the `<…>` they no longer have, and
the `ir` gate's sorted round trip — which prints an `Own` node as its
source slice — said so on the first run.

What remains on the corpus is `errors`' message and position
disagreements (25: 18 recovery positions, divergence #30, and seven
semantic ones, closed in the entry below) and the two `basics.k` static asserts the
reference crashes on.

## Seven `errors` disagreements, four mechanisms — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W2. `kg_vfs`, `kg_resolve::module::read_failed`, the compat
binary's loader; passes 16 and 19 (`post_desugar`, `validate_program`),
`looped::dimension_bracket`; `kg_const`'s `eval_mux`.*

The seven non-parser rows of `cargo xtask errors` are closed: agree
694 → 701, disagree 25 → 18, and the 18 left are divergence #30's
parse-recovery positions. Each mechanism is a fact about the reference
that no message or position in the corpus states outright.

**The reference's frontend types a node, then folds it, children first,
and a resolved type sticks** (`Inference.hs:50`, `Type.hs:1170-1171`).
So a mux selector written as literals is already a literal when the mux
is first typed, and `infer (MuxF (IntLiteral _ x) a)` types an
out-of-range one `TUnresolved` (`Type.hs:1237-1238`): it never folds and
never errs. "Invalid selector `N` for the `mux` with M elements" is
reached only by a selector a *name* folds, a round later, after the mux
took `tMux`'s type — `mux(four, …)` over `const uint3 four = 4`, or an
enum constant. `T1<2 ? 3 : 5>` is therefore pass 12's "Unresolved
argument" (`constexpr.k::6,75`), `uint32 x = mux(4, 0, 1, 2, 3);`
*compiles* in the reference's frontend, and `const auto x = mux(4, …)` is
"Could not deduce variable type". `kg_const` had a test pinning the
selector error on `constexpr.k::6,75`, which are `expected:1` for the
other error. Left silent here, honestly: the out-of-range literal mux
under a `static assert`, an array dimension or a `const auto` — each the
holder's own error in the reference, none in the corpus.

**`desugarError` replaces a node, and `desugar` is a `cata`**
(`Desugar.hs:66-69`). Pass 16's `unresolved ParamIntF{}` replaces an
`int<…>` whose width did not fold, width and all, so: nothing inside it
is reported — not an earlier pass's error, not pass 19's — and an inner
`int<…>` or `clog2` is replaced first, which makes the outer width
unfoldable and the outer's error the only one. A type in a width never
folds (no `eval` arm makes a value of a type but the sizes), so
`int<int32>` is pass 16's width error at the `int`, not pass 19's "Invalid
use of a type" at the `int32` (`type-check.k::4,14,15`). A test here said
"the reference reports both" for `int<bitsizeof (foo + 1)>`; the oracle on
that very program prints one error. The pass-16 verdict is asked only
where pass 19 would already have rejected, so it moves which error a
rejected program shows, never whether it is rejected. Not ported, the
same mechanism: `clog2` — `uint32 z = clog2(foo);` over a type is pass
16's clog2 error in the reference and pass 19's here — and a mux in a
width, where `int<(1 ? 8 : int32)>` compiles in the reference and pass
19 still rejects it here (pass 19 never looks inside a width in the
reference; skipping widths wholesale would also silence the reference's
own parse-time error on `int<mux(1, int32, 8)>`, so only replaced widths
are skipped).

**megaparsec's notes decide positions, and `many` re-notes.** The
program's `many p = noted $ Seq <$> MP.many (notedWithDocs p)`
(`Parser.hs:114`) notes each *element* from where it starts, so an
unattributed array's dimension, `many (brackets expression)`, is noted
from its `[`; a memory's one dimension, `Seq . pure <$> brackets
expression` (`:529`), keeps the expression's own note: `static
[[memory]] uint32[0] _mem;` is reported at the `0` (`basics.k::173`), a
copy's at its first token too.

**A file that exists is found, readable or not.** `findFile` stats; the
read that follows throws, and `displayException` is GHC's text:
`<path'>: hGetContents: invalid argument (cannot decode byte sequence
starting from N)`, N the first undecodable byte in decimal (a sequence
truncated by the end of file names its lead byte), or `openFile:
permission denied (Permission denied)`; `<path'>` is the path as the
search joined it. The `Vfs` decided existence by reading and answered
`None` for all three, so a binary import was "Can't find file" — and the
compat binary read a non-UTF-8 command-line file as empty and exited 0.
The same `readFileUtf8` sets `utf8_bom`: a leading byte-order mark is the
decoder's, and a file opening with one, which compiles in the reference,
was rejected here by the lexer. GHC 9.6.6's wording; the spec had guessed
"invalid byte sequence".

## The tools built from the checkout alone, and a library checked at load — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W8.4 and W8.5. No verdict moved; what moved is what a build needs.*

**The generated ABI code is checked in, and the generators are
`kg-abi-gen`'s.** Three build scripts ran bindgen over
`../kanagawa/compiler/cpp`'s headers, two of them under every crate above
`kg-backend-sys`, so building `kg` — or `kg-lsp`, which links no backend —
needed the reference beside the checkout and libclang (`docs/history/audit-2026-09-22.md` §4.4).
`kg-backend-sys/src/bindings.rs` and `kg-ptbridge/src/backend.rs` are now
sources `cargo xtask codegen` writes and `--check` compares, each under a
banner naming the headers, the reference commit and an FNV digest of the
headers. The generators went to `kg-abi-gen` rather than
`xtask/src/codegen.rs`: that crate already held the one bindgen
configuration, and `kg-ptrace`'s build script — which keeps generating,
since the interposer records the reference's own runs and is wanted only
where the reference is — still uses it, so the interposer and the
checked-in bindings cannot be configured apart. `xtask` drives.
`codegen` refuses a reference the pin does not name (`guard::check_pin`)
and headers not as that commit has them (the pin hashes only `library/`
and `test/`), and because the banner names the commit, moving the pin
makes `--check` red until the files are regenerated — on purpose: the
regeneration is the record that the bindings were re-derived for the new
reference.

**The old bindings were never formatted.** bindgen's default formatter
runs `rustfmt` from the build script's directory, and `rustfmt` found
this tree's `rustfmt.toml`, `disable_all_formatting = true`: the OUT_DIR
`bindings.rs` was one 2-line token dump. Checked in, its text is what
`--check` compares, and a formatter that depends on the machine's
`rustfmt` and the directory it runs from would make the check compare
formatters. The bindings now go through `prettyplease` (bindgen's
`Formatter::Prettyplease`, a library pinned by the lock). `backend.rs` is
hand-assembled text and needs no formatter: below its banner it is
byte-identical to the build script's output. For the bindings, identity
was shown by parsing both files with syn 3 and unparsing both with
prettyplease — equal. A token-string comparison is *not* equal and is the
wrong instrument: prettyplease writes a trailing comma wherever it breaks
a list (`["Alignment of PlacementOptions",]`, `Error,>`, `where P: …,`),
which the token stream keeps. What can still move `--check` between
machines is bindgen's own reading of the headers through another libclang
(here Apple clang 21.0.0's); not observed, and the gates run on this one.

**`default-members` leaves out `kg-ptrace`, `kg-abi-gen` and `xtask`,**
so a plain `cargo build` or `cargo test` works in a checkout without the
reference; `--workspace`, which the gates use, builds all three. The list
is explicit — a glob cannot exclude — so a new crate is added by hand or
plain `cargo test` skips its tests. Evidence, in a `git archive` of the
branch in the scratchpad with no `../kanagawa` beside it,
`KANAGAWA_ROOT=/nonexistent/kanagawa` and `LIBCLANG_PATH=/nonexistent`:
`cargo build --release --locked --offline -p kg-cli -p kg-lsp` green in
25 s, 76 crates compiled, none of them bindgen or clang-sys; a plain
`cargo build` green; `--workspace` red only at `kg-ptrace`'s build script,
"reference header not found". The `../kanagawa-build` path compiled into
`kg_backend_sys::locate` went too (the plan's other clause of W8.4): it
never existed beside a worktree, and every gate and script names the
library.

**The library carries no version.** The backend exports the 85
`parse_tree.h` functions and `InternalTests` and nothing that reports a
version (`nm -gU`); its `LC_ID_DYLIB` says current version 0.0.0; the
`VERSION` file (1.2.0) becomes `RELEASE_VERSION` in `CMakeLists.txt:11-31`
and reaches only the Haskell executable, through `-DRELEASE_VERSION_*`
(`compiler/hs/CMakeLists.txt:38-49`, `ReleaseVersion.hs`). So W8.5's
"the backend's version against the headers'" can only be the library's
symbols against the headers' declarations: `Backend::load` refuses, before
any call, a library that does not define every declared function but
`ParseStages` (declared, never defined, §1). Before, bindgen's
`dynamic_link_require_all(false)` — needed for `ParseStages` — let any
library load, and one that was not the backend was found out by a panic at
its first call. The check catches a library whose headers lack a declared
function and a file that is not the backend; it is blind to a changed
signature, `Options` layout or enum numbering under the same names (C
symbols carry no types) and to a function the library adds (the exports
are not enumerated). Those are held at generation — `codegen --check`
against the pinned headers, `tests/layout.rs` and bindgen's layout
asserts — and that the gates' library was built from the pinned reference
is the build's to keep true. The refusal names the commit and the
headers' digest so a reader knows which backend is wanted.

**The refusal's type was chosen so the cache key would not move.**
`kg-ptbridge/src/real.rs` is one of the four files the backend cache keys
by meaningful text, and it maps `Backend::load`'s error into
`LoadError::Load(path, e)`. `load` now returns `Refused` (`Dlopen` or
`Mismatch`) and `LoadError::Load` carries a `Refused`, so `real.rs`
compiles unchanged and the cache stays warm. A cache hit never loads the
library, so no check runs on a hit; the check is a function of the
library, which the key names by path, size and modified time. The key
still omits the generated `replay_call` (now `kg-ptbridge/src/backend.rs`;
sprint W6), which this change did not touch.

**A refused library is a failure in `tests/smoke.rs`, not a skip.** The
smoke tests skipped on any load error, so a check that refused the real
backend — `ParseStages` not tolerated, planted — read as two skips. They
now skip only when no library is found.

## The editor reads the loop: the diagnostics' own, and each instance's widths — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3.5. `Db::editor_loop`, `Db::looped`'s in-flight slot,
`kg_base::cancel::detached`; `kg_hir::position::CopyIndex`,
`Looped::{answer_at, callee_at}`, `Db::ir_answer_of_definition`;
`kg-lsp`'s hover, inlay hints and signature help, `handlers/instances.rs`;
`xtask resilience`'s hover side.*

Hover, inlay hints and signature help read the program-wide loop first,
and the CST engine only where the loop has no type to show. Three
decisions a reader would otherwise have to rediscover.

**The editor reads the loop the diagnostics run, and no other.**
`Db::diagnostics` stops at a buffer's first parse-stage error, before the
passes and so before the loop — the reference's `Main.hs:73-75`, per file
— and on such a buffer a type feature that ran the loop itself would pay
what the diagnostics deliberately do not. Measured on `risc-v.k` under the
keystroke bench's settings and the editor's budget: a keystroke that
breaks the parse costs 57 ms of diagnostics, and the loop over that
buffer another 870–930 ms (the CST table 16 ms), where a clean keystroke
is ~990 ms with the loop already in it; `array.k` 7 ms against 315–360
ms. Inlay hints are re-asked on every edit and signature help on every
`(` and `,`, so every broken keystroke would have cost a clean one's
price. `Db::editor_loop` shares `diagnostics`' gate
(`Db::before_the_passes`) and its memo (the same root set), and answers
`None` past the gate: the buffer is answered by the CST engine, as it
always was. So the resilience gate's buffers — every one fails to parse —
are, today, not served from the loop at all; its IR side is what the
editor will serve there once W3.4's resilient mode makes the loop run on
them, and its total `editor-reads-loop` (0) says so. Hover alone could run
the loop on a broken buffer, since it is not a keystroke — 16 ms becomes
~900 ms on `risc-v.k` the first time after an edit — and was not made to:
the owner's call.

**`Db::looped` runs once per program, however many ask.** The language
server answers diagnostics on a lane of their own and requests on a pool,
both read-locking one `Db`; an inlay hint asked while the diagnostics'
loop is running missed the memo and ran a second loop beside it. The miss
path now goes through a slot per root set — the program it is for and a
`OnceLock` — so a second caller for the same program waits for the first.
The computation is detached from the request that started it and answers
to the database's token alone (`kg_base::cancel::detached`): a
`$/cancelRequest` for a hint that happened to start the loop would
otherwise throw away work the diagnostics then redo; an edit still stops
it, and a waiter then runs it itself, into the same raised token. The
slot is matched by program *identity*, and two threads loading one program
at once each mint their own `Arc<Program>` — a race of the memo layer's
that this does not fix (the diagnostics load the program milliseconds
before their loop starts, so a request racing that window is rare, not
impossible); `navigate.rs`'s test loads the program first for the same
reason. The price is latency, not work: a hover or a hint asked while an
edit's loop is still running waits for it — up to the loop's ~1 s on
`risc-v.k` — where the CST table answered it in milliseconds. Serving the
CST answer meanwhile and refreshing (`workspace/inlayHint/refresh`) was
the alternative, and was not taken: inside a template's body the CST
engine has no answer, so every keystroke would blank a body's hints and
redraw them a second later — the flicker `inlay_hints.rs` exists to avoid.

**A template's body is shown as its instances, not as one of them.** The
written body has no type — `inferType` visits a template for its
condition only (`Inference.hs:63`) — and each instance's copy has its own,
which the language's widths make different: `auto w = v + 1` is `uint9` in
`take<uint8>` and `uint17` in `take<uint16>` (`kg-oracle --no-base
--passes 19` prints both copies so). Picking one — the first, the one the
caret's call implies — would state a fact about one instance as if it held
for the text, so every distinct type is shown with the instances that give
it, in the order the loop decided them: hover's fence holds a line per
type with the instances as a `//` comment, the hint reads `: uint9 |
uint17` with the tooltip naming which is which, and a line under each says
how many instances typed it, which did not, and whether the editor's
budget stopped the loop with more to make. The copies are found by the
text they were copied from — `Src::expanded` keeps the head and the
`Own`ness and pushes the instance onto `via` — in the module that declares
the template, which is where `kg_sem::elaborate` makes them; the instance
is named from the copy's own declaration, the `TInstance` the reference
notes there, through `unmangleInstanceName` (`Type.hs:176-177`): the
spelling a `while compiling` note uses. Where the caret's context does
imply an instance — a call — signature help shows it: the callee's type at
the call (`FunctionCall`'s function, which `resolve` renamed,
`Template.hs:158-159`), `(uint16) -> void take  // take<uint16>`, a
deduced call included; inside a template's body, one line per callee with
the enclosing instances that call it.

**The nine completion disagreements were one mechanism, and the loop was
right in all nine.** Both files are snippet accumulators, and the
candidate is a declaration whose initializer names a key the buffer
declares twice: `constexpr.k`'s first `const auto c = true ? b : a;`
(line 1047) beside a second snippet's `const int8 b`, and `basics.k`'s
first `auto y = x << amt;` inside the first of many `main`s, beside a
later `main`'s `const int32 x`. The CST engine's environment answered the
twice-declared key from a later snippet's declaration, through its
duplicate-key handling (`passes::types`' `Declarations`, its `registered`
and `blocks`), and typed them `const int8` and `int63`; the loop keeps the
first, as `getSymbols''`'s `HashMap.fromList . reverse` does
(`Symbols.hs:44`), and typed them `const uint1` and `uint63` — what
`kg-oracle --typed --passes 19` gives each snippet alone (`b` folds to
`1`, `c` to a `uint1` literal; `tShiftL` keeps the left operand's
signedness, `uint32` widened by `2^5 - 1`, `Type.hs:894-897`). Which later
declaration the CST engine picked, and why that one, was not traced: the
reference rejects either whole buffer at parse time (a redefinition,
`SymbolTable.hs:200-201`), so no reading of the buffer is the reference's,
and per snippet the loop's is. Not fixed in the CST engine, which is to be
deleted and no longer answers where the loop does; completion's details,
still the CST engine's, keep the disagreement until completion moves too.

Driven the way a user meets it — the release `kg lsp` over stdio, a copy
of `test/library/data/array.k` under a manifest importing `library/`: once
the diagnostics landed, a hover on `TestPrefixSumHelper`'s `auto naturals
= indices<array_size>();` answered in 6 ms with six lines, `uint2[4]
naturals  // TestPrefixSumHelper<4>` down to `uint5[24]`, under the
budget's caveat, and `AssertArraysEqual`'s induction variable `const
uint2` / `const uint3` (two instances on one line) / `const uint5` /
`const uint6`; the 47 inlay hints in 1 ms. The keystroke bench (the
diagnostics alone) read 995 ms on `risc-v.k` before and 957 ms after, one
pass each under load.

The resilience gate's hover side reads the editor's own query: agree 1496
→ 1497, a new pass set `copies` 0 → 134 — hovers inside template bodies,
from `assert_equal`'s six instances to `RandomReadScheduleTest<4, 10>`'s
`const uint4` against `<8, 20>`'s `const uint5` — every other set
unmoved; proven by planting `Class::Neither` for a copies answer (134 →
0). Left: completion on the loop (the same query), the loop on broken
buffers (W3.4), and a re-measure of how many of the library's `auto`
bindings are annotated now (184 of 1030 on the CST engine, 2026-09).

## The loop's floor, kept rather than recomputed — 2026-10-10

Sprint W5.2–W5.5, on the program-wide loop alone. Interleaved A/B
against `f8e8c72`, release `kg check`, `/usr/bin/time -l`:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `test/library/data/array.k` | 3.10 s, 48.5 G instr, 1.41 GB | 0.95 s, 14.3 G instr, 0.24 GB |
| `test/library/processor/risc-v.k` | 6.22 s, 94.4 G instr, 1.74 GB | 2.65 s, 39.7 G instr, 0.68 GB |

(peak footprint; the reference's own peaks are 0.55 and 1.1 GB). Every
step was graded by `infer-identity`, its `--dump` diffed against
`f8e8c72`'s (304/304 identical each time) and `scripts/fast.sh loop`
(every ratchet +0/−0). What a later reader needs:

**Every cache here rests on one invariant: a node changes only through
`ExpArena::node_mut`, and the arena logs every index it hands out.**
The arena is append-only; a rewrite mints a replacement and re-roots. So
anything known of a subtree — what it files in a symbol map
(`kg_sem::symbols::Filed`), what shapes it holds (`kg_hir::facts`), what
a snapshot copied of it (`ExpArena::fork_into`) — stays true until a
write in place, and each cache checks the log: `Filed` against the
writes inference vetted harmless (`symbols::harmless`), `facts` by
forgetting the written node and every node derived from it (parent edges
recorded as facts are derived), a snapshot by copying the logged nodes
again. A new way to change a node in place that bypasses `node_mut`
breaks all three silently; `infer-identity` would see it only where it
changes a result.

**The whole walk is the reference for all of it.** `KG_INFER_FULL` (and
`infer-identity`'s first run) keeps no facts, builds every symbol map
whole and copies snapshots whole; the incremental run does all three.
So `infer-identity` grades each mechanism over every corpus root without
a switch of its own, and its mutants (a `needs` too narrow, a write
reported harmless that is not) go red there: 153–221 roots differ.
`KG_SYMBOLS_CHECK=1` compares every kept map with the whole walk's
directly.

**The memory was the allocator's, not ours.** `array.k` held 531k arena
nodes (182k reachable, 60 MB at 112 bytes a node) and 210 MB live in
all, at a 1.4 GB footprint: `vmmap` showed 1.2 GB of "Malloc Large
(empty)", blocks freed and kept by macOS's allocator for reuse.
`MallocLargeCache=0` took the same run to 191 MB. The churn was the
snapshots: every arena forked and every type map cloned twice a round,
freed after the pass, each round's copies larger than the last so none
was ever reused. Keeping the storage fixed it (1.4 GB → 0.25 GB);
refreshing it from the write logs made it cheap. Compaction (W5.2 as
planned) would drop the 350k superseded nodes — about 40 MB on
`array.k` — and is not the lever it looked: measure footprint with and
without `MallocLargeCache=0` before designing for memory again.

**`desugar`'s algebras (W5.3) were measured first and not rewritten.**
Clone, compare and drop were about a quarter of each rewrite pass; the
walk itself was the rest. So the walk went: each pass declares the
shapes its algebra acts on (`desugar_within`, `ShallowRewrite::needs`),
and a subtree holding none is passed over. A shape is a property of the
subtree (a `Function` is rewritten by `desugarLambdas` when its *body*
holds a lambda), so the facts are subtree facts and the contract is
"the algebra hands back every node of a subtree holding none of them";
a per-node filter — `Option<Exp>` algebras — would need a second,
narrower contract per pass, and is what is left of W5.3.

**What remains** (risc-v.k, `sample`, after): inference ~35% of the
run (the walk of the units each fixpoint must revisit), deduction's
per-call symbol lookups, the passes outside the loop
(`undefined_symbols`, the sorter's fingerprints — a fifth of `kg
check`), and the snapshot itself, which a layered arena (the frozen
prefix shared, appends beside it) would remove.

## Completion and member navigation on the loop, and one program per input state — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3.5. `Db::{completions_with, loop_members_at,
ir_answer_of_completion, editor_loop_ready, definition_of_declaration}`,
`Looped::members`, `navigate.rs`'s `loop_field`; `kg-lsp`'s completion;
`xtask resilience`'s completion side; the parse, item-tree and program
memos.*

Completion's details read the query hover reads, and member lists (`s.`)
and go-to-definition on `s.f` read the loop's type of the base: `static
Box<4> a; a.` offers `items` `uint32[4]` and `first` `() -> uint33`,
`auto p = make<uint8>(1); p.` offers `Pair`'s fields and `p.lo` jumps to
them, where the CST engine typed neither base and offered nothing. Five
decisions a reader would otherwise have to rediscover.

**Completion reads the loop once the diagnostics have computed it, and
never waits for it.** Hover, inlay hints and signature help wait for an
edit's loop (the entry before this one). Completion did too, first, and
it made the popup the loop's latency. Measured over stdio — the release
`kg lsp` on a copy of `test/library/processor/risc-v.k` under a manifest
importing `library/`, a scope list of 253 candidates at `assert`, three
edits each, load 6–15 — in milliseconds:

| asked | before this work | waiting for the loop | `editor_loop_ready` |
|---|---|---|---|
