| as a clean edit lands | 101–104 | 2140–2200 | 101–112 (the CST engine's, 70 typed) |
| after that edit's diagnostics | 7–11 | 9–14 | 53–56 (the loop's, 89 typed) |
| as a broken edit lands | 100–110 | 96–107 | 108–115 |

`Db::editor_loop_ready` is `Db::editor_loop`'s gate and then the memo
alone — the loop of the program as it stands, none while it runs. The
price is an answer that depends on when it is asked: as an edit lands the
CST engine's, after its diagnostics the loop's. A popup is transient and
asked again at the next trigger, which reads the loop; a hover or a hint
stays on screen until the next edit, and waits. The ~45 ms after the
diagnostics is the first reader after an edit building each module's
position and copy indexes and naming the instances (in-process on
`risc-v.k` under the bench's settings: ~20 ms first, ~1 ms after, the
indexes ~6 ms of it); hover and hints pay the same once. Navigation —
go-to-definition, and references, rename and highlight, which resolve
through `definition_at` — waits as hover does: a jump is asked once and
must not depend on timing. So a document highlight on a field selector
asked while an edit's loop runs waits for it; the client asks for it
asynchronously, and it lands late rather than stalling the typing.

**A member is what the aggregate's own text declares.** The loop's class
body holds more than the text does: a member template's instances are
copies one expansion deeper, placed *ahead* of the template
(`twice<|$uint@8|>` before `twice`); the function `abbreviatedFunctionTemplate`
keeps beside its template is `Donated`; a function taking a function is a
template (`higherOrderFunctions`, `Function.hs:313-361`) whose instances
carry mangled names — which the gate's first run on the loop's lists
offered, `hof<|@@data@closure@make_capture1<…>|>`. So `Looped::members`
takes a `Variable`, `Function` or `FunctionDecl` — or a function
template's function — at the aggregate's own expansion and `Own`, in the
text's order (a rewrite moves declarations within the body), and the
candidate is the item tree's declaration it was written as
(`Db::definition_of_declaration`, `declaration_node` read backwards),
under its written name and only of the kinds the CST engine's list
offers. The member's type is the instance's own, the copy's node's — not
the declaration's answer, which inside a class template is every
instance's (`a.items` would read `uint32[4] | uint32[8] | uint32[16]` in a
program with three `Box`es; a mutant showed it). The fields come off the
declaration rather than off `TClass`'s field list (`Type.hs:1197`) because
that list holds variables only, and the methods are what
`lookupSymbolByName (x ++ [y])` finds under the class (`Type.hs:1359`).

**The loop's answer stands where it has one.** A base the loop decided
is not an aggregate has no members — an empty list, not a question for the
CST engine — and a field the loop's aggregate does not hold is no jump. The
CST engine is asked only where the loop has no type: none it would print
(`Unresolved`, `Untyped`, an undeduced `Auto`, an error), or no node. A
base inside a template's body is typed per instance; each instance's
aggregate is listed and merged by name, each member's type grouped by
instance as `IrAnswer::Copies` groups a declaration's, and a field two
instances' aggregates write apart (`get<A>`'s `s.x` against `get<B>`'s) is
no jump, a pick between them being a guess about which instance the reader
means.

**The gate grades what the editor will serve; a failing list's ledger
line pins the fault, not the copies.** The completion side's IR answers
are now the editor's queries — each candidate's detail
`Db::ir_answer_of_completion`, a member list `Db::loop_members_at`, graded
name by name and then detail by detail. A candidate only the copies type
is `Copies`, ranked in a list below `Agree` (a list that agrees wherever
the CST engine types keeps its `agree` item) and above `Neither`. The
first run of that churned 86 failing items — the same keys, the same CST
answers, IR digests changed only because a template's candidate (`array`,
`Foo`) now spelled its instances' types beside an unrelated fault. Such a
candidate grades nothing, there being no reference answer to hold it to,
so a failing list's line spells it as it did before, and only a list
classed `copies` spells the copies. A member list the CST engine leaves
empty is not graded — no reference answer — and is counted
(`completion-loop-only`, 9: a local class's `Do` and `x`, which the
reference's own pass 6 leaves `TUnresolved`, `Type.hs:1195-1196`;
`this`-captured fields; fuzzed buffers' `auto`s). Reading after: agree
1497 → 1499 (two member lists the loop now reads, both agreeing), every
failing set unmoved.

**The nine adjudicated disagreements cannot leave what the editor serves
on those buffers.** Each sits in a snippet accumulator that declares a key
twice, which is a parse-time error (`SymbolTable.hs:200-201`), so no such
buffer passes the editor's gate and the CST engine answers there, as it
did. In the gate they stay `disagree`: the reference side is the CST
engine's answer by the gate's construction, and the loop's, adjudicated
right, is the IR side. They leave when the loop runs on broken buffers
(W3.4).

**One program per input state.** The race the entry before this one left:
the diagnostics and a request on one edit both missed `Db::program`, both
loaded it, and each held its own `Arc`; `Db::looped`'s in-flight slot is
matched by program identity, so the second replaced the first's slot and
ran a second loop. Each layer a racer misses — the parse (by text stamp),
the item tree (by parse), the program (by revisions and trees) — now
looks under its write lock for an entry another racer stored for the same
inputs, and returns that. Exact: the adopted value equals the one the
racer computed, from the same inputs; only the allocation it holds
changes. Proven by eight `Db::looped` callers behind a barrier on five
fresh edits, nothing loaded first: one loop each, 20 runs of 20; dropping
any one layer's adoption gives "round 0: two loops"; `edit-identity` (a
quarter of the roots, `scripts/fast.sh loop`) 87 of 87 identical.

Left before the CST engine can be deleted, for the editor: the loop on
broken buffers (W3.4) — a member list typed fresh, `a.` mid-statement, is
the CST engine's, since that buffer does not parse; method navigation
(`c.Go()`, which neither engine answers); and the CST table's remaining
readers — `Db::type_of_definition` as every feature's fallback,
`members_of`, `field_definition`'s second half, the inlay hints' fallback
— which go with W3.6–W3.7 once the gate's `ir-silent` (757 hover, 324
completion) is at parity.

## Methods through the receiver, and every declaration the instances reach — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3.5. `Db::{definitions_at, member_answer_at, member_callee_at}`,
`navigate.rs`'s `navigation_loop` and `loop_member`, `Looped::members`;
`kg-lsp`'s definition, hover and rename, `handlers/instances.rs`'s
`called`.*

Go-to-definition on a method — `c.Go()`, `fixture.Run<3>(t)`, a method
of a template instance's copy — was answered by neither engine: the
loop's member lookup (`loop_field`, now `loop_member`) kept fields
alone, and the CST engine's half (`field_definition`'s, now
`member_definitions`') reads fields alone. A member after a `.` now resolves
through the loop's type of the receiver, as a field did, and six
decisions a reader would otherwise have to rediscover.

**A method is reached through the receiver's type and lands on the
class's text.** `c.go` is `method (typeOf c) go` — `lookupSymbolByName (x
++ [y])` under the class (`Type.hs:1358-1362`) — never a name in scope, so
it is `Looped::members` of the receiver's type, as for a field, and the
member is mapped back to the declaration it was written as
(`Db::definition_of_declaration`): an instance's copy keeps the
template's head (`Src::expanded`), so `a.Get(0)` on a `Box<4>` lands on
`Box`'s `Get`, through `using Box4 = Box<4>` alike; a member template's
member is its function, whose name token files the `Template` item first,
so `fixture.Run<3>(t)` lands there. The CST engine's half stays fields
only: it is to be deleted, and a buffer that does not parse gets no method
jump until the loop runs there (W3.4).

**Where the instances reach several declarations, the answer is all of
them.** `Engine` declaring `Go` in each branch of a `static if (Fast)`,
reached as `e.Go()` inside `run<F>`'s body, is the first branch's `Go` in
`run<true>` and the second's in `run<false>` (`static_control` splices
the branch an instance takes into its class copy, `Constexpr.hs:358-370`).
A pick would state a fact about one instance as if it held for the text —
the reason a field two instances declare apart was no jump — and a list is
no pick: `Db::definitions_at` answers both, and go-to-definition sends the
protocol's `Location[]`. So does that field now: `get<S>`'s `s.x`, `A`'s
`x` in `get<A>` and `B`'s in `get<B>`, offers both. In the text's order, not the loop's: the loop
decides `run<false>` before `run<true>` (by the arguments), and a list of
places is read top to bottom. `Db::definition_at`, the one-answer query
references, rename, highlight and signature help read, is it when there
is exactly one and declines otherwise. Hover names each declaration under
the fence and counts them.

**Hover on a member is the instance's member, a member template's call
the instance it compiles.** The declaration's own answer inside a class
template is every instance's — `Box::Items` reads `() -> uint32[4] //
Box<4>` and `() -> uint32[9] // Box<9>` — which is not what `a.Items()` on
a `Box<4>` calls; `Db::member_answer_at` reads the member off the
receiver's aggregate (the member's own copy node, as completion's detail
already did), per enclosing instance inside a template's body. A member
template's own declaration has no one signature, and the call says which
instance: `Db::member_callee_at` is `Looped::callee_at` on the call the
selector heads — `(uint32) -> uint32 Run  // Run<3>`, where the
template's answer lists `Run<5>` beside it — rendered by the function
signature help renders with (`instances::called`).

**A method holding a lambda is `Donated`.** `desugarLambdas` rebuilds a
function round what is left of its body (`Function.hs:206-214`), and the
rebuilt node wears the method's own range as a donor's. `Looped::members`
admitted `Own` nodes alone — to leave out the function
`abbreviatedFunctionTemplate` keeps beside its template — and so dropped
every method holding a lambda, which in the library is most of them:
completion after `test.` in `test/library/control/loop.k`'s
`pipelined_wait_test` offered `flag` and not `Run` (main's binary, the
same stdio session), a list the CST engine had right before the loop's
replaced it. A `Donated` function standing at its own declaration is now a
member unless an `Own` member claims the same text — the abbreviated
leftover, which `a_loop_member_list_offers_what_the_text_declares` pins
(`twice` twice without the dedupe). A small change in `looped.rs`, which
another line of work owns; the resilience gate is unmoved (its member
lists hold no such method).

**Navigation reads the loop the root buffer's diagnostics run.** The
field lookup asked `Db::editor_loop(roots, f)` with `f` the file the name
is in. References and rename resolve every `.x` in every file a buffer's
program reaches, and for a clean import under a buffer that does not
parse that gate passed and ran the loop the buffer's diagnostics never
run — the 900 ms on `risc-v.k` a broken keystroke does not pay. The gate
is now the root's (`navigation_loop`); a miss count pins it (0 → 1 with
the old gate).

**References and rename fall out, and the rename refuses where it cannot
place a use.** Both resolve each candidate with `definition_at`, so a
method's uses through receivers the loop types are found; references
under-reports the rest honestly. A rename may not, and refuses on three
grounds, each naming the file or line. *An aggregate's member is
importable*: the rename module called a class member file-local, which
stopped being true for fields when they resolved through types
(2026-09-06) and is not true for methods — `main.k` holding a `Counter`
calls `c.Go()`. *A `.name` reaching this member and another by
instance* (the `static if`): skipping it leaves `run<true>` calling a
`Go` that no longer exists, taking it renames a `Go` `Engine<false>`
does not have. *A `.name` outside any template that resolves to
nothing*: a method's call in a buffer that does not parse, where no loop
runs. An unresolved `.name` *inside* a template's body is not refused:
the receiver has a type only in the instances, the base library is full
of bodies no program instantiates, and refusing there refused most renames
of a common name. The hole that leaves: a body the editor's four rounds
(`PassBudget::INTERACTIVE`) had not instantiated yet — its use is missed,
and the next full check reports it.

Driven over stdio — the release `kg lsp`, a fixture of the four shapes,
and a copy of `test/library/control/loop.k` under a manifest importing
`library/` (whose diagnostics show 25 "Failed to instantiate template"
errors at the editor's four rounds, as main's binary does; `kg check`
none): `fixture.Run<-10, 10, 3>(tag)` lands on the local `Fixture`'s
`Run` and hovers as `(type.newtype::newtype<uint32>) -> void Run  //
Run<-10, 10, 3>`; `test.Run()` and the `while_do` fixture's
`fixture.Run()` — both holding lambdas — land and list; every request
answered in ≤ 6 ms once the diagnostics were in.

## The keystroke, by phase — 2026-10-10

Sprint S6's last open target, the bench's keystroke on `risc-v.k` (≤ 400
ms), without carrying the loop across edits (W7.5d, awaiting the owner).
Interleaved against `1df2e17` on a quiet machine, `cargo xtask bench
--filter keystroke`: 598.6 / 623.5 ms → 310.3 / 323.1 ms. Seven commits,
each graded by `infer-identity`, its `--dump` against `1df2e17`'s (304/304
identical every time) and `scripts/fast.sh loop` (every ratchet +0/−0);
the numbers per step are in the commits and in `performance.md` §10.
What a later reader needs:

**The keystroke stage is its own program, and now has its own table.**
`--filter phases` prices `risc-v.k` under the recorded compile's
settings, where its loop is 0.92 s; the `keystroke` stage runs it under
`rooted_settings` (`mini-base.k`, the mock device), where the loop is
0.34 s and the edited file's sorted lowering was another 0.13 s. Read the
wrong table and the lowering is noise. `--filter keystroke-phases` runs
the stage's own case — N keystrokes after a warm-up, each one's wall
time and the phases of all together — and `--keystrokes 10` less
`--keystrokes 0` under `/usr/bin/time -l` is ten keystrokes in
instructions, which the machine's load does not move. Every lever below
was picked off a `sample` profile of that run, aggregated inclusively
(the scripts are not checked in: `sample <pid> 20` and a call-tree
fold).

**Most of it was work whose answer was already known to be "no".** Four
of the cuts test a cheap necessary condition before the expensive
question, each exact by construction rather than by measurement: every
key a symbol lookup probes ends in the name looked up, so a name that
ends no key cannot be found (`moveFunctions`' body-local map,
deduction's `Template`-filed names, `intrinsics`' five names), and a
fingerprint match needs the base's path first (`resolve`). The pattern
to reuse: find the part of the expensive question whose absence already
answers it. Three more keep an answer that cannot move for as long as
it is kept: a scope's declarations, read once (its statements are in
text order, so "one ending before the use declares it" is "the first
one does"), `declared_anywhere` once a name, an argument list's
rendering once a `resolve` pass (the rewriter only appends).

**A deferred value must not keep its source alive.** The harvest's
fingerprints were 18% of a keystroke, read only where `nub` weighs two
hits; they are now computed on first read from the harvested IR and the
interner (`kg_hir::sort::Fingerprint`). The sorted memo, which compares
an importer's recorded answers on every later lowering, keeps the
*value* of what `nub` compared and nothing of the rest: keeping the
deferred one would hold every imported module's IR of that moment for
as long as the importer's memo stands — nothing the identity gates can
see, since the answer is the same. `an_importers_memo_keeps_no_imported_ir_alive`
pins it with a `Weak`, red for a compared answer and for one not.

**The editor's footprint had no bound, and it was the allocator.** A
warm `Db` re-checking `risc-v.k` grew ~90 MB a keystroke — 0.28 GB
cold, 1.18 GB after ten, 1.87 GB after twenty — and stayed at 0.23 GB
with `MallocLargeCache=0`: the same retention the previous entry found
for one run (macOS keeps freed large blocks, and each round's are larger
than the last), compounding across edits in `kg lsp`. mimalloc holds it
at 0.54 GB after ten keystrokes and after thirty, and costs 18% fewer
instructions a keystroke (cycles 5–10%). `kg`, `kanagawa` and `xtask`
declare it as the global allocator, `xtask` so that the bench and the
gates run the frontend as `kg` does; four crates came with it
(`mimalloc`, `libmimalloc-sys`, `cc`, `find-msvc-tools`) and the system C
compiler at build time. The backend's C++ keeps its own `malloc` —
nothing is freed across the two — and the backend gate with its cache
off agreed on all 73 `library/data` programs under it. A one-shot `kg
check` peaks a little higher (`risc-v.k` 0.70 → 0.78 GB). Reverting it is
one commit (`120ef09`).

**LTO was measured and left out.** Fat LTO with one codegen unit: −8%
instructions, −7% cycles a keystroke, and a release rebuild after a
one-file edit to `kg-sem` 17 s → 107 s; thin: −6%, 31 s. Every gate tier
rebuilds release, so the testing loop would pay it on every run; a
separate profile for shipped binaries is where it would go.

**What remains**, per `risc-v.k` keystroke (311 ms; `KG_LOOP_PROFILE`
and the phase table): the loop 227 ms — inference 69 (each fixpoint's
first iteration walks and re-counts every unit the passes made), the
round prefix 50 (`moveFunctions`' two catas over each parent's body),
deduction's walk 20, instantiate with `resolve` 18, the symbol maps and
snapshots ~20, pass 1's heads and `redundantNameScope` ~20 — and outside
it the CST passes 22, the program's assembly 15, the copies' check 16,
the lowering 9. All of it starts again from the edited file's lowering
on every keystroke; M6's ≤ 100 ms is W7.5d's, not more of this.

**The target was met on the bench's program, not the editor's.** A user
editing `risc-v.k` in a project that imports `library/` has the full
base library — the recorded settings, 50 modules where `mini-base.k`
gives 38 — and there a keystroke is ~0.88 s (`bench --filter
keystroke-phases --recorded`, 25 keystrokes, load ~3; the release `kg
lsp` over stdio on a copy under such a manifest, ~1.35 → ~0.95 s an
edit). Its loop is ~0.69 s, and inference ~45% of it: every keystroke
re-infers the whole library from fresh trees, which no cut here can
remove and carrying the loop across edits (W7.5d) would. The sprint's
≤ 400 ms is written against the bench's stage; whether the bar should
be the recorded program's is the owner's to say, and the instrument for
it now exists.

## The editor on a buffer that does not parse: the last loop, mapped — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3.4. Decided on the numbers below before any of it was built;
what was built, and what it measured, follows the decision.*

Hover, completion, member lists and method navigation read the loop on a
buffer that parses and the CST engine on one that does not — and typing
`a.` mid-statement is one that does not, so the member list a user meets
most is the CST engine's. Two designs were on the table: **(a)** run the
loop on the broken buffer itself, for the answers only (never its
diagnostics: the reference stops at a parse error, `Main.hs:73-75`), and
**(b)** keep the last loop computed on a parsing state and answer from it,
positions mapped across the edit.

**What a broken keystroke costs.** `risc-v.k`, `core.` typed at the end of
a statement in `ProgramTest`'s method; a scratch stage of `cargo xtask
bench`, five keystrokes each, load 3–4:

| per keystroke | the bench's settings | the recorded settings (the editor's program) |
|---|---:|---:|
| a clean one: the diagnostics, the loop in them | 290–370 ms | 857–1008 ms |
| a broken one: the diagnostics stop at the parse error | 23–25 ms | 26 ms |
| the broken buffer's own loop — (a)'s price | 234–273 ms | 680–687 ms |
| the CST engine's member list | 12 ms | 12 ms |
| mapping the loop's text onto the buffer's (`TextMap`) | 0.09 ms | |

**What each would serve.** The resilience gate's IR side answered three
ways (its 140 buffers, the editor's settings and budget; `KG_PROTO`, a
throwaway switch):

| the 64 fuzzed buffers (mutants of clean files) | hover agree / ir-silent / ir-only / copies | completion agree / ir-silent / ir-only |
|---|---|---|
| (a) the mutant's own loop | 474 / 8 / 461 / 51 | 235 / 162 / 48 |
| (b) the clean file's loop, mapped by common prefix and suffix | 275 / 207 / 294 / 42 | 159 / 266 / 20 |
| (b) the clean file's loop, mapped by a line diff | 468 / 14 / 473 / 48 | 188 / 215 / 42 |

The 76 error-recovered corpus files never parse, so (b) has nothing for
them; their own loop, (a), answers hover agree 485, ir-silent 749, ir-only
58, copies 83 and completion agree 305, ir-silent 162, disagree 9 (the nine
adjudicated loop-right in "Completion and member navigation on the loop").

**Decided: (b) for every reader, and (a) once where there is nothing to
map.**

- **(a) per keystroke is out.** Completion never waits, and at the `.` that
  asks for it the broken buffer's loop is 0.24–0.68 s away: (a) cannot
  serve the member list it exists for. Every broken keystroke would cost a
  clean keystroke's loop where it costs 24 ms of diagnostics today. What it
  serves that (b) does not is text the last loop never saw — a declaration
  typed in the broken region — which is 47 of the fuzzed buffers'
  completion lists (a list is graded by its worst candidate) and 6 hovers.
- **The mapping is a diff, not a prefix and a suffix.** The fuzzer makes
  one to four edits at random places, and so does a user who leaves a
  line broken and edits elsewhere: one changed span from the first edit to
  the last lost 199 hovers. A line diff refined by characters within each
  changed run keeps everything between (`kg_db::text_map`). A range maps
  where its first and last characters are unchanged, each through its own
  run — so a node enclosing the edit is the node it was, and its answer
  the last one the loop had (graceful staleness, `ir-elaboration.md`
  §2.6) — and a node whose own edge is new (`foo` edited to `foobar`, `a`
  typed before its `.`) is nothing the loop knew.
- **A base typed fresh is typed by its name.** `a.` typed mid-statement is
  new text, so its base maps to nothing; a base that is a name resolves to
  its declaration (`Db::definition_at`, which works on any parse), and the
  loop's type there is the receiver's — inside a template's body, each
  instance's.
- **Completion reads the newest loop there is**, mapped: the edit's own
  once computed, the last one before. It still never waits and never runs
  one, and now answers from the loop as a clean edit lands too, where it
  answered from the CST engine.
- **(a) once: a buffer with no loop at all** — opened broken, or evicted
  from the memo — runs its own loop for a hover, once; every later
  keystroke reads that loop mapped, as (b), until a parsing state's loop
  replaces it. Hover only: it is asked for, not sent per keystroke as
  completion, inlay hints, signature help and document highlight are. It
  costs that buffer one clean keystroke's loop, once; the diagnostics
  never read it, so the gutter shows the parse error and nothing the loop
  invents.

**Built** (`kg_db::text_map`, `kg_db::looped::EditorLoop`, `Db::{editor_loop,
editor_loop_ready, editor_loop_or_own, base_answer}`; `kg-lsp`'s hover and
completion; `xtask resilience`'s IR side). A `Looped` keeps the parse each
module was lowered from; an `EditorLoop` is a loop and, for each module
whose parse has moved on since, the `TextMap` from the loop's text to the
buffer's — rebuilt from the trees once per edit (1.6 ms on `risc-v.k`) and
kept beside the loop until the next. Every question the editor asks of a
loop goes through it: `answer_at` and `callee_at` map the range in,
`members` maps each member's declaration out. Three readers, by how much
they may wait:

| | buffer parses | buffer does not | readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Db::editor_loop` | the diagnostics' loop (waits) | the last loop, mapped | inlay hints, signature help, navigation |
| `Db::editor_loop_ready` | the newest loop, mapped (never waits) | the last loop, mapped | completion |
| `Db::editor_loop_or_own` | as `editor_loop` | as `editor_loop`, else its own, once | hover |

Two choices a reader would otherwise have to rediscover:

- **A member list an edit reshaped is not the loop's.** When any member's
  declaration no longer maps — `first`'s closing brace deleted — the whole
  list declines and the CST engine is asked, rather than a list missing
  the member the user is editing, which would say the aggregate has fewer
  than it does.
- **A rename does not act on a mapped answer.** A node that encloses an
  edit keeps the answer it had: `static Counter c;` retyped `static Engine
  c;` while the buffer is broken still reads `Counter`, and a hover saying
  so is the last good answer. A rename of `Counter::Go` acting on it would
  rewrite `c.Go()`, now `Engine`'s (measured: the refusal mutated away, it
  did). So a member's rename refuses while a buffer in its search reads its
  loop through an edit, naming the use, as it refused before for a method
  no engine placed; references list such a use, as the last good answer.
- **A node is the same node if its first and last characters are, and not
  if only its head is.** Mapping a declaration by its start and its name
  would answer the 8 hovers and 49 completion lists below — and answer
  with the clean file's type where the mutation changed it: `const bool
  False` lost its `const` in one mutant, and its type with it. The strict
  rule raised no disagreement; the loose one could.

**The resilience gate** now asks what the editor serves, in the state an
editor would hold each buffer in: a fuzzed buffer is laid over its clean
file after the clean file's loop has run (as its diagnostics would), and
an error-recovered file, which never parsed, is asked its hovers first —
the first runs its own loop — then its completions. `cargo xtask
resilience`, before → after:

| | before (each buffer's own loop, which no editor read) | after (the editor's loops) |
|---|---|---|
| hover | agree 959, ir-silent 757, ir-only 519, neither 1707, copies 134, declined 1422 | agree 964, ir-silent 764, ir-only 537, neither 1700, copies 135, declined 1398 |
| completion | agree 540, ir-silent 324, disagree 9, ir-only 101, neither 8 | agree 495, ir-silent 375, disagree 9, ir-only 95, neither 8 |
| `editor-reads-loop` / `-runs-own-loop` | 0 / — | 61 / 79 |

What the editor *serves* from the loop went from none of the 140 buffers
to all of them — the nine adjudicated disagreements included: on those
accumulators, once a hover has run their loop, the editor shows the
loop's `const uint1` and `uint63`, right per snippet, where it showed the
CST engine's. The ledger: `agree` 1499 → 1459 (+17/−57), `ir-only` 620
→ 632 (+44/−32), `copies` 134 → 135 (+12/−11), `cst` 5058 → 5082 (+24),
`disagree` 9 → 9 (+0/−0). All 57 `agree` items lost are on fuzzed buffers —
49 completion lists and 8 hovers whose candidate or declaration the
mutation wrote or reshaped (the `const` above; a stray `"` swallowing
`main` to the end of the file; a `<` taking an initializer's tail), text
no loop has seen, which the editor answers from the CST engine as it did
before. The never-parsed files lost nothing; they gained 3, and `cst` 24
questions, from methods now resolved through the loop on a broken buffer
(`definition_at`). Ten of the 44 new `ir-only` answers — the clean file's
loop typing what the CST engine does not on the broken text — checked
against `kg-oracle --typed --passes 19` on the clean file: `eq` and `lt`
`TBoolean`, `test696_a` `GetN<70>` (and `<0>`, `<2>`, `<1>`), `x` `TUnsigned
1`, `fifo_width_alignment` `TConst (TUnsigned 4)`, `Foo44::x` `TSigned 5`
(the mutant had nested it inside `TestCase6`): every one the reference's.
`fuzz/010`'s copies now read `in , , ` — the clean file's loop names no
instance of `tranpose_test`, made inside `TestTranspose<…>`'s copies,
where the mutant's own loop named three; a gap in `Looped::name_instances`
for nested copies, not traced here.

**Latency.** The keystroke bench (`cargo xtask bench --filter
keystroke`, `risc-v.k` worst, interleaved against `211c2ea`, load 6.5 →
2.2): before 303.0 / 306.6 ms, after 304.4 / 312.2 ms — the diagnostics
run nothing new. Over stdio, the release `kg lsp` on a copy of
`risc-v.k` under a manifest importing `library/` (the editor's real
program; opening it 883 ms), `MULHU.` typed after `DisasmTest`'s `auto
MULHU = cast<Instr>(…)`:

| | before (`211c2ea`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| completion as the edit lands | `[]` in 44 ms (the CST engine's) | `Instr`'s `r` `i` `s` `b` `u` `j` in 18–29 ms |
| diagnostics | 44–45 ms, the syntax errors | 19–30 ms, the syntax errors |
| hover on `LUI`, below the edit | "Type not yet inferred" | `processor.risc_v.isa::Instr LUI`, 16–17 ms |

On a fixture of the shape the plan names (`a.` typed at the start of
`Runner<4>::run`, `a` a `Box<N>` member): `items uint32[4]`, `first () ->
uint32` in 2 ms; `g`, moved a line, `uint33 g  // Runner<4>`; `a.first()`
jumps to `Box::first` — before, `[]`, "not yet inferred", `null`. The
same `risc-v.k` opened broken: diagnostics 6 ms; completion before any
hover the CST engine's `[]` (63 ms); the first hover runs the buffer's own
loop, 677 ms; then hovers in 0–22 ms and completion from the loop,
through the next broken keystroke too.

**What still keeps the CST engine alive for the editor:** text no loop has
seen (a declaration typed or reshaped since the last loop, a member list
whose aggregate an edit reshaped); a buffer opened broken until a hover
runs its loop; and everywhere the loop has no type — the editor's four
rounds leave most of `risc-v.k`'s template bodies uninstantiated —
`Db::type_of_definition` as every feature's fallback, `members_of`,
`field_definition`'s second half, the inlay hints' fallback. The gate's
`ir-silent` (hover 764, completion 375) is that remainder; carrying the
loop across edits (W7.5d) would let a broken keystroke's own loop replace
the mapping where it is stale.

## The passes after instantiation onto the loop, one at a time — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `kg_db::passdiff`, `cargo xtask passdiff`,
`kg_sem::check::TextPass`, `passes::FromLoop`. Pass 14 first.*

**The instrument is the CST run itself, recorded in place.** A pass's
verdicts depend on where it runs: the CST run calls it only past the
checkpoints (`Frontend.hs:38-52`, per file here), over a sink that may
already hold what a later pass reads (`null (errors a)`, `TypeCheck.hs:162`,
the conversions' poison). So the differential does not call the CST pass
on its own: every CST run calls `passes::judge_text` in the pass's place,
and while `xtask passdiff` records that pass on the thread it also runs the
CST pass over a copy of the sink and keeps what it adds. The loop's side is
what `Looped::text_for` filed for the module — exactly what the run admits
in the pass's place once it is switched. Identical in every module whose
run reaches the pass is the switch changing no diagnostic; a module whose
run stops before the pass is not compared, since neither side is admitted
there. Its blind spot, stated: a verdict the loop gives where the CST run
never reaches the pass is never graded, and is never shown either.

**The loop's text verdicts are computed ungated.** `kg_sem::check` gates
the copies' passes program-wide (`raised.is_empty()` after the refusals and
pass 9), the reference's one flag. The text verdicts are computed whether
or not that flag is set, and the CST run admits them behind its own per-file
checkpoints, as it ran the CST pass: the switch then changes *which code*
decides, never *when it speaks*. Moving the gate to the program-wide flag
is a separate step with its own gate evidence, once every pass is on the
loop.

**What the loop's pass 14 sees that the CST pass never did.**
`validateExtern` is `desugar validate` (`Frontend.hs:304-313`): every node,
a template's own body and both branches of a `static if` left standing in
one included, and `removeTemplate` (pass 15) keeps a template's diagnostics
(`Frontend.hs:299`). The CST pass skipped every template body and every
`static if` branch (`reached_only_after_elaboration`), and named only a
simple name this file declares once. `kg-oracle --errors` (2026-10-10)
refuses `extern S;` of a struct declared in an uninstantiated class
template's body; inside `static if (true)`; `extern K<uint8>;` of a struct
template's instance; and `extern T;` of a template's own parameter,
*whatever its argument* — `getSymbols` files no parameter
(`Symbols.hs:52-68`), so the lookup fails and the catch-all refuses. Inside
a copy the reference reports the copy's verdict too, framed. None of these
is in the corpus (`passdiff` read 2 CST verdicts, both shared); the loop's
pass gives each, and `kg check` now prints each probe's first error where
the reference does.

**The base run and the text door have no pass 14.** The base run
(`Db::check_with(.., false)`, the second census's error gate) reads no
loop, and a moved pass runs after instantiation in the reference
(`Frontend.hs:55-66`), so nobody judges it there; `check_source`, the
one-file door with no loop, keeps the CST pass until its deletion and then
has none.

**Pass 10, and a difference the reference settles.** The loop's `cata
typeErrors` reads the loop's types, folded as `inferExpTree` folds them
(`Inference.hs:47`); the CST pass read the CST engine's table and stood
down wherever a constant it could not fold might have changed the rule
(`fold_divergent`). On the corpus the two agree on all 47 verdicts the CST
pass gives, and the loop adds two: `auto-placeholder.k::33,34`, `x / -1`
and `x % -1`, "Division/Remainder with negative denominator is
undefined" — the reference's second error, after pass 17's "Could not
deduce variable type". A difference is not always a defect of the move,
so `passdiff --oracle` puts each one in a snippet to `kg-oracle --errors`
(the `errors` gate's reading, cached) and passes where the reference
gives every verdict only the loop gives and none only the CST pass
gives; a root that differs stays red, unasked. The paren rule needed the
text: `term = noted $ choice [… hidden (parens expr) …]` notes `(a <<
b)`'s error at the `(` (`Parser.hs:836,845`), the IR has no node for the
parentheses, and `looped.rs`'s `paren_note` moves the verdict out over
every enclosing pair, as `bracket` and `capture_list_note` do for theirs.
Inside a copy pass 10 has no version on either side — `bool + 1` in
`f<bool>`'s body is the reference's error, framed, and neither engine's —
left for a change with its own gate evidence.

**Deleting a moved pass's CST code.** `FromLoop` carries the loop's text
verdicts always and says apart whether a moved pass whose CST code is
still there is the CST's (`cst`: the text door, `KG_CST_TEXT`); a pass
whose code is gone is admitted (`FromLoop::admit`) under either.
`passdiff` refuses a pass with no CST side left — it would read
identical everywhere, having compared nothing (`PROBED`, held to the CST
run by a test).

**Pass 13, and the reference's notes.** The CST pass gave a member's
refusal no note when the class's own file exported it, never followed a
public object to its class, and gave an imported class's refusal from the
exporting module's run. The reference's `err x e = NotedExp (note (unfix
x) <> n)` stacks notes by `Src`'s `<>` (`Parser/Syntax.hs:623-626`), and
`expandErrorStack` renders the stack's right spine (`Error.hs:185-189`):
`export Foo;` then `extern Foo;` are two notes in that order, and a class
held as a public object is noted at the object, then its own `extern`,
then its holder's — `kg-oracle --errors`, 2026-10-10. `kg_sem::check`'s
`Note` is that algebra, and `exportableClasses` is `mapWith` per module
(`old <> new`) and `Map.unions` across modules (the first module wins).
Two things only the text can say were moved there, as for pass 10: a
verdict is filed under the module whose `export` made its class
exportable, where the CST run gave it (`TextVerdict::home`), and its
ranges start at the first token — the IR wears a declaration's leading
comment, which no note includes (`basics.k::177`). `passdiff --oracle`
compares every note's position as well now; all 14 differences were the
loop's.

**Pass 18, and a difference nothing can settle.** The CST pass scanned a
string's text and judged only a hole it could type without inference; the
loop's reads every hole's type and every alignment's fold. On the corpus
they agree on 7 of the CST pass's 9 verdicts, and the other two are alike
in all the reference prints — position and message — and apart in the
range's end: `"{ {} }"`'s hole, which the CST's text split ended after the
space before the `}`. The reference prints no end, so no oracle can settle
such a pair; `passdiff` books it, listing both sides on every run, and
does not count it as a difference. A change it would not book: a position,
a message or a note.

**Where it stopped, and why.** Four passes moved — 14, 10, 13, 18 — each
with the CST pass recorded in its place agreeing with the loop or settled
by the reference. Pass 17 did not: a type the loop left undecided is the
reference's verdict when nothing else failed (`auto x;`) and the shadow
of an error elsewhere when something did (a refusal in a helper module;
`datetime.k` under `mini-base`), and the reference tells the two apart by
its one flag, which stops every pass after the first that errs, program-
wide. The CST run's checkpoints are per module, and passes 1–9, 12 and 16
at the text still decide them, so the loop's check cannot know the flag,
and the CST pass's syntactic certainties were what kept it honest. Every
pass whose verdict is "this was left undecided" — 16's `unresolved`, 17,
much of 19's — waits on that choice (the sprint plan's W3 step 1 entry
lists three). Measured, the readings that show it: `passdiff --oracle
--pass deduceAuto` 16 apart, 5 unsettled, all cascades; with undecided
types silent, 7 unsettled, all the reference's own `TUnresolved`.

## A copy is named by what the loop recorded, not by the tree's shape — 2026-10-10

The W3.4 entry left a gap untraced: hover listed `tranpose_test`'s
instances as `in , , `. `Looped::name_instances` named each `while
compiling` frame by the first node of its expansion a walk from the root
met, taking that node for the copy's declaration. A node of a copy can be
reachable from outside it: `unit::test<1>(TestTranspose<false, false>)`
passes a function template's instance as a value, and the walk met a
`Seq` of `TestTranspose<…>`'s copy first, marked the expansion seen, and
never named it. Measured with a probe on `fuzz/010`: expansions 2–4 (the
three `TestTranspose<…>`) met an untyped `Seq` first, 9–11
(`tranpose_test<…>`) a struct-typed node.

The loop now records, as `instantiate` makes each copy, the expansion its
nodes carry and the `TInstance` `setTypeOfInstance` notes on its root
(`kg_sem::Elaborated::copies`, `Template.hs:125`), and the editor spells
the frame from that (`unmangleInstanceName`, `Type.hs:176-177`). Nothing
is read back off the tree, and the walk is gone. `resilience` +13/−13,
every pair a rename: 11 lists that read empty now name their instances
(`mod_mapping<4>, mod_mapping<8>`, `EccMemTest<512>, EccMemTest<8192>`),
and `template-instance-identifiers.k`'s chain gains the `A2_t<2>` frame the
walk had dropped. A hoisted local function reads `Run@Foo@Do<uint32>`,
which is the reference's `pretty (last x)` of the hoisted name.
`hover::a_function_instance_passed_as_a_value_is_named` goes red ("2
unnamed") with the walk restored.

## The program-wide flag, and pass 17 on the loop — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1, continued. `Db::program_erred_through_pass_9`,
`kg_sem::check::TextVerdict::undecided`, `kg_sem::check::deduce_auto`,
`passes::FromLoop`. The lead's decision (a), scoped: the sprint plan's W3
entry of the same day.*

**What the flag is.** The reference has one `hasErrors`, set by `checkPar`
after the pass-1 composite, by `instantiateTemplates`' `hasErrors'`, and by
pass 9's `or errs`, each over the whole program (`Frontend.hs:44-52,85-86`,
`Template.hs:55-56,84`); once set, every later pass is skipped
everywhere. The CST run keeps a gate per file, which is the editor's
shape and stays. For one class of verdict that is not enough: a type left
*undecided* can be another module's fallout — the instantiation an error
there stopped is what would have decided it — and the module is then
correct. `test/library/data/datetime.k` under `mini-base` read 19 such
(`library/data/datetime.k`'s `memory<…>` is undefined there), and
`template-param-default.k::13,14` two (a refusal in the helper). Those, and
only those, wait on the program's flag now.

**Where it is computed.** Folded, first error wins: the parse stage of
every module (the reference never enters `frontend` past one,
`Main.hs:73-75`); the loop's own part, `Checked::erred` — a refusal or a
round's error, pass 9 in a copy, and a name a rewrite made that pass 9
rejects (`desugarLambdas`' `make_capture1()` with no base library: the
reference's "Symbol name not in scope", which no text here can place, so
it is not reported, only counted — four kg-db unit tests over capturing
lambdas without a base went red without it); and each module's CST run
through pass 9 at its text (`undefined_symbols::Through9::erred`). A CST
run seeded with the copies' errors closes at pass 1, so its gate says
nothing of its own text; the flag runs such a module again unseeded.

**What it costs, and why lazily.** The CST runs are memoized nowhere —
deliberately, `db.rs`'s docs — so "paid on first open, not per keystroke"
was not on offer: every keystroke makes a new program and a new loop, and
a sound key for one module's early verdict would have to hold every name
the whole program declares (pass 4 and pass 9 look names up program-wide).
So the flag is asked only where a verdict waits on it. `kg check` reads it
off the runs it makes anyway — a module holding such a verdict runs last,
so nothing runs twice. The editor runs the other modules through pass 9
only when its own buffer holds one, on threads (each with its own program
context: a syntax tree is no `Sync`). Measured 2026-10-10 over stdio, the
release `kg lsp`, a root of `import data.vector` plus `const auto ZZ = ZZ;`
under the full library (36 modules): 29–35 ms a keystroke at `c9f6f28`,
56–59 with the runs in a row (20–28 ms of them), 39–41 on threads. A clean
buffer pays nothing: `bench --filter keystroke` interleaved 316.9 / 352.0
ms before, 310.7 / 336.2 after; `risc-v.k`'s first open under `library/`
within noise. And a program the editor's four rounds truncate — every one
importing `library/` I tried but the smallest — gives no undecided verdict
at all, so it never asks.

**Pass 17's two classes.** `deduceAuto` writes `typeof n` back as syntax
(`Type.hs:1595-1610`), and where `expFromType` has nothing to write
(`:1612-1650`) the `auto` becomes the error. The loop's port judges every
type: `TInitializer`, `TError`, `TTemplate`, an array of no dimensions,
`TUntyped` are refused whatever else happens (per file, as before); a type
with an unresolved or undefined part and nothing else wrong is
*undecided*, and waits. Two undecided ones the syntax settles, which the
CST pass trusted and the loop keeps: no initializer at all (`try _ Nothing
= TUnresolved`, `Type.hs:1108`) and a `static for` over a bound no fold can
give (`constIndexType`, `:1113`; `certainly_runtime`, the same reading the
loop's `static if` check already used). Without that, the editor — whose
loop the budget truncates on any real library program — showed no error
for `auto x;`; with it, it shows the CST pass's.

**Three things the reading taught.** The note of a `for`'s induction
variable starts at the `auto`, past the `const`: `uninitConst` notes
`Const <$> typ` after the keyword (`Parser.hs:451`; `auto-placeholder.k::7`
at 5:19, where an ordinary `const auto x` is noted at the `const`). A
variable pass 10 reported at is not pass 17's: `errorMsg` replaces the node
(`Error.hs:147-148`), so `static for (const auto i : -3)` is "can't be
negative" alone (`basics.k::2`) — `type_errors` now returns the nodes it
replaced. And a standing `static if`'s branches are not walked: pass 16
replaced it with its own error first (`Frontend.hs:406`).

**passdiff.** The probe now records, beside the CST pass, what the run
*admits* in the pass's place — the flag applied — rather than what
`Looped::text_for` files. `deduceAuto --oracle`: 11 programs apart, all
ir-only, all settled for the loop, 0 unsettled; red under the flag never
set (3) and always set (6).

**A trap, for the next worktree.** `UPDATE_EXPECT=1 cargo test` in a
`.claude/worktrees/` checkout rewrote the *main* checkout's
`crates/kg-db/tests/memo.rs`: expect-test 1.5.1 takes the *outermost*
ancestor holding a `Cargo.toml` for the workspace (`to_abs_ws_path`), and
the main checkout is an ancestor of every worktree. It was put back byte
for byte at once (the six lines it changed were the only difference). In
a worktree, set `CARGO_WORKSPACE_DIR` to the worktree, or update the
expectation by hand.

## Pass 16 on the loop: what the fold left standing — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `kg_sem::check::post_desugar`, `passes::judge_text`.*

**The pass reads the fold's leftovers, not a fold of its own.** The CST
pass folded each `static assert`, `clog2`, width and `static if` predicate
itself and, since nothing had run before it, reported only when its fold
*succeeded* with a value the reference rejects, or the expression could
not fold whatever resolved later (runtime names, bare literals). The loop
folds in place as `evaluateConstexpr` does, so a node still standing at
the end is the reference's leftover, and `unresolved`/`staticAssert`
(`Frontend.hs:393-407`) judge it as they stand. The `cata` matters:
`desugarError` replaces a node and everything inside it, so the walk is
post-order and a replacing verdict drops its subtree's
(`int<clog2(0)>`, `static if (clog2(0) == 1)` — one error each,
`kg-oracle --errors`).

**Three places the reference never judges, which a leftover alone does
not show.** An error passes 1–8 left inside — the reference's flag stops
pass 16 then; such an `Exp::Error` now also sets the loop's own part of
the flag (`Checked::erred`), since the CST run reports inference's errors
from its folder after every pass and never gates on them. A shift of two
literals the fold left — a negative count, on which the reference
*crashes* (Haskell's `shiftL`; `basics.k::4,5` are `expected:0` only
because the harness counts `Error` lines): no verdict. And a type where a
`static assert`'s value goes, the reference's parse error.

**The folder's own errors, and why the CST pass still runs.** The first
reading left one difference no rule in the loop could settle:
`uint<2 * bytesizeof 1>` (`constexpr.k::124`), where the reference reports
`bytesizeof`'s error alone. That error is pass 6's — `evaluateConstexpr`
raises it — and the CST run raises it from its folder only because pass
16's CST code folds that width; without the CST pass running, the error
vanished from the output altogether (measured: the merge base prints it,
the first switch did not). So the CST pass keeps running, on a copy of the
sink, for its folds; and a fold that raised an error keeps the loop's
pass-16 verdicts out, as the reference's flag would. It goes when the loop
reports pass 6's verdicts at the text itself — the deletion that would
otherwise follow this switch waits on that.

**Price a walk before landing it.** The first `post_desugar` was a
recursive walk returning a `Vec` per node and cloning each `Exp`: the
keystroke bench, interleaved against the merge base, read +20–25 ms on
`risc-v.k` in two rounds (355 / 336 ms against 333 / 310). One explicit
stack and one output vector truncated on replacement: 334 / 338 / 319 /
313 against 341 / 329 / 333 / 329 — noise. Every pass `kg_sem::check`
runs walks the whole program on every keystroke.

## `checkReturn` reaches the body's top level only — 2026-10-10

Found by the W3 pass-17 work and traced here: `if (c) { return {0}; }
return 1;` in an `auto` function was rejected ("Non-empty initializer
list cannot initialize type uint1"), and `kg-oracle --errors` accepts it.
The reference applies `checkReturn` through `renote (fmap $ renote
checkReturn) $ body e` (`TypeCheck.hs:76`): the body's own statements,
one level, so a `return` inside an `if`, a loop or a block is never
conversion-checked by pass 19. A taken `static if` branch is the top
level, since `staticControl` splices it into the body and
`removeNestedSeq` flattens it (`Constexpr.hs:44-47,125`). Probed with an
`S` returned as `uint8`: the oracle rejects it at the top level, in a
taken `static if` branch and in a template's copy at the top level, and
accepts it one `if` or block down, template or not. Both our checkers
converted every `return`: the CST pass now requires the `return`'s
block to be the function's body (it never enters a `static if` branch),
and the loop's check hands the function type to the body and through
`Seq`s only. Every gate +0/−0 — the corpus never returned an invalid
value one level down — so `conversion::only_a_return_at_the_body_s_top_level_is_converted`
pins it, red under each of three mutants. What the backend makes of such
a `return` is the backend's to say, as in the reference.

## The backend's messages, graded — 2026-10-10

Sprint W6 asked for the number behind §8's first decision (whether source
locations join the parity bar): `backend` graded the first `Error N` and
the exit code, never the line that names the place. It now also compares,
for every program both compilers reject with the same *backend* code
(N > 1), the first error line with each side's directory cut to the
file's name — `Error 53 at: syntax_test_temp_file.k (5): Unions cannot
contain strings` against the reference's own. 204 of 256 are identical;
the 52 others keep the code and the message and differ in the line
(`string.k::0`: 5 against 6; checked whole, every one of the 52 differs in
the line alone). That is divergence #25 — our spans and the reference's
are different objects — reaching the one place a user reads a backend
location. Ratcheted as the `message` pass set, so the count may only rise;
`cargo xtask backend --verbose` prints both lines of each difference.

The first version counted `Error 1` too and read 993 of 1102, committed
with "the 109 differ in the line" written from one example. Checked
whole, 57 of the 109 were the frontend's `Error 1` lines — positions,
booked divergences #7 (the reference's parser rejects where a later pass
here does: `dependent-template.k::2`, 4:1 against our 8:1) and #30 — which
the `errors` gate grades. The measure is the backend's lines alone now;
the baseline was re-blessed (−789, the frontend programs leaving the set
by definition, not by regression).

## Pass 19 on the loop: `checkConversion` first, and a seed that closed the run — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `kg_sem::check::TextPass::CheckConversion`,
`Cx::judged_as`, `passes::judge_text`.*

**Three pieces, because the CST made three.** `validateProgram` is one
`desugar'` — a `cata` (`Desugar.hs:71-74`) — whose `VariableF` clause is
`checkShadowDecl $ checkVarDecl x` and whose call clause is
`checkFunctionArgs` (`TypeCheck.hs:33-216`). The CST port split it by
module: `conversion.rs` (the three `checkConversion` sites and the
arity), `shadow.rs` and `validate_program.rs` (everything else). Each
moves on its own `passdiff`, since each has its own CST code to compare
and delete; the loop's side stays one post-order walk (`Cx`), each site's
verdicts filed under the piece it belongs to.

**The seam was a seed, and a seed closed the run.** The loop's check had
judged every conversion site — copies and the module's own text alike —
and filed the text's as unframed "seam" verdicts among the copies'.
`Db::frontend_diagnostics_in` seeds the CST run with those
(`run_through_9`'s `out`), so a conversion *error* at the text was in the
sink before pass 1, and the pass-1 checkpoint closed the run: every
later pass at that module's text was lost. `uint8 x = s;` beside `static
assert(clog2(0) == 1)` printed the conversion alone, where `kg-oracle
--errors` prints both; and `uint8 x = s; nosuch();` printed the
conversion, where the reference's pass 9 sets its flag and it prints the
undefined name alone (both probed against `b221969`'s `kg check`). Filing the text's verdicts under their pass instead —
admitted in its place, seeding nothing — fixes both for conversions. The
other text-site verdicts of the walk (enum checks, a global closure, `op=`
under pass 10) still seed until their own move, and the copies' still
seed at pass 1: the next item.

**Ungated at the text, as before.** The walk now runs whatever the
loop's own part of the flag says; only the copies' verdicts are dropped
when a refusal or pass 9 in a copy set it (`Template.hs:55-56`,
`Frontend.hs:86-87`). Before, the walk ran only with the flag clear, so
a program with a refusal anywhere had no loop conversions at all — and
the CST pass's stood in.

**What the reading taught.** `passdiff --oracle` could not settle a
warning: the oracle prints warnings only under `--Werror`, only those
enabled (`conversion` is off by default, `Options/CmdArgs.hs:111-117`),
and only where the program raises no error (`app/Main.hs:93-96`). It now
asks a second time, every kind switched on after the snippet's own
switches. Of the 32 programs apart, five were narrowing warnings only
the loop gave, all the reference's (`template-argument-deduction.k::33`
`Fn_T_U<uint2>(x, y)`); the rest were seam verdicts the CST pass
missed or placed elsewhere (a whole designated list against the
element). The one rule the CST pass had and the loop lacked: `bitsizeof`
of a class is `TUnresolved` for good (`tWidth TClass{} = Nothing`,
`Type.hs:718`), so `assert(bitsizeof(_c309) == 40)` is "Invalid
conversion from `unresolved` to `bool`" (`basics.k::110`).

**`checkShadowDecl` next, and the CST pass's note was the name.** The
loop's tree is the one pass 19 reads — `moveFunctions` has hoisted every
nested function to its parent's qualifier, `desugarLambdas` every lambda
— so the reference's lookup, `lookupInScope (init declScopeName)` over
the program's map (`TypeCheck.hs:110-121`), is the whole rule; the CST
pass had to reconstruct the hoisting from the text (`survives_hoisting`).
`passdiff` put 23 programs apart, and 22 differed in one thing: where the
note goes. `noteContext x declName` stacks the shadowed declaration's
own note, which starts at its first token — `bool x;` at `bool`, a class
member `uint64 V;` at `uint64` (`kg-oracle --errors --Wshadow --Werror`,
2026-10-10) — where the CST pass noted its name. No gate grades a note's
position but `passdiff`, so the CST's had stood since the pass landed.
Two of the 23 are corpus roots the oracle cannot read (its parser
rejects the `>>` in `library/test/internal/assert.k:59`, which every
`test.unit` importer pulls in); each was probed as a snippet of the same
shape.

**The rest of `validateProgram`, and what an earlier pass replaced.** The
CST pass judged each clause over the written text, and the sink told it
only pass 16's width verdicts (`WidthUndecided`) to stay out of. The
reference's `errorMsg` and `desugarError` *replace* the node they judge
(`Error.hs:147-148`), so pass 19's `cata` never meets anything inside an
earlier pass's error: `uint32 x = 1 + (uint32);` is pass 10's "Invalid
operands" alone and `clog2(uint32)` pass 16's argument error alone
(`kg-oracle --errors`, 2026-10-10), where the CST run printed "Invalid use
of a type as an expression" beside each — second errors, which no gate
grades. The loop's walk now carries the ranges of every earlier text
verdict that errs — passes 10, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, computed before the
walk now, and pass 12's, which the walk itself raises after the arguments
it judges and so is applied when the walk ends — and no `validateProgram`
verdict is admitted inside one (`type-check.k::38`: `Foo<auto, false>` is
pass 12's "Unresolved argument", no `auto`). Two more the IR made plain:
a `struct` declared in a body is a declaration, not a type in statement
position (`data/closure/core.k:17`, which every program imports — the
first reading put all 3099 programs apart); and an `auto` the loop holds
is pass 19's only where the text wrote it — an abbreviated template
leaves a rewrite's copy of its signature beside it (`extern-class.k::15`'s
`void Do(auto x);`, `numeric/int/operator.k`'s `increment` in a program
whose instantiation stopped), which the reference never has standing.

## The text seeding gap: every verdict at its own pass — 2026-10-10

*`kg_sem::check::Stage`, `passes::Carried`, `Db::frontend_diagnostics_in`.*

**What the gap was.** The loop's check raised its verdicts in the copies
— and, until pass 19 moved, its verdicts at a module's own text too — and
`frontend_diagnostics_in` handed every one to the module's CST run as the
sink it starts with. The first checkpoint, after pass 1, reads the sink
(`Early::has_errors`): one seeded error closed the run there, and every
later pass at that text was lost. So the run's checkpoints were not the
reference's (`Frontend.hs:38-52`): an error was in the module's error set
from pass 1, whatever pass raised it. `uint8 x = s;` beside `static
assert(clog2(0) == 1)` printed one error where the reference prints two
(the example the pass-17 work found), and the gap ran both ways — a
copy's pass-19 conversion was printed beside the module's own pass-9
error, which in the reference had stopped every pass after 9.

**What it is now.** Two rules, one per kind of verdict. At a module's
text a verdict is its moved pass's (`TextPass`) and is admitted in that
pass's place; the last two text sites that still seeded — a `static
assert`, which pass 16's text verdicts already judge, and an `op=`'s
`Binary`, pass 10's — went there. In a copy a verdict carries the pass it
is the reference's (`Stage`: a refusal, a round's error and inference's
in a copy are pass 8's, `instantiateTemplates`; a copy's undefined name
pass 9's; the rest after 9), enters the sink at that pass — before the
checkpoint after 8, before the one after 9, before pass 10, where pass
12's and pass 16's poisoning read it — and is shown only where the run got
that far. A module whose own text stops it at pass 1 shows no refusal; one
stopped at 9 no copy's conversion. Both are the reference's per-module
reading of its one flag, the per-file shape the editor stands on kept: a
module is still not silenced by another's error.

**What it cost and what it moved.** No gate moved: the corpus's
must-reject snippets have no copy verdict beside an earlier error of their
own text. Three probes pin it (`tests::a_copys_verdict_enters_the_run_at_
its_own_pass`), each `kg-oracle --errors`' reading. **The keystroke
bench did move: `risc-v.k`, its worst file, 324 → 440 ms** (`cargo xtask
bench --filter keystroke`, each commit built in one directory with every
source touched, 2026-10-10: `b221969` through `29f8bee` 324–335 ms,
`e8c2987` 446, `d86eeee` 440, two directories agreeing). Under the bench's
settings (`mini-base`) the file's copies raise errors at pass 9 and after
it, and those used to close its CST run at pass 1 — the file's own passes
2 to 19 never ran, and `kg check` on it printed 16 errors where it prints
26 now: pass-9 verdicts — `static_cast`, `memory_norep`, `memory_init`,
`async_exec`, which `mini-base` leaves out of scope — in modules whose
runs the seeds had closed, `risc-v.k` itself and `processor/risc_v/
internal/core.k` among them. Putting the pass-9 and
after-9 seeds back at pass 1 restores 332 ms (measured); the stage-8 ones
alone make no difference. So the cost is the module's ordinary CST run,
which the gap had been skipping; it is exact, and it is not free — the
CST runs are memoized nowhere. The A/B readings recorded for the pass-19
switches above stand: the same bisect reads them flat.

**A trap in the A/B, for the next reader.** `git archive | tar -x` keeps
each file's commit time as its mtime. Re-extract an *older* commit over a
build made later and cargo rebuilds nothing — the "before" binary is the
last one built. And a release binary's speed here moves with the path it
was built at (the crates' metadata hashes, hence codegen-unit
partitioning): one source tree read 330 ms built in one directory and 440
in another. Build both sides in one directory, touch every source after
extracting, and read each twice.

## Pass 9 on the loop: ten causes, traced before anything moved — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `kg_sem::check::Undefined`, `TextPass::UndefinedSymbols`,
`kg_sem::check::CopiedName`, `kg_hir::Refused`, `passes::judge_text` in
`undefined_symbols::run_through_9`.*

**The first reading, rebuilt.** The previous session's prototype — the
copy walk judging written nodes at the text too, admitted in the CST pass's
place — was not committed; rebuilt the same way, `passdiff
undefinedSymbols --oracle` read what it had: the CST pass giving 635
verdicts, 3003 programs identical, 96 differ (cst-only 297, ir-only 6), 95
unsettled. Every difference was then traced to one of ten causes before
any behaviour changed; each was put to `kg-oracle --errors` — a corpus
snippet, or for a root (the oracle cannot read most under `mini-base`: its
parser rejects `library/test/internal/assert.k:59`, or the very undefined
template the difference is about) a snippet of the root's shape.

**The loop's bugs, five.**

1. *A value's name read as a rewrite's.* The walk skipped every node at
   the text that was not `Written::Own`, taking `Donated` for "a rewrite
   made it" (`make_capture1` with no base). But the lowering donates a
   value's `QualifiedIdentifier` the `NamedValue`'s range — one CST node,
   two IR nodes — so every undefined *value* at the text was skipped:
   `static_cast`, `make_pair`, `index_t` as a value, `HARTS`. The test is
   now the name's identifier. Two thirds of the first reading.
2. *Where a name is noted.* A scoped type name is noted at its last
   identifier, as the parser notes it (`Outer::Inne` at `Inne`,
   `type-identifier.k::14,15,22`); a free call's qualified callee over the
   whole path (`freeFunctionSpecifier`, `Parser.hs:772-780`).
3. *`err n` replaces the node.* `Backend::Sv` is `Sv`'s verdict alone
   (`options.k::5`): the qualified identifier's error replaces its subtree,
   the undefined qualifier's with it (`Frontend.hs:101-102,134`). The walk
   reported both.
4. *A name a rewrite copied.* `higherOrderFunctions` copies a
   function-typed parameter's type into the template parameter it makes,
   so `([[last]] is_last) -> void Do`'s `is_last` is judged on a copy whose
   identifier the rewrite made (`higher-order-functions.k::210`). Neither
   kind of rewrite-made identifier can be told from the other in `kg-sem`;
   the text can: `kg_sem::check::CopiedName` carries the identifier's range
   and spelling, and `looped.rs` admits the verdict where the text spells
   the name there, and counts it toward the flag alone where it does not
   (`make_captureN`, whose note is the capture list).
5. *Two of divergence #7's stand-ins.* Where the reference's *parser*
   rejects, the CST pass's verdict stood in, and the loop had none: (a) a
   path the sorter refused — `optional<uint32>`, `index_t<N>`,
   `static_cast<uint32>(…)`, `b1<10>` under `mini-base`, whose `<` no
   parse-time template opens ("unexpected '<'") — which the lowering keeps
   as an unsorted `Exp::Path` the engine never types; and (b) a template
   template parameter's default nothing declares, `typename Memory =
   memory`, which `templateSpecifier` rejects at the name (`Parser.hs:368`,
   `bitarray.k:17`) and the lowering reads as a value. For (a) the lowering
   now records what the sorter knew when it refused (`kg_hir::Refused`: the
   scope qualifier every `ScopedNameF` of the path would carry, whether the
   parse-time table answered the head, whether the path is written as a
   type), and pass 9 judges the head as it would a `ScopedNameF` with no
   qualifier: not in scope when neither the parse-time table nor
   `lookupInScope` from that scope finds it. For (b) the default's name is
   a type name, once — the copy an instance leaving the parameter out takes
   is judged as the value the lowering read, and dropped.

**The CST pass's mistakes, five; the loop was the reference's.**

6. *A body inference never types.* `inferExpTree` infers a function whose
   parameters are not all resolved no further than the parameters
   (`Type/Inference.hs:58`), and a lambda not at all until it is
   desugared (`:55`) — so names in such a body are never `TUndefined`, and
   pass 9 says nothing there. The CST pass judged them by syntax:
   `DecoderTests(register_index_t reg, int_t imm)` in `risc-v.k` under
   `mini-base`, every `pipelined_for(n, [](index_t<n> i) { … })` body.
   Probe: `inline void h(nope x) { uint8 m = static_cast(x); }` — the
   reference reports `nope` alone.
7. *A template's body.* A higher-order function is a template
   (`higherOrderFunctions`, pass 2) and a generic lambda an abbreviated one;
   pass 9 restores a template's body unjudged (`Frontend.hs:93-94`) and
   judges its copies, framed. The CST pass judged `TestBitwiseOp`'s body
   (`bits.k:716`) and a generic lambda's (`risc-v.k:4000`) at the text,
   unframed, instantiated or not.
8. *A `mux` no fold decides.* `evaluateConstexpr` replaces a `mux` only
   when its selector folds (`Constexpr.hs:311-314`); a standing one is
   walked whole. The CST pass skipped every case and the selector:
   `ENABLE_M ? … : …` (`testbench.k:9`), `(cycles() % 2 == 0) ? …`
   (`test_cases_41.k:379`). Probe: `x == 2 ? nope_then : nope_else` —
   both reported, and the CST pass compiled it clean.
9. *A hint's type partition.* `hints tIsType` filters by the declaration's
   inferred type (`Frontend.hs:141`); the CST pass by its kind, so an alias
   whose target is undefined — `using pair_t = pair<…>` with `pair` out of
   scope — was offered as a type name (`export_class_test_cases_2.k:177`,
   `custom-instr.k:114`'s `int_t`). Probe: `using pair_t = nope; using
   pair_u = uint32;` then `pair x;` — "Perhaps you meant: `pair_u`" alone.
10. *Settled by the reference outright*: four snippets the loop gives and
   the CST pass did not — `static-if.k::42`'s `Do` on an instance whose
   `static if` dropped it, `lambdas.k::21`'s capture, `function-
   constants.k::1,3`.

**The reading after.** `passdiff undefinedSymbols --oracle`: the CST pass
giving 635 verdicts — 3083 programs identical, 16 differ (cst-only 21,
ir-only 11); the 4 snippets settled for the loop by the reference, the 12
roots by the probes above, one class each (6: `external_class.k`,
`vector.k`, `modular.k`, `mmio.k`, `risc-v.k`, `common_subexpression.k`;
7: `bits.k`, `risc-v.k`; 8: `testbench.k`, `test_cases_41.k`,
`schedule.k:93`; 9: `export_class_test_cases_2.k`, `custom-instr.k`,
`mmio.k`). `query.rs`'s test-library walk now gives the reference's own
reading of `mmio.k` — four `HARTS`, not the six it booked as a divergence
— and `testbench.k`'s `ENABLE_M`, which it said this port did not give.

**The census's gate, and a defect it was hiding.** The base run
(`Db::check_with(.., false)`, `Db::instances`' error gate) reads no loop,
and the earlier switches left it no pass after 9. Pass 9 at the text went
the same way at first, and `xtask ir` went red: `test/logic/
memory_test_cases_3.k` under `base.k`, whose only errors are pass 9's
(`ECC_SUPPORT`), opened the gate, and the second census decided
`PointerChase<array>` in round 1 where the reference decides it in round 2
(`kg-oracle --template-iterations 1` against `2`). The gate is a
*deliberate* over-approximation (`instances::Gate::Errors`: any error,
passes 9 to 19 included, only ever loses instances), so the base run now
takes pass 9's verdicts at the text from the loop — the loop never reads
the census, so there is no cycle — and nothing else of it
(`FromLoop::pass_9_of`). `xtask ir` is byte-identical to `main`'s last run
but for timings (170 root sets decide, 311 gated). The census's round-1
reading of a template template argument is left as found; W3.7 deletes
the census.

**What the instrument cannot see** stays as for the other passes: a module
whose run stops before pass 9 is not compared. And a name a rewrite minted
that pass 9 rejects — `make_captureN` with no base library — sets the
program's flag but closes no module's run after 9, so that module's
passes 10 to 19 still speak where the reference's flag would have stopped
them (a no-base higher-order call shows pass 12's "Could not deduce all
arguments"); it was so before the move wherever the text held no other pass-9 error, and no corpus program has it.

**Deleting the CST pass, and the guard it held.** The deletion found what
the switch had lost and no gate could see: the CST pass returned at once
where the program's symbol map held `$errors` — a module with a syntax
error, the symbol `checkPar` reads to set the flag program-wide
(`Frontend.hs:48-52,85`) — or where any import had failed to load, after
which the reference never enters the frontend (`Main.hs:73-75`) and every
name the missing module would have supplied looks undefined. `Db::check`
stops at the parse stage before either, so every `passdiff` run, every
gate, saw nothing; the editor's per-file gate (`Db::diagnostics`) runs a
clean buffer's passes while another module is broken, and the loop's pass
9 then called `cthing` "not in scope" in `main.k` because `b.k`'s `import
c` found nothing. The guard is now `undefined_symbols::stands_down`, as
the CST pass had it. **For the next switch**: before deleting a CST pass,
read every early `return` in it — a guard against a program the rooted
door never reaches is invisible to an instrument that reads the rooted
door.

**What the keystroke paid.** Interleaved, each commit extracted into one
build directory with its sources touched (`cargo xtask bench --filter
keystroke --json`): before the switch the worst file, `risc-v.k`, read
440.5 / 436.4 / 441.2 ms and the corpus 7545 / 7496 / 7537 ms; at the
switch, both passes running, 434.3 / 440.0 and 7838 / 7763; after the
deletion 402.8 / 417.2 / 397.4 and 7661 / 7615 / 7662. The worst file
gained 30–40 ms — under `mini-base` it holds dozens of undefined names,
each hinted by both passes until the deletion — and the corpus lost ~1.6%,
unattributed; the likeliest share is the modules a wrong CST verdict had
closed after pass 9 (a template's body, a body inference never types),
which now run passes 10 to 19.


## `FRONTEND_COMPLETE` set — 2026-10-10

The owner's decision (`sprint-parity.md` §8, "Answered 2026-10-10"),
taken on the condition the constant's own comment set while it was
`false`: `--strict`, which scores as if it were `true`, fails nothing, and
has failed nothing since 2026-09-28. Set, `conformance` reads **2681/2681,
241 undecidable** where it read 2602/2602, 320 undecidable — the 79 warning
assertions are graded now, and every `expected:1` snippet that compiled
cleanly would be a failure, not a shrug. The 241 left are the assertions
that expect a C++ backend code, which the frontend must not decide and
`backend` grades end to end; the headline says "undecidable without the
backend" accordingly. Every ratchet held, +0 / −0.

`strict-ledger` scored the scoreboard's reading with a literal `false`
— a second reading that would have gone on saying 2602 after the flip,
and that `status-md`'s `conformance` row is rendered from. It reads
`FRONTEND_COMPLETE` now, so the two readings agree and the ledger still
follows if the constant is ever set back. The rule that a pass unsure
whether the reference rejects stays silent is unchanged — a missed error
now fails one assertion where it used to be undecidable, but an invented
one still breaks an `expected:0` and possibly the 241 deferred to the
backend (`CLAUDE.md`, "Where you cannot be exact").

## Pass 6 on the loop: the fold's errors in the tree — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `kg_sem::infer`'s `evaluate_constexpr`,
`kg_sem::check::fold_errors`, `TextPass::InferType`, `passes::Early`'s
`folder_speaks`.*

**Why it came first.** Pass 16's CST code could not be deleted after its
switch: its folds raised the folder's own errors — pass 6's, which the
loop's tree did not hold at the text — and where one did, the loop's pass-16
verdicts were held back (`constexpr.k::124`). The loop's fold declined every
`desugarError` the reference makes (`kg_hir::constexpr::value`: "the
checking passes' to report and never a value"), and the CST folder reported
them from whichever CST pass happened to fold the node.

**What the reference does, and what the loop now does.** `evaluateConstexpr`
replaces the node it cannot fold with an `ErrorF` that keeps the node's note
(`NotedExp n $ eval e`, `Constexpr.hs:122`): `Div`/`Mod` by a zero literal
(`:181-186`), `bytesFromBits` on a width not whole bytes (`:274-275,349-351`),
`maybeAt` failing a `mux`'s selector (`:353-355`), an illegal `decltype` or
offset (`:345-347`). The node was `TUnresolved` (`infer (BinaryF …)` of two
literals, `Type.hs:1182-1185`) and becomes `TUntyped` on the next iteration
(`infer ErrorF{} = TUntyped`, `:1294`), so nothing above it folds. The loop
already made the last two; it now makes all of them, in place
(`Cx::replace`, `kg_sem::infer`), and its untyped arm types the error node as the
reference does. A `mux` selector out of range errs only where a later fold
gave it: a literal one types the mux `TUnresolved` (`Type.hs:1237-1238`) and
the fold's guard never lets it through.

**Where it is reported.** Every such node at a module's own text — written
`Own`, under no copy's frame, not a round's conflicting deduction — is pass
6's verdict (`fold_errors`), walked as inference walks: a template's
parameters (`Inference.hs:63`; `template <uint<bytesizeof int4> N>` is
rejected uninstantiated), never its body. It enters the CST run in pass 6's
place, before the checkpoint after 8, so a module with one shows nothing
from pass 9 on. In a copy the same node is raised framed at pass 8's stage,
as inference's own errors there already were: `4 / N` in `f<0>` is "Division
by zero" at the body with `f<0>` as its note — the reference's, and new.
A `mux` case the fold did not select takes its error with it (`mux(1, 1 / 0,
2)` is clean in both), as a deleted `static if` branch never folds.

**The folder that no longer speaks.** The CST run's evaluator is shared by
passes 6, 12 and 16, and its errors were reported at the run's end and read
by the checkpoint. Once the loop speaks for pass 6 (`folder_speaks` false:
not the text door, not `KG_CST_TEXT`) they are neither: they are the CST
side `passdiff` records — at pass 6's place for the `decltype` and size
checks, at the run's end for the folds (`passdiff::record_more`), since a
fold the CST pass 16 made raised there. The base run takes pass 6's text
verdicts from the loop with pass 9's (it is before `hasErrors'`,
`Template.hs:55,84`); `xtask ir` is byte-identical but its timings.

**passdiff inferType --oracle.** 12 CST verdicts on the corpus, all shared;
one program apart, `constexpr.k::124`: the loop's `bytesizeof 1` error now
closes that module's run at pass 8, so the CST pass 16 that used to raise it
never runs — the reference's own error, settled. Red with the loop's
verdicts dropped (13 unsettled). The corpus pins little of this, so six
rooted-door tests do (`tests::infer_type`, each a `kg-oracle --errors`
probe, each caught by its mutant).

**Two positions.** Parentheses: `term = noted $ … parens expr` renotes the
inner node from the `(` (`Parser.hs:836,845`), and `(4 % 0)` is reported
there; the CST folder reported the inner expression, the loop's verdict
moves out as pass 10's does (`paren_note`). The other, found and left: a
binary operator's node is noted at the *operator* (`binaryNoted`,
`Parser.hs:78-89`), and only the root of an `expression` is renoted from its
start (`expr' t = noted $ …`, `:832`). So `uint32 x = 4 / 0;` is at the `4`
but `1 + 4 / 0` at the `/`, `static assert(1 / 0 == 0)` at the `/`, and pass
10's `a + true + 1` at the first `+` (`kg-oracle --errors`). Both engines
note every node at its CST range's start (divergence #25), so the two passes
that report a binary node print an operand's position one token early; no
corpus first error is such a node (`errors` agree 701).

**Not reproduced: the stop.** `instantiateTemplates` returns at once once
`hasErrorSymbol` holds after a round's passes (`Template.hs:56,84`), so an
error from passes 2–6 anywhere means no copy is ever made. The loop keeps
instantiating; what its copies then raise is shown only in a module whose
run passes its own checkpoints. Unchanged by this move, and unmeasured.

## Pass 12 on the loop: four causes, and the LT pass 4 reported early — 2026-10-10

*Sprint W3 step 1. `TextPass::UnresolvedTemplates`, `passes::Early`'s
`held`, `kg_sem::check::CopiedName::pass`.*

**Two sides that both spoke.** Since W1.4 the loop judged every pass-12
arm on an instance left standing at a module's text, and the CST run
admitted those verdicts before its own pass 12, whose three arms then ran
too; the run's dedup merged what both said alike. And pass 4's CST code
reported pass 12's "Could not deduce all arguments" itself, where the
argument list is decided — before any checkpoint, since its kind is exempt
from the one after 8. Moving pass 12 made the loop's the only voice, and
the comparison had to hold the early LT for pass 12's place
(`Early::held`), recording it even where the run stops short of pass 12:
the reference never reaches pass 12 once pass 9 erred, so `take(1)`
beside `nosuch()` is pass 9's error alone (`kg-oracle --errors`), where the
CST run printed both — the blind spot "a module the run stops before the
pass in" would otherwise have hidden it.

**Four causes, traced before anything changed** (9 programs unsettled at
first):

1. *The template's note wore its documentation.* `errorMsgWithContext (note
   $ unfix t)` (`Frontend.hs:419`) notes the declaration from its first
   token; the IR's range takes in the comment the parser attached
   (`println`'s note at `print.k:29`, the reference's at `:39`; `basics.k::
   3,20,21,23`). `token_note`, as passes 13 and 19 use it. This was the
   output before the move as well, on every LT a no-deduction `println`
   gives: no gate grades a note.
2. *"Undefined template" at the text was nobody's.* The loop left it to
   pass 9 ("an undefined name is pass 9's") — but `undefinedSymbol
   (TemplateInstance a _)` judges the arguments only (`Frontend.hs:96-97`),
   so the name is pass 12's: `template Go<bool>()` over a `Go` a dead
